article_content: A sharp, darkly comedic stage play called Ulster American is set to debut in London, bringing together three powerhouse performers: Woody Harrelson, Andy Serkis, and Louisa Harland. Written by acclaimed Irish playwright David Ireland and directed by Jeremy Herrin, the production opens at Riverside Studios in Hammersmith on December 13, following previews starting December 4. The story centers on a volatile rehearsal room where an Oscar-winning American movie star, a British director, and a Northern Irish writer clash over creative control, cultural missteps, and the hidden costs of fame. As tensions rise, the line between fiction and reality blurs in this unflinching satire about privilege, voice, and who gets to tell which stories. Harrelson steps back onto the London stage for the first time since the early 2000s, portraying Jay Conway—a larger-than-life Hollywood icon. Serkis returns to live theater after years dominating film roles as Leigh Carver, the director trying to keep everything together. Harland plays Ruth Davenport, the sharp-tongued playwright whose perspective is constantly undermined. Behind the scenes, the design team led by Max Jones, Oliver Fenwick, and Emma Laxton crafts a world that mirrors the chaos onstage. The play, which first stunned audiences in Edinburgh in 2018 and took home two major Fringe awards, continues to challenge norms with biting wit and raw honesty.

article_content: Before they became household names as the iconic duo Walter White and Jesse Pinkman in the Emmy-winning series Breaking Bad, Bryan Cranston and Aaron Paul spent years grinding through minor roles and odd commercials just to make ends meet in Hollywood. Archival clips reveal Cranston pitching Preparation H hemorrhoid cream in the 1980s, appearing as a doctor in a forgotten TV episode, and hawking Coffee-Mate in a 1988 ad. Meanwhile, Paul can be spotted competing on The Price Is Right in 2000 and playing a high school dance host in Third Rock From the Sun in 1999 — years before their breakout. Both actors also had fleeting moments in mainstream films, including Paul’s small part alongside Tom Cruise in Mission: Impossible 3. These roles, though barely noticed at the time, were stepping stones in a long, uncertain journey. When Breaking Bad concluded its run on AMC in October 2013, it did so with a record-breaking 10.3 million viewers — the largest audience the show had ever drawn. Creator Vince Gilligan described the finale as both 'satisfying' and 'unapologetic,' a fitting end to a story that defied conventions. The series dominated the 65th Primetime Emmy Awards, taking home seven awards — including three consecutive Best Actor trophies for Cranston, two for Best Supporting Actor for Paul, and a Best Supporting Actress win for Anna Gunn, who portrayed Skyler White. With four nominations for Outstanding Drama Series, Breaking Bad cemented itself as one of television’s most celebrated dramas.

Klip arhivál demonstra Cranston promoviendo Preparation H krem pa hemorroides na e 1980, aparesiendo komo un doktor na un episodio olvidá di teleri, i promoviendo Coffee-Mate na un anons di 1988. article_content: (CNN) — The sound of loud grunts and shrieks has become a defining feature of top-level tennis — a cacophony accompanying high-stakes matches as stars compete for the sport’s most prestigious titles. This week at the Australian Open in Melbourne, the year’s first Grand Slam, the vocalizations of three-time Grand Slam champion Maria Sharapova and World No. 3 Victoria Azarenka have drawn significant attention. Their clash in Saturday’s women’s final could bring the controversy to a peak, with the No. 1 ranking also on the line. 'About Maria, what can I say?' said eighth seed Agnieszka Radwanska after her quarterfinal loss to Belarus’ Azarenka on Tuesday. 'It’s pretty annoying — it’s just too loud.' Throughout her career — which includes reaching World No. 1 and winning Wimbledon at age 17 in 2004, followed by two additional Grand Slam titles — Sharapova has been known for the volume of her on-court vocalizations. 'I’ve heard it a few times over my career,' said the 24-year-old Russian. 'You’ve watched me grow up. You’ve watched me play tennis. I’ve been the same throughout. No one important has ever told me to change. There’s no rule change now, and I don’t hear one is coming — so what difference does my answer make?' Currently, the WTA Tour has no explicit rule prohibiting grunting. However, its regulations do forbid hindrances — unintentional disruptions like a hat falling off or a ball dropping from a pocket, which result in a let. If an umpire deems a hindrance deliberate, the player loses the point. Though the International Tennis Federation’s 2012 rulebook does not mention grunting, the WTA has stated it is working to reduce excessive vocalization among younger players without disrupting those who developed their game under current norms. 'Everyone who watches tennis knows grunting is part of the game, and we’re aware some fans find it bothersome,' a WTA statement read. 'We’re exploring ways to address excessive grunting, especially for newcomers, without negatively impacting established players. We must take these concerns seriously and review our rules and educational approaches.' Martina Hingis, a five-time Grand Slam champion who retired in 2007 after a 13-year career, won three consecutive Australian Opens from 1997 to 1999. Now competing in the seniors’ event in Melbourne, she said the noise is more distracting for spectators than players. 'Sometimes, when they stretch more, it gets louder — and you wonder, What are you doing?' the 31-year-old said. 'Other times, they grunt heavily on the service line, but the ball has no weight. I think it’s mostly an issue for spectators.' Due to the intensity and uniqueness of Azarenka’s screams, the Rod Laver Arena crowd began imitating her during her second-round victory over Australian Casey Dellacqua. 'Of course I hear it — I’m not deaf,' Azarenka joked. 'But it’s fine for me. I respect the crowd. I just stay focused on my game.' With the WTA focused on educating the next generation, opponents of Sharapova and Azarenka may have to endure the loud vocalizations for the foreseeable future — or perhaps invest in earplugs.

'Mi ta oí e sonidu pa un puña di bês na mi karrera,' di e rusa di 24 aña. 'Mi ta mirá mi kresé. Mi ta mirá mi joga tenis. Mi ta e mesmu tutu e karrera. Nadie importante ta di mi pa kambia o fá algo diferente. Na momentu no ta havi un kambiá di reglamentu. Mi no oí ku ta bini un, asina ku no ta importá ku ta respon di mi, ¿no?' Na momentu, no ta havi regla espesífiko di WTA ku ta prohibí gemidos. Però, e reglamentanan nan ta prohibí obstáku — diskursashonan inintensióna komo un sombrero ku ta bai, o un bola ku ta sali di bukso. Pa e kasu, ta kalla un let i e punto ta repleyá. Un obstáku ku ta konsiderá intensióna pa e árbitro ta rezultá na pérdida di un punto. Tin e reglamentu di Federashon Internashonal di Tenis di 2012 no mensiona gemidos, WTA ta ekspliká ku ta trabá pa reduí e gemidos eksesivo na e pròxima generashon di jugadoran, sin afektá e jugadoran ku ta desenbolbi su jògo ba e kondishonan aktuala. 'Tutu ku ta mirá tenis sabe ku gemidos ta partidu di e jògo, i nos ta konsiente ku alguno fanatiko ta halla e ta fastidia,' ta leí un declarashon di WTA. 'Nos ta eksplorá maneras pa reduí gemidos eksesivo, spesialmenti pa jugadoran mas jóven ku ta komensá, sin afektá negativamente e jugadoran ku ta desenbolbi su jògo ba e sistemá aktuala. Nos ta kredé ku nos ta nesesita pa adresá e konsernan ku ta eksprimí pa alguno fanatiko i mirá e reglanan i politikanan di edukashon pa konsiderashon.' Martina Hingis, kampéon di cinco Grand Slam ku ta retirá na 2007 despues di e karrera di 13 aña ku ta ganá tres Australian Open konsekutivo di 1997 a 1999, ta di ku e sonidu ta mas fastidia pa espectador i mirador i ta casi no notá pa jugadoran. E antigu númeru 1 mundial, ku ta joga na e evento di senior na Melbourne, ta admití ku ta sorprendí pa alguno di e sonidu ku ta sali di e otro lado di e kou. 'E ta mihó a vegata ku ta estirá mas, e ta mihó ruidoso — i e ta komo: ¿Qué ta fás? O a vegata e ta un gemido pesá i e ta na e línea di servis, pero e bola no ta tin pesu. Pero mi ta kredé ku e ta mas un problema pa e espectador.' Dank a volumen i naturaleza únik di e gritonan di Victoria Azarenka, e audiensia di Rod Laver Arena ta koma imitá e ta durante un biktoria di segundu ronda contra Casey Dellacqua di Australia. 'Por supuestu mi ta oí e,' di e jovén di 22 aña, riendo. 'Pero e ta bini pa mi. Mi ta respetá e audiensia, lo ku e ta fás. Mi ta trata pa mantiene kontrá pa mi jògo.' Ku WTA ta konserná na edukashon di e pròxima generashon di talentu, e opunentenan di Sharapova i Azarenka ta pode ta tolerá e gritonan di konsiderashon pa e futur próksimo — o ta komensá usa tapa oído.

article_content: Tiger populations are rising in the jungles of India and Nepal, bringing these apex predators closer to human settlements—and sparking an urgent effort among conservationists to prevent conflict. To meet this challenge, experts are turning to artificial intelligence, a set of technologies designed to reason and decide much like humans. Last month, researchers from Clemson University in South Carolina and several NGOs published findings in the journal BioScience on their use of AI-enabled cameras. These small, smart devices were installed around protected areas in both countries, aiming to safeguard villagers from tigers—and tigers from poachers. The system, named TrailGuard, can instantly differentiate tigers from other animals and send real-time images to park rangers or nearby residents. According to the study, it successfully detected a tiger just 300 meters from a village and identified a group of poachers. 'We have to find ways for people and tigers—and other wildlife—to coexist,' said Eric Dinerstein, one of the study’s authors and leader of the tech team at the Resolve NGO. 'Technology offers us a powerful, low-cost way to make that possible.' TrailGuard is among the first AI camera systems to accurately identify and transmit images of a wild tiger—and it has nearly eliminated false alarms caused by passing boars or falling leaves. Beyond tigers, similar AI tools are being tested globally: In Gabon, AI helps monitor elephant movements; in the Amazon, sensors detect chainsaws and tractors signaling illegal logging. Four years ago, Google partnered with researchers and NGOs to launch Wildlife Insights—a platform that automates species identification from millions of camera trap images, drastically cutting manual labor. Conservation leaders like Dinerstein believe such innovations are vital to achieving global targets: protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans by 2030, eventually expanding to 50%. 'An early warning system is the critical piece,' he emphasized. The recovery of tigers—from just 1,411 in 2006 to roughly 3,500 today—is a sign of progress, though their historic population once reached 40,000 in mid-century India. Still, experts remain cautious. Jonathan Palmer, head of conservation technology at the Wildlife Conservation Society (who was not involved in the study), noted that AI species recognition is still emerging. 'We recommend independent verification of all AI identifications,' he said. He also questioned whether AI should be deployed on-site or processed later on servers. Yet despite these uncertainties, Dinerstein is expanding TrailGuard’s reach—with elephants now in his sights. 'They wander out of parks constantly, destroying crops, causing chaos in villages, and even derailing trains—killing dozens each year. The opportunity to prevent this is enormous.'
translated_content: E populashon di tigres ta subiendo na junglas di India i Nepal, traiendo e predadornan mas akèr di komunidatnan humanan—i ta spikando un esforsu urgente di konservashonista pa prevenir konflikto. Para responde es desafio, e ekspertronan ta gira nan ta e inteligensia artifisial, un konsjunto di teknologianan ku ta razona i také decisionan komo homanan. Mes pasá, investigadornan di Clemson University na Karolinanan di Sú i varios ONG’s ta publiká e rezultadonan na revista BioScience so e uzo di kameras akomodá ku inteligensia artifisial. E dispositivonan pikin i inteligente aki ta pone na alredor di zonas protehí na e dos nasiónnan sud-asiátiko, pa proteje komunitanan kon e tigres—i e tigres kon e pòtakonan. E sistema, nombrá TrailGuard, ta distingui instantanemanente e tigres di otro spesies i ta mandá imajen nan an tempo real a rangers di parke o residentnan akèr. Segun e studia, e sistema ta detektá un tigre solamente 300 metro di unda un vila—i ta idendifiká un grupu di pòtakonan. 'Nos tin que bini solushonan pa hombrenan i tigres—i otro fauna silvestre—pa bivi junta,' di Eric Dinerstein, un di e autores di e studia i lider di e ekipa di teknolojia na NGO Resolve. 'Teknolojia ta ofresí nos un oportunidat poderosu i barata pa lográ es meta.' TrailGuard ta un di e primèr sistemanan di kamera ku inteligensia artifisial pa idendifiká i transmití imajen di un tigre silvestre—i e ta casi eliminá e alarmas falsa causá pa jabalínan ku pasa o fògus ku ta bai. Mas allá di e tigres, herramientanan similá ta ser probá globalmenti: Na Gabón, inteligensia artifisial ta ajuda pa monitorisá movimentonan di elefantenan; na Amazon, sensornan ta detektá sonidonan di sierras, traktornan i otro maquinaria ku ta señalá deforestashon ilegal. Kuatro aña pasá, Google ta asosiá ku investigadornan i ONG’s pa lansa Wildlife Insights—un plataforma ku automatiza idendifikashon di spesies di miliunan di imajen di kamera trampa, reduzindo grandemente e trabao manual. Konservashonistanan komo Dinerstein ta kredi ke innovashonnan esé ta vital pa lográ metan global: proteje 30% di tierra i mar di Tierra pa 2030, eventualmenti expandí a 50%. 'Un sistema di alarma temprano ta e pieza krítiko,' el ta enfatizá. E rekuperashon di e tigres—di solamente 1.411 na 2006 a aproksimadamente 3.500 hodi—ta un signo di progreso, ansi ke e populashon historiko ta bini 40.000 na India na mitat di siglo 20. Aisko, ekspertronan ta konserva prudensia. Jonathan Palmer, lider di teknolojia di konservashon na Wildlife Conservation Society (ku no ta involukrá na e studia), ta nota ke idendifikashon di spesies ku inteligensia artifisial ta aínda na su infansia. 'Nos rekommenda verifikashon independiente di todo idendifikashon ku inteligensia artifisial,' el ta di. El tambe ta kuestiona si inteligensia artifisial ta mas efikas pa ta deployá na sitio o procesá despues na servidornan o laptopnan. Aisko malgrá es incertidumbre, Dinerstein ta expandí e uzo di TrailGuard—kon elefantenan na mira ahò. 'E ta sali for di parke kontinuamente, destruí krop, ta krea kaos na vilanan, i hasta ta kaba trennan—mata docenan di hombrenan cada aña. E oportunidat pa prevení es ta enormis.'

article_content: In a harrowing incident, 76-year-old Eileen Lee, a grandmother from Sydenham, south London, has been psychologically trapped in the horrors of World War II after a police car crashed into her backyard on August 22, 2012. The sudden impact — loud crashes, shattering glass, and the sight of emergency vehicles — triggered traumatic flashbacks to her childhood, when a bomb destroyed her family’s home in Bromley. Now, at the sound of any sudden noise, she crouches on the ground, covers her head, and cries out, 'Run for cover, the bombs are dropping.' Her daughter, Maxine Lee, 49, says her mother was mentally well before the accident but now suffers severe PTSD. She confuses hospitals with air raid shelters and does not recognize familiar faces. 'It’s taken her right back to the war days,' Maxine said. The police vehicle, which had overturned while pursuing a motorbike, demolished the garden fence and terrified Eileen, who feared her pomeranian dog, Coco, was trapped beneath it. Emergency services responded, but according to Maxine, officers offered no comfort — not even a cup of tea. Maxine is seeking legal advice, accusing authorities of neglect: the garden remained unsecured for three days, and no formal apology was made. In response, the Metropolitan Police confirmed they launched a full investigation and that a senior officer met with the family to discuss the incident.
translated_content: Na un incidente tristí, Eileen Lee, 76 aña, un abuela di Sydenham, sure di Londres, ta konservá psikolójikamentu atrapá den horroran di Segundu Guèrra Mundial despues ku un karu di polis se derrumbá den su jardín trasero na 22 di agostu, 2012. E impactu súbito — ruidonan fuerte, vidrio se rompi, i e presensia di vehikulan di emergensia — ta activá flashbakan tráumátiko di su infansia, ku un bomba a destruí kas di su famí na Bromley. Ahora, pa ogu ku e ruido súbito, el ta krouká den e suelo, ta kubrí e kabe ku e mananan, i ta gritá: 'Kor pa kubí, e bomba ta cayendo.' Suh hija, Maxine Lee, 49, ta dixe ku su mami ta bini bini bini sanu antes di e akidént, pero ahorsá ta sufrí severo PTSD. El ta konsundí hospitá pa refuxio di bomba i no ta rekonosé fisonomian. 'El ta leva e mami ta bini bini den e dia di guèrra,' Maxine ta dixe. E karu di polis, ku ta derrumbá ku ta persigui un motosiklet, a destruí e barda di jardín i ta espantá Eileen, ku ta tene miedo ku su perro pomeranian, Coco, ta debaon di el. Servisionan di emergensia a respondí, pero segun Maxine, e polis no ta ofresí konfort — ni siquiera un tasa di té. Maxine ta buská asistensia lehal, akusándo autoridat pa neglizensia: e jardín ta konservá sen sekuridat pa tres dia, i no ta ofresí un disculpá formal. En respuesta, e Metropolitan Police ta konsirma ku el ta lansa un investigashon kompletu i ku un ofisial senior a reúní ku e famí pa diskutí e asuntu.

article_content: CNN reported that Mitchell Guist, a star of the reality TV show 'Swamp People,' died on Monday in Louisiana. According to Assumption Parish Sheriff Mike Waguespack, Guist was aboard a boat near Belle River Landing in southern Louisiana when he reportedly suffered a seizure. A companion on the boat witnessed the incident, pulled both boats to shore, called 911, and administered CPR. Guist was transported to Teche Regional Medical Center in Morgan City, where he was pronounced dead. The History Channel issued a statement expressing deep sorrow: 'We are extremely saddened to report that our friend and beloved member of the 'Swamp People' family, Mitchell Guist, has passed away earlier today. Mitchell passed on the swamp, doing what he loved. We appreciate your respect for the Guist family's privacy and hope you join us in sending our thoughts and prayers to his brother, Glenn, and the rest of the Guist family.' 'Swamp People' is a popular History Channel series that follows the lives of alligator hunters in Louisiana. Glenn Guist, Mitchell’s brother, is also a cast member on the show.

article_content: Detroit, Michigan (CNN) — Six men appeared in federal court on Thursday, a day after being arrested in raids targeting a group of African-American Muslim converts whom the FBI alleges sought to establish an Islamic state in the United States. Luqman Ameen Abdullah, the alleged leader of the group, was fatally shot during a raid in the Detroit area on Wednesday after firing at law enforcement officers attempting to apprehend him and four others. An FBI canine was also killed. Authorities say Abdullah served as imam at a Detroit mosque, where he reportedly preached about offensive jihad, including violence against the U.S. government and law enforcement. According to a criminal complaint, Abdullah repeatedly told three confidential informants he would never surrender, stating, 'If they’re coming to get me, I’ll just strap a bomb on and blow up everybody.' Abdullah was one of 11 men charged on Tuesday with conspiracy to commit federal crimes, including theft from interstate shipments, mail fraud related to arson proceeds, illegal possession and sale of firearms, and tampering with motor vehicle identification numbers. Eight suspects were in custody, including one already incarcerated on an unrelated charge and another arrested on Wednesday and added to the charges, according to U.S. Attorney spokeswoman Susan Plochinski. An additional suspect was taken into custody in Canada on Thursday, per an FBI statement. Two men remain at large. Mujahid Carswell, also known as Mujahid Abdullah, was arrested in Windsor, Ontario, by Canadian authorities. He is the 30-year-old eldest son of Luqman Abdullah. Canadian border officials are holding him on immigration violations. Of the six suspects appearing in court on Thursday, Abdullah Beard was ordered held without bail. Muhammad Abdul Salaam and Gary Laverne Porter, a 38-year-old teacher arrested at a local school, had their bail hearings delayed. Ali Abdul Raqib was granted a $10,000 unsecured bond; Abdul Saboor received a $100,000 bond despite prosecutors’ request for no bail. Acie Pusha, arrested Wednesday and described by prosecutors as 'minimally involved,' was given a $10,000 bond. The FBI’s criminal complaint states the group conducted target practice in the basement of a mosque, leaving holes in concrete walls. It also references discussions about possible attacks on government buildings, including Detroit’s federal courthouse and FBI offices, as well as disrupting the 2006 Super Bowl in Detroit. However, none of these planned acts formed the basis for the charges. Two law enforcement sources indicated that details about potential attacks were included in the complaint to provide context for the group’s broader objectives. 'They had to earn money for their mosque and the Ummah,' one source said. 'And the purpose of the Ummah was to set up a separatist state.' The Ummah, as described in the complaint, is a network primarily composed of African-American Muslims, including some who converted to Islam while incarcerated. It is led by Jamil Abdullah al-Amin — formerly known as H. Rap Brown — a 1960s radical and former Black Panther who once declared, 'Violence was as American as cherry pie.' Al-Amin is currently serving a life sentence in Colorado’s Supermax prison for killing two Georgia police officers. FBI Special Agent in Charge Andrew Arena contacted local imams and civil rights leaders during the raids 'to bridge any gaps that could possibly arise,' according to FBI spokeswoman Sandra Berchtold. 'He’d rather they hear it from him,' she added. 'We have a good relationship with the community and we want to keep it that way.' The 43-page criminal complaint, filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and unsealed Wednesday, relies heavily on information from confidential informants identified as S-1, S-2, and S-3. S-1 reported that Abdullah encouraged followers to 'pick up guns and do something' instead of pursuing goals peacefully. S-2 recorded a December 12, 2007, conversation in which Abdullah said, 'I got some soldiers with me... if I say, 'Let’s go, we’re going to go and do something,' they would do it.' S-3 stated that on March 21, 2008, Abdullah told him, 'The FBI is the enemy of Islam.' Other charged individuals include: Mohammad Abdul Bassir, also known as Franklin D. Roosevelt Williams — currently imprisoned at Ojibway Correctional Facility in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula; Mujahid Carswell; Mohammad Philistine; Yassir Ali Khan; and Adam Hussain Ibraheem. Acie Pusha was arrested Wednesday and added to the charges, though Plochinski declined to elaborate on his specific allegations. The two remaining fugitives are Mohammad Philistine, also known as Mohammad Alsahi, a 33-year-old resident of Ontario; and Yassir Ali Khan, 30, believed to reside in both Ontario and Warren, Michigan. All defendants are described by the FBI as members of a group alleged to have engaged in sustained violent activity over many years and known to be armed. The complaint was filed by the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division in the Eastern District of Michigan. CNN’s Susan Candiotti, Carol Cratty, and Ross Levitt contributed to this report.

article_content: David Cameron confessed that bringing Andy Coulson on board as his communications director was a decision that still weighs heavily on both of them. Although he considered several candidates—including former BBC reporter Guto Harri—he ultimately picked Coulson in 2007, explaining that he was the only tabloid editor willing to take the job. Cameron stressed that Coulson had resigned from the News of the World after the phone-hacking scandal broke, and had assured him, his chief of staff Ed Llewellyn, and Cabinet minister Francis Maude that he had no knowledge of the illegal activities. Those assurances were also accepted by the police, the Press Complaints Commission, and a parliamentary committee. Still, it later emerged that Coulson had never undergone the standard security clearance required for the role—a gap Cameron downplayed as irrelevant. At the Leveson Inquiry, Cameron firmly rejected calls for government-imposed press regulation, arguing it could endanger press freedom. Instead, he backed a powerful, truly independent self-regulatory body, with real consequences like mandatory front-page apologies and financial penalties for breaches. He also dismissed proposals to ban the mixing of news and opinion, saying headlines often naturally blend fact and perspective. Cameron suggested that newspapers refusing to join the new system could lose access to official government briefings, effectively making membership compulsory. He praised Lord Hunt’s efforts to improve accountability and acknowledged that public figures, himself included, must accept heightened scrutiny—even when it extends to their families.

Cameron ta enfatizá ku Coulson ta dimiti di News of the World despues di skándalo di hackeo di telofononan a yega, i ta asegurá e, su jefe di staff Ed Llewellyn, i ministro di Kabinete Francis Maude ku el no ta sabe na nada di atividat ilegal. Aña, ta sali pa lu pa ku Coulson no ta haya pasa un verifikashon di sekuridat estándar ku ta exijí pa e puesto—un faltante ku Cameron ta minimizá komo irrelevante. article_content: A rare dummy parachutist, used to deceive German forces on D-Day, has been discovered in a garden shed in Britain. At least 500 of these 3-foot decoys — nicknamed 'Ruperts' — were dropped alongside SAS soldiers at four locations away from the Normandy beaches to mislead enemy defenses. Deployed under cover of darkness, the canvas 'paradummies' were designed to ignite upon landing, preventing the Germans from recovering them. Yet one survived — found at the bottom of a garden alongside once-top-secret RAF maps and documents. Six SAS soldiers were parachuted in with the dummies, carrying equipment that simulated the sounds of battle to enhance realism. Though half the size of a human, they appeared lifelike to observers on the ground at night. Meanwhile, thousands of Allied airmen conducted operations elsewhere in the early hours of June 6, 1944, ahead of the main invasion. The discovered Rupert was accompanied by RAF maps intended for a team monitoring the Royal Navy’s bombardment of German coastal defenses. Operation Titanic, the codename for this deception, successfully diverted German troops from the true invasion zones. The dummies were made of hessian cloth, stuffed with sand and straw, and featured in the 1962 film The Longest Day. The artifacts were found by a woman clearing out her late grandparents’ belongings; it remains unclear how the dummy returned from Normandy to Britain. To further confuse German radar, Allied planes dropped bundles of 'window' — now known as chaff — which created false echoes. Just ten bombers used this tactic to simulate hundreds of aircraft. Radio jammers also disrupted communications over northern France to conceal the approach of 1,000 planes carrying paratroopers. On the beaches, soldiers used rocket-propelled grappling hooks to scale Normandy’s cliffs rapidly. They were followed by 'Donald Duck' Sherman tanks — modified to float and propel themselves ashore using their engines. Kevin King of Marlow’s Auctioneers in Buckinghamshire, which sold the dummy for £900, said: 'It’s rare to come across previously unknown paradummies. In the 1970s, a full batch was found on an airfield; some are now in museums.' The American equivalent, called 'Oscars,' was inspired by German tactics first used during the invasion of the Netherlands in 1940. Similar decoys were later deployed in Vietnam, Iraq, and Afghanistan.

At menos 500 di ese dumi 3-pié — konosí komo 'Ruperts' — ta ser lanzá ku SAS soldadonan na katorke lòkalidat pa lej di e pleyanan di Normandía pa desvia e defensanan di e enemigu. Lançá na korsa di nochi, e dumi di kanoa 'paradummies' ta diseñá pa prende ku ta aterisá, pa previni e Germanen di rekuperá e. Pero un ta sobreviví — diskubrí na fons di un kantin ku e mapanan y dokumentanan raku di sekretu di RAF. Ku ta mitat di tamanyo di un homa, e ta parese realista pa observadornan na tera na nochi. E Rupert diskubrí ta akompañá pa mapanan di RAF pa e ekipa ku ta monitorá e bombardamentonan di la Marina Real di defensanan alemán na e kosta. Operashon Titanic, e kódnom pa estra tejedura, ta éksito di divi e tropan di Germania for di e zonan reál di invazion. E dumi ta fá di kanoa hessiana, relléná ku sán i paja, i ta prezentá na e pelikula di 1962 The Longest Day. E artefaktonan ta ser diskubrí pa un muger ku ta limpiá e bodega di su abuelonan; ta déskonosí komo e dumi ta regresá for di Normandía pa Britania. Pa mas konfundí e radar alemán, avionan aliadu ta lanzá bultonan di 'window' — konosí komo chaff — ku ta krea eko falsa. Sólo diez bombardeonan ta usa estra téknika pa simula hundridas di avionan. E ta seguí pa tanke 'Donald Duck' Sherman — modifiká pa flotá i propulsa for di e agua pa bini na e pleyanan. Kevin King di Marlow’s Auctioneers na Buckinghamshire, ku ta vende e dumi pa £900, ta di: 'Ta raro pa topá paradumi pa antes no konosí. Na e 1970, un lot kompletu ta ser diskubrí na un aeropuerto; unos ta na museonan hodi.' E ekivalente amerikanu, konosí komo 'Oscars,' ta inspirá pa téknika alemán primèr usá na invazion di Países Bajos na 1940. Estra dumi ta usá tambe na Vietnam, Irak, i Afganistán.

article_content: Angel di Maria is the latest player to don Manchester United’s legendary No 7 shirt — a jersey once worn by icons like George Best, Eric Cantona, David Beckham, and Cristiano Ronaldo. To honor their legacy, he visited the Manchester United Museum at Old Trafford, where he expressed deep admiration for the club’s history. 'It was great to visit the museum and learn about the club’s history,' he said. Di Maria hopes to one day be considered a hero by United fans, just as those before him were. Since joining the club, the 26-year-old Argentine winger has made a promising start, scoring two goals in his first four appearances, despite United’s challenging start to the season. The team, managed by Louis van Gaal, prepares to face Everton at Old Trafford this Sunday, aiming to build on last week’s 2-1 victory over West Ham. The museum currently features exhibits on George Best’s career, '10 Years of Wayne Rooney,' and 'United at War,' which explores the club’s role during both World Wars. Admission to the museum is free until the end of October, while guided stadium tours cost £18 for adults and £12 for juniors and concessions. Di Maria remains focused on making his mark at Old Trafford — and perhaps one day, joining the pantheon of No 7 legends.

article_content: Vanessa Kirby and Lauren Dark have stepped on board as executive producers for Thunder, Switzerland’s official submission for the Best International Feature Oscar. Through their production company, Aluna Entertainment, they’ll be lending their full support to the film’s awards campaign. Set in the year 1900, Thunder tells the story of 17-year-old Elisabeth, played by Lilith Grasmug, who returns to her remote mountain village after spending five years in a convent. Her sister’s unexpected death calls her home — not just to grieve, but to help run the family farm. Yet what she finds isn’t comfort, but confinement: rigid village customs and a heavy silence around her sister’s passing push Elisabeth to challenge everything she’s been taught. Director Carmen Jacquier uses the film as a powerful vehicle for advocating women’s right to define their own lives — to move freely, love openly, and connect with their bodies and spirits without shame. Kirby and Dark expressed deep admiration for Jacquier’s bold, poetic storytelling, calling her a groundbreaking new voice in cinema. Jacquier, in turn, said having Kirby and Dark on board feels like a powerful alignment of purpose — one aimed at building a world where women aren’t silenced. Since its world premiere at TIFF in 2022, Thunder has traveled the international festival circuit, earning over a dozen accolades including two Swiss Film Prizes and the Women in Motion Emerging Talent Award at Cannes. In the U.S., Dekanalog is releasing the film, with a launch at New York’s IFC Center on October 25 and a rollout to Los Angeles beginning November 10. The film was produced by Flavia Zanon and Joëlle Bertossa of Close Up Films.

Kuando e historia ta situá na e aña 1900, Thunder ta konta e historia di Elisabeth, un muchacha di 17 aña, interpretá pa Lilith Grasmug, ku ta bini baka pa su buki montañoso despues di pasa 5 aña na un kónvento. La muerte repentina di su hermana ta mandá e bini — no solamente pa lamento, sino pa ajuda pa manehá e granja di famí. Pero lo ku e ta bini baka ta no konforto, mas konfinamentu: kostumbres rígido di e kómunita i un silensio pesá riba la muerte di su hermana ta empuja Elisabeth pa desafia todo lo ku e ta aprentá. article_content: On March 10, 2011, David Simmonds, a 21-year-old former seasonal worker at Thorntons, brutally attacked and killed Jia Ashton, a 25-year-old economics graduate, as she walked home along a wooded path in Derbyshire known as the Yellow Brick Road. Simmonds, who stood 6ft 2in and weighed 19 stone, inflicted catastrophic injuries on the 6-stone victim, including a ruptured heart and broken ribs, resulting in her death from chest compression. Pathologists likened the severity of her wounds to those from a high-impact car crash or fall from a great height. After the murder, Simmonds buried her body under logs and rocks, scattered her belongings—including her glasses, MP3 player, mobile phone, and coat buttons—around Sleetmoor Woods, and even discarded her shoulder bag 15 feet up in a tree. He then calmly went to a local shop to buy fish and chips, fabricating a story to friends that scratches on his face and arms resulted from a pub brawl meant to 'protect a girl.' Jia Ashton, described in court as conscientious, determined, and focused, had recently discussed starting a family with her husband, Matthew Ashton, a 26-year-old schoolteacher and piano tutor. The couple had briefly argued days before her death, prompting Matthew to stay overnight at a local hotel—an act that initially raised police suspicion, though he was fully cleared within days. Detectives investigating the case received multiple reports of a disheveled man acting suspiciously in the woods. A list of registered homeless individuals provided by the local council led them to Simmonds, whose fingerprints and DNA matched evidence collected at the scene. Despite having no prior criminal record, Simmonds was not in the national DNA database until this case. Initially pleading not guilty and scheduled for trial in November 2011, Simmonds unexpectedly changed his plea to guilty at Nottingham Crown Court. Judge Michael Stokes QC condemned the killing as motivated by more than robbery, stating: 'I am satisfied that, whatever the motive, you intended to kill her.' The judge highlighted the grotesque imbalance between attacker and victim, calling it 'a most cruel and wicked manner' to deprive Jia and Matthew of their future together. Simmonds was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 28 years before parole eligibility. Matthew Ashton released a statement after the guilty plea: 'I hope that justice will be done and that this despicable being will never be free to kill again.' Jia’s body was found three days after her disappearance by a mountain rescue dog. No sexual assault occurred, but her clothing had been disturbed, and contact DNA was recovered from her abdomen.
translated_content: Den 10 di mart, 2011, David Simmonds, un hende di 21 aña ku ta trabahá pa Thorntons komo laborant temporal, ataká brutalmente i matá Jia Ashton, una gradua di 25 aña en ekonomia, den kaminu na kasa su pa un senda boskosu na Derbyshire ku ta konosí komo 'Yellow Brick Road'. Simmonds, ku ta mide 6ft 2in i pèsá 19 stone, infliji lesionan kritiko pa e viktimá di 6 stone, inkluyendo un kardia ruptura i kosta rompidu, resulta na muerte pa kompresión di torax. Patologoan lo konsiderá e gravedat di e heridanan komo e di un akidente di auto o kaida di un edifisio altu. Despues di e asesinato, Simmonds enterrá e kuerpo su ba lógan i ròk, sparsá e pertenensianan su—inkluyendo e gafas, MP3 player, telèfonu mobil, i botones di kamisa—pa Sleetmoor Woods, i hasta tira e bolson su 15 pí di altu den un arbol. Despues el ta yega pa un tienda lokal pa koma pescadu i papas fritu, i fabriká un historia pa amigu nan ku e rasponan na su kara i brazonan ta rezulta di un pelea na un bar pa 'protehí una muchacha'. Jia Ashton, konsiderá na korte komo konscientiosa, determiná, i enfoká, tabata diskutí recientemente na startí un família ku su maridu, Matthew Ashton, un maestró di skol primaria i tutor di pianó. E pare ta tení un disputa brev pa dia anterrior di e muerte, ku ta kousa Matthew pa dormí un nochi na un hotel lokal—aksion ku tabata kousa suspisón di polisia, mas el ta ser ekskluí totalmenti den dias. Detektivanan ku ta investigá e kaso ta bini informashon di mustranan ku un hende desaliñá ta aktivá suspisiosamente na e bosknan. Lista di personanan ku ta registrá komo sin hogar, ofresí pa konsil lokal, ta leva a Simmonds, ku e huellanan di dedo i ADN su ta koresponde ku e pruebanan kolektá na e sitia. Malgrá e no ta tení konvikshon anterior, Simmonds no tabata na baza di ADN nasional hasta e kaso. Inicialmenti el ta pledé no kulpabil, i tabata programá pa juicio den noviembre 2011, mas Simmonds ta kambia su pledé pa kulpabil na Nottingham Crown Court. Juez Michael Stokes QC ta kondena e asesinato komo motivá pa mas ke robo, declará: 'E ta konsiderá ku, cualke motibo, el ta tení intensión pa matá e.' E juez ta resalta e desbalans grandioso ente atakan i viktimá, lo konsiderá komo 'un manera mas cruel i maldá' pa privá Jia i Matthew di e su futuro junto. Simmonds ta sentensia a vida kun un termino minimo di 28 aña antes di parol. Matthew Ashton ta publicá un declaración despues di e pledé di kulpabil: 'E ta espere ku justisia ta fá, i ku e hende abominabel denki ta no libe pa matá den nuevamente.' E kuerpo di Jia ta bini ekspozí tres dia despues di e desaparishon pa un kàni di reskate di montaña. E no tabata havi asalto seksual, mas su ropa tabata bini moví, i ADN di kontakto ta konservá na su abdomen.

article_content: A 27-year-old Brazilian actor, Tiago Klimeck, died after accidentally hanging himself during a live performance of 'The Passion of the Christ' in Itarare, Brazil, on April 6. Klimeck, who portrayed Judas Iscariot, was wearing a safety harness beneath his costume, as required for the scene described in the Gospel of Matthew. Despite this precaution, he suffered prolonged oxygen deprivation, leading to severe brain damage. He remained in a medically induced coma for over two weeks before passing away at Hospital Santa Casa de Misericórdia in Itapeva. The official cause of death has not yet been released. According to CNN affiliate TV Record, the harness and rope used in the performance had been borrowed from the local fire department for the third consecutive year. Police investigator Jose Victor Bassetti noted that Klimeck was not directly supervised during the scene because he was considered experienced with the equipment. Eyewitness Luiz Carlos Rosner, who runs a sandwich cart near the performance site, recalled the chaos when cast members realized Klimeck was unresponsive. 'One actor came to me desperate,' Rosner told TV Record. 'He said someone was hanging and wanted to cut the rope — I hesitated to give him a knife in the middle of the crowd.' The harness and rope are now under analysis at the Criminal Institute of Sorocaba.

Malgre es precausón, el ta sufrí desfisiença di oksíjeno prolongá, lo ku ta leva na danos serio di kerebro. El tabata sta den koma mediko inducí mas di dos semana antes di mori na Hospital Santa Casa di Misericórdia na Itapeva. La kausa oficial di muerte aún no ta publicá. Segun CNN afiliá TV Record, arnés i korda ku ta usa na performans tabata prestá pa kuerpo di bomberos lokal pa terser anyo konsekutibo. Investigador di polisia Jose Victor Bassetti ta nota ku Klimeck no tabata supervizá direktemente duranti skena, pa konsidera ku el tabata eksperientá ku e ekipamentu. Testigu Luiz Carlos Rosner, ku ta ten un karro di sándwich nasí di sitio di performans, ta rekordá es krisis ku atoranan ta diskubrí ku Klimeck tabata inresponzivu. 'Un ator ta kome na mi desesperá,' Rosner ta di TV Record. 'El ta di ku algién ta keda ahorká i el ta bini korta e korda — mi ta hesita dá e knifé pa mitad di krowd.' Arnés i korda tabata stá den analisis na Institutu Kriminál di Sorocaba.

article_content: Prince Harry is being considered for appointment as Commanding Officer of the Household Cavalry Regiment, potentially assuming the role by 2023. The prince, currently a captain in the Blues and Royals — one of two regiments comprising the Household Cavalry — has successfully completed all required military examinations and is on track for promotion to major, with the possibility of reaching lieutenant colonel by 2023. According to sources, Harry has expressed that he would be 'honoured' to lead the oldest and most senior regiment in the British Army. He reportedly told colleagues, 'Every serving officer wants to command their own regiment — and I am no different.' Commissioned in 2006, Harry trained as an Apache gunner and pilot, completing two operational tours in Afghanistan: first in 2008 as a forward air controller, then in 2012 as an Apache pilot stationed at Camp Bastion in Helmand province. He was promoted to captain in April 2011 and qualified as an Apache aircraft commander in July 2013. Currently serving as a staff officer at Horse Guards Parade in London, he is expected to return to active duty with the Blues and Royals in the coming year. A senior officer praised Harry’s ambition, stating, 'I am absolutely delighted Harry has set his sights high. Every officer at his stage should be ambitious enough to want to command their regiment. He is a very capable officer and has proved his worth in battle.' If appointed, Harry would become the first serving royal to hold the rank of brigadier (one-star general) while actively serving in the British Army. The Household Cavalry comprises the operational Household Cavalry Regiment (HCR), equipped with armored vehicles, and the ceremonial Household Cavalry Mounted Regiment (HCMR), which performs duties such as the Trooping the Colour and the State Opening of Parliament.

article_content: Billions of people worldwide rely on daily commutes to get to and from work—and the ways they travel reveal astonishing diversity. Photographs from cities around the globe capture the intensity, ingenuity, and occasional serenity of these journeys. While commuters in the UK may be familiar with packed Tube trains and gridlocked roads, elsewhere, the experience looks radically different. In Soweto, South Africa, passengers cling tightly to overcrowded trains. In Taiwan, more than 15 million motor scooters fill intersections, waiting at traffic lights. In Bolivia, the world’s highest and one of the largest cable car systems shuttles residents between La Paz and El Alto. In Beijing, rush-hour trains are so full that commuters are literally pressed together. But not all commutes are chaotic. Along Chicago’s river, passengers glide peacefully on water taxis. In Amsterdam, cyclists enjoy free ferries connecting neighborhoods. In New Delhi, a boy sells coconuts to stranded drivers. In Tijuana, a woman applies makeup while waiting at the Western Hemisphere’s busiest border crossing. Even in the dense streets of Hong Kong’s Mongkok or Harare’s Mbare suburb, people move with quiet resilience. Photographer Andy Wong has documented these moments across major global cities—from the glowing light trails of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge at dusk, to the subdued subway rides in Pyongyang, where foreign visitors are limited to just one or two stops. These images don’t just show transportation—they tell stories of endurance, adaptation, and humanity in motion.

Mientras komutanan den Reino Uní ta konsidera trennan i kars nan krowdá komo normal, den otro siudatnan e eksperiensia ta mustra diferente. Den Soweto, África di Sur, pasajeronan ta agarra forta e frontal i lateral di trennan krowdá. Den Taiwán, mas di 15 mion di scooters ta konsentra na semaforonan. Den Tijuana, un muher ta aplica maquillaje mientras ta espèr na kruzeru mas aktivo di e Hemisferio Occidental. Even den e kalinan densu di Mongkok, Hong Kong, o Mbare, Harare, pòple ta mòve ku resiliensia silensioso. article_content: A deceptive credit card scheme has emerged, targeting unsuspecting shoppers with tiny, recurring charges of $9.84 labeled as 'customer support' fees. These unauthorized transactions appear on statements under unfamiliar website names, leading users to fake support portals that promise full refunds — but never deliver them. According to the Better Business Bureau, fraudsters count on people overlooking minor charges, assuming neither consumers nor banks will bother investigating such small amounts. Victims who call the provided phone number often receive reassuring verbal confirmations that the charge will be reversed — yet the refund never shows up. The scheme appears tied to the massive 2013 Target data breach, where hackers stole personal and payment details of roughly 70 million customers. While the exact method of card theft remains unclear, cybersecurity expert Brian Krebs, who runs the blog KrebsOnSecurity, suggests the scam operates through a global network of affiliate sites stretching from Cyprus to India and the UK. The BBB urges anyone seeing a $9.84 charge to review their recent statements, dispute the transaction immediately with their bank or card issuer using the number on the back of their card, and consider canceling their card if they suspect compromise. 'This isn't just about one charge — your data is already out there, and criminals will try again,' they warn.

Segun el Better Business Bureau, los fraudeur a konta ku lus ta ignorá kantidat pequeñu, asumiendo ku nian konsumidor nian bank no ta bini investiga es monto tan chikito. Lus ku ta kallá el numèro di telefonu a menudo ta resibí konfirmashon verbal ku ta prometé kanselashon — pero el reembolsu no ta aparese. Es esquema a aparentemente ligá ku el brecha masivu di Target di 2013, ku hackers a roba informashon personal i pagamentu di aproksimadament 70 mion di kliënte. Mientras el metòdiku exacto di robo di kaart a no ta klár, el eksperto di sekuridat Brian Krebs, ku ta administrá el blog KrebsOnSecurity, ta sugeri ku es esquema ta operá atraves di un red global di afiliá ku ta estendi di Chipre a India i Reino Uní. 'E no ta solamente akí un kargu — su datonan a sali, i los krimináles a bini den nuevamente,' ta di el.

article_content: Washington (CNN) — Latino voters strongly support President Barack Obama and the Democratic Party, despite dissatisfaction with the administration’s deportation policies, according to a survey released Wednesday by the Pew Hispanic Center. The findings offer encouraging news for Obama and Democrats heading into next year’s election, as Hispanics are the fastest-growing demographic group in the United States and represent a major voting bloc. The survey found that Latino registered voters favor Obama over Republican presidential candidates Mitt Romney and Texas Governor Rick Perry by more than a 2-to-1 margin. These results mirror those from the 2008 presidential election, when Obama received 67% of the Latino vote compared to 31% for Republican nominee Senator John McCain. Hispanic voters have long aligned with the Democratic Party, and the Pew survey confirms this trend: Two-thirds of Hispanic registered voters identify with or lean toward the Democrats, while only 20% do so for the Republicans. 'It is interesting that among Latino voters — particularly those who are registered — there is strong support not just for the Democratic Party, but for Barack Obama personally,' said Mark Hugo Lopez, executive director of the Pew Hispanic Center, in an interview with CNN. The survey, conducted in both English and Spanish among 1,200 Hispanic adults from November 9 to December 7, has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.6%. While support for Obama remains high, the survey also revealed widespread disapproval of his administration’s immigration enforcement. Deportations reached 395,000 in 2009 and 387,000 in 2010. Among Latino respondents, 59% disapproved of how the administration handled deportations, while only 27% approved. Surprisingly, fewer than half of Hispanic respondents — just 41% — knew that deportations had increased under Obama compared to the Bush administration. Of those aware of the increase, 77% disapproved of the policy; even among those unaware, over half still expressed disapproval. According to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Hispanics accounted for 97% of all deportees in 2010. More than 90% of Latino respondents in the survey support the DREAM Act — a Democratic initiative backed by Obama that offers a path to legal residency for undocumented youth who pursue higher education or military service. Republicans have consistently blocked its passage in Congress. In the CNN interview, Lopez noted that the top concerns for Hispanic registered voters remain jobs, education, and health care — consistent with priorities in previous years. CNN’s Catherine Shoichet contributed to this report.

E rezultadonan ta buenas notis pa Obama i Demokrátiko pa e elekshon nan próksimo, ku e grupu demográfiko más rápidamente kresiente di e pais ta e Hispano i ta komponé un bloku di votan importante. E sondeu ta demonstrá ku e votan registrá Latina/o ta prefere Obama riba kandidatonan presidensial Repúblikano Mitt Romney i Gobernador di Texas Rick Perry pa un margen di más di 2 a 1. article_content: Luis Suarez’s time at Barcelona is hanging in the balance. Since arriving for a staggering £75 million from Liverpool, the Uruguayan striker has struggled to find the net, scoring just three times in 12 appearances across all competitions. His underwhelming start has intensified scrutiny at Camp Nou, especially after the sudden departures of sporting director Andoni Zubizarreta and club legend Carles Puyol — both of whom were instrumental in bringing him to the club. With Barcelona’s president Josep Maria Bartomeu accelerating presidential elections amid growing unrest, Suarez now finds himself at the center of a turbulent transition. Although the club insists there are no immediate plans to sell him, top Premier League sides including Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, and Chelsea are keeping a close eye on his situation. Adding to the complexity, FIFA’s upheld one-year transfer ban — stemming from illegal contact with underage players — means Barcelona cannot sign a direct replacement even if they wanted to. Meanwhile, head coach Luis Enrique, whose own future is uncertain following rumored tensions with Lionel Messi, has tried reshaping Suarez’s role in attack without success. Suarez’s lone La Liga goal came in a 5-0 win over Córdoba in December; his other two strikes came in Champions League matches. The club has precedent for moving on quickly from expensive flops — recall Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s loan to AC Milan after failing to thrive under Pep Guardiola. As Suarez battles to regain form and stability, his Camp Nou future remains deeply uncertain.

E start mala ta amenta e presion na Camp Nou, spesialmente depués di e salidanan repentina di direktor deportivo Andoni Zubizarreta i leyenda di e klup Carles Puyol — ki ambos ta jera fundamenta pa tra el pa aki. Pa adisiona e komplikashon, e ban transferensia di un aña di FIFA, ki ta bini di kontaktan ilegal ku jugadores menór di eda, ta impide ku Barcelona ta pone un sustitutu direto, aun si nan ta bini. Mientras, e entrenador Luis Enrique, ku e propiu porvenir ta incierto despues di rumores di tensión ku Lionel Messi, ta traha pa reajusta e rol di Suarez na ataque sin éxito. E klup ta tin precedente pa separa rapido di jugadores costoso ki no ta kumplí — recorda e prestá di Zlatan Ibrahimovic pa AC Milan despues di no ta prospera ku Pep Guardiola. Mientras Suarez ta lucha pa bini forma i estabilidad, e porvenir di el na Camp Nou ta sigui mesteriosu.

article_content: On August 15, 2012, a tour bus carrying the American punk band Baroness lost control in heavy rain near Brassknocker Hill in Bath, Somerset, plunging roughly 30 feet down an embankment. The 52-seat coach, which had just completed a show in Bristol, was headed to the Talking Heads venue in Southampton—the final stop of its UK tour. Nine people were aboard, including band members John Baizley, Peter Adams, Matt Maggioni, and Allen Blickle. Two individuals—the driver and another passenger—were seriously injured and trapped in the wreckage. Firefighters used hydraulic cutting equipment to extract them, while seven others sustained minor injuries. All nine were taken to hospital: four to Frenchay Hospital in Bristol and five to the Royal United Hospital in Bath. Emergency services mobilized swiftly: ten fire engines, two Wiltshire units, six ambulances, rapid-response paramedics, and critical care teams responded. Though the Great Western Air Ambulance was dispatched, poor weather grounded the helicopter. The coach, black and red in color, had skidded through a fence, struck a guardrail, and came to rest on its wheels, surrounded by fallen branches and debris. The crash closed roads for several hours, prompting police to request drivers to detour. The band’s international tour dates in Belgium and Germany were postponed, and ticket holders for the canceled Southampton show received full refunds. A band representative expressed gratitude to emergency responders and shared hopes for a full recovery for all affected.

article_content: A large New Jersey shore family that suffered losses during Superstorm Sandy will share a $20 million lottery jackpot — a windfall one of the 18 siblings called 'a great pick-me-up.' Members of the Endreson family gathered at the Beachwood Community Center on Thursday afternoon for a news conference. A lottery spokesperson confirmed the siblings’ ages range from 53 to 76. The New Jersey Pick-6 prize will also be divided among three children of a brother who passed away several years ago. Sixty-nine-year-old John Endreson became emotional as he described rebuilding his home after Superstorm Sandy ripped through the shore in late October 2012. 'The hardest part was seeing other people who were devastated,' he said. 'I was able to rebuild my house and help my family and my brothers. I was quite fortunate. I just feel so lucky — and this is just the icing on the cake.' Another sibling recalled how their late mother began playing the lottery years ago and always promised all her children would share in any winnings. Faith Schiabor recounted receiving a frantic call from her sister Sigrid, who had bought the winning ticket. Sigrid Endreson told reporters she bought the ticket while stopping for milk at a 7-Eleven — then forgot about it for nearly two weeks. When she finally checked it and saw 'See Cashier' on the screen, she ran it again before heading to the counter — and broke down in tears. 'I called my sister to come get me. I didn’t think I’d make it,' she said. 'I think I won the lottery!' The family has chosen a lump-sum payout of $14 million, which amounts to approximately $10 million after taxes. 'It’s going to help the family, and it’s going to help Ocean County,' Schiabor said. 'It’s just a great pick-me-up for all of us.'

article_content: 2014 was a landmark year in technology, characterized by rapid innovation across multiple fronts. Smartphones grew larger, with manufacturers like Apple, Motorola, and Google following Samsung’s lead in popularizing the 'phablet'—a hybrid between phone and tablet. What was once seen as a novelty is now standard. The iPhone 6 Plus, Motorola’s Nexus 6, and Samsung’s Galaxy Note 4 all featured screens exceeding 5.5 inches, enhancing video, gaming, and browsing experiences. Uber continued its global expansion in 2014, entering five new Australian cities after its 2013 debut in Sydney and Melbourne. Though criticized by taxi unions and regulators over safety concerns regarding its Uber X service—allowing rides in non-commercial vehicles—the company remained confident in regulatory acceptance. Bitcoin, the leading cryptocurrency, suffered a major setback in February 2014 when Mt. Gox, its largest exchange, collapsed amid a suspected cyberattack. Its value dropped nearly 50%, falling from around $800 USD in January to roughly $400 USD by year-end. Despite this, entrepreneurial efforts persisted, including the rollout of Bitcoin ATMs and debit cards in Australia. Facebook cemented its status as the world’s dominant social platform, reporting 1.35 billion monthly active users—with 64% logging in daily. Revenue surged 59% year-over-year to $3.2 billion, primarily driven by mobile advertising. While CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s long-term investment ideas unsettled some investors, the company ended the year financially robust. Google Glass, once heralded as the future of wearable tech, faced public resistance over privacy fears. Users worried wearers could secretly record surroundings. As a result, Google halted public sales and shifted focus to smartphones and smartwatches. Competitors like Epson and Huawei are developing similar devices, but mainstream adoption remains uncertain. Smartwatches, long plagued by clunky designs, are evolving. Samsung, LG, Sony, and Motorola released models, but none broke through. Apple’s highly anticipated Watch, unveiled in September 2014, is expected to launch in early 2015—and may finally bring wearable tech into the mainstream. The streaming revolution gained unstoppable momentum. Netflix officially announced its March 2015 launch in Australia, prompting competitors like Foxtel to slash prices. Local players including Stan (by Nine and Fairfax) and EzyFlix are also entering the market, signaling a turning point for traditional broadcast TV. Virtual reality moved from concept to reality in 2014. Samsung’s Gear VR and Google’s Cardboard offered affordable, smartphone-powered VR experiences. In 2015, Sony’s Project Morpheus (for PS4) and Facebook’s Oculus Rift are expected to deliver premium, dedicated headsets—opening doors for immersive gaming and entertainment. Mobile payments are poised for breakthrough in 2015 with Apple Pay. New iPhones will let users store credit cards and pay by tapping terminals, verified via fingerprint. Early U.S. feedback has been positive. Though only a third of Australians currently trust phone payments, Apple’s brand credibility may accelerate adoption. Tablet sales growth plummeted to just 7.2% in 2014, down from 52.5% in 2013, according to IDC. Larger smartphones are replacing tablets for many users, and people keep tablets longer—often two years or more. iPad sales are expected to stagnate, with Apple possibly retiring the iPad Mini. Forrester predicts Apple may introduce a 13-inch iPad to rival Microsoft’s Surface Pro 3.

article_content: One woman discovered it’s possible to survive a week eating only foods represented by emoji — though it’s far from healthy. New York-based writer Kelsey Rexroat documented her experiment for The Atlantic, observing that her emoji-only diet was 'essentially the opposite of Atkins' because it centered on desserts, rice-heavy meals, and alcoholic drinks. Not only did she restrict herself to items with emoji equivalents, but she committed to consuming all 59 emoji foods over seven days. While staples like milk and bananas were already in her fridge, unfamiliar symbols like oden and dango led her to consult Emojipedia — the definitive reference for emoji meanings maintained by the Unicode Consortium. She found oden — a savory broth with fish cakes and eggs — at a local restaurant and dango — sweet rice dumplings — at a Japanese market. Though she enjoyed increased seafood and fresh fruit, sugar and white rice emerged as dominant themes: 'Of the 59 food emoji, eight incorporate rice, and 11 are desserts,' she noted. Her week included red wine, sake, a tropical cocktail, and beer — leading her to conclude, 'Clearly, the emoji diet is not for teetotalers.' She also lamented the absence of emoji for cheese, garlic, chips, and popcorn. 'I had a moment of dismay when I realized there’s no cheese emoji,' she wrote while eating spaghetti, forced to skip the aged Gruyere she’d bought days before. Currently, a Change.org petition calling for a hot dog emoji has gathered over 407 supporters. Ultimately, Rexroat reflected: 'The emoji diet hasn’t left me hungry or dissatisfied — if anything, my dessert binge added a few pounds — but it slimmed down my wallet, since I bought more groceries to replace what was in my pantry.' In a related experiment, New York couple Alex Goldmark and Liza Stark communicated exclusively through emojis for a month as part of a New Tech City project. They found emoji excelled at conveying affection and joy but fell short for planning or logistical discussions — confirming that while emojis enrich emotion, they don’t replace words.

article_content: Australia was on the verge of announcing it had discovered its own Loch Ness Monster after strange S-shaped and loop-shaped formations were detected by a Bureau of Meteorology radar off the west coast of Western Australia. The unusual images sparked widespread online speculation, with some weather groups dubbing the initial 80-kilometer-wide formation the 'Rottnest Monster' because it appeared near Rottnest Island. Speculation intensified when a second similar shape was observed, deepening public intrigue. A first radar image showed a giant squiggle that fueled rumors of a mysterious creature lurking off the coast of Rottnest Island. The loop-shaped pattern further encouraged comparisons to the legendary Loch Ness Monster. However, the mystery was resolved later that afternoon when the Department of Defence confirmed the formations were caused by a naval exercise in the area. 'The unusual pattern that appeared on the Bureau of Meteorology's Perth radar on Wednesday the 12th was the result of a Defence exercise off the west coast of Australia,' a Defence spokesman said. 'This is a regular training activity involving ships and aircraft, designed to prepare a Navy warship for operational deployment. The exercise is ongoing.' 'The environmental conditions at the time created a rare opportunity for this routine activity to appear clearly on weather radar displays.' WA Weather Group administrator Sean Gray, 39, admitted he had hoped the formations signaled another life form, like a Loch Ness Monster. 'The explanation totally ruined it — the mystery is over,' he said. 'But if we’re going to have a rumor, let’s give it a name — the Rottnest Monster. It could boost tourism and attract guided tours.' Online groups had speculated the squiggles might indicate a new cryptid, potentially giving Rottnest Island its own version of the Loch Ness Monster. Gray noted people had seen naval activity nearby, but he didn’t believe it explained the radar anomaly. 'What got everyone was how long it lingered and how it moved with the wind — slow-moving, slower than an aircraft dumping fuel, yet faster than a helicopter. The theories floating around aren’t scientific.' Bureau of Meteorology meteorologist Rabi Rivett initially said there was no clear explanation but eliminated meteorological causes. 'It's not meteorological. Clouds aren’t picked up by weather radar — that’s not their purpose.' Military chaff was also ruled out: 'Chaff usually disperses rapidly. But this formation held its shape as it moved northwest — that rules out chaff.' 'If this were military activity, they’d have had to fly a very precise signature in a short time. And it didn’t distort in the wind — which it should have if it were airborne debris.' WA Weather Group spokesperson Peter Coe, 19, said the formation confused even seasoned weather enthusiasts. 'It could be something like a Loch Ness Monster — but that wouldn’t show up on radar,' he said. Coe, who has been part of the Perth-based weather group since 2010, added: 'I’ve never seen anything like this before. That shape was highly unusual — and it captured everyone’s imagination.'

Imajenan estranho ta spika un frenesi di rumeor online, ku algunos gruponan di meteorologia ta bautizá la formaçion di 80 km di diamentro komo 'Rottnest Monster', por ku el ta aparesí riba hawanan di Rottnest Island. 'E kondishonan ambiental riba kosta di Vest-Australia ku e tempu di e aktividat ta ofresí un oportunidat úniko pa e atividat rutinario ta bini visibele na display di radar meteorologiko.' Administrador di WA Weather Group Sean Gray, 39, ta di ku el ta esperá ku e formaçionan ta un señal di otro forma di vida komo un criatura tipo Loch Ness Monster. 'E eksplanashon ta arruiná totalmenti — e misterio ta akabá,' el di. 'Mi ta pensá si ta bini un rumeor, ta da un nomber i fa e ta un Rottnest Monster. E ta bon pa turismo i ta pòt ta tra turismonan.' Criatura misteriosu: Gruponan online ta spikulá ku e squiggles ta pòt dá Rottnest Island su propio Loch Ness Monster. Sr. Gray ta di ku pèrsonanan ta bini spota aktibidat di marina na e area, mas el no ta kredé ku e ta kauza di e formaçion. 'E kosa ku ta ta ta to’ mundo es ku e ta tan largo na radar i e ta move ku e viento,' el di. 'E ta move lento, mas lento ku un avión ku ta dumpia kombustibel, mas rapido ku un helikopter. E insinuashonan ku ta pasá no ta basá na siensia.' Meteorolojista di Bureau di Meteorologia Rabi Rivett ta di ku e ta nengun eksplanashon pa e forma gigante, mas el ta usa un proseso di eliminashon pa descartá kauzanan. 'E ta nengun meteorologiko. Nube ta nengun piká pa radar, e ta nengun pa e ta fás.' Chaff militar tambe ta descartá: 'Chaff ta generalmenti dispersa rapido. Mas e fakto ku e ta mantene su forma ku el ta move norwest ta descarta e.' 'Si e ta militar-relacioná, el ta fás un trabayu muy bon di volá e firma na un periódo korto di tempu,' el di. 'E ta nengun kambia di forma ku el ta move — ku e ta atrapá na e viento el ta kambia.' Portavoz di WA Weather Group Peter Coe, 19, ta di ku e formaçion ta kauzá konfuzion na entusiasmonan di meteorologia. 'E ta pòt ser algo komo un Loch Ness Monster, mas e ta nengun ta bini na radar,' el di. Sr. Coe ta partidario di gruponan di entusiasmo di meteorologia, ku ta basá na Perth, den 2010 i el ta di ku el ta nengun ta bini e formaçion anterrior. 'E forma espesífiko ta spika un grand interes — e ta un poko estranho.'

article_content: In 2017, the UK will introduce a new 12-sided £1 coin designed to combat counterfeiting—currently, an estimated 45 million fake coins are in circulation. While the Royal Mint and Treasury estimate the total national cost at £15–20 million, industry groups argue the true expense could exceed £100 million. Over 100,000 parking machines nationwide will require costly recalibration, at approximately £500 per unit, totaling £50 million. Additionally, more than 450,000 vending machines, 60,000 public payphones, and even supermarket trolleys and laundry equipment must be upgraded to accept the new coin. Local councils, facing ongoing budget constraints, worry these expenses will lead to higher parking fees or delayed road repairs. Small businesses share similar concerns: replacing outdated coin mechanisms is expensive, and many lack the resources to absorb the cost. The British Parking Association and the Automatic Vending Association agree the new coin is necessary for security but urge careful planning to prevent cost burdens from falling on the public. A major benefit: the new design could prevent nearly 40 million counterfeit coins from being used in parking machines each year. To avoid full-scale upgrades, some retailers may offer plastic tokens compatible with trolley security slots. The Treasury has allocated a £200 million fund for post-winter infrastructure repairs—but whether this can be used for coin-related upgrades remains uncertain. Unlike the rushed 2012 coin change, stakeholders now have three years to prepare. Yet many still question why the financial responsibility rests largely with local operators rather than the central government that mandated the change.

Mientras ku Royal Mint i Tesorería ta estimá ku kostu total nasional ta £15–20 million, grupon di indústria ta arguménta ku kostu real ta pudi subí mas ku £100 million. Mas ku 100.000 maquinanan di parkeo na totu e pais ta nesesita rekalibrashon, ku aproksimadamente £500 pa maquina, totalizando £50 million. article_content: Kathryn Bigelow and Mark Boal, the creative team behind the Oscar-nominated film Zero Dark Thirty, met with senior U.S. intelligence officials—including Michael Vickers, the top civilian intelligence officer—to learn firsthand about the mission that led to Osama bin Laden’s death in 2011. According to newly released documents, the filmmakers were given an extensive overview of the planning and execution of Operation Neptune Spear, including insights from CIA operatives and Navy SEALs involved in the raid on bin Laden’s compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan. The transcripts, obtained by the nonprofit group Judicial Watch through a Freedom of Information Act request, reveal that the briefings occurred just months after the operation. Critics, including Judicial Watch’s president Tom Fitton, argue that the Obama administration granted privileged access to filmmakers with close ties to the White House, possibly to shape public perception ahead of the 2012 presidential election. While the film portrays President Obama as calm, deliberate, and resolute—especially in the now-iconic Situation Room scene—some observers believe it subtly glorifies his leadership, painting him as a moral hero. The movie also features a controversial torture sequence, which Bigelow has defended by shifting focus to policy makers rather than the military. The Department of Defense has since opened an inquiry into whether Vickers violated protocols by sharing sensitive information. Bigelow and Boal maintain they accessed only unclassified material and followed all official procedures during their research, which spanned several years. Despite the film’s success—including five Oscar nominations and a Golden Globe win for Jessica Chastain—many operational details remain undisclosed. For instance, the destruction of a stealth helicopter after a hard landing, and reports that bin Laden had been quietly watching TV news about himself during his years in hiding, have not been officially confirmed. In February 2012, Pakistani authorities demolished the compound to prevent it from becoming a site of pilgrimage. Bin Laden’s body was buried at sea, following Islamic customs, after President Obama famously declared, 'We got him.'

article_content: Every year, hundreds of millions tune in for the Super Bowl—not just for the football, but for the dazzling cheerleaders, blockbuster halftime shows, and the electric atmosphere that turns the game into a global spectacle. If the rules of American football still feel confusing—even after years of watching—you're not alone. FEMAIL spoke with top players and broadcasters to break it all down, simply and clearly. Many people outside the U.S. compare American football to rugby, but that’s misleading. As Channel 4’s NFL presenter Nat Coombs explains, the real difference lies in possession: the ball rarely changes hands, so teams play cautiously, protecting it like a treasure. That’s why you see fewer long passes and more methodical drives. The goal? Move the ball down the field to score. A touchdown—when the ball crosses the opponent’s end zone—is worth six points, followed by a chance to add one or two more. Alternatively, teams can kick a field goal through the uprights for three points, usually from within 50 yards to avoid risky turnovers. Veteran TV host Vernon Kay likens the game to chess—each player has a specific role, and every play is meticulously planned. The quarterback is the general, calling signals and directing the offense through four attempts, or 'downs,' to gain at least ten yards. Succeed, and they get another set of four downs. Fail, and they turn the ball over—or punt it away. This year’s matchup pits the Denver Broncos against the Seattle Seahawks. Denver, led by veteran QB Peyton Manning, is favored—but don’t count out Seattle’s legendary defense, nicknamed the 'Legion of Boom.' Their secondary, anchored by stars Richard Sherman and Earl Thomas, allowed just 14 points per game this season, making them one of the toughest units in NFL history. Detroit Lions quarterback Matthew Stafford adds that Denver’s running back, Knowshon Moreno—a former college teammate of his—could be the hidden X-factor if the weather turns rough in New Jersey. And while the game unfolds, fans aren’t just watching—they’re playing along. Twitter’s 'Omaha' drinking game, based on Manning’s pre-snap call, has gone viral. Yes, it’s silly. No, it’s not officially endorsed. But it’s part of the fun. The halftime show delivers star power: Bruno Mars, one of the youngest performers ever, joins forces with the Red Hot Chili Peppers for a high-energy set. Meanwhile, the commercials? They’re events in themselves. And let’s not forget the snacks. Experts like Steven Raichlen recommend jalapeño-stuffed hot dogs, grilled to perfection—because when you’re cheering for hours, you need fuel. Whether you’re here for the touchdowns, the tunes, or the chili-cheese fries, the Super Bowl isn’t just a game—it’s a celebration.

Si e regla di e fútbol amerikano aínda ta parese kompliká—mes ku ta mira pa aña—tú no ta solu. FEMAIL a preguntá pa jogaoranan i comentaristanan ta eksplika e todo, simpli i klár. article_content: The winner of the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced Friday morning in Oslo, Norway. This year, the Nobel Committee received a record 241 nominations — 53 of them organizations — reflecting global interest in peace and human rights advocacy. Among the nominated organizations is WikiLeaks, the platform founded by Julian Assange that has published classified military and diplomatic documents, including those related to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and thousands of U.S. State Department cables. Several key figures from the Arab Spring movements are considered leading candidates. These include Wael Ghonim, the former Google executive whose social media campaigns helped ignite protests in Egypt; Tunisian blogger Lina Ben Mhenni, who courageously documented regime abuses before the uprisings; and Israa Abdel Fattah, a co-founder of Egypt’s April 6 Youth Movement, instrumental in organizing early digital resistance. Other prominent nominees include Sima Samar, a pioneering Afghan human rights advocate; Cuban dissident Oswaldo Payá Sardinas; and Jordanian scholar Ghazi bin Muhammad, a vocal proponent of interfaith dialogue. The Russian civil rights group Memorial — renowned for defending refugees and victims of political persecution in conflict zones — is also among the contenders. By law, the Nobel Committee keeps all nominee names confidential for 50 years. Last year’s laureate, Chinese dissident Liu Xiaobo, was unable to attend the ceremony while serving an 11-year prison sentence for 'inciting subversion of state power,' according to Chinese authorities. In 2009, U.S. President Barack Obama received the prize for his 'extraordinary efforts to strengthen international diplomacy and cooperation between peoples.' Earlier this week, other Nobel Prizes were awarded: Swedish poet Tomas Transtromer won Literature for his 'condensed, translucent images' that offer fresh insight into reality; Israeli scientist Daniel Shechtman received Chemistry for discovering quasicrystals; American and Australian physicists Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt, and Adam Riess were honored for proving the universe’s accelerated expansion; and biologists Ralph Steinman, Bruce Beutler, and Jules Hoffmann were recognized for discoveries in immune system activation. While former German Chancellor Helmut Kohl has been mentioned in media reports as a possible nominee, the Nobel Committee does not confirm any nominations until half a century after they are submitted.

article_content: A day after Serena Williams exited the Eastbourne tournament, her sister Venus faced a similar end — falling to Daniela Hantuchova in a tense three-set quarterfinal. The Slovak player prevailed 6-2, 5-7, 6-2 in gusty conditions on England’s south coast, securing her first-ever win against Venus after 11 straight defeats. Venus, returning after a five-month break due to an abdominal injury, showed flashes of her former power, particularly in the second set, where she fought back to level the match. But Hantuchova held firm in the deciding set, breaking Venus twice to close out the match on her first match point. Speaking afterward, Hantuchova said she focused solely on her own game, not past encounters. 'I felt good after yesterday’s win and wanted to keep building momentum,' she told the WTA site. 'I’m not where I want to be yet, but I know I’m moving in the right direction — and that feels amazing.' Venus, meanwhile, praised Hantuchova’s grit and admitted the wind made play unpredictable. 'She’s been chasing this win for years,' Venus said. 'I didn’t have the luck today, but I’m happy with how I’ve been competing. This tournament gave me exactly what I needed heading into Wimbledon.' Hantuchova added that she’s thrilled to see the Williams sisters back on tour. 'They’re huge for the sport,' she said. Up next, Hantuchova will meet fifth-seeded Petra Kvitova, who came back from a set down to defeat Agnieszka Radwanska 1-6, 6-2, 7-6. In the other semifinal, France’s sixth seed Marion Bartoli advanced after Victoria Azarenka retired at 6-2, 2-0, while Australia’s seventh seed Samantha Stosur edged out top-ranked Vera Zvonareva 4-6, 7-6, 6-4. On the men’s side, Serbia’s Janko Tipsarevic booked his semifinal spot with two straight 6-3, 7-6 wins over Mikhail Kukushkin and Grigor Dimitrov. Japan’s Kei Nishikori, ranked 59th, and Italy’s Andreas Seppi also advanced after defeating Rainer Schuettler and Olivier Rochus respectively.

Pero Hantuchova ta mantene firme na set decidí, rompiendo servis di Venus dos vei pa tèrmina partidu na primérik punto di partidu.
