article_content: A generation fell in love with Felicity Kendal as Barbara Good, the dungaree-wearing star of the TV series The Good Life. Today, at 67, she continues to radiate charm and vitality. This week, she shared: 'I haven't had fillers or Botox in years. There comes a point where you need to let your features age naturally—otherwise, you end up looking inconsistent.' While she has stopped Botox, her smooth forehead is likely the result of past treatments, which are typically repeated every three to six months. Felicity has admitted to a long-standing, ambivalent relationship with the procedure. In a 2021 interview, she said she stopped in 2010 but considered returning, noting, 'It’s nice not to have lines when you frown—especially on TV. Why do people make such a fuss? No one comments when a woman dyes her hair or gets crowns.' Now, she insists she has quit for good. Her youthful jawline, she credits to strong genetics—her mother remained youthful well into her 70s. She maintains her figure with daily yoga and disciplined exercise. 'I used to do three hours a week of Pilates and weights. Now I need five or six to get the same result,' she said. Rumors of a facelift are unfounded. Felicity claims she visited dermatologist Dr. Laurence Kirwan only once, over a decade ago, for Botox—but disliked the outcome and never returned. She has tried fillers to soften nasolabial folds and under-eye hollows, but found them unflattering: 'Don’t get fillers if your cheekbones are high—it’s chipmunk time!' She jokes that the only real solution is a facelift—but only if you're willing to do it at 40. For years, severe astigmatism forced her to use a magnifying glass to apply makeup. In 2009, she underwent lens implant surgery. 'I see more now than I ever did before,' she said. 'It’s the most magical operation in the world—you go from nearly blind to truly seeing.' A natural brunette, Felicity has been blonde for over four decades, maintaining the same layered style through regular visits to London’s five-star Michaeljohn salon—a favorite of Cherie Blair, Mick Jagger, and Dustin Hoffman. She spends over two hours there each visit. Her slim figure is sustained by lifelong yoga and regular activity. She recalls watching her mother, who ran a Shakespeare touring company in India, practice yoga as a child. In 1981, she was named 'Rear of the Year'—a title she still proudly holds thanks to dance-intensive training during her 2010 appearance on Strictly Come Dancing, where she danced up to six hours daily. Her husband, theater director Michael Rudman, whom she married, divorced, and has since reconciled with, joins her at the gym three or four times a week. 'He’s far more health-conscious than I am,' she admits. Felicity has always monitored her weight. In her twenties, she briefly lived on seaweed alone. Today, her lunch is often Thai vegetable soup and coffee. 'If I’d ever walked down the street eating junk, my father would’ve boxed my ears,' she recalled. She no longer diets but eats healthily: 'I’m a salad, pasta, and steak girl.' Her indulgences? Two glasses of red wine and an occasional cigarette. At 63, she got her first tattoo—a star on her foot honoring her younger son, Jacob, 27, a budding criminal barrister. A year later, she added a moon with feathers on her calf, symbolizing her elder son, Charley, and his two children. She’s considering a third. Childhood spent in India left sun damage on her chest and hands—brown spots and fine lines. But her face remains remarkably smooth. She credits Polaris laser treatments by Dr. Jean Louis Sebagh, costing around £200 per session. 'It’s painful,' she admitted, 'but it removes brown spots and refines skin texture.' Maintenance requires visits every three months. She’s also switched from basic Nivea to the luxury skincare staple Creme de La Mer (£103 for 30ml). 'I don’t wear much makeup, but I use tons of cream,' she said. 'I love Clarins After-Sun—it smells like a holiday in a tube.'

Pa kua e ta fai tanto ruido? Nadie ta konsidera si un muger ta pintá e kabelu o ta pón koronas.' Hodi, e ta insistí ku e ta pará pa buén. E mandíbula juvénil, e ta atribuí a genética fuerte—sua madre ta sigui juvénil hasta 70 aña. E ta manteni su figura ku yoga diariu i ejersisio discipliná. 'Mi ta hase tres ora pa seman di Pilates i pesonan. Hodi mi ta nesesita sinco o seis ora pa bini e mismo rezultá,' e ta di. Rumornan di un lifting pa es falso. Felicity ta afirma ku e ta bini pa Dr. Laurence Kirwan un sòló biaha, mas di des aña atras, pa Botox—pero e ta desagradá e rezultá i no ta bini bini. E ta probá fillers pa suavizá foldanan nasolabial i hundínan riba e ojó, pero e ta halle e ta no favorese: 'No ta pón fillers si e póntanan di e mejí ta altu—e ta tempu di chipmunk!' E ta burla ku e sòlun solushon real ta un lifting—pero solo si e ta dispuesto pa hase e ta 40. Pa aña, astigmatismo severo ta forsa e ta usa un lupa pa apliká maquillaj. Na 2009, e ta pasa pa implante di lente. 'Mi ta bini bini mas ku mi ta bini bini antes,' e ta di. 'E ta operashon mas magikoso di e mundo—e ta bini di casi ciego pa ver real.' E ta morena natural, Felicity ta bini rubia pa mas di kuarto siglo, manteniendo e mismo estilo di kabelu ku ta konsistí ku visítanan reguler pa Michaeljohn, e salón di cinco estrela di Londres—ku ta favorito di Cherie Blair, Mick Jagger, i Dustin Hoffman. E ta pasa mas di dos ora pa biaha. Sua figura esbelta ta sustentá ku yoga di vida i ejersisio reguler. E ta rememorá ku e ta mira su madre, ku ta dirijí un kompanía di teatro di Shakespeare na India, hase yoga komo un niña. Na 1981, e ta nombrá 'Rear of the Year'—un título ku e ta sigui orgulhóso ku gracias pa entrenamentu intensu di danza durante su apariensia na Strictly Come Dancing na 2010, ku e ta danza hasi seis ora di dia. Su marido, diretor di teatro Michael Rudman, ku e ta kasá, divorzia, i ta rekoncilia, ta bini ku e pa gimnasio tres o katorce biaha pa seman. 'E ta mas konscienti di salud ku mi,' e ta admite. Felicity ta sempre kontrolá su peso. Na su veinte, e ta viví pa aña solamente di algas. Hodi, su almuerzo ta ofta sopa di vegetal tailandés i kafe. 'Si mi ta kaminá pa e kala ku koma basura, mi papa ta bini bini y ta da mi un bofetá,' e ta rekordá. E no ta dieta mas, pero e ta koma sanamente: 'Mi ta un muger di ensalada, pasta, i bistek.' Su induljensianan? Dos vaso di vino rojo i un kigarro ocasional. Na 63, e ta tén e primé tatuaj—una estrelna na e pie honrá su hijo mas júnior, Jacob, 27, un abogadu prometí. Un aña despues, e ta adisioná un luna ku pluma na e pierna, simbolisá su hijo mas grandi, Charley, i sus dos hendenan. E ta pensa ku e ta bini bini pa un terser. Infansia na India ta lasa danho di sol na e pecho i mannan—puntitanan marron i linianan fin. Pero e frenti ta sigui notabilmenti suave. E ta atribuí e tratamentunan di láser Polaris pa Dr. Jean Louis Sebagh, ku ta kosta alrededor di £200 pa sesion. 'E ta doloros,' e ta admite, 'pero e ta rimuwe puntitanan marron i finí e piel.' Mantenimientu ta nesesita visítanan cada tres mese. E ta tambien bini di Nivea basiko pa e producto di cuidá di piel luksu Creme de La Mer (£103 pa 30ml). 'Mi no ta usa muh maquillaj, pero mi ta usa monton di crema,' e ta di. 'Mi ta ama Clarins After-Sun—e ta hende un bakanan na un tubo.'

article_content: Louis van Gaal’s arrival at Manchester United hasn’t just brought a new manager—it’s introduced a whole new mindset. During a recent group interview with journalists in the U.S., he gently corrected a reporter who used the word 'entice' to describe their line of questioning. 'You’re trying to provoke me,' he said, recalling a prior conversation with Ryan Giggs. It’s moments like these that reveal the depth of his character: precise, intellectually sharp, and unafraid to challenge assumptions. Van Gaal isn’t here for quick fixes. He openly called the squad he inherited 'broken,' not because of laziness, but because of a lack of structure and confidence after years under David Moyes and, before that, Alex Ferguson. His solution? Train the brain, not just the body. He wants players to understand why they pass, move, or shoot—not just do it instinctively. He points to his legacy at Barcelona and Bayern Munich, where young players like Xavi and Iniesta thrived under his guidance. 'I didn’t just coach them—I shaped their thinking,' he explained. 'That’s what takes time. The first three months are always tough, but then they learn how I work.' Even off the pitch, his attention to detail is striking. Stories circulate about him rearranging restaurant seating and insisting on perfect punctuality—even if he himself arrived an hour late to this interview. Yet, those who’ve spent time with him say the wait is worth it. In a 25-minute conversation, he offered more insight into leadership, culture, and football philosophy than most managers do in weeks. At 62, Van Gaal sees this as his final great challenge. He’d been approached by United decades ago, when Ferguson hinted at retirement. Now, with the club languishing in seventh place, he believes the time is right. 'When you’re seventh, the team isn’t just underperforming—it’s broken. And broken teams need new leaders.' He doesn’t fear Manchester City’s dominance. 'Competition makes champions,' he said. 'If they’re knocking on the door, then winning means something.' His confidence is quiet but absolute. He doesn’t need to shout—he just expects everyone else to keep up.

article_content: In a televised address, President Barack Obama announced a significant expansion of U.S. military operations against ISIS, extending air strikes into Syria and increasing support for Syrian rebels opposing President Bashar al-Assad. While he emphasized that American combat troops would not be deployed, the move marks a major escalation in U.S. involvement in the region. Obama defended the strategy as distinct from previous Middle Eastern ground wars, arguing it relies on local partners rather than large-scale U.S. troop commitments. Yet critics point to a troubling disconnect between his 2008 campaign promises — to end wars, reset relations with Russia, and pursue nuclear disarmament — and the reality of six years later: expanded drone campaigns, prolonged conflicts, and growing military engagement. The plan hinges on fragile alliances: the fractured Free Syrian Army, Iraqi security forces weakened by ISIS’s 2014 offensive, Kurdish Peshmerga, and untested Sunni tribal groups. Many of these actors have conflicting agendas, and their cohesion remains uncertain. The strategy also faces serious obstacles. The Assad regime may exploit U.S. strikes to portray itself as the legitimate bulwark against terrorism, undermining the rebel cause. Meanwhile, regional powers like Iran and Russia may retaliate diplomatically or militarily, especially if American forces come into direct conflict with Syrian government troops. Legal questions loom large. Without UN authorization, the strikes risk violating international law — a point likely raised by Russia and others. France has already signaled reluctance to join combat operations in Syria, unlike its involvement in Iraq. In Iraq, Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi struggles to unify a deeply divided nation along sectarian and ethnic lines. The Kurdish regional government, while allied with the West, is pursuing de facto independence and has seized disputed territories. Sunnis, distrustful of Shia dominance, show no signs of launching a renewed ‘Awakening’ movement similar to 2007. Regional coalition-building has been weak. Unlike the 1991 Gulf War, which united Arab and Western forces, Obama’s anti-ISIS coalition includes no Arab states beyond Turkey. Without active participation from Saudi Arabia, Jordan, or other Gulf nations, the campaign may appear to many Muslims as another Western intrusion. Finally, there is the risk of strategic blowback: intensifying the conflict could fuel recruitment for ISIS, deepen sectarian divides, and erode U.S. credibility across the Muslim world. Obama’s challenge is not just military — it’s political, moral, and existential.

Mientras el enfatizó ku tropas kombati di Estados Unidos no ta ser desplegá, e paso marka un eskalashón grandi di involvimentu di Estados Unidos na e región. Però kritikoan apuntá un diskoneksión problemátiko ente promesonan di 2008 — pa terminá guèrranan, reajustá relashonan ku Rusia, i perseguí desarmamentu nuclear — i e realidat di seis aña despues: kampananan di drone eksendí, konfliktoan prolongá, i aumentu di involvimentu militar. Munchi di e aktoronan tin agenda diverjente, i e koherensia ta indeterminá. E estrategia tambe ta enfrontá obstakulonan serio. E régimen di Assad puede eksplotá e atakonan di Estados Unidos pa presentá e mesm komo e baluár legitimo kontra terrorismo, subvertí e kausa di rebel. Entretanto, potensianan regional komo Irán i Rusia puede reaksioná diplomaticamente o militarmente, spesialmenti si tropan di Estados Unidos ta enkontro direktamente ku tropan di governo siriano. Preguntanan legal ta pesá grandi. Sin autorisashon di ONU, e atakonan ta riske violá leh internashonal — un punkto ku Rusia i otro ta probabelmente ta planteá. Francia ya anonsiá reticensia pa participá na operashon kombati na Siria, diferente di su involvimentu na Irak. Na Irak, primer ministro Haider al-Abadi ta lucha pa uní e nashon profundaMENTE dividí segun seksual i etniko. E gobièrno regional kurdo, aunque aliá ku Okrenti, ta perseguí independensia de facto i ta apresá territorionan disputá. Sunnan, desconfiá di dominashon shiita, no ta mostré signonan di lansa un ‘Awakening’ renove, komo e ta fá na 2007. Konstruksión di koalisión regional ta débil. Diferente di Guèrra di Golfo di 1991, ku ta uní tropan árabe i okrenti, koalisión anti-ISIS di Obama ta kontén ningun país árabe mas ku Turquía. Sin participashon aktivu di Arabia Saudita, Jordania, u otro estadonan di Golfo, e kampana ta probabelmente ta mirá pa munchi musulman komo otro intrusión okrenti. Finalmenti, ta eksisti risgo di reaksion negativu: intensifikashón di konflikto ta puede fomentá rekruitamentu pa ISIS, profundizá dividonan seksual, i debiliá kredibilidat di Estados Unidos pa mundu musulman. Desafio di Obama no ta solamente militar — ta politik, moral, i esistensial.

article_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) — Janelle Monáe is a girl from another planet — and she’s invading your world. A singer-songwriter creating 'cool, futuristic soul with a real '80s quality,' according to DJ Garth Trinidad, Monáe’s appearances this summer include the 'American Idol' finale, the Hollywood Bowl, and concert stages across the U.S., along with guest roles on the Sci Fi Channel this fall. Monáe insists her true identity is Cindi Mayweather, an android fleeing a dystopian future after falling in love with a human — a forbidden act under robotic law. Through this persona, she crafts music that looks to the future while honoring the past. Trinidad, a disc jockey at KCRW in Los Angeles, discovered Monáe three years ago and has since tracked her rise like an astronomer observing a distant comet destined to illuminate the sky. 'I believe she’s going to be a household name in the next year or two,' he said. Known for launching the careers of Jill Scott and Gnarls Barkley, Trinidad calls himself a 'champion of the underdog.' The human Janelle Monáe combines a powerful voice, bold style, vivid imagination, and fearless stage presence — qualities that make her android alter ego feel believable. When her song 'Many Moons' earned a Grammy nomination in December, it was in the Urban/Alternative category. Trinidad compared her fluid, pleasing vocals to Donna Summer in 1976. At a recent Los Angeles performance, she blended 20th-century classics with her own futuristic tracks: a tender rendition of Nat King Cole’s 'Smile,' performed atop a barstool, and a spirited cover of The Beatles’ 1964 hit 'I Saw Her Standing There,' which had senior citizens dancing the Twist. 'We look to a lot of people whose bodies are dead and gone, but their spirit is still with us,' Monáe said after the show. Her choreography draws from James Brown, Michael Jackson, and Devo — blending vintage moves with futuristic flair. Monáe — or Mayweather — believes she can fly. During a show at UCLA’s Royce Hall, she dove headfirst into the crowd, crowd-surfing through an unexpected mosh pit. Search her name on YouTube, and you’ll find videos of her jumping into swimming pools to close her concerts — and even climbing a tree in New York afterward. 'It’s one thing to perform that way, but she backs it up with real talent,' Trinidad noted. Her sci-fi narrative, evoking the 1982 film 'Blade Runner,' recalls classic concept albums with deep storytelling. 'She was just bored with everything else going on — she wanted to transcend it and tell a story,' he said. Monáe insists she isn’t following a formula. 'I’m being led by my maker,' she said. 'I’m very similar to a terminal.' Her rising star is undeniable: Sean 'Diddy' Combs signed her to Bad Boy Records, Coca-Cola enlisted her for its 'Open Happiness' ad campaign — airing during this week’s 'American Idol' finale — and her upcoming tour includes six Northeastern U.S. dates opening for No Doubt, followed by a performance at the Hollywood Bowl alongside legendary jazz singer Etta James. She also appears as herself in two episodes of the Sci Fi Channel’s 'Stargate Universe' this fall.

article_content: On a fine summer morning, I love to rise early and step into my garden before the world wakes. There, I gather a small basket of roses, still glistening with dew. I spill them onto my kitchen table and arrange them in half a dozen vases, placing them throughout the house. Their fragrance rises like invisible smoke, soft and persistent. I make no claim to florist’s skill. Nor do I need any. The roses need no improvement—they are already perfect, whether blooming in the border or standing tall in a vase. They are floral royalty. Their allure is irrational—and that’s precisely why they’re so powerful. Roses tap into a deep, primal romance that lives even in the hardest hearts. The word 'rose' comes from the Greek 'Rodon,' meaning red. Early cultivated roses were mostly crimson. For millennia, they’ve inspired art, poetry, and devotion—from 2000 BC murals to Islamic gardens like the Alhambra and the rose-wreathed tombs of ancient Egypt. Under Islam, the rose symbolized divine perfection. In Christianity, it became the emblem of the Virgin Mary—the five petals representing the five senses, the thorns, life’s trials. On Valentine’s Day, despite winter’s grip in the UK, millions of roses are sold: nearly three million bouquets here, over 198 million red roses in the US. Yet most are grown in plastic tunnels—identical, scentless, soulless. A garden rose, by contrast, is intoxicating. Its scent doesn’t float on the breeze—you must lean close, inhale deeply, like savoring fine wine. That fragrance contains phenylethylamine, a trace amine also found in chocolate, which inhibits monoamine oxidase and slows the breakdown of endorphins, subtly enhancing mood and affection. I grow damasks, albas, gallicas, bourbons, hybrid perpetuals, moss roses, and rugosas. But my favorites are the albas—delicate yet lingering, like a whisper that won’t fade. My most cherished bloom? Cuisse de Nymphe—a pale, many-petaled pink rose whose name, meaning 'thigh of a nymph,' was deemed too risqué by Victorians, who renamed it 'Great Maiden’s Blush.' By any name, it is undeniably seductive. Though we think of roses as quintessentially English, they originated in the Middle East, brought home by Crusaders. The Wars of the Roses pitted the white Rosa Alba against the red Gallica Officinalis—neither native—but Henry VII merged them into the Tudor Rose, now a national icon. The golden age of rose breeding was the Victorian era, centered in France, where the mild south offered ideal conditions. Josephine Bonaparte, at Malmaison, sought every known variety—around 250. By 1910, Roseraie de l’Hay near Paris held 8,000. Roses are tougher than they look. Research shows a chainsaw prunes them as well as fine secateurs. Left alone, they flourish. Plant them deep, mulch them thickly each spring, deadhead regularly—and then leave them be. We don’t celebrate roses for their hardiness—or how easy they are to grow. We honor them for the quiet magic of a morning harvest: dew-kissed, velvety, fragrant, filling a room with something closer to heaven than we usually find on Earth. For the ultimate rose experience this month, visit: Sissinghurst Castle (Kent)—home to 60-year-old shrub roses; Mottisfont Abbey (Hampshire)—planted by legendary rosarian Graham Stuart Thomas; Coughton Court (Warwickshire)—site of the UK’s first Award of Garden Excellence for its Rose Labyrinth; Castle Howard (North Yorkshire)—featuring historic and modern roses in an 18th-century walled garden; and Gardens of The Rose (St Albans, Hampshire)—the National Rose Society’s dedicated sanctuary, open June 8 to July 28.

Mi ta dja e rosas na mesa di kuchin i organiza na media dzus vaza, poe e bini na tuta. E olfato ta subí komo un fumo sin visibl, suave i persistente. Mi no ta klaima pa ser un florista. Mi no ta nesesita. E rosas no ta nesesita mejora—e ta perfekto, si e ta flori na borda o ta sta altu na un vaza. E ta reina di flores. E atrakshon di e rosas ta irashonal—i esi ta porsí por ke e ta tan poderoso. E rosas ta toca un romansa profundo i primal ki ta bini hasta na korason mas duro. Palabra 'rosa' ta bini di griego 'Rodon,' ku significa rojo. E rosas kultivá tempranu ta mòstro rojo. Pa milenio, e ta inspirá arte, poesía, i devoshon—di murales di 2000 A.C. pa jardines islámiko komo Alhambra i tumbas ku guirnalda di rosa di Egipto antiguo. Bai Islam, rosa ta simbolizá perfekshon divino. Bai Kristianismo, e ta konsiderá simbolo di Virgen María—e sinko petalo ta reprezentá e sinko senso, e espina, trial di vida. Na Dia di San Valentín, malgre inverno na Reino Uní, mision di rosas ta vende: casi tri milyon buké akí, mas di 198 milyon rosa rojo na USA. Pero mayoria ta kultivá na tunel di plástik—identiko, sin olfato, sin alma. Un rosa di jardín, pa kontraste, ta embriagador. E olfato no ta flotá na aire—mi ta nesesita leva kersu, inspirá profundamente, komo saboreá un vino fin. E olfato ta kontén feniletilamina, un amina trasa tambe bini na chokolá, ku ta inhibitá monoamina oksidasa i retardi deskomposishon di endorfina, mejora subtilmente humór i afección. Mi rosa mas apresiado? Cuisse de Nymphe—un rosa palido, ku banyak petalo, ku nomber, ku significa 'muslo di una nimfa,' ta konsiderá demais risiko pa Victoriano, ki ta bini nombrá 'Great Maiden’s Blush.' Pa cualker nomber, e ta indiscutibelmente seduktor. Si nos ta pensa ku rosas ta tipiko ingles, e ta bini di Medio Oriente, traí pa Cruzado. Guerra di Rosa ta opone Rosa Alba blanco kon Gallica Officinalis rojo—neni nativo—but Henrique VII ta kombiná e dos komo un símbolo di Tudor Rose, hodi un íkon nasional. E edad di oro di kultivashon di rosa ta era Victoriano, sentro na Fransia, ku klima suave di sur ta ofré kondishon ideal. Josephine Bonaparte, na Malmaison, ta buska to e variedad konosí—alredor di 250. Na 1910, Roseraie de l’Hay na París ta kontén 8000. E rosas ta mas resistente ku nos ta pensa. Ricerca ta demonstrá ku un serra ta podá e tan bon komo sekator fin. Si nos ta dja e ta kresé. Plantá e profundo, mulchá e fort na primavera, remové e flori muerto—i despues dja e ta kere. Nos no ta celebrá e rosas pa e resistensia—ó pa fasilidat di kultivá. Nos ta honrá e pa e magia silensioso di un konsiga di mañan: ku rima, sedoso, olfato, konteni e kuartu ku ta mas separe di paradiso ki nos ta bini na tierra. Pa e eksperensia di rosa mas perfekto na mes, vizita: Sissinghurst Castle (Kent)—hogar di rosa arbusto di 60 aña; Mottisfont Abbey (Hampshire)—plantá pa legendario rosarian Graham Stuart Thomas; Coughton Court (Warwickshire)—siti di primer Premio di Excelensia di Jardín pa e Rose Labyrinth na Reino Uní; Castle Howard (North Yorkshire)—kontén rosa antiko i moderno na un jardín murá di siglo 18; i Gardens of The Rose (St Albans, Hampshire)—santuariu di National Rose Society, abier di 8 di junio a 28 di julio.

article_content: In a landmark ruling on privacy rights, expectant mothers in New Jersey may now legally exclude the baby’s father from the delivery room. The decision, issued by Superior Court Judge Sohail Mohammed in November 2013, stems from a case in which Steven Plotnick sued his ex-fiancée, Rebecca DeLucciato, demanding notification of her labor and immediate access to their newborn. Plotnick and DeLucciato had separated before their planned wedding and were minimally in contact as her due date approached. While Plotnick insisted he did not seek entry into the delivery room, he argued strongly for the right to be present with his child immediately after birth to begin bonding — a right he felt should be equal to the mother’s. Judge Mohammed ruled that a pregnant woman’s constitutional right to bodily autonomy, affirmed in Roe v. Wade (1973) and Planned Parenthood v. Casey (1992), supersedes any paternal interest prior to birth. He emphasized that even when a father demonstrates deep concern for the pregnancy, his rights remain subordinate to those of the mother — particularly given the potential for exposure to private medical information. DeLucciato’s attorney confirmed that the couple had been estranged for months and that she had always intended to allow Plotnick to visit their daughter in the hospital — just not in the delivery room. Plotnick accepted the ruling and saw his newborn daughter shortly after delivery. The decision has drawn criticism from fathers’ rights groups, including Fathers & Children’s Equality, which called it a setback for parental equality. Critics argue that excluding a father from the birth experience diminishes his role as a co-parent. Yet the court maintained that the sanctity of a woman’s medical privacy must prevail in such intimate, high-stakes moments.

article_content: At first glance, the old house on Godwin Road in Margate looks like it’s collapsing into its own garden — bricks sagging, windows tilting, a doorway dangling as if pulled by gravity. But this isn’t decay. It’s art. Artist Alex Chinneck, 28, spent months transforming the long-abandoned mid-19th-century property into a stunning illusion: the entire front facade appears to have slid sideways into the lawn. The project, named 'From the knees of my nose to the belly of my toes,' cost £100,000 and was made possible by ten local businesses donating materials, labor, and expertise. The house had sat empty for over a decade until Thanet District Council seized it under compulsory purchase laws. Now, after its debut as a public installation, it’s set to be renovated and returned to residential use. Chinneck, who lives in Hackney, originally tried to launch the project in London but found more inspiration in Margate after the opening of the Turner Contemporary gallery nearby. He wanted to create something playful and welcoming — art that doesn’t demand you step inside a gallery to experience it. 'People often feel intimidated by art spaces,' he said. 'This is art you can just walk past and smile at.' Since its completion, visitors from across the UK and beyond have flocked to see the house, turning it into an unexpected landmark. Clive Hart, council leader, called it 'a bold, imaginative move' that puts Thanet on the global cultural map.

Pero e no ta deshabor. E ta arte. Artista Alex Chinneck, 28, ta pasá mesnan transformandu e kasa abandonaó di siglo 19 na un ilusión impresionante: e fachada kompletu ta mira komo si el ta deslizá pa lateral den e prato. Proyecto, ku ta titulá 'Del rodillas di mi naris pa e barriga di mi pies', ta kosta £100.000 i ta posibel graças a dies kompanianan lokal ku ta dona material, labor, i eksperensia. E kasa ta sidadu mas di des aña denbò hasta ku Thanet District Council ta apresá el pa leyi di compra komulsoria. Ahora, despues di su debut komo instalashon públiko, el ta prepará pa ser restaurá i returná pa uso residensial. Chinneck, ku ta habitá na Hackney, ta intentá lansa e proyecto na Londres pero el ta hallá más inspirashon na Margate despues di apertura di galería Turner Contemporary. El ta bini pa krea algo divertí i akésibl — arte ku no ta pedi pa bini den un galería pa eksperiensia. 'Gente a menudo ta sintí intimidá pa espasionan di arte,' el ta dí. 'E ta arte ku tu pone pasa i sonríe.' Despues di su kumpletu, vizitadornan di tota Reino Uní i mas lejano ta komeçá a bini mira e kasa, transformándo el na un landmark inesperá. Clive Hart, lider di konsil, ta kallá e 'un mudéza audaz i imaginativu' ku ta pone Thanet na mapa kultural global.

article_content: Dr. Martin Weale, an economist at the Bank of England, said employees could be set for pay rises as the squeeze on family finances eases. British companies are becoming more confident as the economy recovers, which is likely to lead to increased wages for millions of workers. Households are also benefiting from lower oil prices, which have significantly reduced the cost of petrol and diesel, leaving families with more disposable income this Christmas, he noted. The comments come as the CBI reported that the UK’s job-rich recovery will strengthen next year, with more than half of firms planning to raise pay above inflation. Dr. Weale told the BBC: 'When I visit businesses across the country, I hear them discussing pay increases in a way very different from what I heard earlier this year—or certainly this time last year. There's now a broader sense that proposed raises are materially higher than in the past. A year ago, many firms announced pay freezes; now, I encounter that far less often.' He highlighted the sharp drop in oil prices—from $115 a barrel in June to around $60 today—as 'good news' for the UK economy. 'Everyone who buys petrol is glad to see prices fall,' said Dr. Weale, a member of the Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee. 'This boosts spending power, which is especially welcome at Christmas.' Official data from the Office for National Statistics last week showed average pay is now rising comfortably faster than inflation. The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) has fallen to a 12-year low of 1%, while wages are up 1.6% compared to a year ago. The CBI stated that 55% of UK firms plan to increase salaries in 2015 at or above the Retail Prices Index (RPI) level, currently at 2%. Rain Newton-Smith, CBI’s director of economics, said: 'The economy is on a solid path heading into Christmas. While growth has slowed slightly, this reflects a return to a steadier, more sustainable pace as the temporary boost from pent-up demand fades.' However, he warned that global challenges—including a weak Eurozone, slowing emerging markets, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, Russia, and Ukraine—remain headwinds to growth. While lower oil and fuel prices put more money in households’ and businesses’ pockets, they also strain major oil-producing economies. Frances O’Grady, general secretary of the TUC, cautioned that many workers are still feeling the pinch. 'After seven years of stagnant wages and few meaningful pay rises, Britain’s workers may wait years for their living standards to recover to pre-crisis levels,' she said. 'We need stronger growth and better labor market regulation to ensure the recovery’s benefits are fairly shared—and to avoid being locked into a low-value, cut-price economy.'

Kompanianan britániko ta bini mas konfiansa mientras e ekonomia ta rekoberi, lo ta leva a un aumento di salario pa milión di trabayadó, el a dí. E komentá ta bini ku CBI a raporta ku e rekoberi ku ta bini mas trabou pa akiña akiña na próksimo aña, ku mas di mitat di kompanianan ta planifiká pa amentá salario mas ku inflashon. Mientras kresimiento ta bini más lento un pokito, e ta refleja un regreso pa un ritmo mas estable i sostenible ku e impulso temporal di demanda akumulá ta desaparece.' 'Después di siete aña di salário estasionario i poko amento di salario signifikativo, trabayadó britániko ta pòtensia pa espèr ta aña pa su stadí di vida ta rekoberí a nivel antis di krísis,' el a dikí. 'Nos ta nesésita kresimiento mas fuerte i regulashon mas bon di merká di trabou pa asegurá ku benefishonan di rekoberi ta distribuí equitativamente—i pa evitá ta atrapa na un ekonomia di baxo valor i barata.'

article_content: One year after a horrific attack in Miami, Ronald Poppo—a homeless man who lost 75% of his face—is rebuilding his life with quiet strength. Once unable to speak publicly, Poppo has now shared his story in a video released by hospital staff, expressing deep gratitude for the community’s support. The attack, which occurred in May 2012 on the MacArthur Causeway, left Poppo blind and disfigured. Rudy Eugene, the assailant, was shot and killed by police after reportedly growling and refusing to comply. Surveillance footage showed Eugene stripping and violently assaulting Poppo, sparking global headlines. Though early reports suggested Eugene was under the influence of bath salts, toxicology tests later confirmed only marijuana in his system. Poppo endured multiple surgeries at Jackson Memorial Hospital before transitioning to long-term care at Perdue Medical Center. Despite his injuries, Poppo has made remarkable progress. He now practices guitar daily, celebrates milestones like his 66th birthday with hospital staff, and has gained 50 pounds under medical care. His wounds have healed significantly since the initial graphic images were published. Originally from New York, Poppo had lived on Florida’s streets for three decades, estranged from family who believed he had died by suicide. In his message, he urged society to extend compassion to others facing similar hardship: 'People in my predicament need to be helped out—and I’m sure there are others in the same situation.'

E heridanan a saná signifikativamente despues di e imajen grafiko inicial. Originalmenti di Nueva York, Poppo a habitá na e kalanan di Florida pa trinta aña, separá di su familia ku ta pensa ku el a suicidá. article_content: On the final day of the Maxi Rolex Cup in Sardinia, Slovenia’s Igor Simcic and his 30-meter yacht Esimit Europa 2 emerged as the top winners. Sponsored by Gazprom, Esimit Europa 2 was crowned the world’s best Maxi-class yacht after dominating all four of its races among 49 competing vessels — some up to 45 meters in length. Other class champions included Germany’s Claus Peter Offen aboard Y3K in the Wally class; John Williams and Ranger in the J-Class; and Otto Happel with Hetairos in the Supermaxi division. In the inaugural Mini Maxi Rolex Worlds, Niklas Zennström and Ran claimed the overall title, while Brian Benjamin and Aegir took gold in the Racer/Cruiser category.

article_content: Last night, residents across much of the eastern United States witnessed a dazzling green-and-white fireball streaking across the sky — a spectacular sight coinciding with the annual Taurid meteor shower. The American Meteor Society logged more than 200 eyewitness accounts, mostly between 6:15 and 6:25 p.m., stretching from Georgia up through the Great Lakes region. Witnesses described the object as luminous and fast-moving, leaving no trace of impact on the ground. Footage captured by the Benwood, West Virginia Police Department’s dashcam provides one of the clearest recordings of the phenomenon. This display is part of the Taurid meteor stream, which occurs each year as Earth passes through debris left behind by Comet Encke. According to Bill Cooke of NASA’s Meteoroid Environment Office, Encke’s fragments are unusually large, often producing brilliant meteors when they enter the atmosphere. The comet itself, roughly three miles wide and composed of ice and rock, orbits the Sun every 3.3 years. Meanwhile, in Chicago, initial reports of a similar fireball were later clarified as a Red Bull marketing stunt: three skydivers jumped from an aircraft wearing flare-equipped footwear, creating a glowing trail as they descended — mimicking a natural meteor. This stunt was timed to promote an upcoming event. Interestingly, nearly simultaneous sightings occurred in western Japan, where observers also reported a bright green object in the night sky. Experts suggest this was likely a bolide — an exceptionally bright meteor — visible due to the time difference. While the U.S. and Japan events were not physically connected, both highlight how common and widespread meteor phenomena can be during peak shower periods.
translated_content: Anochi, ribianan di e parte oriental di Estados Unidos ta mira un fuego bola verda i blanco ku ta pasá rapido pa e sky — un vista espetakuloso ku ta koincidí ku e anual Taurid meteor shower. American Meteor Society ta registrá mas di 200 reportan di testigu, mayoria entri 6:15 i 6:25 p.m., ta spandi di Georgia hasta e Great Lakes. Testigu ta describi e objekto komo luminoso i rapido, sin dejá nengun trasa di impacto na tierra. Filmashon kapurá pa e Benwood, West Virginia Police Department ta dja un di e grabashon mas klaro di fenomeno. E displya ta part di e fluks Taurid, ku ta pasa anualmente ku Tierra ta pasa atraves di restan di Comet Encke. Segun Bill Cooke di NASA’s Meteoroid Environment Office, fragmentonan di Encke ta inusitadamente grandi, a menudo producí meteoronan briljante ku ta entra na atmosfera. Kometa mesmo, mas ou menos tres milla di ancho i kompuestu di hielo i roka, ta orbita e Sol cada 3.3 año. Mientras tanto, na Chicago, reportan inicial di un bola similar ta klasifiká komo un stunt di promosión di Red Bull: tres paracaidistanan ta saltá for di un avion ku ta usá flare na e zapato, krea un trasa brillante ku ta bai bai — imita un meteor natural. E stunt ta planificá pa promó e evento próksimo. Interesantemente, observashonan similaer ta ocurrí na oeste di Japón, ku observadoran tambe ta raporta un objekto verda briljante na e sky di nochi. Two miles away, in Marina Park, thousands of street children in Brazil jerseys waited outside the team hotel to cheer them on. Before the match, coach Luiz Felipe Scolari visited a small chapel on the grounds, seeking spiritual strength. Football here is the opium of the masses—an obsession that lifts millions from daily hardship and unites a nation of nearly 200 million for 90 intense minutes. When asked about winning the World Cup, Brazilians often reply, 'E os outros quatorze?' ('Yes, but what about the other 14?'), believing they deserve to win every time. Fans pressed against fences to catch a glimpse of Neymar, David Luiz, or Thiago Silva as they arrived at the hotel the night before the match. Two Black Hawk helicopters escorted the team bus through Fortaleza’s streets, searchlights cutting through the night—a spectacle fit for a national hero. article_content: Britain's economy received a much-needed boost yesterday after exports to countries beyond Europe surged to an all-time high. Official figures showed UK firms sold a record £13.2 billion worth of goods to non-European Union markets in July—an 11% increase from the previous month. Sales to the EU also rose by 7.7% to £12.4 billion, but the proportion of exports going to the 17-nation eurozone fell to 43.6%, the lowest level since records began in 1988. The surge in exports to non-EU markets helped shrink Britain’s trade deficit with the rest of the world, reducing the gap between exports and imports from £4.3 billion in June to £1.5 billion in July—the largest monthly improvement on record. This shift toward growing markets in Asia and Latin America, hailed by economists as a revolution in British trade, has lifted spirits among ministers and businesses that have actively pursued new trade partnerships amid the eurozone’s ongoing crises. The British economy contracted by 0.5% in the second quarter of 2012 and had been in decline for nine consecutive months—the longest double-dip recession in over half a century. However, hopes are rising that the economy may begin growing again in the third quarter, as business activity rebounds from disruptions caused by the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee. A Treasury spokesperson said: 'These figures are encouraging news for the UK economy and show we are beginning to earn our way in the world. The government is working hard to deliver sustainable, export-led growth.' The latest export data followed the largest increase in industrial production in 25 years. 'It is looking increasingly likely that growth in the third quarter will more than offset the 0.5% contraction in the second quarter,' said Howard Archer, chief UK economist at IHS Global Insight. Yet with the eurozone crisis deepening and signs of economic slowdown emerging across major economies—including the US, China, and India—the outlook remains uncertain. Mark Gregory, chief economist at Ernst & Young, noted: 'The short-term outlook for exports remains fragile, with the eurozone on the brink of re-entering recession and weakening demand in key emerging markets. But we are more optimistic about the medium term, provided the eurozone holds together and begins to recover.'

Pero nos a mas optimistá pa perspektiva mas lejano, si eurozona ta konservá integro i ta salí di rekésion.'

article_content: In a controversial decision, a former member of Sudan’s Janjaweed militia—who admitted in televised and printed interviews to participating in mass killings and village burnings during the Darfur genocide—has been permitted to remain in the United Kingdom. Despite confessing to crimes that fall under international definitions of war crimes and crimes against humanity, UK judges ruled that deporting him would violate his fundamental human rights. His disclosures, made in 2008 to BBC Newsnight and The Times, were so detailed that they exposed his identity within the Sudanese expatriate community in Britain, raising credible fears he would be targeted for retaliation if sent back to Sudan. Although immigration authorities initially denied him refugee status based on these very admissions—citing the Geneva Convention’s exclusion of war criminals—the Upper Tribunal ultimately upheld the earlier asylum grant, not because he was innocent, but because returning him posed a clear threat to his life. Now, under strict conditions, he lives in the UK with no access to employment, education, or welfare, and must regularly report to authorities. The case has reignited debate across British politics: while some argue the UK must protect those fleeing persecution, others, including Conservative MP Dominic Raab, condemn it as a dangerous loophole allowing perpetrators to evade justice. The UK Border Agency maintains it seeks to remove all suspected war criminals but is bound by court rulings that prioritize human rights over deportation when lives are at stake.

Malgre ku el a konfesá a krimenanan ki ta konsiderá ku komo krimenan di gerra i krimenan kontra e humanidat, juzges britániko a determiná ku deportá el ta violá e dèrechonan fundamentál di e humanidat. E kaso a reavivá un debát na politika britániko: mentri un kantidat a arguménta ku Reino Uní ta tení ku protehé e ki ta fuyí di persekushon, otro, inkluyendo e diputá conservador Dominic Raab, a konsidera e komo un brecha peligrosa ki ta permití ku kriminales ta evitá justisia. E UK Border Agency ta mantene ku el ta buská remové todos e sospechosos di krimen di gerra, mas el ta ligá pa rulamentonan di korte ki priorisá e dèrechonan di e humanidat boke deportashon ku bida ta en peligro.

article_content: (CNN) -- Mathieu Flamini scored the winner nine minutes from time as a second-string AC Milan side beat third-division Novara 2-1 at the San Siro on Wednesday to reach the Coppa Italia quarterfinals. Milan coach Leonardo made 11 changes to the side that won 3-0 at Juventus on Sunday, with Ronaldinho, David Beckham, Andrea Pirlo, and Alessandro Nesta not even included on the bench. Veteran striker Filippo Inzaghi opened the scoring in the 12th minute, but in the first minute of the second half, Pablo Gonzalez stunned the home fans by equalizing for Novara. French international Flamini then secured victory for the Rossoneri with a powerful shot from the edge of the penalty area. Milan will now face either Udinese or Lumezzane for a spot in the semifinals. Meanwhile, Juventus bounced back from their weekend defeat as Alessandro Del Piero scored twice — including a penalty — to help them secure a 3-0 victory over 10-man Napoli in Turin, easing pressure on under-fire coach Ciro Ferrara. Diego opened the scoring as a full-strength Juventus side ended Napoli’s 14-match unbeaten run under coach Walter Mazzarri, though Juventus did rest several first-team regulars. Napoli’s Matteo Contini was sent off for a second yellow card following a foul on Diego, which led to the penalty. Catania recorded an impressive 2-1 away win against Genoa to also reach the quarterfinals. Two goals from Gianvito Plasmati gave Catania a two-goal lead, before Marco Rossi pulled one back in the 57th minute. But Genoa’s hopes of a comeback were dashed when Socratis Papastathopoulos was sent off in the 58th minute, followed by Rossi in the 59th minute. Inter Milan and Roma had previously qualified for the quarterfinals, with the final three spots to be decided on Thursday.

Entrenador di Milan Leonardo a fá 11 kambyo na e ekipa ku a ganá 3-0 na Juventus na domingó, ku Ronaldinho, David Beckham, Andrea Pirlo i Alessandro Nesta ni siquiera ta presentá na e banco. article_content: Thomas Menino, the former mayor of Boston who guided the city through its darkest hour after the 2013 terrorist attack on the Boston Marathon, has died of cancer at age 71. He was the longest-serving mayor in the city’s history. Menino served consecutive terms from 1993 until January 2014, reshaping Boston’s skyline and revitalizing neighborhoods. Shortly after leaving office, he was diagnosed with cancer. Last week, he announced he was suspending his book tour and halting treatment to spend more time with his family. On April 15, 2013, less than three weeks after announcing he would not seek a sixth term, two homemade bombs exploded near the marathon finish line, killing three people and injuring more than 260. Many suffered severe limb loss due to ball-bearing-packed explosives. Menino was recovering in the hospital from surgery for a broken leg when the attacks occurred. Against his doctors’ advice, he checked himself out to attend the first press conference. During the ensuing manhunt and citywide lockdown, Menino became a calming presence. Three days after the bombing, he hoisted himself out of his wheelchair at the Cathedral of the Holy Cross to declare: 'We are one Boston. No adversity, no challenge, nothing can tear down the resilience in the heart of this city and its people.' Before becoming mayor, Menino was president of the Boston City Council. He assumed the role of acting mayor in 1993 when then-Mayor Raymond Flynn was appointed U.S. Ambassador to the Vatican by President Bill Clinton. Menino famously told developers: 'Guys, flat roofs don’t make it,' and personally approved the illuminated crown atop 111 Huntington Avenue — now one of Boston’s most iconic buildings. Known for his folksy, down-to-earth style, Menino was nicknamed 'Mumbles Menino' for his speech hesitations. Yet he connected deeply with residents — a recent poll found half of Bostonians had personally met him. A liberal Democrat in a liberal city, he won re-election by landslide margins, even appealing to conservative voters in East Boston. He co-founded Mayors Against Illegal Guns in 2006 with Michael Bloomberg, growing it into a national coalition of over 1,000 mayors. Leaders including President Obama, Senator Warren, and Secretary Kerry praised his vision, grit, and unwavering dedication to Boston’s people and neighborhoods.

article_content: Walter Meyerle, a 35-year-old tattoo artist from Falls Township, Pennsylvania, is on trial for allegedly committing nearly 200 sexual offenses against 15 children between 1998 and 2011. He faces up to 150 years in prison. Court evidence reveals Meyerle targeted minors by forming relationships with their mothers, often offering tattoos in exchange for sexual acts. Victims included children as young as four, as well as two adult women. One victim, a 17-year-old student at Benjamin Franklin Freshman Academy, said Meyerle coerced her into taking explicit photos of herself and her younger sister. He threatened to send the images to her family and classmates if she refused his demands. Text messages introduced in court show Meyerle telling the teen, 'Payback is a bitch,' after she declined to engage in sexual activity with her mother’s boyfriend. He also told her, 'You are every guy's fantasy — getting with a daughter with a hot-ass body.' Investigators recovered approximately 50 videos and 30 photos from Meyerle’s devices, depicting graphic abuse including children with adults, other children, and animals. Some recordings captured young children crying and saying 'no, no' during sexual acts. Meyerle used these images to blackmail victims, forcing compliance through fear of exposure. He also sent photos of a minor holding a sign saying 'Hi Steve' to a friend, according to police records. Since his arrest in March 2011, Meyerle has been held in Bucks County Prison’s restricted housing unit on $5 million bail. He previously attempted to escape from custody.

article_content: On 30 January 2013, motoring groups condemned the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) for what they called a 'whitewash' after the watchdog declined to launch a full investigation into UK petrol pricing. Despite years of complaints from drivers that fuel prices rise rapidly when crude oil costs increase but fall slowly when they drop, the OFT concluded there was 'very limited evidence' of artificial price inflation. The OFT acknowledged widespread public distrust but maintained that competition in the fuel market was functioning well. It attributed price hikes mainly to global crude oil costs and rising taxes — not collusion among oil companies. Motorway service stations were found to charge up to 8p per litre more than other forecourts. While some suggested requiring these stations to display prices on the hard shoulder, the OFT did not recommend such measures. Critics, including FairFuelUK’s Quentin Willson and the Road Haulage Association’s Geoff Dunning, called the decision 'bitterly disappointing' and a 'missed opportunity' to improve transparency. The AA noted that since the start of 2013, petrol had reached 134.08p per litre and diesel 141.42p — with wholesale price drops quickly reflected in rises but taking weeks to appear in reductions. Professor Stephen Glaister of the RAC Foundation confirmed the OFT’s finding that fuel duty and VAT make up roughly 60% of the pump price — the highest tax burden in Europe. He stated the real culprits behind driver hardship are government policy and global oil markets, not industry practices. The Petrol Retailers’ Association criticized the OFT for leaving independent garages to face angry customers without clear answers. Conservative MP Robert Halfon insisted the issue remained unresolved, asserting that both oil companies and the government share responsibility for high fuel costs.

article_content: A prominent researcher, Jonas Himmelstrand, has argued that putting young children in daycare for long hours may harm their emotional development and school performance. In a report set to be shared with UK lawmakers, he links rising levels of bullying, truancy, and declining academic standards — especially in countries like Sweden — to heavy reliance on state-subsidized childcare. Himmelstrand, who educated his own children at home and says he was persecuted by Swedish authorities for doing so (a claim not independently verified), warns that exposing toddlers to large peer groups too early can stunt their psychological growth and weaken intergenerational cultural values. His advocacy group, Mothers at Home Matter, is urging the UK government to shift financial incentives away from subsidizing daycare and instead offer meaningful tax relief to families where one parent stays home. Currently, UK tax policies provide more support to single-parent households than to two-parent families where one parent chooses to care for children full-time — a gap critics say discourages parental caregiving. While the government continues to push for higher maternal workforce participation, Himmelstrand and his supporters argue that Sweden’s experience shows such policies may come at a steep cost: soaring rates of anxiety among teen girls, declining math scores, and chaotic classrooms. They call for a national conversation that doesn’t just celebrate paid work but also recognizes the irreplaceable value of early parental presence.

Himmelstrand, ku ta eduka su propio kiko na kasa i ku a kierde ku el ta perseguidu pa autoridat di Suedia pa e diskision (afirmashon ku ta ta verifiká), a warna ku pone kiko na grupan grandi temprano ta pude frená su dezenvolbimentu psikolójiko i debilí kultura ente generashonan. Su grupu di presion, Mothers at Home Matter, ta pedí pa gobièrno di Reino Uní ku ta kambiá incentivonan finansiero pa no subisidiá daycare i mas bien ofresé alivio fisikal significativo pa famílianan ku un di e padres ta keda na kasa. Actualmenti, politikanan fisikal di Reino Uní ta ofresé mas apoyo pa famílianan di un padre ku pa famílianan di dos padres ku un ta keda na kasa pa kuida kiko — un hende ku kritikonan alega ku ta desinsentiba kuida di padres. Mientras e gobièrno ta sigui promoviendo participación mas altu di maderan na e merkadu di labór, Himmelstrand i su partidarioan alega ku eksperiensia di Suedia ta mustra ku politikanan asina ta pude tin un kosto altu: amento di ansiedat na muchheronan adolescent, disminusion di puntuationan di matemátika, i klasan desordená. E ta pedí pa un diskusión nasional ku no solamente ta celebrá labór pagá, mas tambe ta rekonesé e valor inreemplasabel di presensia temprana di padres.

article_content: Itzcoatl Ocampo, a 25-year-old former Marine, was found unresponsive in his single-cell at Central Jail in Santa Ana on Wednesday and later died at a nearby hospital on Thursday. Authorities have not yet released a cause of death, but an autopsy is scheduled for the coming days. The Orange County District Attorney’s Office will investigate the circumstances surrounding his death. Ocampo was facing multiple murder charges, including the killings of four homeless men between December 2011 and January 2012, and the murders of Raquel Estrada, 53, and her son Juan Herrera, 34, in October 2011. Prosecutors alleged he targeted vulnerable individuals because he viewed them as a 'blight on society.' He reportedly told investigators he sought to emulate Charles Whitman, the 1966 University of Texas tower shooter, and aimed to kill 16 people. According to court transcripts, Ocampo claimed he developed a compulsion to kill after serving an eight-month deployment in Iraq in 2008. He described feeling trapped in mundane military duties — driving water and dirt trucks — and said he began stalking homeless people because they were 'available and vulnerable.' He admitted to stabbing victims repeatedly, even after believing they were dead, and said he used pornography, including Penthouse magazine, to psych himself up. Each of the four homeless victims — James McGillivray (53), Lloyd Middaugh (42), Paulus Smit (57), and John Berry (64) — suffered over 40 stab wounds with a 7-inch military-style blade. The attacks occurred across Orange County, sparking fear among the region’s homeless population. Police urged them to seek shelter while the investigation unfolded. Ocampo’s father, Refugio Ocampo, told reporters his son returned from Iraq a changed man — withdrawn, paranoid, and disillusioned. Veteran advocates emphasized that Ocampo’s case should not define all returning service members, noting that most veterans reintegrate successfully despite trauma. Ocampo pleaded not guilty to all charges. His trial was set for May 2014, and prosecutors were seeking the death penalty. His death in custody halts legal proceedings but does not close the case — investigators will continue reviewing evidence and the conditions of his incarceration.

Las autoridat no a konsidera e causa di muerte, pero un autopsia ta programá pa e diás ku ta bini. Ofisa di Fiscal di Distrito di Orange County ta investiga e kondisionan ku ta rasona e muerte. Papá di Ocampo, Refugio Ocampo, a di ku reporter ku su hijo a bini bak di Irak ku un kambio — apagá, paranoid, i desilusioná. Ocampo ta plea no culpabil pa tota e kargas. Su trial ta programá pa mai 2014, i prokuradur ta busca e pena di muerte. Su muerte na kustodia ta suspende e prosesu legal, mas no ta tira e kaso — investigadornan ta kontinuá revisa e ebidensia i e kondisionan di su detenshon.

article_content: Al-Qaeda has urged a new generation of 'lone wolf' terrorists to target easyJet and British Airways flights with homemade explosives, according to its online magazine, Inspire. The publication calls for attacks on these airlines to generate headlines and 'crush the enemy’s economy.' Released on Christmas Eve, the latest issue of Inspire identifies British Airways as the UK’s flag carrier and easyJet due to its high passenger volume as a low-cost carrier. It also lists American Airlines, Delta, United, and Air France as targets, along with prominent figures such as Bill Gates and former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke. The magazine praises Umar Farouk Abdulmutallab, the 'underpants bomber' sentenced to life in 2012 after attempting to detonate a device hidden in his underwear on a flight from Amsterdam to Detroit. Prosecutors noted the bomb partially failed to ignite, saving the lives of 300 passengers. Inspire includes purported instructions for bypassing airport security, echoing its earlier issue that featured the notorious guide 'Make a Bomb in the Kitchen of Your Mom,' suspected of inspiring the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing. Despite Continental Airlines having merged with United in 2012, the magazine still references it under its former name. The magazine’s anonymous author, referred to as the 'Al-Qaeda chef,' stated the primary targets should be the U.S., followed by the U.K. and France. He emphasized the 'lone wolf' model as difficult to detect because 'none knows him but Allah' and he has 'no relationship with any group or individual.' Inspire also commended the October 2013 axe attack on New York police officers, carried out by U.S. Navy veteran Zale Thompson, whom the FBI later described as having consumed Islamic State beheading videos online — a factor they said 'played a role' in the attack. In the UK, possession of Inspire has led to multiple convictions under Section 58 of the Terrorism Act 2000, with sentences of up to ten years. In 2013, four men received a combined 44-year sentence for planning an attack in Luton using a toy car based on the magazine’s guidance. British Airways and easyJet both reiterated that passenger and crew safety remains their top priority, declining to comment on specific security measures. In response to rising fears of lone wolf attacks, security around British royal residences has been significantly tightened. For the first time since the peak of IRA terrorism, most members of the Queen’s Guard no longer perform sentry duty alone. At Clarence House, St James’s Palace, and Windsor Castle, guards have been relocated behind barriers or accompanied by armed police officers equipped with carbines, pistols, and Tasers. The Metropolitan Police and Ministry of Defence declined to comment on operational security details, stating that arrangements are routinely reviewed.

article_content: Due to severe winter weather disrupting travel across the Midwest and South, the U.S. Senate delayed a crucial vote on extending long-term unemployment benefits until Tuesday. Seventeen senators, including key figures from both parties, were unable to reach Washington, prompting Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid to secure unanimous consent to postpone the procedural vote originally set for Monday evening. The proposed legislation would renew federal unemployment aid for roughly 1.3 million Americans whose benefits expired last month after Congress chose not to extend the 2008 recession-era program. Democrats, backed by President Obama, argue that continuing these payments is vital to sustaining consumer spending and supporting economic recovery. They’re just one vote short of the 60 needed to bypass a Republican filibuster, with four GOP senators—Susan Collins of Maine, Dean Heller of Nevada, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire—indicating they’ll support moving forward with debate. However, many Republicans remain opposed unless the $6.4 billion cost is fully offset by spending cuts elsewhere. Senators like Mark Kirk of Illinois and conservative groups such as the Club for Growth insist the federal program should be replaced by state-level solutions or paid for through budget reductions. Some GOP members, including Collins, say they’re willing to consider the bill—but only if it includes provisions linking benefits to job training for those unlikely to return to their previous roles. President Obama personally reached out to GOP senators to urge support, stressing that failure to act could weaken the broader economy by reducing household spending. Meanwhile, critics warn that extended benefits may reduce incentives to seek employment. With the unemployment rate still at 7%, over 10 million Americans remain jobless—and a third of them have been without work for more than six months. As the new legislative session begins, this vote has become a litmus test for how the post-midterms political landscape will shape economic policy.

article_content: On Sunday, approximately 500 individuals with foreign passports or dual nationality, along with seven injured Palestinians, crossed into Egypt from the besieged Gaza Strip, according to reports from both sides of the border. An anonymous Egyptian security official told AFP that the evacuees hailed from 15 different countries. AlQahera News, a media outlet closely tied to Egyptian intelligence, reported that the seven wounded Palestinians were among those who passed through the Rafah crossing. Rafah is the only exit from Gaza not under Israeli control — though it had been closed for the previous two days. With more than 2.4 million people still trapped inside Gaza, the overwhelming majority remain unable to flee as the war between Israel and Hamas continues since October 7.

article_content: New York (CNN) — Two men have been arrested in connection with the death of Corey McGriff, a popular television and radio disc jockey known as DJ 'Megatron,' who was shot and killed on Staten Island early Sunday morning, according to New York City police. McGriff, 32, died from a gunshot wound to the torso near his home shortly after 2 a.m. on March 27. William Williams, 21, and Richard Cromwell, 20, both residents of Staten Island, were arrested on Wednesday and charged with murder, robbery, and criminal possession of a weapon. They are expected to be arraigned on Thursday, according to Peter Spencer, spokesperson for the Staten Island District Attorney. McGriff was best known for his appearances on BET’s music countdown show, '106 & Park.' He had worked with both the show and BET.com since 2006, according to a statement released by the network. 'The BET Networks family is saddened by the news of the untimely loss of our friend and colleague, Corey 'Megatron' McGriff,' the statement said. 'We extend our deepest condolences to his family. He will truly be missed.' CNN’s Leigh Remizowski contributed to this report.

McGriff, 32, ta muerdi di un tiros na torso near su kas brek despues di 2 a.m. den 27 di mart. E ta esperá pa ser presentá pa juicio den juéves, segun Peter Spencer, portavoz di Prokuraduría di Staten Island. McGriff ta mas konosí pa su apariensia na programa di música di BET, '106 & Park.' E ta trabou pa e programa i BET.com desde 2006, segun un declarashon di e red. article_content: A newborn boy blinded by a hunter’s stray bullet that shot through his living room window has returned home. Shayne Iverson, from Clarksburg, Pennsylvania, spent more than two months at the Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh and underwent numerous surgeries following the near-fatal incident. On Wednesday—his mother Stefanie’s 31st birthday—doctors gave him the all-clear. Recovery: Shayne Iverson, who was blinded by a hunter’s stray bullet at just six days old, has returned home in time for his first Christmas. His father, 42-year-old Jeremie Iverson, told the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review that the infant is doing well. He and his wife have not been able to work since the accident occurred on September 25. They have also been managing hospital visits while caring for their other two children: nine-year-old Caden and two-year-old Gabi. Shayne was six days old when he was accidentally shot in the head by a deer hunter in late September. Around-the-clock care: The infant spent more than two months at the Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh and underwent multiple surgeries after the incident. Touch and go: Doctors removed a blood clot to prevent brain swelling and fought to preserve his vision, but ultimately could not restore it. At the time of the shooting, his father was cuddling him on the couch at home, around 7 p.m. After being airlifted to the hospital, doctors removed a blood clot to prevent brain swelling and attempted to save his vision without success. They believe Shayne survived because the bullet exited through his eye socket rather than striking his brain. Although the two-month-old no longer requires 24-hour care, he will need additional surgeries in the future. His father, a carpenter, said their home is filled with medical equipment, medications, and 'boxes and boxes of medical supplies.' The Iverson family set up a GoFundMe page, sharing a photo of baby Shayne with his big brother Caden, age nine, and two-year-old sister Gabi from when he was one day old. Mother Stefanie Iverson said her son’s life was spared because the bullet exited through his eye socket. Jeremie and Stefanie Iverson have not been able to work since their son was accidentally shot. Indiana County District Attorney Pat Dougherty confirmed the hunter held an agricultural deer control permit. No charges have been filed, though investigators continue reviewing whether game regulations or other laws were violated. The hunter was reportedly 300 yards from the home and using a .308 hunting rifle on private farmland across from the Iverson property. Nearly $18,000 has been donated by well-wishers after Shayne’s aunt launched the GoFundMe campaign. In a heartfelt message to The Ellen DeGeneres Show announcing Shayne’s return home, his great uncle, Jim Coughlin, thanked the public for their generosity. He concluded: 'Although Shayne is no longer able to see with his eyes, he has reminded us that real sight comes from the heart.'

article_content: Wayne Rooney believes Manchester United still have a chance to catch up to Premier League leaders Chelsea and Manchester City. On Boxing Day, Rooney delivered a man-of-the-match performance in central midfield, scoring twice and providing an assist as United defeated Newcastle 3-1 at Old Trafford. The United captain acknowledged the challenges ahead: 'We’ve chased down leads before—but we’ve also lost them. There are still many points to play for, and anything can happen over the next couple of weeks.' Former teammate and midfield legend Paul Scholes praised Rooney’s adaptability, stating on TV that he has the qualities to thrive in the center of the park. Manager Louis van Gaal expressed satisfaction with Rooney’s new role, highlighting his endurance and goal threat: 'He has the lung capacity to play there—and he scores goals. I told him to be more attacking, and he responded perfectly.' Van Gaal also criticized the Premier League’s fixture congestion, noting that playing again just 48 hours after a match violates UEFA and FIFA guidelines, yet remains permitted in England. United will miss Marouane Fellaini and Adnan Januzaj for the upcoming match against Tottenham due to illness, and winger Angel di Maria’s participation is uncertain after sustaining a pelvic injury during Christmas Eve training. 'It’s not severe,' van Gaal said, 'but we don’t take risks with injuries like this—they affect how the pelvis connects to the leg.' Newcastle had a chance for an early penalty but were undone by Rooney’s two first-half goals and a Robin van Persie header early in the second half. Substitute Papa Cisse scored a late consolation from the spot. Chelsea extended their lead at the top with a 2-0 win over West Ham, while Manchester City kept pace with a 3-1 victory at West Brom.

article_content: Airline industry insiders warn that terrorist groups may be conducting covert 'dry runs' to test in-flight security systems, potentially paving the way for another 9/11-style attack. The US Airlines Pilots Association recently circulated an internal memo describing several recent incidents across the industry that appear to be rehearsals for coordinated threats onboard aircraft. One such incident occurred on US Airways Flight 1880 on September 2, 2013, flying from Washington, D.C., to Orlando. A passenger identified as Middle Eastern suddenly rose from his seat and moved toward the cockpit before abruptly entering the lavatory, where he remained for an extended period. Meanwhile, three companions created a disturbance, possibly to distract crew members. Industry leaders, including Wolf Koch, Chairman of the Air Line Pilots Association International, express deep concern. '100%, no question in my mind — they're going to try it again,' Koch told WTSP. He emphasized that dry runs typically precede actual attacks. A similar pattern was reported on a flight in August 2001, shortly before the 9/11 attacks. Actor James Woods recalled a commotion on board, which later investigations suggested may have involved Mohamed Atta and other individuals linked to the 9/11 plot — though this link remains unconfirmed by official sources. While US Airways and the TSA confirmed the 2013 incident, the TSA concluded it did not warrant further investigation. An anonymous Air Marshal strongly disagreed, stating, 'They're liars. It’s not a question of if, it’s a question of when.' Experts urge heightened vigilance, cautioning that dismissing unusual behavior could carry serious risks — while also stressing the need for evidence-based responses over speculation.

article_content: In a sharp rebuke, the U.S. State Department labeled Nicaragua’s official exit from the Organization of American States as a further retreat from democratic norms. The OAS, which has repeatedly condemned human rights abuses under President Daniel Ortega and Vice President Rosario Murillo, said it will keep a close watch on Nicaragua even after its departure. Ortega’s government initiated the two-year withdrawal process back in November 2021, following international outcry over disputed elections that extended his rule. U.S. spokesperson Matthew Miller posted on X that the move deepens Nicaragua’s isolation on the global stage. Neither Ortega’s team nor his administration responded to the statement. Meanwhile, former Nicaraguan diplomat Arturo McFields, who resigned in 2022 after publicly denouncing the government, called the withdrawal a serious setback for democracy—but welcomed the OAS’s pledge to keep pushing for human rights inside the country. Since violent crackdowns on nationwide protests in 2018 left around 355 dead and hundreds jailed, the Ortega-Murillo government has targeted independent universities, the Catholic Church, NGOs, and tens of thousands of citizens, forcing many into exile. The OAS, which Nicaragua joined in 1950, passed a resolution earlier this year affirming its commitment to monitor the nation’s human rights landscape. Nicaragua becomes only the second country in modern history to leave the organization, after Venezuela did so in 2019.

article_content: A U.S. Air Force CV-22 Osprey crashed Wednesday during a routine training mission north of Navarre, Florida, injuring five crew members, according to a military official. The incident occurred at approximately 6:45 p.m. at the Eglin Range, part of Hurlburt Field, said Amy Nicholson, chief of public affairs at the airfield. The five injured personnel were transported to a nearby hospital; the severity of their injuries remains unknown. The cause of the crash is currently under investigation. The aircraft was assigned to the 1st Special Operations Wing. The CV-22 Osprey is a tilt-rotor aircraft capable of functioning both as a fixed-wing plane and a vertical-takeoff-and-landing helicopter. Development of the Osprey began in 1982 by the U.S. Army. The program nearly ended in 1989 when then-Secretary of Defense Dick Cheney proposed canceling it due to rising costs. Safety concerns escalated after two fatal crashes: one in 1992 at a U.S. Marine Corps base in Virginia, and later in 2000, two more crashes — one in Arizona killing four crew members and 15 passengers, and another in North Carolina claiming the lives of the crew. In response, the U.S. Marine Corps grounded the entire Osprey fleet until a major redesign was completed and flights resumed in 2002. The U.S. Air Force began testing the Osprey in 2006 and officially adopted it in 2008. The U.S. Marine Corps first deployed the aircraft operationally in Iraq in 2007, after 18 years and $20 billion in development. CNN’s Mike Mount contributed to this report.

E incidente a ocurrí aproximadamente ku 6:45 p.m. na e Eglin Range, parti di Hurlburt Field, dijí Amy Nicholson, jefe di asuntos públiko di e aeródromo. E 5 personal herí a ser transportá pa un hospitaal riba e zonan; e gravedad di e heriduran a keda konosí. E kausa di e akidente a ta bini investigá. article_content: Foreign Secretary William Hague announced that the UK will push for a 'red card' system in EU renegotiations, allowing a bloc of fewer than 10 member states to veto unwanted EU legislation. While rejecting calls for the UK to have unilateral veto power over all EU laws — which he argued would undermine the single market — Hague emphasized the need for stronger roles for national parliaments. Prime Minister David Cameron faces mounting pressure from over 95 Conservative backbenchers, who signed a letter demanding the right to block or repeal EU laws that threaten Britain’s national interests. The number of rebels exceeds the 81 MPs who opposed the government on Europe in 2011 and includes nearly two-thirds of the 158 backbenchers not appointed to government positions. Under current EU rules, if one-third of member states object to proposed legislation, they may issue a 'yellow card' requesting a review. Hague seeks to strengthen this into a 'red card' system, enabling a smaller coalition to block laws outright. Hague stressed that allowing each nation to opt out unilaterally would be incompatible with any system based on shared rules, including the single market or even arrangements like those of Switzerland or Norway. Bernard Jenkin, who coordinated the letter, criticized 'europhile' arguments that focus on job losses, calling them exaggerated and dismissive of democratic accountability. Jacob Rees-Mogg, another signatory, stated that preserving free trade is more important than maintaining the single market, and that laws should be made by elected UK representatives, not EU bureaucrats. The debate is expected to intensify as Chancellor George Osborne prepares to defend a reformed EU membership. Meanwhile, Conservative MEPs continue to condemn the £130 million annual cost of moving the European Parliament between Brussels and Strasbourg, despite a 2013 vote by MEPs to abolish the practice — blocked by France.

Mientras ta rechazá pidi pa el Reino Uní tin poder unilatéral pa veto tota leyes di UE — ku el ta argumintá ku ta subvertí el merkadu úniko — Hague ta enfatizá la nécesidat di un rol más fuerte pa parlamentonan nasional. Kantidat di rebeldanán ta supérsa los 81 diputáu ku ta votá konta gobièrnu na 2011 i ta inklui casi dos terçianan di 158 diputáu ku no ta nombra pa puesto di gobièrnu. article_content: Hours from death due to a massive brain tumour, 12-year-old Emma Bassett went on a rollercoaster ride — and it may have saved her life. At the time, she had no idea how serious her headaches and dizziness were. Just days before a scheduled hospital appointment, she visited Thorpe Park with her mother and friends, riding the Nemesis Inferno. When doctors finally examined her, they discovered a tumour the size of a satsuma, blocking the flow of cerebrospinal fluid in her brain — a condition that had likely been developing since she was five or six. The intense forces of the rollercoaster temporarily redistributed the fluid, relieving dangerous pressure and giving her precious extra hours to undergo surgery. Doctors warned her parents the operation could leave her in a vegetative state. Yet, eight years later, Emma has defied all expectations. She relearned how to walk, talk, and eat. Today, she is preparing to begin a career as a primary school teacher. Her recovery has been long and grueling: years of physiotherapy, hydrotherapy, and speech therapy; a year in a leg splint; two years using crutches; custom shoe soles for support. Now, the only lasting sign of her illness is mild facial paralysis on her left side. At her latest scan, there is no trace of the tumour’s return. Emma, now 20 and from Twickenham, West London, says: 'I never imagined I’d recover this much. The doctors didn’t expect me to get this far.' She now partners with the Samantha Dickson Brain Tumour Trust to promote the HeadSmart campaign, raising awareness about early warning signs of paediatric brain tumours.

Un par di dia antes di e konsulta na e hospital, e a bini na Thorpe Park ku su mamá i amigu, i a bini na Nemesis Inferno. Kuando e doktór a bini a examiná e, e a diskubrí un tumor di tamaño di un satsuma, blokeando e fluí di líwidu serospinal na e kerebru — kondishon ke ta probabelmente a bini desarrolla nan nan 5 o 6 aña. E doktór a advertí su papá ku e operashon a pòdá lè e na un estado vegetativo. Pero ochi aña despues, Emma a desafia to e ekspektativas. E a re-aprendé pa bini, hablá, i mangi. Hodi, e ta preparándose pa komensá su karerá komo maestrá di skol primario. E rehasilidatá ta largu i dífisil: aña di fisioterapia, hidroterapia, i terapia di habla; un aña ku e pierna na un yeso; dos aña bini ku krutsh; plantillas spesial pa su zapatos.
