article_content: David Moyes earned his first point as Real Sociedad manager in a hard-fought 0-0 draw against Deportivo La Coruña at the Riazor Stadium. His arrival sparked immediate drama — Deportivo assistant coach Roberto Cabellud was sent off after a heated exchange with Moyes in the 29th minute of the first half. The incident followed Cabellud’s dismissal by referee Eduardo Prieto Iglesias, triggered by an argument with the fourth official. As Cabellud walked past the Real Sociedad bench, Moyes gestured calmly for him to settle down, prompting Cabellud to approach the Englishman before being escorted off the field. Despite limited time to prepare and key absences — including injured midfielders Xabi Prieto and David Zurutuza, plus central defender Íñigo Martínez — Moyes oversaw a noticeably improved performance from his squad. Real Sociedad created several clear chances: Sergio Canales had a shot saved on the face by Fabricio, Carlos Vela fired just wide, and Esteban Granero missed from close range. Deportivo threatened too, but goalkeeper Zubikarai made a series of vital stops, including a spectacular late save from José Rodríguez. The result mirrored the opening-game draws of former Real Sociedad managers Harry Lowe (1930–31) and John Toshack (1985–86), and was a marked improvement over Chris Coleman’s 2-0 defeat in 2007. While not a win, the performance gave Moyes reason for optimism as he prepares for his first home match against Elche next weekend.

article_content: Eight years after her tragic disappearance, Shafilea Ahmed’s parents have finally been charged with her murder. Shafilea, a bright 17-year-old from Warrington with dreams of becoming a lawyer, vanished in September 2003 after telling friends and counselors she feared being forced into a marriage she didn’t want. Her body was found months later near the River Kent in Cumbria, and a coroner concluded she had been violently killed—likely by smothering or strangulation. Initially, police had no grounds to press charges, and her parents were released. But in 2010, new information emerged from her younger sister, Alisha, who had been arrested for an unrelated armed robbery. Alisha, now in witness protection, reportedly shared details implicating their parents in Shafilea’s death. The siblings’ relationship had long been strained, and Shafilea had confided in others about feeling trapped by cultural expectations. She wrote poems and lyrics describing her pain: 'I feel trapped,' she wrote. 'All they think about is honour.' Her parents, Iftikhar and Farzana Ahmed, appeared in court wearing traditional clothing, silent and composed. They pleaded not guilty, and their defense has consistently claimed Shafilea accidentally drank bleach during a blackout, mistaking it for juice. But investigators now believe the truth lies deeper—rooted in a refusal to let their daughter choose her own future. The case, long dormant, has reignited conversations about honor-based violence in immigrant communities and the urgent need for early intervention when young people cry out for help.

article_content: As Cesc Fabregas readies to depart Barcelona, Arsenal are seriously exploring the chance to bring him back — thanks to a buy-back clause they secured when he left in 2011. The clause, worth £25 million, can only be activated if Fabregas formally requests to leave the Catalan side, a move now looking increasingly likely under new manager Luis Enrique, who considers him surplus to requirements. While Barcelona hope to recover as much as possible of the £35 million they invested in the Spanish midfielder, they’re open to negotiations. Arsenal, still deeply connected to their former captain, see him as a natural fit for a midfield overhaul, especially given his familiarity with Arsène Wenger’s system. Though Manchester City and Chelsea are keeping tabs on his availability — partly because he qualifies as a homegrown player under Premier League rules — Arsenal hold a unique advantage: Fabregas has long been linked with a return to the Emirates, and insiders suggest he’d welcome it. Manchester United, despite past interest, aren’t pursuing him this summer. With transfer windows opening, all eyes are on whether Arsenal can turn nostalgia into reality.

article_content: Few experiences rival the pure bliss of lying on a pristine white-sand beach, surrounded by swaying palm trees under 32°C heat, a gentle breeze brushing your skin, a chilled blended coffee beside you, and the turquoise sea just steps away. This is the quintessential holiday fantasy — two precious weeks away from the daily grind, saved for all year long. But what if you could take that escape even further? Not just by leaving your office behind, but by shedding your clothes entirely? That’s the defining feature of Karisma Resorts’ Hidden Beach Resort in Mexico’s Riviera Maya — a nudist sanctuary nestled right next to its clothing-optional sibling, El Dorado Seaside Suites. Located midway between Tulum and Playa del Carmen on the Quintana Roo coast, the two resorts share a border but offer vastly different atmospheres. El Dorado welcomes guests in swimwear; Hidden Beach welcomes them in nothing at all. At the heart of Hidden Beach lies a stunning infinity pool with a bar at its center — perfect for sipping cocktails while lounging bare-skinned under the sun. Guests from El Dorado are welcome to visit for a daily fee, dipping their toes — or their entire bodies — into the nudist experience. El Dorado Seaside Suites accommodates up to 1,000 guests and boasts multiple world-class restaurants, including an acclaimed Asian eatery serving exquisite sushi. Its expansive grounds feature daily beachside activities and a luxurious spa. Just next door, Hidden Beach Resort offers an intimate retreat with only 42 rooms, one pool, one bar, and one restaurant. Here, nudity is the norm — though not mandatory — and a strict no-swingers policy ensures a serene, connection-focused environment. Both properties operate under a 'Gourmet Inclusive' model — meaning gourmet dining, premium drinks, and curated experiences are included, elevating them far beyond standard all-inclusives. Rooms are spacious, featuring flat-screen TVs, private jacuzzis, and outdoor balconies with king-sized beds. I was invited to Hidden Beach to experience its signature chocolate and UV body painting parties, hosted by international event firm Social Exposure. Learning it was a nudist resort sparked both excitement and hesitation. I’d never been nude in public before — and yet, the idea of shedding not just clothing, but societal expectations, felt strangely compelling. I stayed at El Dorado and visited Hidden Beach for a full day, including both themed events. My morning began with room service: coconut cream oat porridge, vegetable omelette, fresh fruit, and coffee. Later, by the shore at El Dorado, I enjoyed salmon and eggs before walking just ten steps over to Hidden Beach with my friend — both of us still in bikinis and towels. What unfolded was surreal: a quiet, elegant scene of couples lounging, playing volleyball, and chatting effortlessly — all completely nude. Most were decades older than us. After a few minutes, we realized: wearing clothes here felt weirder than not wearing them. We took off our swimsuits. Instantly, the tension dissolved. We joined the volleyball games, laughed with strangers who became friends, and felt a rare sense of belonging. Back at El Dorado, we barely spoke to anyone. At Hidden Beach, we connected deeply — without words. The chocolate body painting party began as art — intricate designs on skin — then exploded into a joyful food fight. Chocolate-dipped fruit, whipped cream, and paintbrushes turned into weapons. The UV party featured black lights, music, a live band, and an artist spraying glowing Japanese flowers on women and wild animals on men. Nudity didn’t just allow creativity — it invited it. Afterward, we showered — and ate far too much cake. Chocolate has deep roots here. Ancient Mesoamericans drank cacao as early as 1900 BC. Painting with it felt strangely ceremonial — a modern ritual echoing tradition. To deepen the experience, I booked a Temazcal ceremony with the resort’s resident shaman. Inside a steamy, cave-like structure, we chanted, sweated, and inhaled herbal vapors believed to cleanse body and spirit. The ritual — likened to returning to the womb — was intense, silent, and profoundly moving. We emerged shaken, calm, and renewed. An hour-long debrief with the young shaman revealed insights we hadn’t expected. On our final day, we visited Chichén Itzá — one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Before the guided tour, we swam in a mystical cenote, its crystal waters lit by shafts of sunlight filtering through limestone ceilings. Then, we wandered the colonial streets of Valladolid, admiring colorful sugar skulls and artisan stalls. Standing beneath El Castillo during sunset, watching the shadow of a serpent glide down the pyramid’s staircase — a phenomenon tied to ancient astronomical knowledge — I felt awe. The contrast between sacred history and sensual freedom was striking. Leaving the Riviera Maya, I felt not just rested, but transformed. Bolder. More present. The nudist resort wasn’t about sex — it was about surrender. Surrender to nature, to community, to vulnerability. And in doing so, I found something unexpected: true peace.

Na Hidden Beach, mi ta konektá profundament — sin palabras. E party di chocolate body painting ta bini komo arte — diseño detayá na piel — pero ta eksplodí na un lucha di comida alegre. Fruta ku chocolate, crema batí, i pincel ta bini arma. E party di UV ta tin luza negra, música, banda en vivu, i un artista ku ta sprai e kolór di flor japones pa muller i animal salvaj pa homber. Nudismo ta nunka solamente permít creatividat — ta ta invita. Después, mi ta dusha — i mi ta koma demasiá torta. Chocolate ta raízes profundo akí. Antiguo Mesoamerikanan ta bebe kakaó hasi 1900 A.C. Dentro di un estruktura humíd i kaverna, mi ta kanta, ta sudá, i ta inhala vapór di hierba ku ta kredí pa limpiá e kuerpo i espíritu. Despues, mi ta paseá na e kales kolonial di Valladolid, admirándo kran di azúkar colorá i artesanía. Stá riba El Castillo durante el sol poniente, mirándo e sombra di un serpiente ku ta bai pa e escalinata di pirámide — un fenomeno ku ta ligá ku konosimentu astronómiko antiguo — mi ta sentí asombro. article_content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above 16,000 for the first time ever on Thursday, November 21, 2013, as stronger-than-expected job data and subdued inflation fueled investor confidence. The index rose 109.17 points, or 0.69%, to close at 16,009.99. Applications for unemployment benefits dropped to their lowest level since September, nearing pre-Great Recession levels — a sign of improving labor market conditions. Although investors remain uncertain about the timing of the Federal Reserve’s planned reduction of its $85 billion monthly bond-buying program, many believe the economy is strong enough to absorb a gradual withdrawal of stimulus. The U.S. central bank has repeatedly stated it will not reduce support until the economy can sustain itself independently. Corporate performance also contributed: General Motors rose after the U.S. Treasury announced plans to sell its remaining 31.3 million shares by year-end. Williams-Sonoma surged 7.6% after reporting a 16% rise in third-quarter net income, driven by higher sales at West Elm and PBteen. Bank stocks, including Bank of America, gained as expectations of stimulus tapering without immediate rate hikes widened the yield spread between long- and short-term debt — boosting profits from traditional lending. Annual inflation stood at 1%, below the Fed’s 2% target. James Bullard, president of the St. Louis Fed and a voting FOMC member, noted that low inflation provides room to maintain current policy. 'We need to continue the program for now,' he said, 'but if inflation begins to rise, we must act.' Anthony Chan, chief economist at Chase Private Client, remarked, 'We’ve been handed a few one-two punches — the government shutdown, the payroll tax increase — but guess what? Like Elton John, the economy is still standing.' The S&P 500 gained 14.48 points (0.81%) to 1,795.85, and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 47.89 points (1.22%) to 3,969.16.

E índice ta subí 109,17 punkt, o 0,69%, pa tuma 16.009,99. Solicitudes pa benefishon di desempleo ta bai a su nivel mas bajo desde septèmber, ku ta aproksimadamente kual ke ta bini antes di Grand Résesión — un señal di mejora na kondishon di merká di empleo. A pesar di ke investidó ta insegur so timpo di redushon planifiká di programa di kompra di bondu di 85 miliard dolar menswal di Reserva Federal, muhó ta kresé ku e ekonomía ta fuerte sufisiente pa absorbsí un retirá gradual di estímulo. E banca sentral di Estados Unidos ta rekordá ku ta no ta retirá su apoyo hasta ku e ekonomía ta pòr sostené sipi. Rendimentu di korpó tambe ta contribuí: General Motors ta subí ku Departamentu di Tesorú di Estados Unidos anunsia ku ta planifika vende su partisipashon restante di 31,3 milión akshon pa fin di aña. Williams-Sonoma ta subí 7,6% ku ta reportá un subida di 16% na rentabilidad di trimesre terçer, ku ta impulsá pa venta mas alti na West Elm i PBteen. Akshon di bank, inkluyendo Bank of America, ta subí ku espetashon di redushon di estímulo sin subí tasa di interés ta ensanchá e diferensia di rendimiento ente deuda a lóng term i kurto term — amentá ganansia di prestá tradishonal. Inflashon anual ta ta 1%, mas bajo ku meta di 2% di Reserva Federal. James Bullard, presidént di Reserva Federal di St. Louis i mièmbro di voto di FOMC, ta nota ku inflashon bajo ta da espasiu pa mantene política actual. 'Nos tin ku kontinuá e programa pa ora, 'ta el di, 'mas si inflashon ta komeça subí, nos tin ku aksioná.' Anthony Chan, ekonomista jefe di Chase Private Client, ta di, 'Nos ta recibi un par di golpes — e cierre di gobièrn, e auménto di impuestu di nómina — mas adivina, komo Elton John, e ekonomía ta aki pa.' E S&P 500 ta subí 14,48 punkt (0,81%) pa 1.795,85, i e Nasdaq Composite ta subí 47,89 punkt (1,22%) pa 3.969,16.

article_content: Kickstarter campaigns have enabled people to fund diverse projects — from video games and smartwatches to the restoration of historic sites. Now, the platform has turned its attention to potato salad. Zack Brown of Columbus, Ohio, launched a Kickstarter campaign with a modest goal of $10: his dream was to make potato salad for the first time. As of Monday morning, more than 1,545 backers had pledged over $11,000 for the chance to taste his creation. 'I’m a somewhat risk-averse person,' Brown told CNN. 'I love potato salad, but I’d never made it before and wasn’t sure I could do it well. Kickstarter helps people realize their dreams — so it felt like the perfect fit.' Kickstarter is an online platform where supporters pledge money to fund creative projects in exchange for rewards. Often, creators share the final product with backers and offer additional perks as funding milestones are reached. Brown quickly surpassed his stretch goals, prompting him to expand his plan: he’ll use mayonnaise from the natural foods section of his local grocery store, consult with a professional chef, and host a potato salad party in Columbus. He was overwhelmed by the generosity of backers — many from outside the U.S., including the UK, France, and Romania. To honor them, he’s working with a designer to create a recipe book featuring one potato salad recipe inspired by each backer’s country. One reward tier offered a small portion of the finished salad for pledges of $3 or more. With such high demand, Brown admits logistical challenges lie ahead — but remains undeterred. 'I could come to you. You could come to me,' he wrote on his Kickstarter page. 'Or maybe we could partner with a restaurant chain to offer free samples as a promotion.' Brown plans to record the entire cooking process and say the name of every backer aloud during preparation. If the number of contributors keeps growing, he jokes, he might lose his voice by the end. He won’t reveal exact recipes yet — except that they’ll include potatoes from his local store, vinegar in at least one variation, and a vegan option. The cooking will begin after his Kickstarter campaign closes in August.

article_content: In a fiercely contested South American World Cup qualifier, Argentina and Colombia played out a 0-0 draw at Buenos Aires’ Monumental Stadium — a match marked by tension, controversy, and standout goalkeeping. The game turned fiery in the first half when Argentina’s Gonzalo Higuain and Colombia’s Cristian Zapata clashed, leading to both players being sent off by Venezuelan referee Marlon Escalante after Zapata responded to a prior foul. The drama didn’t stop there. After halftime, Escalante disallowed two clear-looking goals by Argentina’s Sergio Aguero for offside, sparking outrage from the home bench. Despite the chaos, Argentina began strongly, forcing Colombia’s keeper David Ospina into a string of brilliant stops. 'Ospina was excellent for us today,' said Colombia manager José Pekerman. Meanwhile, Colombia’s Radamel Falcao squandered a golden opportunity to put his side ahead. Lionel Messi entered the field in the second half, still managing a hamstring issue, but couldn’t unlock the Colombian defense. Although the result was a stalemate, Argentina maintained a five-point lead atop the CONMEBOL table. Colombia moved into second after Ecuador’s 1-0 loss to Peru, where veteran Claudio Pizarro netted the decisive goal. In another key qualifier, Chile edged Paraguay 2-1, crushing the home side’s World Cup dreams and securing fourth place in the group. The fifth-placed team will now face an intercontinental playoff. Across the border in CONCACAF, the United States secured a crucial 2-1 victory in Jamaica. Brad Evans netted the winner after Jermaine Beckford equalized Jozy Altidore’s opener. The win leaves the US level on points with Costa Rica and Mexico, while Panama sits just one point back after holding Mexico to a draw. Costa Rica also kept pace with a narrow 1-0 win over Honduras, keeping their qualification hopes alive.

article_content: In the northern Libyan city of Benghazi, at least 20 people lost their lives and hundreds more were wounded on Friday as massive street protests intensified against longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi. Witnesses described scenes of chaos and courage, with thousands gathering in public squares, chanting demands for Gaddafi and his family to leave the country. Medical staff at Al-Jala Hospital reported that most injuries were caused by gunfire to the head, chest, and neck — a pattern confirmed by international observers. Since protests began on Tuesday, the death toll has climbed to at least 50, according to local sources. Amnesty International cited similar figures, stating that security forces appeared to be operating under orders to use deadly force against peaceful demonstrators. Meanwhile, in nearby towns like al-Baida and Derna, crowds gathered to bury those killed in earlier clashes. Protesters reportedly set fire to police stations and offices linked to Gaddafi’s Revolutionary Committee. Despite the unrest, government forces remained largely absent from the streets of Benghazi, with only three stationary tanks observed — some even engaged in conversation with curious youths. In contrast, state television aired carefully curated footage of loyalist rallies in Tripoli, showing cheering crowds, waving flags, and fireworks celebrating Gaddafi. As communication networks were disrupted and mobile texts warned citizens that protesting violated 'religion and tradition,' families lived in fear. The U.S. president, Barack Obama, joined global leaders in condemning the crackdown, urging Libyan authorities to respect basic rights to assembly and expression. Human Rights Watch and the United Nations echoed this call, labeling the violence as unlawful and disproportionate. Amid the turmoil, protesters claimed to have freed detainees and dismantled symbols of state oppression. Yet, with no independent journalists allowed inside Libya, much of what the world knows comes from activists, diaspora groups, and anonymous sources on the ground.

Pero, ku nengun periodista independiente a permití dentu di Libia, mas ku e mundu ta sabe ta bini pa ativistan, gruponan di diáspora, i fontenan anonimo na terreno.

article_content: A senior British peer and lawyer has warned that plans to regulate the country’s 300-year-old free press may violate the law. Lord Lester, an eminent Queen’s Counsel and the architect behind landmark reforms to Britain’s controversial libel laws, argued that imposing exemplary damages on newspapers refusing to join a new press regulator would breach Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights—protecting freedom of expression. The Liberal Democrat peer emphasized that the British press is already governed by extensive criminal and civil laws, making further state intervention unnecessary. He criticized the 'Hacked Off' campaign led by celebrities, urging instead for an independent self-regulatory system that promotes professional standards and offers effective remedies without encouraging costly litigation. Meanwhile, London Mayor Boris Johnson has called on newspapers to boycott the government’s proposed Royal Charter on press regulation, labeling it a 'monstrous folly.' He traced the origins of the Leveson Inquiry into media ethics to a series of political scandals, including the MPs’ expenses controversy. Last week, the UK’s three main political parties finalized the details of the Royal Charter, establishing a state-backed regulatory framework following the Leveson Inquiry. However, an alternative proposal from the press—calling for an independent regulator with investigative powers, authority to impose fines up to £1 million, mandatory corrections of inaccuracies, and full independence from both industry and politics—was ultimately rejected.

article_content: Sydney (CNN) — Impossible to explain, harder to believe. This week, a young man in the prime of his life went to work. He was the envy of many — he loved what he did and was living a dream he’d held since childhood on a farm. He did not come home. No wall fell on him. No tractor overturned. Headlines have already told us that Australian cricketer Phillip Hughes died as a result of a freak accident: struck on the head by a ball delivered at approximately 140 kilometers per hour. In this age of the relentless news cycle, story angles have been sharpened and pointed. Questions must be asked. One in particular: Could this accident have been avoided? The simple answer is 'yes' — but then come the 'if onlys.' Not just one, but a chorus of them. If only his head had been at a different angle. If only his helmet offered greater protection. If only bouncers were banned. If only... These words are never more tormenting than in times of tragedy. Somewhere, hidden behind the obvious, lies a deeper, more provocative question: What if we — fans, administrators, the media, and players — actively encouraged danger in sport? We do. A fast bowler targeting a batsman’s throat. A quarterback blindsided into the turf. Race cars bumper-to-bumper at 150 miles per hour. Unscripted theater. Why do we watch? Because these moments are exhilarating. For fans, it’s the most captivating live drama. For administrators, it’s revenue through the turnstiles. For the media, it’s ratings and accolades. And for the elite athlete? They may not always enjoy it, but the thrill of dancing on the edge between invincibility and vulnerability is one of the most seductive challenges in risk-laden sports. Phillip Hughes knew this. He felt it. Seeing him kick up his heels and punch the air after scoring a century wasn’t the act of someone who had an easy path — it was the triumph of resilience. When cricket administrators analyze frame by frame his final moments, they’ll see a picture far more complex than a single instant of disaster. Nowhere has this become clearer than in the United States, where the NFL is paying hundreds of millions in legal settlements over concussion-related brain injuries. Former players accuse league officials of concealing known dangers while pressuring athletes to return to play — because that’s what fans wanted, and it made for better highlight reels. And that kept the money flowing. Other contact sports worldwide are taking notice. The days of smelling salts are over. Athletes are commodities — mobile billboards with marketing clauses embedded in their contracts. They must obey their employers, or face dismissal: 'Thanks for your efforts. Good luck in the future.' The pressure is immense. Phillip Hughes knew that. He was on the brink of a recall to the Australian Test team — the highest honor in his sport, his livelihood. Now, he will never get that chance. It’s up to all of us — fans, institutions, and athletes — to decide what this truly means.
translated_content: Sydney (CNN) — Difisil pa ekspliká, mas difisil pa kré. Semana pasá, un mucha den su pico di vida ta bini pa trabá. É ta envidiá pa muchi — é ama lo ke é ta fás, i é ta bivi un sueño ku é ta tení desde kada dia ku é ta un mucha na un granja. É no ta bini pa kasa. Nengun pared ta kai pa é. Nengun traktor ta kai. Kabeza di notisia ta yega pa nos ku kricketista Australiano Phillip Hughes murió komo rezultá di un akidente stranho: bati na kabeza pa un bola ku ta tirá pa aproksimadamente 140 kilómetro pa ora. Den e tempo di e ciclo di notisia kontinuo, angulo di notisia ta mas afilá i punjá. Pregunta ta nesesario pa fá. Una den e mas importante: Kier akidente ta pode evitá? Respuesta simplé ta 'si' — pero aki ta vení e 'si só si.' No solamente un, mas un kantidat di e. Si só si kabeza di Phillip ta bini na ángulo diferente. Si só si e casco di é ta ofresí proteksion mas grandi. Si só si bouncers ta prohibí. Si só si... E palabra no ta mas tormentoso ku den tempu di tragedia. Dinsi di e obvio, ta esconde un pensamentu mas profundo, mas provokativo: Si só si nos — fanátiko, administrador, medía i speldadó — ta animá peligro na deporte? Nos ta fás. Un boulér rápido ta tirá pelota na gorja di un bateador. Un quarterback ta bati na teren. Kares di korsa ta konsa pa 150 milla pa ora. Teatro sin guión. Porke nos ta mirá? Porke e momento aki ta ekscitante. Pa fanátiko, e mas apasionante teatro sin guión. Pa administrador, e dolaran pa e puerta di entrada. Pa medía, e aplauso ku ta bini ku e rating ta salí. I pa atleta elito? Bini, é no ta siempre gusta kadá momentu di e, mas oportunidat pa negosia e lima frágil ente invensibilidad i fragilidat ta un di e mas atractibo desafio na deporte ku ta asosiá ku risiko. Phillip Hughes ta sabor e. É ta sientí e tambe. Mirá é ta bai pa kaba i ta puñá e aire ku é ta celebrá un sénteri no ta un signo di un kampion ku ta tení un lucha fácil — ta un triunfo di resiliensia. Ku administrador di kricket ta analizá frame pa frame e ultimò momentu di Phillip, é ta bini pa un imajen mas komplejo ku un instante di desastre. Nan ta mas klaro den Estados Unidos, ku NFL ta pagá hundrida di millonan pa litigio por lesiones di kerebro relacioná ku konkusion. Ex-jugador ta acusá ofisial di konsebi peligro konosí mientras ta presioná atleta pa bini pa bini pa joga — porke e fanátiko ta wènta, i e ta fás e video di destacá mas bon. I e ta manteni e dolaran fluyí. Otro deporte ku ta kontakto ta mirá pa nan. E dia di sal amoníako ta pasa. Atleta ta komodidat — tablón di anunsio móbil ku kláusula di merkandisí embedá den kontratonan. É ta nesesario pa obeze e boss, o ta kousa: 'Grasias pa e esforsu. Buena sort na e futuro.' Presion ku ta bini ta enorm. Phillip Hughes ta sabor e tambe. É ta na borde di un rekualifikashon pa e seleksion Australiano Test — e honór mas altu di e deporte, e travayu di é. Ahora, é no ta jamás ta bini pa e oportunidat. E ta upa pa nos totál — fanátiko, institushon, i atleta — pa determiná kua e real signifiká.
post_content: RIP Phillip Hughes. A brilliant life cut short by a freak accident — but was it really just bad luck? 🤔 Crickets, football, racing… we cheer danger because it’s thrilling. But are we turning athletes into expendable commodities? #CricketSafety #EndDangerInSport #PhillipHughes

article_content: Lindsay Lohan’s legal troubles continue, but her attorney says the latest charge — a misdemeanor assault tied to a late-night altercation at a Manhattan nightclub — isn’t ready for court. Mark Heller, her lawyer, stated after a recent hearing that no plea was necessary because the case lacks sufficient grounds to move forward. He emphasized that Lohan never struck anyone, insisting she merely asked for privacy during the encounter at the Avenue Lounge on November 29, 2012. Heller went further, suggesting the alleged victim, Tiffany Mitchell, was seeking attention rather than justice. While prosecutors still have weeks to decide whether to drop the case entirely, Heller remains confident Lohan will be cleared. This incident adds to a long list of legal issues for the actress, who has been through nearly two dozen court hearings and five rehab programs since 2007 due to struggles with addiction. Separately, Lohan is preparing for a probation violation hearing in California on January 15. That case stems from a 2012 car crash while she was en route to film ‘Liz & Dick,’ where authorities allege she lied to officers, resisted arrest, and drove recklessly — all misdemeanor offenses. Despite the ongoing challenges, Lohan remains under public scrutiny, her life often portrayed more as tabloid drama than a personal journey toward stability.

article_content: Almost 300 people were arrested in Paris as thousands protested against same-sex marriage, just days before France’s first legal gay wedding. The arrests followed a large demonstration in the city center on Sunday night, with an estimated 150,000 participants. Protesters threw rocks, smoke bombs, and flares at police, who responded with tear gas and baton charges. At least two journalists were seriously injured during the clashes. Violence escalated around prominent landmarks such as Les Invalides and the Eiffel Tower, primarily involving CRS riot police and hooded far-right demonstrators, some affiliated with the GUD (Groupe Union Défense). France’s same-sex marriage law, which also permits adoption, was passed by the French Parliament on May 18, making France the 14th country in the world to legalize same-sex unions. 'Traditional France has been threatened by these new measures, and that’s why we’ve taken to the streets,' said Jerome Martin, a 23-year-old protester. 'The violence reflects our frustration at being betrayed by liberal politicians.' The protests, strongly supported by the Roman Catholic Church, have become a platform for the French right to oppose the Socialist government led by President François Hollande. Interior Minister Manuel Valls confirmed that about 100 of those arrested were known far-right activists. Around 4,500 police officers were deployed to manage the crowd. Despite the unrest, a public survey released Sunday showed 53% of French citizens support same-sex marriage and adoption. France’s first legal same-sex wedding is scheduled for Wednesday in Montpellier. Tensions heightened after Dominique Venner, a far-right writer linked to nationalist circles, committed suicide inside Notre Dame Cathedral on May 21, leaving a note condemning same-sex marriage and calling for 'spectacular' acts to defend French identity. President Hollande’s administration condemned the violence, emphasizing that the law had been duly passed and validated by the Constitutional Council. The conservative UMP party was divided: some leaders, including party president Jean-François Cope, joined the march and invited youth to join their ranks, while others, like former Prime Ministers François Fillon and Alain Juppé, stayed away, arguing that change should come through parliamentary action, not street protests. The demonstrations have grown into a broader movement of resistance against Hollande’s government, which faces criticism over economic stagnation and unemployment above 10%.

article_content: MELBOURNE, Australia — Lawyers for Di Sanh Duong, the first person charged under Australia’s foreign interference laws, argued in court Friday that a donation to the Royal Melbourne Hospital, delivered via a federal minister, was never intended as a covert attempt to influence politics on behalf of the Chinese Communist Party. The 68-year-old Melbourne businessman and community leader, who arrived in Australia as a Vietnamese refugee in 1980, has pleaded not guilty to charges of preparing for foreign interference — a crime punishable by up to 10 years in prison. His case marks the first prosecution under legislation passed in 2018 designed to combat covert foreign influence and industrial espionage. The controversy centers on a novelty check for AUD 37,450 (approximately USD 25,800 at the time) presented by Duong to then-Cabinet minister Alan Tudge at a public event in June 2020. The funds were raised from Melbourne’s local Chinese-Australian community to support the hospital’s pandemic response. Defense attorney Peter Chadwick told jurors that Duong, widely known as 'Sunny,' categorically denied any attempt to sway Tudge. Chadwick emphasized that Duong, president of the Oceania Federation of Chinese Organizations, acted out of concern for his community’s reputation during a time when anti-Chinese sentiment surged due to the pandemic. Chadwick also rejected claims that Duong was recruited by or colluded with the Chinese Communist Party. He noted that while Duong once ran as a candidate for the conservative Liberal Party in 1996 and remained politically engaged, his policy proposals — including a proposed high-speed rail link between Melbourne and Brisbane — were dismissed by party officials as unrealistic. Prosecutors, however, allege Duong believed Tudge would become Australia’s next prime minister and sought to build goodwill accordingly. They argue this represents a broader pattern of subtle foreign influence, not espionage. 'This isn’t about James Bond,' said prosecutor Patrick Doyle. 'It’s about influence — quiet, persistent, and strategic.' The trial, which continues next week, has drawn international attention as it underscores deepening strains in Australia-China relations since the law’s enactment.

E kaso, ku ta kontinuá na pròksima seman, ta atrai atensión internashonal por e ta subrayá e tensiónnan ta aumentá na relashonan Australia-Kina depués di implementashon di leyes.

article_content: In Santiago, Chile, Sebastián Piñera was officially sworn in as president on Thursday, assuming leadership during the recovery from a catastrophic 8.8-magnitude earthquake that killed more than 500 people and impacted nearly 2 million. Despite the devastation, Chile’s economy remains strong and its democratic foundations solid. Piñera, a 60-year-old billionaire, economist, and former senator educated at Harvard, succeeds Michelle Bachelet — a widely admired leader who steered the country through the global recession and advanced progressive social policies. He is the first conservative president since the end of General Augusto Pinochet’s military rule in 1990. Though Bachelet defeated him in the 2005 election and supported his opponent in January’s runoff, Piñera emphasized unity, saying, 'This isn’t the time for conflict between government and opposition — we must act as one nation.' Hours before the ceremony in Valparaíso, a 7.2-magnitude aftershock rattled the region as dignitaries entered the congressional hall. Bachelet, barred by constitutional term limits from running again immediately, bid farewell with emotion, declaring, 'I leave sad because of our people’s pain, but with my head held high — proud of what we’ve built as a nation, proud of the country we are.'

Malgre la destrushon, ekonomia di Chilé ta mantene sólido i fundashon demokrátiko su. Piñera, un bilionario di 60 aña, ekonomista, i eks-senador formá na Harvard, ta suksesór di Michelle Bachelet — un lideresa mui apresia ku ta guia el país atraves di la krisis ekonomiko global i promove politikas sosial progresivo. article_content: Silvio Berlusconi, the former Italian Prime Minister, has been ordered to perform at least one day of community service per week at an elderly care home as part of his one-year sentence for tax fraud. The 77-year-old has also had his passport confiscated and is banned from leaving the Lombardy region, where his primary residence is located. This restriction prevents him from visiting his properties in the Alps and the Caribbean and may hinder his ability to campaign for his Forza Italia party ahead of the upcoming European Parliament elections. Last month, an earlier request to travel to the Netherlands for a meeting of anti-EU parties was denied. This is the latest in a series of setbacks for Berlusconi, who was expelled from Parliament last year after Italy’s highest court upheld his original four-year prison sentence for tax fraud. However, under a recent amnesty law, his sentence was reduced to one year, allowing him to serve it through house arrest or community service instead of incarceration. Berlusconi is also appealing separate convictions related to having sexual relations with a 17-year-old prostitute, known as 'Ruby the Heartstealer,' abuse of office, and leaking a confidential police wiretap. Despite being barred from holding or running for public office, he continues to lead Forza Italia and remains a dominant figure in Italian politics.

E 77-añoso ta tene su pasapòrti konfiská i ta prohibí pa sali for di Lombardia, ku e rezidensia prinzipal ta loká. E restrishon ta previni e pa bisi propieda na Alpes i Karibe i ta pudi prense su kampanha pa e partidu Forza Italia pa e elekshon di Parlamento Europeo ku ta yega. Mes pas, e petishon pa sali pa Holanda pa un reunión di partidonan anti-UE ta negá. E ta e últim di una serie di contratiempunan pa Berlusconi, ku ta ekskluí di Parlamentu aña pasá despues ku e kòrti más alt di Italia ta uphold su sentensia original di katorse aña pa frega tributario. Malgras e ta prohibí pa hóldi o kandidatí pa ofisio públiko, el ta sigui lidera Forza Italia i ta sigui un figura dominante na politika italiana.

article_content: Nearly 54 years after vanishing during a routine training flight over the Pacific, the wreckage of a U.S. Air Force T-33A jet has been located on the seabed of Santa Monica Bay, just off the coast of Los Angeles. The discovery came as a surprise — searchers were originally hunting for a different plane, a P-51D Mustang piloted by World War II Women Airforce Service Pilot Gertrude Silver, which disappeared in 1944 and remains the only missing WASP aircraft. The breakthrough began when Gary Fabian, a Texas-based computer enthusiast and founder of the volunteer group UB88.org, noticed unusual shapes in high-resolution satellite imagery of the bay. He passed the coordinates to Ray Arntz, a Southern California dive operator and fellow UB88.org member. Arntz descended with his team and spotted a scattered debris field rich in aluminum, followed by unmistakable landing gear. Further inspection revealed a manufacturer’s stamp on a 50-caliber machine gun part — a telltale clue pointing to a T-33 Shooting Star. The jet’s engine type ruled out the Mustang, confirming it was something else entirely. Cross-referencing military records, the team matched the location and date to the 1955 disappearance of a T-33 carrying two pilots: Lt. Richard Martin Theiler and Lt. Paul Dale Smith. After months of quiet verification, the team contacted surviving relatives before going public. The group, which includes veteran aircraft archaeologist Pat Macha, has spent years locating forgotten warplane wrecks across California, often at their own expense. Their mission? Not fame or fortune, but closure — for families and history alike. 'We do this because someone needs to,' Arntz said. 'And because we care.'

E descubrimientu ta salí pa sorpresa — e búsikadornan ta buskando originalmenti pa un otro avion, e P-51D Mustang pilotá pa Gertrude Silver, un pilot di e Women Airforce Service durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial, ku ta desaparecí na 1944 i ta e úniko WASP ku e restonan aínda no ta bini enkontá. E kruksa ta komensá ku Gary Fabian, un entusiasta di komputa di Texas i fundador di e grupu voluntero UB88.org, ku ta notá formashonan rara na imajen di satélite di alta resolushon di e bahía. É ta mandá e koordinadanan pa Ray Arntz, un operadór di buká di Sur California i miembru di UB88.org. Arntz ta bini bai ku e ekipa i ta bini notá un kampos di restonan sparsá, ku muhò aluminio, seguido pa e tren di aterisaje indubitable. Inspeksión mas adelanti ta revelá un sello di fabricante na un part di un ametralladora di .50 — un klé ku ta apuntá pa e T-33 Shooting Star. E motor di e jet ta eksklui e Mustang, confirmándo ku é ta otro kosa totalmenti. Kruza referensia ku dokumentonan milita, e ekipa ta konfirmá e lokashon i data ku e desaparishon di e T-33 na 1955 ku dos pilotonan: Tenienti Richard Martin Theiler i Tenienti Paul Dale Smith. Despues di mese di verifikashon silensioso, e ekipa ta kontaktá família supervivienti antis ku é ta publiká. E grupu, ku ta inkluí e arkeólogu di avionan Pat Macha, ta pasá aña buskando restonan di avionan di guèrra olvidá na California, a menudo pa su propio kosto. E misión? No fama i dinero, mas bien kierre — pa famílianan i historia. 'Nos ta fás e kosa pa alguien ta nesesitá,' Arntz ta di. 'Y pa nos ta kere.'

article_content: This mesmerizing image reveals the inner workings of a single human cell, broken down into its smallest molecular components. What appears like abstract art is actually a detailed map of cellular machinery — tiny structures working in unison to keep the cell alive. Using a groundbreaking technique called Exchange-PAINT, researchers in Boston have captured ultra-sharp images of four key cellular elements simultaneously: microtubules (green), mitochondria (purple), Golgi apparatus (red), and peroxisomes (yellow). Each plays a vital role in cellular function, much like workers on a bustling construction site. Exchange-PAINT leverages custom-designed DNA strands that bind selectively to specific biomolecules. A fluorescent dye attached to a complementary DNA strand lights up only when the two connect — causing the target molecule to 'blink'. By capturing these blinks over time and layering the images, scientists assign each molecule a distinct color, building a full-color composite view of the cell’s interior. This method achieves resolution below 10 nanometers — smaller than an antibody — far surpassing the 200-nanometer limit of conventional light microscopy. It builds on an earlier technique, DNA-PAINT, developed by Harvard’s Ralf Jungmann, which could only image up to three molecules at once. To validate the technique, researchers created 10 unique DNA origami shapes resembling the digits 0 through 9. Exchange-PAINT successfully resolved each one in a single image, proving its precision. The same method was then applied to fixed human cells, clearly identifying multiple cellular components. Dr. Peng Yin of Harvard Medical School says seeing many components at once is essential to understanding how cells truly function. 'If you can see only a few things at a time, you’re missing the big picture,' he explains. Scientists hope this innovation will revolutionize disease diagnosis and therapy monitoring by allowing clinicians to observe cellular changes with unprecedented clarity. Don Ingber, founding director of the Wyss Institute, predicts these insights will lead to new medical breakthroughs.
translated_content: E imagen mesmorisante ta revela e interno di un sengul selula humana, desmembra na su komponentes molekular mas pikin. Lo ke ta parese como arte abstrak ta realidat un mapa detallá di maquinaria selular — strukturan pikin ku ta trabou pa mantiene e selula vida. Usando un teknik revolusionario denombra Exchange-PAINT, investigadornan di Boston ta kapturá imajenanan ultrapikin di kuartro elemennto selular importante simoltaneamente: mikrotubulanan (verde), mitokondrianan (purpure), aparato di Golgi (rojo), i peroksisoman (amarillo). Ku tabata funshoná esensial pa funshonamentu selular, komo obreronan na un sitio di konstruksion animá. Exchange-PAINT ta usa tiras di ADN personalizá ku ta binda selektivamenta pa biomolekulan especifico. Un tinta fluorescente atashá pa un tira di ADN komplementario ta lumina solo ku e dos ta binda — hende e molekula objektivo ta 'parpeleá'. Pa kapturá e parpeleamentonan na tempu i superponé e imajenanan, e kientífikonan ta asigna cada molekula un kolor distinto, formándo un kompósito kolorí pa e interno di e selula. E tekniko ta logra resolushon mas abajo di 10 nanómetro — mas pikin ku un anticuerpo — superándo e limitá di 200 nanómetro di mikroskopio di lus konvensional. E ta basá na un tekniko anterior, DNA-PAINT, desarroyá pa Ralf Jungmann di Harvard, ku ta pone kapturá maksimo tri molekulan simoltaneamente. Pa validá e tekniko, investigadornan ta krea 10 forma uniko di ADN origami ku ta parese e digitonan 0 pa 9. Exchange-PAINT ta kapturá klaramente kada un na un sengul imajen, probándo su presishon. E mismo tekniko ta aplica pa selulan humana fiksá, identifikándo klaramente múltipli komponente selular. Doktor Peng Yin di Harvard Medical School ta dí ku mira mas komponentenan simoltaneamente ta esensial pa komprende kómo selulan ta verdaderamente funshoná. 'Si bo ta mira solamente uns pouké kòs, bo ta perdé e bista grand,' el ta eksplika. E kientífikonan ta espéra e innovashon ta revolusioná diagnostiko di doença i monitorisá di terapia pa permití klínikonan observá kambio selular ku claridat sin precedente. Don Ingber, direktor fundador di Wyss Institute, ta predí ku e insigtan den e eksperimentonan ta konduzi pa novu avansonan médiko.

article_content: In a festive twist on crime prevention, PCSOs from West Yorkshire’s Kirklees Central Neighbourhood Policing Team have released a playful remake of Disney’s 'Let It Go' — but with a serious message. Instead of Elsa’s icy liberation, the officers sing about staying safe, reporting crimes, and never drinking and driving. The three-minute video features real members of the public helping officers with everyday tasks — like guiding seniors across the street — alongside a heartfelt sign language performance by students from Spring Grove Junior School in Huddersfield. The rewritten lyrics turn the anthem into a community call-to-action: 'Ready to go, ready to go, we’ll keep you safe from crime. Call it in, and we’ll come to you — let the storm rage on. The rain never bothered us anyway.' Another powerful line warns: 'It’s funny how some people think it’s fine to drink and drive,' followed by footage of emergency crews gathered around a damaged vehicle. Inspector Jon Dunkerley said the team wanted to build on the success of their earlier 'Silent Night' video, which drew over 10,000 views online. Choosing 'Let It Go' was easy — its melody is instantly recognizable, and it appeals to every age group. 'We aimed to entertain, amuse, and inform — all at once,' he said. The project was a true community effort: Huddersfield University lent their recording studio and technical expertise, while local schools and residents stepped in to act, sing, and sign. With burglary down 13.5%, robbery and violent crime each dropping 5.6% over the past year, and victim satisfaction holding steady at 88.5%, the officers believe their creative approach is working. As they close the video, they wish everyone a safe and happy Christmas — and remind viewers that safety is a team sport.

article_content: A cyberattack campaign targeting Apple, Facebook, and Twitter — along with dozens of other organizations — has been linked to an Eastern European hacking group, according to new reports. Two anonymous sources familiar with the investigation told Bloomberg that the hackers sought proprietary research and intellectual property to sell on underground markets. Apple confirmed that some employee devices were compromised after visiting a maliciously altered website for iPhone developers. The site exploited a known vulnerability in Oracle’s Java browser plugin. Similarly, Facebook reported that its internal systems were infiltrated through the same method. Neither company found evidence that customer data was accessed. Earlier in January, Twitter disclosed that approximately 250,000 user accounts may have been affected, with names and email addresses potentially exposed. As details emerged, speculation pointed toward Chinese state-sponsored actors. However, the Chinese government has consistently denied involvement. Cybersecurity experts now believe the attacks more likely originated in Eastern Europe. Tom Kellermann, former commissioner of President Obama’s cybersecurity council and head of security at Trend Micro, noted that while China receives significant attention, 'the most advanced cybercriminals are from the Eastern Bloc and Russia.' He warned of a growing 'giant arms bazaar' in Eastern Europe, where cyber-tools are sold to criminal syndicates and even terrorist groups — blurring the line between state and non-state threats. The attacks employed a 'water hole' strategy: hackers compromised frequently visited developer forums — such as iPhone Dev SDK — to plant malware. Victims unknowingly triggered infections upon visiting the site. Once inside, attackers pivoted to target corporate networks. iPhone Dev SDK acknowledged the breach, stating: 'We have no reason to believe user data was compromised, but to be safe, we've reset all user passwords.' Security experts attribute the success of these attacks to persistent flaws in Java. In January, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security issued a public alert about the risks. Apple emphasized that Macs running OS X Lion do not come with Java pre-installed and automatically disable the plugin after 35 days of inactivity.
translated_content: Un kampana di atak kiber ku ta taht Apple, Facebook, i Twitter — junto ku decenas di otro organizashon — ta ligá ku un grupu di hacker di Europa Oriental, segun rapor nu. Dos fountan anonimo ku ta konosé e situashon ta di Bloomberg ku e hacker ta buská informashon propietario i intelectual pa vende na merká subterráneo. Apple ta konsirmá ku dispozitivo di algun empleadu ta komprometí despues di bini na un sitio web modifiká pa desarrolladó di iPhone. E sitio ta eksplotá un vulnerabilidad konosí na plugin di Java di Oracle. Similarmente, Facebook ta reportá ku e sistema interno di e kompanía ta infiltrá pa e mesmu metòd. Ningun kompanía ta enkontá evidensia ku datu di kliente ta akseßá. Antes na januari, Twitter ta disklosá ku aproksimadamente 250.000 kuentan di usuario ta pòtensialmenti afektá, ku nombra i adresan di email ta pòtensialmenti eksponí. Ku detayenan ta salí, spekulashon ta apuntá na atakante di estado Kines. Sinembargo, e gobièrno Kines ta negá kontinuamenti envolvimientu. Eksperonan di sekuridat kiber ahora ta kré ku e atak ta mas probabelmente originá na Europa Oriental. Tom Kellermann, komisario anterior di konsilu di sekuridat kiber di presidente Obama i jefe di sekuridat na Trend Micro, ta notá ku mientras Kina ta resebi atensión signifikanti, 'e hacker mas avanzá ta di Blok Oriental i Rusia.' É ta warna pa un 'bazar di armas grand' ku ta kresé na Europa Oriental, ku herra kiber ta vende na sindikatonan kriminal i hasta gruponan terorista — borra e líniña ente estado i no-estado. E atak ta empleá un estrategia di 'water hole': hacker ta komprometí forum di desarrolladó ku ta mester bini — komo iPhone Dev SDK — pa plantá malware. Vítima ta activá infekshon sin sàbi. Una vei dentro, e hacker ta pivotá pa taht red di kompanía. iPhone Dev SDK ta aknowledge e violashon, diendo: 'No ta tin motivu pa kré ku datu di usuario ta komprometí, pero pa ser seguro, nos ta reseteá todos e kuentan di usuario.' Eksperonan di sekuridat ta atribui e sukés di e atak pa falan persistent na Java. Na januari, e Departamento di Seguridat Interna di Estados Unidos ta emití un alerta publiko pa risiko. Apple ta enfatisá ku Mac ku ta korre OS X Lion no ta trae Java instalá automaticamente i ta deshabilitá automaticamente e plugin despues di 35 dia di inaktividat.

article_content: Sky Sports is currently the frontrunner to secure the UK broadcasting rights for what many are calling the richest fight in boxing history: Floyd Mayweather Jr. versus Manny Pacquiao. The odds on Sky winning the bid mirror those at Las Vegas casinos — roughly 1-3 — the same as Mayweather to win the bout. But with hundreds of millions of dollars at stake and two of the greatest pound-for-pound fighters ever facing off, nothing is guaranteed. The battle for UK rights is heating up. BT Sport, flush with cash and already a major player in Premier League football, is eager to make a bold statement by entering the boxing arena. ITV, returning to top-tier boxing after nearly a decade, sees this as a golden opportunity to reclaim mainstream relevance — especially since it’s not restricted by the BBC’s public service rules against pay-per-view. Even BoxNation, Frank Warren’s niche boxing channel, is weighing a one-off pay-per-view option to boost subscriptions. Estimates put the cost of UK broadcast rights between £5 million and £10 million, with Sky likely to open at £6 million. But with multiple bidders and the potential for massive ad revenue and PPV sales, the final price could climb higher. The fight airs live at 4am UK time on May 2 at the MGM Grand, yet demand shows no sign of slowing. In the United States, Showtime and HBO are splitting rights at $99.95 per viewing, with projections suggesting over three million buys — potentially shattering the 2.4 million record set by Mayweather vs. De La Hoya in 2007. That could mean over $300 million in US PPV revenue alone. Broadcasters expect to keep half, though negotiations suggest a smaller cut may be agreed upon this time. Behind the scenes, the spectacle extends beyond TV. Ringside seats are priced up to $5,000 — and already selling illegally for over $25,000. Hotels on the Las Vegas Strip anticipate a $1 billion windfall from gaming, dining, and closed-circuit viewings costing $150 or more. Some US theaters are even negotiating to screen the fight live. Meanwhile, Mayweather and Pacquiao continue their pre-fight theatrics — from shared popcorn at a Lakers game to chess sessions in the Philippines. Mayweather claims he made the fight happen; Pacquiao insists he signed first. Their verbal sparring matches the intensity of their training: Mayweather, disciplined and calculating; Pacquiao, relentless and humble. Elsewhere in boxing, Gennady Golovkin has accepted a $1 million wager to face Julio César Chávez Jr. at super-middleweight — a risky move for the undefeated middleweight king. And after a hard-fought 11-round battle, Martin Murray shared a drink with Golovkin the next morning, a rare gesture of sportsmanship after a brutal stoppage.

Pero ku hundreds di milionan di dólar na stak i dos di e korpo mas grandi di to tiempu ta bini jodi, nan ta nada garantiá. E batalla pa e direkto di transmisión na Reino Uní ta bini más fuerte. BT Sport, ku ta repleto di dinèr i ta un jugador grandi na Premier League, ta kere fá un declaración audaz pa entrá na e mundo di boxeo. ITV, ta bini bak na boxeo di alto nivel despues di casi un dékada, ta mira e oportunidat pa rekuperá su relevansia na e público — spesialmenti pa ku nan ta nán restríktá pa e reglamenton di BBC pa no ta vende pa pay-per-view. Na Estados Unidos, Showtime i HBO ta dividí e direkto di transmisión ku un prijs di $99.95 pa cada visualisashon, ku projeções ta sugeri ku más di trés millón di komprasonan — posiblemente rompi e rékord di 2.4 millón di Mayweather vs De La Hoya na 2007. Algun teatronan na Estados Unidos ta negosia pa transmite e pelea live. Mientri tanto, Mayweather i Pacquiao ta kontinuá ku e su teatralidat pre-pelea: di komé popcorn na un partidu di Lakers h asta partidu di ajedrez na Filipinas. Mayweather ta kliama ku el ta fá e pelea pasa; Pacquiao ta insiste ku el ta firmá primèr. E disputa verbalnan ta koresponde ku e intensidat di e entrenamentonan: Mayweather, discipliná i kalkuladó; Pacquiao, implaká i humil. Nan otro partidu di boxeo, Gennady Golovkin ta akseptá un apuesta di $1 millón pa jodi Julio César Chávez Jr. na super-medio-peso — un movimientu arriesgá pa e rey di peso medio sin derota. Y despues di un batalla dura di 11 ronda, Martin Murray ta koma un bebida ku Golovkin e dia siguinte, un gesto raro di deportividat despues di un parada brutal.

article_content: When a group of feminist students at Royal Holloway University were mockingly labeled 'The Ugly Girls Club' during a campus discussion on sexual consent, they didn’t retreat—they doubled down. Instead of being hurt by the insult, they turned it into a powerful act of defiance. They launched a social media campaign under the hashtag #uglygirlsclub, inviting people to share funny, exaggerated selfies that playfully rejected traditional ideas of beauty. Photos poured in from all over the UK: students pulling silly faces, wearing ridiculous expressions, and holding signs like 'I’d rather be ugly than a sexist w*****'. Among them, Alex Vosper puckered her lips and rolled her eyes, captioning her photo, 'Proud to be hideous.' Elena Barnard crossed her eyes and wrote, 'Sometimes I look cracking, and sometimes I say stuff that’s cracking—the stuff I say lasts longer.' Daniel Tremor, a male supporter, held up a sign rejecting sexism outright. Natasha Barrett, president of the feminist society, explained that while the posts began as jokes, their purpose was deeply serious: to help people see their value beyond how they look. Many participants shared that the campaign gave them newfound confidence and made them vow never to delete their so-called 'unsatisfactory' photos again. The initiative joins other national efforts like 'Reclaim Your Campus' and the NUS's fight against lad culture, proving that humor can be a potent tool in challenging harmful norms and building self-worth.

Bo ta lansa kampanha sosial media bai hashtag #uglygirlsclub, invitando to pa komparti selfie humoristiko i exagerá ku ta rechazá pa forma burla e ideanan tradisional di bela. Foto ta bini dende to e Reino Uní: studiantenan ta fasí ekspresionnan tonto, ta usá ekspresionnan ridikuloso, i ta tené letranan komo 'Mi prefiri ser ugly ku un sexist w*****'. article_content: Last night, Democratic Representative Hakeem Jeffries opened a powerful hour-long speech by the Congressional Black Caucus on the House floor, invoking the phrase 'Hands up, don't shoot' — a rallying cry adopted by protesters nationwide following the August 2014 shooting of 18-year-old Michael Brown in Ferguson, Missouri. Jeffries, representing New York, declared, 'This is a cry from communities across America — fed up with police violence in Ferguson, Brooklyn, Cleveland, Oakland, and beyond.' He emphasized that the outcry reflects deep frustration with a criminal justice system that repeatedly fails to hold officers accountable for excessive force. Texas Representative Al Green echoed this sentiment, praising the St. Louis Rams players who raised their hands before their Sunday game as a symbol of solidarity. He called the gesture a 'movement that will not dissipate.' Other members, including Congresswomen Yvette Clarke and Marcia Fudge, joined in, declaring that young people of color refuse to live in fear. Fudge expressed disappointment that the grand jury declined to indict Officer Darren Wilson, calling the decision 'another slap in the face' and comparing it to the deaths of Trayvon Martin and Tamir Rice. The speeches followed a White House meeting between President Barack Obama and civil rights leaders, law enforcement officials, and community activists — including two representatives from Ferguson. Obama pledged to keep pushing for improved police-community relations until the end of his presidency, stating, 'We’re not going to solve every problem, but we’re going to make things better.' Although the phrase 'hands up, don't shoot' became a powerful symbol of the movement, the U.S. Department of Justice later found no conclusive evidence that Brown had his hands up or uttered those words before being shot. Despite this, the slogan endures as a unifying expression of grief and a call for systemic reform.

Jeffries, ku ta reprezentá Nueva York, a declará, 'Ezé ta un grito di komunidat nan globalmente — stugá pa violensia polisial na Ferguson, Brooklyn, Cleveland, Oakland, i mas.' Malgre ezé, e lema ta persistí komo un ekspresion unificá di tristeza i kall pa reforma sistémiko.

article_content: Washington (CNN) — President Barack Obama and visiting German Chancellor Angela Merkel acknowledged Friday that significant differences remain between their governments regarding surveillance programs, following revelations by former NSA contractor Edward Snowden. Speaking at a joint news conference at the White House, Obama told reporters, 'We're not perfectly aligned,' noting the United States has no blanket no-spy agreement with any nation—not even its closest allies. Merkel, addressing business leaders later, stressed the need to balance technological capability, national security, and individual privacy. 'In a nutshell,' she said, 'an end never justifies the means—and not everything that is technically feasible ought to be done.' Germany and other allied nations voiced strong objections after Snowden’s 2013 disclosures exposed U.S. surveillance of foreign leaders and mass monitoring of international phone calls and internet communications in counterterrorism efforts. While the Obama administration maintained that all countries engage in some level of espionage, the President has since ordered reforms to U.S. surveillance practices. Obama admitted it had 'pained' him to witness how deeply the Snowden leaks strained relations with Germany, a vital partner. Merkel confirmed that diplomatic talks have yet to bridge the divide. 'Over the past few months, we’ve seen considerable differences of opinion and interest between Germany and the United States on this issue,' she said. 'I don’t believe we’ve fully overcome this—even after my visit.' CNN’s Tom Cohen and Laura Koran contributed to this report.

Hablando na konferensia komun na White House, Obama ta dixe pa reporteronan, 'Nos ta pa perfectamente aliniao,' nanotando ku Estados Unidos no ta teni un akordu di 'no-spy' konsidera pa nansi—ni siquiera pa aliadonan mas kieridu. Merkel, hablando pa lideran negosio despues, ta enfatisá la nécesidat di balanseá kapasidat tekniko, seguridat nasional, i privasidat individual. 'Na un palabrashon,' el ta dixe, 'un fin no ta justifika medionan—i no ta todo lo ku ta teknikamenté posible ta debí faze.' Alemania i otro nasión aliadu ta protestá fuerte despues di revelashonan 2013 di Snowden ku ta eksponé surveilans di Estados Unidos pa lideran foran i monitoreo masivo di llamadanan internashonal i konsa internet pa esfuerzonan kontre terorismo. Mientras ku administrashon Obama ta manteni ku to nansi ta engajá na algun nivel di espionaje, prensidente ta ordená reformanan pa programnan di surveilans di Estados Unidos. Obama ta admití ku el ta 'dolorí' pa bini ku kuán profundo revelashonan di Snowden ta afektá relashon ku Alemania, un sosiega vital. Merkel ta konsirma ku dialogonan diplomatiko ta pa puerta abri. 'Na los útimo mes, nos ta bini diferensias signifikativu di opinyon i interes ente Alemania i Estados Unidos riba esti asunto,' el ta dixe. 'Mi ta kreí ku nos ta pa superá esti problema—mes ku mi visita.' CNN su Tom Cohen i Laura Koran ta konsiribuí na esti reporte.

article_content: In January 2013, British grandmother Lindsay Sandiford was arrested at Bali’s Denpasar Airport after customs officials discovered nearly five kilograms of cocaine concealed in her suitcase — valued at over £1.6 million. She claimed she was forced into the scheme by a network of fellow Britons living in Bali, including Rachel Dougall, Julian Ponder, and Paul Beales. According to Sandiford, Beales slipped the drugs into her luggage during a meeting in Bangkok. She later told authorities that Dougall was the true owner, though both denied the accusation. Two days after the meeting, Sandiford flew to Bali carrying the contraband. Once caught, she broke down upon learning she could face execution. She immediately named Dougall and Ponder as the masterminds, saying they instructed her to deliver the package to them. The couple, known locally for their opulent lifestyle — renting a villa for £1,000 a week with no visible income — were subsequently arrested. Beales, suspected of providing muscle for the group, was also detained. Police staged a sting operation, placing Sandiford in a modest hotel room under surveillance while she waited to be contacted. Ponder arrived at the hotel, and Beales was apprehended nearby. Dougall was later arrested too. Yet despite Sandiford’s testimony, prosecutors struggled to build a solid case: all communication occurred via phone, and a crucial SIM card from Dougall’s villa was never recovered. Dougall received only a one-year sentence for concealing evidence — time already served — and could return to the UK within months. Beales was jailed for four years for possessing a small quantity of hashish. Ponder maintained he believed the wrapped package labeled 'Enjoy Sweet Candy' was a birthday gift for his six-year-old daughter. His lawyer argued he was entrapped by Sandiford, who, once arrested, turned informant. Meanwhile, Sandiford wept uncontrollably as she was sentenced to death by firing squad. A verdict on Ponder’s fate was imminent — if convicted, he could become the 13th British citizen abroad sentenced to death for drug offenses.

É ta afirma ku é ta forzá pa entra na un red di otro britániko ku ta bini na Bali, inkluyí Rachel Dougall, Julian Ponder, i Paul Beales. Segun Sandiford, Beales ta pone ku kokain na maleta su duranti un reunió na Bangkok. É ta kuenta na autoridat ku Dougall ta e propietario verdadero, pero ambos ta nega e acusashon. Dos dias despues di e reunió, Sandiford ta biaha na Bali ku e droga. Despues ku ta atrapá, é ta rompi na lagrima ku ta oí e posibildad di eksesekushon. Dougall ta arrestá tambe. Pero malgre e testimonio di Sandiford, promotor ta bai strugá pa konstruí un kaso sólido: tota komunikashon ta pasa na telèfono, i un SIM-kard krítiko di villa di Dougall ta nunka ta rekuperá. Dougall ta bini un sentsia di un año pa konsebi e krimen — tiempu yá servío — i ta puede bini bak na Reino Uní dentu di meses. Beales ta prisioná pa katorse año pa posesion di un kantidat pequeno di hashish. Ponder ta mantene ku é ta kredi ku e paquete envolbí ku e rótulo 'Enjoy Sweet Candy' ta un regalo di kumpleanos pa su hija di seis años. Su abogá ta arguménta ku é ta atrapá pa Sandiford, ku, despues ku ta atrapá, ta bini informante. Mientras, Sandiford ta lagrima sin kontrol ku é ta sentsiá a muerte pa fusilamentu. Un verediktu pa e kaso di Ponder ta esperá — si konsiderá kulpa, é ta pode bini e 13mo britániko ku ta konsiderá muerte pa ofensas di droga.

article_content: In the quiet aftermath of a heartbreaking military funeral, one loyal dog became the silent symbol of devotion. Hawkeye, a gentle Labrador retriever, stayed by the casket of his beloved owner, Navy SEAL Petty Officer Jon Tumilson, refusing to move even as thousands paid their respects. The image — captured by Tumilson’s cousin, Lisa Pembleton — spread across the world, touching hearts with its raw honesty. Tumilson, 35, was one of 38 American service members killed on August 6, 2011, when a rocket-propelled grenade struck their Chinook helicopter over Afghanistan. Born in San Diego and raised in Rockford, Iowa, he had dreamed since childhood of joining the Navy SEALs — a goal he achieved with quiet determination. Though many assumed Hawkeye was a trained military working dog, those close to Tumilson clarified he was simply a cherished family pet. When Jon was deployed overseas, Scott Nichols, a close friend, stepped in to care for him. Now, in a tender twist of fate, Hawkeye has been formally willed to Nichols — the very person who gave him comfort during Tumilson’s long absences. At the packed funeral held at the Rudd-Rockford-Marble Rock Community School, over 1,500 people filled the gymnasium — including Iowa Governor Terry Branstad and Senator Charles Grassley. Navy Lt. Robert Bradshaw told Tumilson’s parents, George and Kathleen, that they raised not just a son, but a true hero. ‘He wasn’t afraid to die,’ said Nichols. ‘He was afraid of leaving his parents behind.’ Fellow soldier Boe Nankivel added, ‘If he knew he’d be shot down going to help others, he’d still go.’ His sister Kristie remembered how, even when others called his dreams impossible, she always believed he’d make them real. And now, Hawkeye — the faithful companion who never left his master’s side — will spend his days in the arms of someone who knew Jon’s heart. In grief, there is peace. In loss, there is love. And sometimes, the most powerful stories aren’t told in words… but in silence, loyalty, and a wagging tail.
translated_content: Na l’ultim di un funeral tristemente, un kier leal ta bini e simbolo silensioso di devosion. Hawkeye, un Labrador retriever dulse, ta sta bi e kofre di su amá Jon Tumilson, un SEAL di Marina, nan mester pa bini pa mas di mil personanan ku ta rende respeto. La foto — takí pa Lisa Pembleton, prima di Tumilson — ta spresi na mundu, ta toca kardanan ku su honestidat pura. Tumilson, 35, ta un di 38 soldadonan Amerikano ku ta morí na 6 di agostus, 2011, ku un RPG ta bai e helikopter Chinook di e nan na Afganistán. Na San Diego nasí i kresí na Rockford, Iowa, el ta soñá desdi kikeña di bini un SEAL di Marina — un objektivo ku el ta lográ ku determinashon silensioso. Aunque mukin ta pensa Hawkeye ta un perro di servisio militar, e personanan ku ta sibé Tumilson ta klare ku el ta solamente un perro di famíia. Ku Jon ta ta bini pa misión, Scott Nichols, un amigu próksimo, ta bini pa kuidá e. Ahora, na un giro dulce di e fatu, Hawkeye ta formalmenta heredá pa Nichols — e mesmo persona ku ta da e konsuelo ku Jon ta ausente. Na e funeral plen di e Rudd-Rockford-Marble Rock Community School, mas di 1.500 personanan ta konsentri na e gimnasio — inkluyendo guvernador di Iowa Terry Branstad i senador Charles Grassley. Tenient di Marina Robert Bradshaw ta dí pa e padres di Tumilson, George i Kathleen, ku e ta kresí no solamente un hijo, mas un héroe. 'El ta no temí di morí,' di Nichols. 'El ta temí di lasa su padres atras.' Soldadu Boe Nankivel ta adisioná, 'Si el sabe el ta bai morí pa yuda otro, el ta bini igual.' Su hermana Kristie ta rememorá ku, aun ku mukin ta konsidera su soñanan imposibel, el ta siempres saba ku el ta bini lográ e. Y ahó, Hawkeye — e kier leal ku nan mester pa bini di su amo — ta bini pasa su dia na brazonan di e persona ku ta sabe e kard di Jon. Na tristeza, ta hende. Na perdida, ta amor. Y a vegada, e historianan mas poderoso no ta kontá na palabranan… mas na silensio, lealdad, i un cola kande.

article_content: During a Mid Devon Hunt on Dartmoor in July 2013, protester Hayden Macey, 68, is accused of driving his Land Rover into the rear of a £90,000 racehorse ridden by Michelle Westcott, causing the animal to rear and throw her to the ground. Prosecutors allege that after the collision, Macey exited his vehicle, approached Westcott, and grabbed her by the throat. Westcott, who was riding a horse named 'According to Lawrence' along a narrow, steep lane, testified that she was not obstructing the path and that Macey honked his horn multiple times before striking the horse’s hind legs, forcing it into a stone wall. She sustained injuries to her leg and arm and was unable to bear weight on her leg for two weeks. The horse suffered a strained back. Macey denies all allegations. He claims Westcott was riding unnecessarily slowly and deliberately blocked the road during his monitoring of the hunt. He asserts that she struck the roof of his stationary vehicle with her riding crop, startling the horse and causing it to rear. He insists there was no physical contact with Westcott and that he raised his hands only to shield himself from her whip. Witness Sarah Wheeler, also in the Land Rover, corroborated Macey’s version, stating that Westcott swore at him and struck the vehicle before the incident. Both parties provided conflicting statements to police. Macey, who has monitored hunts up to three times a week for 30 years, said he has endured physical attacks in the past due to his activism. He maintains the entire accusation is 'absurd, ridiculous and preposterous.' The case continues at Exeter Magistrates Court, where Macey faces charges of assault and failure to report an accident.
translated_content: Durante un Mid Devon Hunt na Dartmoor den 2013, e protestant Hayden Macey, 68, ta akusá di e kere di su Land Rover na e kuxa di un kavalo di korsa di £90.000 ku e ta kaba, Michelle Westcott, ta bini e kavalo pa bai e tera. E prosikutor ta afirma ku despues di e kolidensia, Macey ta sali di su kars, ta aproksimá pa Westcott, i ta agará e gorgo di e. Westcott, ku ta kaba un kavalo kallá 'According to Lawrence' na un kaminu angusto i pendiente, ta testifika ku e ta mester no blokeá e kaminu i ku Macey ta sona e korneta mas ku sinku biaha antis di e kere na e kuxa di e kavalo, forsa e pa bai kontra un pèdra. E ta bini lesioná na e pierna i brazo i ta no pò pone pesu na e pierna pa dos semaná. E kavalo ta bini konsidirá ku e spalda ta lesiona. Macey ta nega todi e akusasion. E ta klama ku Westcott ta kaba mester lentamente i ta blokeá e kaminu durante e monitorisashon di e kasa. E ta aserma ku e ta bini bati e techo di su kars estasionario ku su látigo, sorprenda e kavalo i ta bini bai. E ta asegurá ku e ta no tena kontakto fisiko ku Westcott i ku e ta subí e man pa proteje su kabe di e látigo. Testigu Sarah Wheeler, tambe den e kars, ta koresponda e vershon di Macey, afirmando ku Westcott ta jurá pa e i ta bati e kars antis di e incidente. Todi e partidu ta dà konta kontradiktoriu pa e polis. Macey, ku ta monitorisa kasa mas ku tres biaha pa semaná duranti 30 aña, ta klama ku e ta bini ataká fisikamente antis pa e kampanha pa animales. E ta mantene ku e akusashon ta 'absurdu, ridikuloso i preposteru.' E kaza ta konsidera na Exeter Magistrates Court, ku Macey ta enfrenta akusasion di asalto i no raporta un akidente.

She says HE chased & attacked them. Both stories clash — who’s telling the truth? #HuntProtest #DartmoorDrama #JusticeForHorses

article_content: Mark Cavendish won the seventh and final stage of the Tour de San Luis after outpacing rival Fernando Gaviria in a frenzied sprint to the finish line. Cavendish entered the final day in 90th place overall, having been narrowly beaten by Gaviria in the first and third stages in Argentina. But the Manxman used his elite sprinting expertise to defeat the 20-year-old Colombian by a fraction of a second on Sunday and claim the stage victory. Cavendish completed the final leg in a time of two hours, 33 minutes, and 29 seconds. Afterwards, he paid tribute to Argentine rider Dani Diez, who won the overall tour. 'This is the second time he has won this race, and the Argentinians have a strong team,' Cavendish told ESPN. Nairo Quintana of Colombia finished third in the overall standings. 'It's the peak of their season, so it's great for European professionals to race here. It's very hot, but it was a good race for the fans and the riders.' Rodolfo Torres finished second overall, and his Colombian teammate Nairo Quintana placed third.

Cavendish a entra na e útimo dia na e 90mo lugar, despues di havi sido batí na linia na e primé i tèrs stá di e korsa na Arjentín. Pero e Hòlandés di Mán a usá e su espeksialidat di sprint pa bai más rápidu ku e kolumbianu di 20 aña di un frakshon di un segundu na dóminku i ganá e stá. Cavendish a kumpletá e útimo tramo di e korsa na un tiempu di dos ora, 33 minüt i 29 segundu. Despues di e korsa, a hónora e arjentino Dani Diez, ku a ganá e korsa general. 'E ta e sekondi veç ku el a ganá e korsa, i e Arjentinos a tin un ékip fuerte,' Cavendish a dixe pa ESPN. Nairo Quintana di Kolumbía a bini tèrs na e klasifikashon general. 'E ta e pico di e sezon di e, asina ku ta bon pa e profesionalan Europeo pa kursa akí. E ta masha kálid, pero e ta un korsa bon pa e fanátiko i e korsan.' Rodolfo Torres a bini sekundu na e klasifikashon general, i su kolumbianu kompanero Nairo Quintana a bini tèrs.
