article_content: Senior BJP leader and former Punjab Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh on Saturday demanded strict action against Rajasthan BJP leader Sandeep Dayma for his hate remarks targeting mosques and gurdwaras in India. Dayma made the comments during a rally in Tijara on Wednesday, in the presence of Balak Nath, the BJP candidate from the Tijara Assembly constituency, and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. On Thursday, Dayma issued a video apology, stating: 'In place of masjid-madrasa, I mistakenly used wrong words regarding Gurdwara Sahib. I apologize with folded hands to the entire Sikh community, which has always protected Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma. I don’t know how I made this mistake. I will repent by visiting a gurdwara. I apologize with folded hands. Sat Sri Akal!' In his apology, Dayma claimed he intended to say 'masjid-madrasa' but accidentally said 'gurdwara.' Amarinder Singh, a member of the BJP National Executive, called for Dayma’s expulsion from the party and legal action, stating: 'People like Dayma, who make mindless and vicious statements, have no place in the BJP.' He argued that an apology alone cannot undo the harm done. On Sunday, a delegation from Punjab BJP, led by Jai Inder Kaur—daughter of Captain Amarinder Singh and president of the party’s Mahila Morcha—filed a formal complaint at the Sector 39 police station in Chandigarh, urging strict action against Dayma and others involved. The complaint stated that Dayma’s speech created an atmosphere of insecurity and violated the religious sentiments of citizens, including those under the police station’s jurisdiction. It emphasized that BJP Punjab’s office falls within this jurisdiction, justifying the filing location. The complaint further cited Article 25 of the Constitution, asserting that Dayma’s remarks infringed upon the fundamental right to freedom of religion. Accompanying Jai Inder Kaur were Punjab BJP OBC Morcha president Amarpal Singh Bonny Ajnala, state secretary Kanwarveer Singh Tohra, spokesperson Pritpal Singh Baliawal, and legal cell co-convenor Harneet Singh Oberoi. Punjab BJP chief Sunil Jakhar, on X (formerly Twitter), condemned the remarks: 'Outbursts against the religious sentiments of fellow citizens cannot be condoned. I have informed central leadership of the hurt caused. The state unit recommends exploring all options to prevent recurrence. No apology can assuage the anger caused by such insensitive remarks.' SAD chief Sukhbir Badal, on Thursday, rejected the apology as 'qualified and weak,' calling Dayma’s remarks 'outrageous, anti-minority, and anti-national.' He stressed that all places of worship—temples, gurdwaras, mosques—are equal and demanded legal consequences for anyone disturbing communal harmony. The Election Commission of India issued a notice to Dayma for violating the Model Code of Conduct. In Tijara, members of the Sikh community protested by burning effigies of Dayma and chanting slogans against Balak Nath and Yogi Adityanath. Balak Nath, attempting to downplay the incident, told reporters: 'The Sikh community has always protected Sanatan Dharm and sanskriti. We hope they will forgive if some mistake was made by some kids.' Despite BJP’s broader outreach to the Sikh community, the party moved swiftly to contain the fallout, though critics argue the response remains insufficient.

article_content: When Maria Sharapova underwent shoulder surgery five years ago, many believed her tennis career was over. Yet today, there's a strong possibility she’ll compete into her 30s before shifting full focus to her thriving business ventures. 'I think she’s going to play another four to five years — through the 2016 Rio Olympics — if she stays healthy and motivated,' said her longtime agent and close friend, Max Eisenbud, in an interview with CNN’s Open Court. Sharapova, who turned 26 last week, is now fully fit — a far cry from 2008, when a recurring shoulder injury sidelined her for nine months. Initial scans suggested inflammation, but after worsening pain following a win in Montreal, an MRI revealed two small tears in the tendon of her right, serving shoulder. What followed was years of rehabilitation, surgery, additional setbacks including a bone bruise, and mental struggles. 'The shoulder is central to tennis,' Sharapova told Open Court. 'My game relies on power and aggression. When you’re out for nine months — with few examples of athletes returning from such injuries — doubt creeps in.' Yet she never lost faith. It took three more years before she reached another Grand Slam final — losing at Wimbledon in 2011. Since then, serious injuries have been absent, though an ankle issue surfaced later that year. 'I felt like everyone else was moving forward while I stood still,' she admitted. Eisenbud’s prediction is welcome news for women’s tennis. Sharapova’s global star power grew exponentially after her 2012 French Open triumph, making her the 10th woman in history to win all four majors. Forbes named her the world’s highest-paid female athlete in 2013, earning nearly $28 million — more than her entire career prize money — thanks to endorsements from Samsung, Evian, Nike, Tiffany & Co., Head, Cole Haan, and Porsche. She also launched Sugarpova, her premium candy line, with plans to expand into China, Japan, India, and England. Still, Sharapova insists tennis comes first. 'Of course I want my candy to sell and my partnerships to last — that’s obvious,' she said. 'But everything I’ve built stems from being a tennis player — not a model or actress. My identity is rooted in this sport.' Her 2013 form confirms her drive: she reached at least the semifinals in every tournament she entered, nearly completing a rare Indian Wells-Miami double. She won Indian Wells but fell to Serena Williams in Miami — marking her 11th straight loss to the world No. 1, though she did win a set against Williams for the first time in five years. An Olympic gold medal remains elusive. She lost to Williams in the 2012 London final and missed the 2008 Beijing Games due to injury. 'I always feel I can be better,' Sharapova said. 'When I step on the court, I feel strong. I know I’m good at what I do. But you can’t stand still. Everyone else is getting faster, stronger, hitting harder — so I have to too.' Now, as defending champion in Stuttgart, she begins her clay-court campaign, aiming to repeat her 2012 success in Madrid, Rome, and Roland Garros — where she defeated Sara Errani to claim her second French Open title. After being written off during her recovery, she cherishes these victories even more. 'Losing is hard — especially after winning so much,' she reflected. 'People comment on matches, but never on the hours of work behind them. But those doubts made me stronger. I’ve spoken to those who doubted me — especially after Paris. But it’s sport. Opinions are part of the game. And I have no problem with that.'

'Mi juego ta bazá na poder i agresividat. Cuando ta bini pa 9 mes — ku poko eemplo di atletanan ku ta regresa for di e lesion — duda ta komeçá.' Pero el ta pa bini na fe. Ta tèn 3 aña mas hsta ku el ta bini pa un final di Grand Slam — perdi na Wimbledon 2011. Despues di e, lesion serio no ta bini mas, aunque un lesion di tobilla ta aparesé mas tarde. 'Mi ta pensa ku todo mundo ta avansá mientras mi ta stá pa un lugar,' el ta admite. Predikshon di Eisenbud ta buen notisia pa tenis femenino. Star global di Sharapova ta amentá enormemente despues di su vitoria na Roland Garros 2012, ku ta faze el e 10ma muller na historiya ku ta ganá los katorse Grand Slam. Forbes ta nombra el e atleta femenina mas pagá di e mundo na 2013, ganándo casi $28 millón — mas ku su total di premios na karrera — graças a patrocinio di Samsung, Evian, Nike, Tiffany & Co., Head, Cole Haan, i Porsche. El ta lansa tambe Sugarpova, su linia di dulseria premium, ku plan pa ekspande na Kina, Japon, India, i Inglaterra. Pero Sharapova ta insistí ku tenis ta primèr. 'Klaro mi ta bini pa ku mi dulseria ta vende i mi asosiashon ta kontinuá — eso ta obvio,' el ta di. 'Pero todo lo ku mi ta konstruí ta bazá na mi koma tenisista — no na mi koma modelo o aktor. Mi identidat ta raizá na e deporte.' Forma di 2013 di el ta konsirmá su motivashon: el ta bini pa semifinal na totu torneo ku el ta joga, casi lográ un doble raro na Indian Wells i Miami. El ta ganá Indian Wells pero perdi na Miami kon Serena Williams — markándo e 11ma vitoria konsekutibo di Williams, aunque el ta ganá un set kon Williams pa primèr vèz na 5 aña. Medalla di oro olímpiko ta keda faltándo. El ta perdi kon Williams na final di Londres 2012 i ta perde e Juegos di Pekín 2008 por e lesion. 'Mi ta sienti ku mi ta podé mejora,' di Sharapova. 'Ku mi ta pone pa e kourt, mi ta sienti fué. Mi ta sienti ku mi ta bon na lo ku mi ta fá. Pero mi ta pa stá pa un lugar. Todo mundo ta bini mas rapido, mas fuerte, bati e bola mas duro — asina ku mi ta tèn ku fá lo mismo.' Hodia, komo kampeona defensor na Stuttgart, el ta komeçá su kampaña na arcilla, aimandu pa repetí su sukés na 2012 na Madrid, Roma, i Roland Garros — ku el ta derota Sara Errani pa ganá su segundu título na Roland Garros. Despues di e eskribí pa perdí duranti su rekuperashon, el ta apresia e vitorianan mas. 'Perdí no ta fasil — spesialmenti despues di ganá tanto,' el ta refleksioná. 'Gente ta komentá na partidanan, mas no ta komentá e ora di trabao tras e kousa. Pero e duda ta fá mi mas fuerte. Mi ta hablá ku e ki ta dubidá mi — spesialmenti despues di Paris. Pero ta deporte. Komentario ta parti di e jogo. Y mi ta no tin problema ku e.'

article_content: A groundbreaking study from Cornell University reveals that our genes may shape the trillions of microbes living in our guts — and some of these microbes could help keep us slim. Researchers identified a bacterial family called Christensenellaceae that is more abundant in people with healthy weights and less so in those who are overweight or obese. What’s remarkable is that this microbial pattern runs in families, suggesting it’s inherited through our DNA rather than simply learned from diet or lifestyle. To test its impact, scientists transplanted Christensenellaceae from human donors into mice. Those mice gained significantly less weight compared to controls, even when fed the same diet. This hints that introducing this specific bacterium might one day help prevent unhealthy weight gain in humans. Previous research had linked gut microbes to conditions like obesity and diabetes, but it wasn’t clear whether genes or environment played the bigger role. Earlier twin studies gave mixed results — until now. The Cornell team analyzed stool samples from 416 pairs of twins, including both identical and fraternal pairs. They found that identical twins — who share nearly 100% of their DNA — had far more similar gut microbiomes than fraternal twins or regular siblings, pointing squarely to genetics as a key driver. Associate Professor Ruth Ley explains that while diet and environment still matter, this is the first solid evidence that our genes actively select which microbes thrive inside us. She believes these findings could lead to personalized probiotics tailored to an individual’s genetic profile — potentially reducing risks for obesity, heart disease, and metabolic disorders. The study, published in Cell, positions Christensenellaceae as a promising candidate for future microbiome-based therapies aimed at promoting long-term metabolic health.

Investigadóres identifiká un familia di bakteria kualifiká komo Christensenellaceae ku ta mas abondante den persona ku ta tin pesu salúdabel i mas menó den e ku ta sobrepesu u obezo. Lo ku ta rikordáblo ta ku e patron mikrobial ta pasa di generashon a generashon, sugirié ku e ta heredá atravez di nos ADN, no solamente aprindí di dieta o estilo di vida. Pa prueba e su efekto, siensianan transplantá Christensenellaceae di donadórs humanó pa souris. E souris ku ta recibí e bakteria ta ganá menó pesu kompará ku e kontrol, even ku ta kome lo mismo. Studia anterior ku ta usa gemelos ta dá rezultadonan mezclá — hasta ahó. E ekip di Cornell analizá muestra di hek di 416 pareh di gemelos, inkluyendo gemelos idéntiko i fraternales. E ta demonstrá ku gemelos idéntiko — ku ta kompartí casi 100% di ADN — ta tin mikrobioma intestinal mas semejante kompará ku gemelos fraternales u hermanan ordinario, indiká ku genética ta e faktor klavi. Profesora Asosiá Ruth Ley explica ku while dieta i ambienta ta sigui importante, e ta e primèr evidensia sólida ku nos genes ta seleksioná aktivamenti ki mikrobi ta prosperá den nos kuerpo. E ta kreí ku e hallazgonan ta puede leva a probiótiko personalizá ku ta adaptá a perfil genétiko di individual — potensialmenti reduzi risiko pa obesidat, enfermedat di kardiak, i desórden metaboliko. E studia, publicá na revista Cell, ta pòne Christensenellaceae komo un kandidato prometedor pa terapia mikrobial futuró ku ta mirá promové salud metaboliko a longo plas.

article_content: Even now, ten years after achieving remission from chronic myeloid leukemia, Geoff Thomas faces a lingering challenge: his eyes no longer produce tears, making high-speed Alpine descents on his bicycle dangerously difficult. Yet, a decade after completing the entire Tour de France route to raise funds for others battling blood cancer, Thomas is returning to the mountains — not as a spectator, but as a champion once again. Riding day after day through the Alps shortly after surviving a life-threatening illness was nothing short of heroic. Navigating steep descents at speeds up to 50 mph, relying only on the glint of headlights ahead, bordered on the extraordinary — even reckless. 'I was a bit deranged then,' he admits today. The former England international and Crystal Palace captain is now preparing for two major charity rides. In June, he will lead 300 amateur cyclists on a London-to-Paris journey, complete with rolling road closures, mechanical support, and peloton-style groupings suited to all skill levels. Later, he will select just 20 participants to follow the exact 2015 Tour de France route — one day ahead of the pros — offering a rare glimpse into the grueling reality of professional cycling. Thomas’s goal: raise at least £2 million over the next two years for Cure Leukaemia, the charity co-founded by Professor Charlie Craddock, the physician who saved his life. When Thomas was diagnosed, only 6% of blood cancer patients had access to clinical trials, and nearly 60% did not survive. He was given three months to live. Beyond his own ride, Thomas helped persuade pharmaceutical companies to release over £100 million in drugs for clinical trials — a legacy few athletes achieve. His former teammates Ian Wright and Mark Bright have already signed up to ride. 'Wrighty thinks he’s the better cyclist,' Thomas jokes. 'But Brighty? He’s lost some weight — you can quote me on that.' With Jaguar Land Rover already on board as a sponsor, and more partnerships in discussion, Thomas hopes his story will inspire the public to donate and help transform outcomes for future patients. 'This isn’t just about cycling,' he says. 'It’s about saving lives.' To learn more or join the ride, visit www.beforethetour.com for the Tour de France challenge, and www.L2Prevolution.com for the London to Paris event.

Pero 10 aña despues di kumpletá e ruta kompletu di Tour de France pa recaudá fundu pa otus ku ta luchá pa kanker di sangre, Thomas ta regresá a e montañan — no komo un espectador, mas komo un kampion otra vei. Bisi día tras día atravez di e Alpes pòst di sobreviví un enfermedad ku ta amenasa su vida ta nada menó ku heroiko. Navegá descensos pronunsiá a velosidat hasta 80 km/h, basá na e brillo di faros di baiante adelant, ta kuasi extraordinario — hasta temerario. 'E yo ta un poko demente den aña,' el ta admití hodi. E antigu kaptin di Crystal Palace i internacional di Inglaterra ta prepará pa dos eventos di karidad. Di junio, el ta liderá 300 bikis amatoriale na un viaje di Londres a París, ku ta inklui blokeo di karretera móbil, apoyo mékaniko, i grupon di pelotón adaptá pa to nivél di habidat. Más tarde, el ta seleksioná solamente 20 participante pa siguí e ruta exactu di Tour de France 2015 — un dia adelantá di e profesionale — ofresiendo un visión rara di e realidat duru di krosa profesional. E meta di Thomas: recaudá ménos £2 millon pa e próksimo 2 aña pa Cure Leukaemia, e karidad ku e doktór Charlie Craddock, e médiku ku ta salbá su vida, ta ko-fundá. Kuando Thomas ta diagnosticá, solamente 6% di pacientes ku kanker di sangre tin akseso pa trial kliniko, i casi 60% no ta sobreviví. El ta dái tres mes pa bibí. Más allá di e su bisi, Thomas ta ajudá pa konvinsí kompanian farmaséutiko pa liberá más di £100 millon di droga pa trial kliniko — un legado ku poko atleta ta lográ. E antigu kumpañero di equipo Ian Wright i Mark Bright ta firmá pa bisi. 'Wrighty ta pensa el ta e biker mejor,' Thomas ta burlá. 'Mas Brighty? El ta perdí un poko di pesu — e ta puede kota mihó.' Ku Jaguar Land Rover ya ta ku e patrocinio, i más asociashon den diskushon, Thomas ta esperá ku e historia su ta inspirá e públiko pa doná i ayudá pa transformá e rezultá pa paciente di aña vení. 'E no ta solamente bici,' el ta di. 'E ta pa salbá bida.' Pa mas informashon o pa inskribí pa e bisi, bini www.beforethetour.com pa e desafío di Tour de France, i www.L2Prevolution.com pa e evento di Londres a París.

article_content: Two young children in Georgia were fatally shot by underage relatives over the weekend, authorities reported. In Savannah, 11-year-old Montrez Burroughs was killed Friday night by a 12-year-old relative while visiting family. In Waycross, 10-year-old Taylor Jowers died after her 15-year-old brother accidentally discharged a shotgun while she was holding it. Both children sustained chest wounds. In neither case were adults present at the time of the shootings, according to reports. Montrez and his mother had recently moved from Savannah to Jacksonville but were in town for the weekend. Witnesses said the boys had been playing with what they thought was a toy gun before finding a real one. Montrez’s cousin, Denisha Coppock, said she saw him alive just 15 minutes before the shooting. 'Your life is precious like that — it can be taken away just like that,' she said. The 12-year-old shooter in Savannah was charged with involuntary manslaughter, reckless conduct, and possessing a firearm under age 18. Family members expressed outrage that the gun's owner has not come forward to apologize or accept responsibility. 'The parent and the child need to be charged,' said Aunt Shaleena Hamilton. 'You have to be responsible for what happens in your home.' In Waycross, Taylor’s brother told her to hold the shotgun while he checked if it was loaded. It fired unexpectedly. He fled to a neighbor’s house, who immediately called emergency services. Taylor was pronounced dead at the scene. Her parents were at work at the time. The Ware County Sheriff’s Office confirmed the shooter was an 'older relative' but declined to specify if it was her brother or confirm whether charges are being considered. The investigation remains open.

article_content: A Kosovar man was arrested abroad and faces charges related to a terror plot involving several suspects from North Carolina, federal authorities said Thursday. Bajram Asllani, 29, a resident of Mitrovica, Kosovo, is charged with providing material support to terrorists and conspiring to murder, kidnap, maim, and injure people abroad, according to the Department of Justice. He was arrested early Thursday in Kosovo under a provisional U.S. arrest warrant issued by the Eastern District of North Carolina. The United States plans to seek his extradition. If convicted, he could face up to 40 years in prison. 'People who are plotting to harm America and Americans are no longer a world away,' said Owen D. Harris, special agent in charge of the FBI in North Carolina. 'This case began in Raleigh, N.C., and now stretches across the globe — a scenario few would have imagined less than a decade ago.' Eight individuals were indicted last year in North Carolina on terror-related charges. The unsealed criminal complaint from April 19 reveals Asllani was part of the same conspiracy. According to the complaint, Asllani solicited funds from the conspirators to establish a base in Kosovo for violent jihad and accepted money to help him travel. Kosovo, which declared independence in 2008, is a predominantly ethnic Albanian country with Islam as its dominant religion. The complaint states that Hysen Sherifi, one of the eight indicted, traveled from Raleigh to Pristina, Kosovo, in 2008 to pursue violent jihad and connected with Asllani. Asllani allegedly provided Sherifi with recruitment materials and instructed him to acquire land for storing weapons and establishing a base. Sherifi returned to the U.S., collected $15,000 in funds via check, but was arrested before sending the money to Kosovo. Asllani also received funds from Sherifi to obtain travel documents. Sherifi reportedly referred to Asllani as 'the brother' in Kosovo — someone who was 'wanted.' Asllani had previously been arrested by Kosovar authorities in 2007 and placed under house arrest. In September 2009, a Serbian court convicted him in absentia for planning terrorist offenses and sentenced him to eight years in prison. Sherifi, a native of Kosovo, is a legal permanent resident of North Carolina. Five of the eight indicted are U.S. citizens residing in North Carolina: Daniel Patrick Boyd, Zakariya Boyd, Dylan Boyd, Ziyad Yaghi, and Mohammed Omar Aly Hassan. Others include Anes Subasic, a naturalized U.S. citizen, and Jude Kenan Mohammad, a U.S. citizen. The complaint notes Daniel Boyd intended to send himself and his sons, Zakariya and Dylan, to Kosovo after Sherifi returned. The boys reportedly communicated online with Sherifi and Asllani in Kosovo. An additional indictment last year charged Daniel Boyd, Sherifi, and Zakariya Boyd with conspiring to murder U.S. military personnel in a plot targeting the Marine Corps Base in Quantico, Virginia. They were also charged with illegal weapons possession.

article_content: London, England (CNN) — A consortium known as the 'Red Knights' has taken a significant step toward launching a $1 billion bid to acquire Manchester United by appointing Japanese investment bank Nomura as its financial adviser. The group, composed of wealthy investors, aims to take control of the English Premier League club currently owned by the American Glazer family. According to a statement, Nomura will collaborate closely with the Manchester United Supporters' Trust (MUST) and other potential investors to coordinate and finalize a formal proposal for the Glazers. The bank’s team, led by Guy Dawson and Andrew McNaught—both of whom advised the Glazers during their 2005 acquisition of the club—will begin by evaluating financial commitments already pledged to the Red Knights and shaping any future offer. The Glazer family has faced sustained criticism for Manchester United’s substantial debt, which recent financial reports show exceeds $1 billion. In response, the owners recently launched a $750 million bond offering to reduce liabilities. The Glazers also own the NFL’s Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Red Knights’ announcement follows the most intense fan protest yet against the Glazers, occurring during Manchester United’s recent Champions League win over AC Milan. Supporters displayed banners reading 'Love United Hate Glazer' and wore green-and-gold scarves—a growing symbol of dissent—at Old Trafford. Although Manchester United CEO David Gill stated last week that the Glazers have no interest in selling the club, the Red Knights remain committed to pursuing the acquisition. Nomura confirmed in its statement that it is reaching out to individuals and entities that have expressed financial backing for the bid.

article_content: The 2023 Women, Peace and Security Index was launched on Tuesday, ranking countries worldwide based on the status of women. The Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO), which co-authored the index with Georgetown University's Institute for Women, found that many of the best-performing countries for women are in Europe — though significant disparities exist across the region. The report notes that societies where women thrive tend to be more peaceful, democratic, prosperous, and better prepared to adapt to climate change. However, researchers warned in their report that 'multilayered crises undermine the status of women and threaten to roll back decades of progress,' citing rising authoritarianism, mass displacement, devastating armed conflicts, and the lingering effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Using 13 indicators — ranging from education and employment laws to perceptions of safety and levels of violence — the index assessed 177 countries globally. Euronews focused on the European results, which included 44 countries, encompassing the Balkans and the Caucasus. Nine of the top ten countries for women are in Europe, despite stark differences between nations. Denmark leads the 2023 rankings, scoring more than three times higher than Afghanistan, which ranks last. Switzerland and Sweden follow closely behind. Ukraine ranks lowest in Europe, with PRIO attributing this to 'particularly low' security scores, exacerbated by Russia’s ongoing invasion, which has increased threats and violence against women. Kosovo and Azerbaijan rank second and third lowest in Europe, respectively. In Kosovo, low scores stem from poor educational and employment outcomes for women, along with very high maternal mortality rates. In Azerbaijan, PRIO highlighted a significantly higher son preference — measured through skewed sex ratios at birth — compared to other European nations. Regionally, Scandinavian countries lead with a composite score of 0.925 out of 1, while the three Caucasus nations — Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan — rank lowest. The Balkans and Eastern Europe follow as the second-worst performing regions. Elena Ortiz, lead author of the WPS Index, stated: 'With its scores, rankings, and robust data, the WPS Index offers a valuable tool for people working on issues of women, peace, and security. Policymakers can use it to pinpoint where resources are needed. Academics can use it to study trends within indicators and across regions. Journalists can use it to give context and perspective to their stories. And activists can use it to hold governments accountable for their promises on advancing the status of women.'

article_content: This week, the UK is on track to experience its hottest Halloween on record, with temperatures forecast to reach 21°C — surpassing cities such as Athens and Rome. While southern England and Wales enjoy unseasonably warm, sunny weather, flash flooding has severely impacted parts of the Midlands and Northwest. In Dudley, West Midlands, students from Castle High School were filmed playing in deep floodwater on Ednam Road, jumping from curbs and lying down in the middle of the road — mere meters from moving vehicles. Teachers nearby worked tirelessly to manage gridlocked traffic as the deluge continued. Local councillor Khurshid Ahmed condemned the children’s actions as 'unnecessary risk,' citing a dangerous road bend that limits driver visibility. Headteacher Michelle King confirmed the school is identifying the students involved and will contact their families, adding that staff were 'saturated' trying to keep roads safe. Meanwhile, across the south, residents embraced the rare autumn warmth: families punted on the River Cam in Cambridge, swimmers braved the Serpentine in Hyde Park, and others relaxed in St James’s Park under golden sunlight. The Met Office predicts the heat will hold through Friday, potentially breaking the 1968 record of 19.4°C for Halloween. Yet in stark contrast, Scotland and the Northwest face persistent rain: Kinlochewe received 172.8mm in 60 hours, prompting amber warnings. For many, it’s a tale of two seasons — sunshine in the south, storms in the north.

Den Dudley, West Midlands, studiantenan di Castle High School ta fotografia ku ta bai pa ludi den aigua di inondashon profundo den Ednam Road, saltando for di e bordo i tuma den e mitat di e kaminu — a poko metri di bichinan ku ta movi. Maestrunan ku ta wòrk den e sitiu ta bini pa diriji tráfiko ku e chubu ta kontinuá. E konselh di lokal Khurshid Ahmed ta kondemna aksionnan di e kierden komo 'risgo nesésario', mencionando ku e kaminu ta tin un kurbu peligroso ku ta limita visibilidad pa konduktornan. E direktor di skol Michelle King ta konsirma ku skol ta identifiká e studiantenan involukrá i ta bini pa hablá ku e orangnan di e bini, amenta ku maestrunan ta 'mogá' intentándo pa mantiña e kaminanan segur. Mientras ki, den su part, habitantenan ta aprovechá e kalmu inesperá di otono: famínan ta puentá den Río Cam den Cambridge, nadadornan ta bai pa Serpentine den Hyde Park, i otro ta relaksá den St James’s Park ku e sol di otono. Met Office ta predikí ku e kalmu ta bini pa konservá hata vièrnès, posiblemente bira rékord di 19.4°C pa Halloween di 1968. Pero den kontraste stark, Escocia i Noroeste ta bini pa bini ku pluvia kontinuo: Kinlochewe ta bini pa rekibí 172.8mm den 60 ora, promoviendo alertan amber. Pa muhó, ta un historia di dos estasonnan: sol den su, tempestad den nort.

article_content: Serbia advanced to the Davis Cup quarterfinals with a convincing 4-1 victory over India in Novi Sad. Viktor Troicki, ranked 18th, sealed the win with a gritty 6-4, 6-2, 7-5 triumph over India’s top player, Somdev Devvarman. Janko Tipsarevic then closed the tie with a dominant 6-0, 6-1 win over Karan Rastogi. Serbia led 2-1 heading into the final day after Troicki’s five-set battle against Rohan Bopanna on Friday and a doubles win by Ilija Bozoljac and Nenad Zimonjic on Saturday. India’s lone point came earlier, when Devvarman upset Tipsarevic in straight sets. Neither team was at full strength — Serbia missed world No. 1 Novak Djokovic, while India was without legends Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi. Serbia’s next opponent is Sweden, who secured a 3-0 win over Russia in Boras. Even though Dmitry Tursunov and Igor Andreev won both reverse singles on Sunday, Russia couldn’t overcome the deficit. In Zagreb, Germany edged Croatia 3-2 thanks to Philipp Petzschner’s nerve-filled 6-4, 7-6, 7-6 win over Ivo Karlovic, after Marin Cilic had thrilled the home crowd with a victory over Philipp Kohlschreiber. France also advanced with a 3-2 win over Austria, as Jeremy Chardy clinched the decisive rubber against Martin Fischer. Jurgen Melzer had leveled the tie at 2-2 earlier by outlasting Gilles Simon in a five-set epic. In Santiago, Andy Roddick made his Davis Cup return since 2009 and delivered a critical 3-6, 7-6, 6-3, 6-3 win over Chile’s Paul Capdeville. John Isner finished the job with a 6-3, 6-7, 7-5 win over Guillermo Rivera, sending Team USA to face Spain in the quarterfinals. Spain, led by Rafael Nadal and featuring David Ferrer and Fernando Verdasco, overwhelmed Belgium 4-0 in Charleroi, with Nadal sealing the sweep by defeating Olivier Rochus 6-4, 6-2. Argentina, already through after a 3-0 start over Romania, completed their 4-1 win with two reverse singles victories. They’ll now take on Kazakhstan, who pulled off the weekend’s biggest upset: a 3-2 win over the Czech Republic in Ostrava — even after their hotel rooms were burglarized earlier that day. Andrey Golubev, ranked 43rd, stunned world No. 9 Tomas Berdych 7-5, 5-7, 6-4, 6-2, and Mikhail Kukushkin followed with a 6-4, 6-7, 7-6, 6-0 win over Jan Hajek to clinch the historic result. On the WTA Tour, Jelena Dokic won her first singles title since 2002 at the Malaysia Open, rallying from a set down to beat Lucie Safarova 2-6, 7-6, 6-4 in a thrilling final. It was her sixth career singles title and a powerful comeback story after years away from the top.

article_content: Michael Schumacher has recovered from pneumonia he developed while in a medically induced coma at Grenoble University Hospital, according to the German newspaper Bild. The seven-time Formula One champion had already overcome the infection before reports surfaced earlier this week. His family released a statement reaffirming their belief that the 45-year-old will continue to improve following the severe skiing accident on December 29, 2013, in Meribel, France. They emphasized that recovery is not about speed, but about steady, controlled progress. Schumacher was skiing with his son and friends when he veered off-piste and struck a rock, sustaining a traumatic brain injury. His helmet split upon impact — a fact confirmed by French investigators. He was airlifted to Grenoble, where surgeons performed two operations to relieve brain pressure and remove blood clots. He remained in a medically induced coma, under 24/7 monitoring. He received nutrition via a feeding tube, oxygen through a ventilator, and underwent daily physiotherapy to prevent muscle atrophy and pressure sores. His swallowing reflex, pain perception, and spontaneous breathing were still suppressed. Pneumonia is a known complication in prolonged coma patients, affecting 30–50% of cases, due to impaired swallowing and respiratory function. His medical team also managed risks of blood clots and urinary tract infections. His wife, Corinna, has stayed by his side throughout. The family has declined to share medical details to protect his privacy but promised to announce major updates. They thanked the global community for its support, saying it helps both them and Michael, who was still in the early stages of regaining consciousness.

article_content: On Friday, a Wisconsin man, Brian Stowe, 29, was sentenced to 27 years in state prison for drugging and sexually assaulting eight women — including a minor — and secretly recording the attacks. He will first serve 15 years in federal prison for the sexual exploitation of a child, following his January conviction. Stowe pleaded guilty in December to 27 felony counts: 16 for sexual assault and 11 for possessing explicit images of his victims. None of the women knew they were being filmed or photographed while unconscious; many trusted him as a friend or coworker. Several worked with him at Epic Systems, a health software company based in Verona, near Madison. Judge William Hanrahan described the crimes as 'cold and calculated,' noting the widespread fear they instilled in the community. 'The devastation is spread far and wide,' he said. 'It makes us all feel less safe.' The case began when a 17-year-old girl reported that Stowe gave her a drink, drove her home, and then assaulted her while she slept — filming the act. Police later searched his apartment and discovered hundreds of images and videos of other women, some taken during a 2010 business trip out of state. Although no physical evidence confirmed the use of drugs, investigators found a digital file on Stowe’s computer labeled 'drug assaults.' During the federal sentencing, U.S. District Judge Barbara Crabb noted that in one video, the victim asked, 'What are you doing?' Stowe, who holds dual U.S. and British citizenship, originally faced 62 felony charges. His plea deal reduced the count to 27. Prosecutors sought a total sentence of over 130 years; his defense requested the minimum necessary to protect public safety and allow rehabilitation. In court, Stowe said: 'I’m not going to have the normal life I would have had I not committed these acts. Please do see the good that does exist in me.' Five victims were present in court; one testified remotely. The Associated Press does not typically identify survivors of sexual assault.

Sinco viktima ta presént na kòrt; un a testifiká pa telefón. The Associated Press no ta identifiká tipikamente supervivientenan di asalto seksual.

article_content: A mother in China has been reunited with her newborn son after he was sold to human traffickers by a doctor. Dong Wan, 31, wept as she held her baby at a hospital in Fuping, following the arrest of obstetrician Zhang Lin, who allegedly tried to sell the infant to traffickers. Zhang reportedly told Dong that her son was born with severe health problems and would not survive. Believing this, Dong signed documents allowing the hospital to take custody of the child. Later, she changed her mind and urged her husband, Lai Guofeng, to contact police. Investigators traced the baby hundreds of miles away in neighboring Henan Province, where traffickers had resold him for a profit of approximately £3,000 ($4,600). Police in Shaanxi Province have arrested Zhang Lin and two suspected accomplices. Authorities are now investigating at least seven other similar cases in the region. The baby, who is healthy, is currently undergoing medical evaluations and is on his way home. Deputy Director Chen Jianfeng confirmed that the suspects cooperated by revealing the child’s location. 'With the help of local police, we found the child,' he said.

'Ku ayuda di polis lokal, nos ta hallá e bebé,' el ta dí.

article_content: To scuba divers and tourists, Belize's famous 'Blue Hole' underwater cave is a wonder — one of the '10 most amazing places on Earth,' according to the Discovery Channel. To scientists, it offers something more: compelling evidence of a severe drought suspected to have contributed to the collapse of the Classic Maya civilization. New research supports this theory, according to Andre Droxler, an Earth scientist at Rice University, who spoke with LiveScience. His team drilled sediment cores from the Blue Hole sinkhole and a nearby lagoon. They discovered that the titanium-to-aluminum ratio shifted significantly during the 9th and 10th centuries — a period coinciding with the decline of the Classic Maya civilization in the Yucatán Peninsula. Higher titanium levels typically indicate increased rainfall, as runoff from the region’s volcanic bedrock carries this element. However, between A.D. 800 and 1000, the ratio dropped sharply, suggesting a prolonged period of reduced precipitation. 'When you have major droughts, you start to get famines and unrest,' Droxler explained. The Maya civilization, renowned for its advances in astronomy, agriculture, and its intricate calendar system — often misinterpreted as predicting the end of the world on December 21, 2012 — dominated the Yucatán during the first half of the first millennium A.D. By 900 A.D., most of its major cities, located in what is now Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, and southern Mexico, had been abandoned. The cause of this collapse has puzzled scientists and historians for decades. While the drought hypothesis is not new, Droxler's findings reinforce earlier studies. In 2012, analysis of a 2,000-year-old stalagmite also revealed evidence of extended drought in the region during the latter half of the first millennium A.D. 'The main finding was that a prolonged drought contributed to the collapse of the Classic Maya civilization,' environmental archaeologist Douglas Kennett told LiveScience in 2012. Droxler and his colleagues published their results in the journal Scientific Reports.

E ta diskubrí ku rasio di titanio-a-alumínio ta kambia signifikativamente durante sékulo 9 i 10 — un período ku ta koresponde ku declin di sivilisashon Maya Klásiko na Península di Yucatán. Nivel mas altu di titanio ta indiká pluvia mas, pa kauza di drenashon di roka volkaniko di regiún. Pero ente A.D. 800 i 1000, rasio ta bai baixo markadament, sugeriéndo un períodu prolongá di precipitashon reduhí. Kauza di es kolapsu ta hasí kientifiko i historiador nan por pone pregunta durante dékadanan. Mientras hipotesis di sekka no ta nôvo, studionan di Droxler ta refuerzá studionan anterio. Pa 2012, analisis di un stalagmita di 2.000 aña ta revelá ebidens di sekka prolongá na regiún durante mitad di últime siglo A.D. article_content: CNN — Ahmed Shafik was Hosni Mubarak’s last prime minister. Now, he hopes to become Egypt’s first democratically elected president. He is running against Mohamed Morsi of the Freedom and Justice Party, the political wing of the Muslim Brotherhood, in the presidential runoff election beginning Saturday. Like Mubarak, Shafik is a former air force officer with deep ties to Egypt’s powerful military — described by Khaled Elgindy, a visiting fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington, as 'the quintessential candidate of the counter-revolution.' Shafik, who briefly served as prime minister during the final days of Mubarak’s presidency, was one of two candidates to advance from Egypt’s first round of presidential voting in May. The runoff between Shafik and Morsi will determine who becomes Egypt’s first democratically elected president. On Thursday, Egypt’s highest court ruled to clear the way for Shafik’s participation in the runoff, invalidating a law that barred former members of Mubarak’s regime from running. The same day, the court also dissolved parliament after declaring the constitutional provisions governing parliamentary elections unconstitutional. Despite his association with Mubarak’s rule, 72-year-old Shafik is attempting to present himself as a man of the people. In the weeks leading up to the May election, his campaign leveraged digital tools — including a website, YouTube channel, Facebook page, and Twitter account — to reach voters. One YouTube video shows him wearing a black T-shirt, greeting supporters and playfully pinching the cheek of a young boy. His campaign posters depict him in formal attire — suit and tie — with a subtle, avuncular smile behind his rimless glasses. His Facebook page features a photo of him as a young man alongside Egyptian President Anwar Sadat, who won a Nobel Peace Prize for brokering peace with Israel before his assassination. During Mubarak’s decades-long rule, Shafik rose through the ranks. When Egyptians rose up against Mubarak in January 2011, the president — nicknamed 'Pharaoh' for his long tenure — made his final cabinet shuffle, appointing Shafik from civil aviation minister to prime minister. Mubarak was ousted less than two weeks later, but Shafik remained in office for several more weeks, pledging his government would report to the military council that assumed control after Mubarak’s resignation. Shafik stepped down on March 3, 2011, after a short-lived attempt to shield Mubarak and his allies from prosecution. As a result, Shafik is backed by many who lost influence following Mubarak’s removal, according to Omar Ashour, director of Middle East studies at the University of Exeter in England and a visiting scholar at the Brookings Institution in Doha, Qatar. His supporters include 'the powerful ones — a coalition of businessmen and generals,' Ashour said. Some members of the Supreme Council of the Armed Forces may also support him, believing he would preserve the status quo. But Ashour doubts Shafik could win a fair popular vote. 'There’s no way he’d win without vote rigging — and if that happened, I think there would be a real risk of another revolution,' he said. Still, Ashour believes such rigging is unlikely, given the Supreme Council’s awareness of Egypt’s volatile stability. Shafik has drawn particular ire from the Muslim Brotherhood, Egypt’s longstanding Islamic opposition movement, which won the largest share of parliamentary seats after the revolution. In April, the Brotherhood organized a mass protest in Cairo’s Tahrir Square — the symbolic heart of the uprising — against the candidacies of Shafik and Omar Suleiman, Mubarak’s longtime intelligence chief. Although both were initially disqualified, Shafik successfully appealed the decision.

E mismu dia, e kòrt tambe ta disolver e parlamentu despues di declará e artikulo konstitusional ku ta regula e eleksion parlamentario komo inkonstitusional. Malgrá e liga ku el ta tin ku e goberná di Mubarak, Shafik, 72 aña, ta intentá ta presentá komo un hende di e populo. Na e semananan ku ta antecedi e eleksion di Mei, kampanha di el ta usa e herraamienta di e eda digital — inkluyí un sitio web, un kanal di YouTube, un pájina di Facebook i un cuenta di Twitter — pa ta konsigui e mensajá. Un video di YouTube ta muestra el ku ta usá un camisa negra, saluda simpatizanti i ta pinza e mejá di un muchachito lindo. E poster di kampanha di el ta muestra el ku ta usá ropa formál — traje i corbata — ku un sonrisa sutil, avuncular, riba e labia i e oio den tras e gafas sin marco. E pájina di Facebook di el ta mostra un foto di el komo un mucha ku ta ku Presidenti di Egipto Anwar Sadat, ku ta ganá Premio Nobel di Paz pa ta fá paz ku Israel antis ku el ta asesiná pa e esfuerçu historiko. Durante e decenanan di goberná di Mubarak, Shafik ta subí na e rangonan. Ku e egiptiano ta levantá konta Mubarak na januari 2011, e presidenti — ku ta konosí komo 'Faraón' pa e su durashon largu — ta fá e su últim shuffel di ministri, promoviendo Shafik di ministru di aviashon sivil a primer ministru. Mubarak ta kaba menos di dos semana mas tarde, pero Shafik ta permanesi na e kargo pa varios dia mas, prometí ku e gobièrnonan su ta reporta na e konsilu militar ku ta asumí kontrol despues di Mubarak ta renunsia. Shafik ta renunsia na 3 di mart, 2011, despues di un intento brev di protehí Mubarak i e su aliadonan konta e prosecushon. Komu rezultá, Shafik ta apoyá pa muhò di e ku ta perdí influensia despues di e remobé di Mubarak, segun Omar Ashour, direktor di studionan di Medio Oriënt na Universidat di Exeter na Inglatéra i un konsultant visitanti di Brookings Institution na Doha, Qatar. E simpatizantonan di el ta inklui 'e poderesonan — un koalishon di negosiantenan i generalenan,' di Ashour. Algun membro di Konsilu Supremu di Fuerzanan Armá tambe ta pòrtá el, pensa ku el ta preservá e status quo. Pero Ashour ta dudá ku Shafik ta pòrtá ganá un voto populo fair. 'E no ta posibel pa el ganá sin manipulashon di voto — i si e ta pasa, mi ta pensa ku ta posibel pa otro revolushon,' el ta di. Aisku, Ashour ta kré ku e manipulashon e no ta probabel, dado e konsiencia di Konsilu Supremu di e situashon volatil di Egipto. Shafik ta bini e objeto di ira spesifiko di Hermanananza Musulmán, e movimientu islámiko antiguo di Egipto, ku ta ganá e porshentajé más grandi di escao di parlamentu despues di e revolushon. Na april, Hermanananza ta organiza un protesta masiva na Tahrir Square, e kórdon simbóliku di e revolushon egipshian, konta e kandidatú di Shafik i Omar Suleiman, jefe di inteligensia di Mubarak. Ambos ta desqualifiká, pero Shafik ta apela i ta ganá.

article_content: Katie Holmes’ lawyer, Jonathan Wolfe, has confirmed that her divorce from Tom Cruise has been settled out of court. The agreement grants Holmes primary physical custody of their six-year-old daughter, Suri, while ensuring Cruise maintains significant visitation rights and joint legal custody. According to reports, the settlement includes specific provisions limiting Suri’s exposure to Scientology — prohibiting attendance at churches, events, or schools affiliated with the religion. These restrictions are designed to ease gradually as Suri grows older. Katie and Tom issued a joint statement affirming their commitment to co-parenting and respecting each other’s personal beliefs. Their representatives emphasized the desire to keep family matters private. Multiple sources indicate that Katie had begun planning her separation months before filing for divorce in late June 2012. One key step was the termination of Bella Cruise, Tom’s 19-year-old daughter, from her clothing line, Holmes and Yang — a move interpreted by insiders as a strategic step to distance herself from Tom’s inner circle. While Cruise’s legal team confirmed satisfaction with the outcome, reports suggest he agreed to a substantial financial settlement, possibly exceeding prenuptial obligations due to goodwill considerations. Suri will primarily reside with Katie in New York, accompanied by her nanny and security team. While some reports claim these staff members will accompany Suri during visits with Tom, others dispute this detail, and no official documentation confirms the arrangement. Former Scientologists have praised Katie’s decision as courageous, noting that leaving the church often results in isolation — including from one’s children. They believe the custody terms reflect a deliberate effort to shield Suri from institutional influence. The divorce was filed anonymously, underscoring Katie’s intent to avoid public scrutiny. Meanwhile, Cruise returned to filming ‘Oblivion’ shortly after the settlement, while Katie and Suri were recently spotted enjoying a quiet day at the Children’s Museum of the Arts.

article_content: A nine-year-old girl named Sonya has been removed from the foster home where she lived for over seven years and returned to her biological father, John McCaul — a man with a criminal past including convictions for transporting firearms and armed robbery. Sonya had been cared for by Kim and David Hodgin of Dickson, Tennessee, since she was two years old. The couple legally adopted her in 2008, but a Tennessee appeals court overturned that adoption in 2009 after McCaul successfully appealed the termination of his parental rights. In January 2024, a judge ordered Sonya to be returned to McCaul in Omaha, Nebraska. The Hodgins were given just three hours’ notice before she was taken from their home. In a heart-wrenching phone call recorded shortly after the removal, Sonya pleads with her foster parents: 'I want you to come and get me.' She describes her father’s home as dirty, with mold and cigarette smoke, and says there is no clean running water. McCaul’s relatives have criticized the Hodgins for publicly sharing Sonya’s story, accusing them of exploiting her image to fund legal fees — including allegations they sold T-shirts bearing her face. They insist Sonya was never mistreated and that McCaul, despite his past, has turned his life around and deserves to raise his daughter. Although Tennessee law prohibits anyone serving more than ten years in prison from retaining parental rights, McCaul’s sentence was reduced to eight years, allowing him to reclaim those rights upon release. His legal team argued the original termination violated due process. According to McCaul’s defense, he was not present during the armed robbery and was charged for a firearm in his vehicle because a passenger had it unholstered — claims not independently verified by courts. The Tennessee Department of Children’s Services maintains that birth parents have the legal right to raise their children, even when foster families have formed deep emotional bonds.

En un konsersashon di teléfonu tristemente sentí ku ta grabá pòsteriór a e keda, Sonya a implorá pa e foste papá: 'Mi ta bini pa bini pa kome mi.' El a describí e kasa di papá komo sucio, ku moho i fumo di sigareta, i el a dí ku no ta tin aña limpi. E Departamentu di Servisionan di Hihinan di Tennessee a mantene ku papá biolójiko a tin e drecho légal pa kresé e hihinan, mes ku e foste familia a forma ligaman emosional profundo.

article_content: For most people, running a marathon is a rare milestone—a dream reserved for a single lifetime. But for Rob Young, 31, a manager at a specialist car parts company in Richmond, South London, it’s just another morning routine. Every day at 2:45 a.m., he rises, laces up his shoes, and completes a full 26.2-mile loop around Richmond Park before heading to work. What makes Rob’s feat extraordinary isn’t just the sheer volume—it’s the story behind it. As a child, Rob survived years of brutal abuse at the hands of his father. He was beaten daily with whatever was nearby—slippers, sticks, wooden planks—and once, he was zippered into a suitcase and thrown down the stairs. The worst moment came when his father hung him by a rope around his neck from a coat hanger, leaving him gasping for air. His mother eventually escaped with him and his sister, but couldn’t care for them both. Rob spent years moving between care homes, surrounded by troubled kids and overwhelmed staff. He felt invisible—until someone told him, at age eight or nine, 'You’re going to turn out just like your dad.' That moment changed everything. Rob chose a different path. He threw himself into school and sports. At 11, his life turned around when he was taken in by the deputy headmaster of a prestigious private school. This man became his father figure—teaching him table manners, how to hold a conversation, and helping him earn top grades. 'I think of him as my real father,' Rob says. Today, Rob lives happily with his fiancée, Joanna, and their two young children. Earlier this year, while watching TV with Joanna, he decided to run 367 marathons in 365 days—not for fame, but to raise money for children’s charities like NSPCC and Dreams Come True. He eats what he loves—chocolate eclairs, Doritos, pasta—and still manages 6,500 calories a day. He runs slowly—about four hours per marathon—so he can still play football afterward and cheer on fellow runners, singing and handing out water bottles along the route. Rob doesn’t see his running as punishment—it’s liberation. He hopes his journey helps other children who’ve suffered feel seen, believed in, and capable of change. 'If I can help even one kid make peace with their past,' he says, 'then all the pain was worth it.'

article_content: A Canadian energy firm, TransCanada, has officially reapplied for federal permission to construct the Keystone XL pipeline — a 1,700-mile project designed to transport heavy crude from Canada’s oil sands to refineries along the U.S. Gulf Coast. The new application focuses specifically on a revised route through Nebraska, intended to bypass the critical Ogallala Aquifer, a major source of drinking water and irrigation for the region. The U.S. State Department confirmed it will conduct a fresh, in-depth evaluation of the proposal, pledging transparency and independence by bringing in an external contractor to re-examine previous environmental studies and assess any new data. While earlier projections suggested a final decision could come in early 2013, the agency emphasized that no timeline is set until the review process begins properly. The pipeline has long been a flashpoint in U.S. politics. Republicans, including former presidential candidate Mitt Romney, have accused President Obama of stalling the project for electoral gain, arguing it would create thousands of jobs and reduce reliance on oil from unstable regions. They point to a provision inserted into the 2012 debt ceiling bill that demanded a 60-day decision window — a move the White House warned would result in automatic denial due to insufficient time for proper analysis. In February, the State Department denied TransCanada’s initial bid after finding the original path threatened the aquifer. Since then, the company proposed an alternative alignment, which Nebraska officials estimate will require six to nine months to fully evaluate. Public hearings will kick off the state-level review, followed by revisions from TransCanada and a final draft environmental report. Supporters like the American Petroleum Institute insist the project has already been scrutinized for over three years across multiple environmental assessments. 'The geology hasn’t changed. The data hasn’t changed. Why redo the work?' asked API’s Marty Durbin. But critics, such as Anthony Swift of the NRDC, counter that our understanding of tar sands oil’s climate impact has evolved dramatically since 2008 — making old reviews inadequate. While the southern leg of the pipeline — from Cushing, Oklahoma, to Texas — was approved in March 2012, the northern stretch remains in limbo. Oil producers argue that completing the full route would ease a regional supply glut in the Midwest, raising prices locally but boosting global market access. Environmentalists, however, warn that expanding tar sands infrastructure locks the U.S. into a carbon-intensive fuel source that may ultimately be exported, undermining climate goals.

La nôu aplicašon se fokaliza spesífikamente na un ruta revisá atraves di Nebraska, diseñá pa evitá el acuífero Ogallala, un fuenté primario di aguá pa beber i irigashon pa la región. El Departamento di Estado di Estados Unidos a konsirmá ku ta realisá un evaluashon fresko i profundo di la propuesta, prometiendo transparensia i independensia pa konsultá un kontratista eksterno pa re-evaluá studion ambiental anterior i asesó ku e nòu informashon. Mientrás ku e estimashon anterior sugeri ku e desishon final ta pòdi kumensá na e primer kuartal di 2013, e agensia a enfatisá ku no ta tení un timeline definí hasta ku e proseso di evaluashon a kumensá propiamente. El pipeline a ser un punto di kontrobersia na politika estadounidens. Repúblikanen, inkluyendo e eks-kandidato presidensial Mitt Romney, a akusá Presidente Obama di retardá el proyekto pa ganá votonan pa eleksion, argumentando ku e ta krea miles di empleonan i reducí dependensia di petróleo di regionen inestábil. E a señalá un disposishon insertá na e leh di techo di deuda di 2012 ku pedí un desishon den 60 dias — un movimento ku e Administrashon Obama a advertí ku ta garantizá rechazo por e falta di tiempu pa un evaluashon apropiá. Febrero, e Departamento di Estado a rechazá e aplicašon inicial di TransCanada despues di konsiderá ku e ruta original ta amenasa e acuífero. Desde entons, e kompania a propón un altenativa, ku e ofishialen di Nebraska a estimá ku ta nesesario 6 a 9 mes pa evaluá kompletamente. Audensianan públiko ta kumensá e evaluashon estatal, seguido pa revisión di TransCanada i un rascunho final di e declarashon di impak ambiental. Partidarien komo e American Petroleum Institute a insistí ku e proyekto a ser esaminá pa mas di tres año atraves di múltipli evaluashon ambiental. 'E tera no ta bini kambiá. E datonan no ta bini kambiá. Porke rehacer e trabao?' a preguntá Marty Durbin di API. Pero kritikonan komo Anthony Swift di NRDC a kontesta ku e konosimentu di impak klimátiko di petróleo di arenas bituminosas a kambiá dramátikamente desde 2008 — haisi evaluashon anterior insufisiente. Mientrás ku e sección sur di e pipeline — di Cushing, Oklahoma, a Texas — a ser aprobá na maart 2012, e sección norti ta aki pa e konsiderashon. Prodyusoronan di petróleo a argumentá ku kompletá e ruta kompletu ta ayudá pa reducí e sobrante di suministru na e Midwest, subí prension lokal pero aumentá e aksesu global. Kritikonan ambiental, sinembargo, a advertí ku expandí infraestruktura di arenas bituminosas ta atorná Estados Unidos pa un fuente di karbon intensivo ku ta posiblemente eksportá, subvertí e obhetivonan klimátiko.

article_content: CNN reported that Ariel Castro, the Ohio man who held three women captive in his Cleveland home for a decade, will deliver a lengthy statement during his sentencing hearing on Thursday. His sister, Marisol Alicea, said the statement will allow people to see 'the other side of Ariel Castro' — not the monster many believe him to be — though she emphasized she is not defending him. 'He must pay for what he did,' Alicea stated. Castro pleaded guilty to 937 counts, including kidnapping and murder, in a plea deal that spared him the death penalty in exchange for life in prison plus 1,000 years. Alicea said she and other family members will not attend the sentencing due to concerns that the evidence presented will be too graphic. The sentencing, expected to last hours, will include victim impact statements and evidence presented by prosecutors, who aim to establish a comprehensive record for potential future appeals. Michelle Knight, one of the survivors, is expected to speak. In a handwritten note posted on the Cleveland Police Community Relations Facebook page, she expressed gratitude for public support: 'It is comforting. Life is tough, but I'm tougher. Just when the caterpillar thought the world was over, she became a butterfly. Thanks.' It remains unclear whether Gina DeJesus and Amanda Berry will speak directly; they may submit videotaped statements or have family members represent them. Prosecutors submitted a forensic psychiatric evaluation by Dr. Frank Ochberg, a leading trauma expert, detailing Castro’s systematic abuse: brutal beatings, repeated rapes resulting in pregnancies, and violent abortions induced by abdominal punches. Ochberg noted that Knight, kidnapped first, endured the longest and most severe abuse. Yet she also acted as caregiver, midwife, and protector — even reviving Berry’s newborn when it stopped breathing and intervening to shield DeJesus from abuse. Castro abducted the three women between 2002 and 2004. They, along with Berry’s six-year-old daughter — whose paternity was confirmed by DNA testing — were held in his 1,400-square-foot home. The women were rescued in May 2013 after Berry shouted for help while Castro was out. Neighbor Charles Ramsey heard her cries and helped free them. Berry immediately called 911: 'I’ve been kidnapped. I’ve been missing for 10 years. I’m free now.' In a July YouTube video, the three survivors thanked supporters: 'Everyone who has been there to support us has been a blessing,' Berry said. 'I'm getting stronger each day.' They have not seen Castro since their rescue.

'El ta bini pagá pa lo ku el ta fá,' Alicea di. Castro ta pled guilty pa 937 kontos, inkluyendo rapto i asinato, na un acuerdo ku ta evitá e pena di muerte pa interkambiá pa vida na prisión mas 1.000 anyo. Na un nota manuskriptu ku ta publicá na Facebook di Cleveland Police Community Relations, el ta ekspresá agradesimentu pa apoiu di e pùbliko: 'Es ta konfortá. La vida ta difícil, pero mi ta más fué. Kòm ku e mariposa ta pensa ku e mundo ta terminá, el ta bini un mariposa. Grasias.' Ta klasifiká si Gina DeJesus i Amanda Berry ta bini da direkto; el ta pode presentá declaración videu ó ta mandá un miembro di famíia pa reprezentá el. E acusashon ta presentá un evaluashon psikiátriko pa Dr. Frank Ochberg, un espejalista di trauma, ku ta detallá abúsu sistemátiko di Castro: púntan brutal, rape repetí, embarasamentonan ku ta terminá pa púntan na e estómagu di e muhér. Ochberg ta notas ku Knight, ku ta raptá primé, ta sufrí e abúsu más largu i más severo. Pero el tambe ta akta komo kuidador, partera, i protetor — hasta reanimá e bebe di Berry ku ta ta pará di bini, i interponé pa protehé DeJesus di abúsu. Castro ta raptá e tres muhér nan entre 2002 i 2004. El, junto ku e bebe di 6 anyo di Berry — ku paternidat ta konsirmá pa test di ADN — ta mantiendu na kasa di 1.400 pies kuadrá di el. E muhér nan ta reskatá na Mei 2013 despues ku Berry ta gritá pa ayuda ku Castro ta fuera. Neibor Charles Ramsey ta oí e grito i ta ajuda pa libera el. Berry ta llamá 911 direkto: 'Mi ta raptá. Mi ta ausente pa 10 anyo. Mi ta libé ahò.' Na un video di YouTube di Julí, e tres supervivientenan ta agradésí e apoyu: 'Kada un ku ta bini pa apoiá mi i famíia mi ta un bendishon,' Berry di. 'Mi ta bini más fué kada dia.' El ta no bini ku Castro despues di e reskata.

article_content: While movie stars steal the spotlight at Comic-Con, a quieter group of performers is gaining well-deserved attention: voice actors. These are the talented individuals whose voices bring beloved animated characters to life — yet few know their names. At the 2013 San Diego Comic-Con, figures like John DiMaggio, Tara Strong, and Tom Kenny were treated like rock stars, a rare moment in the spotlight for performers who typically work unseen. DiMaggio, best known as the voice of Bender and Jake, teamed up with filmmaker Lawrence Shapiro to create the documentary 'I Know That Voice,' a heartfelt tribute to the voice acting world. Featuring legends like 95-year-old June Foray and modern icons, the film captures the deep bonds and mutual respect among voice artists. Unlike on-camera acting, where competition can turn toxic, the voice acting community thrives on collaboration. Many actors say they’re drawn to the craft not for fame, but for the joy of creation. Though studios increasingly hire big-name celebrities to boost box office appeal, veteran performers argue that genuine skill and emotional depth matter far more than a famous surname. DiMaggio jokes that he loves staying anonymous off-convention floors — 'I didn’t get into this to be famous, I got into it to work.' Strong adds that once a character is born in your mind, it stays there, ready to emerge without confusion. As audiences begin to recognize these voices, the community hopes the respect follows — not just at Comic-Con, but everywhere.

Na Comic-Con di San Diego 2013, figuranan komo John DiMaggio, Tara Strong i Tom Kenny ta tratá komo rockstars, un moménto raro na e luz di e spot pa prestajantes kué típicamente ta trabá bai e ojónan. DiMaggio, konosí komo e bòz di Bender i Jake, ta kombiná ku e filmaker Lawrence Shapiro pa krea e dokumental 'I Know That Voice,' un tributu sincero pa e mundo di aktor di bòz. Kon e presénsia di leyendas komo June Foray di 95 aña i íkononan modèrn, e film ta kapta e ligamanan profundo i respetu mutuo ente aktor di bòz. Diferente di e aktsi na kinesa, ku kompetensia ta pone pa tóxiko, e komunidat di aktor di bòz ta prosperá pa kolaborashon. Munchu aktornan ta dike ku ta atrai pa e kariranan pa no pa fama, mas pa e gozo di krea. Aksí ku studionan ta konsidera más i más aktornan famós pa subí e interé di e boza, prestajantenan antiguonan ta argumenta ku habildat real i profundidat emosional ta mihó ku un nombra famós. DiMaggio ta burlá ku ta gusá sta anonimu fora di e kongresonan — 'Mi no ta entre na e kariranan pa ser famós, mi ta entre pa trabá.' Strong ta adiconá ku un vez ku un karaktèr ta nase na mente, el ta sta ahí, prepará pa salí sin confundí. Ku e audiensianan ta kumensá konosé esas bòzenan, e komunidat ta esperá ku e respetu ta seguí — no solo na Comic-Con, mas tónan.

article_content: Though Christmas is still three months away, those hoping to decorate with extraordinary opulence had better start saving—only the wealthiest can afford the dazzling gold Christmas tree unveiled by Takashimaya department store in Tokyo. The tree, priced at £6 million (1 billion yen), features solid gold branches adorned with gold cups, pots, candle stands, and a golden star. Festive touches include red baubles, bows, and flowers for contrast. The exhibit is part of a wider gold products showcase currently running in Tokyo. Also on display: a pair of 80-kilogram gold Chinese lions (40kg each) and a 1.8-kilogram pure gold dragon, valued at £6 million and £171,000 respectively. Due to the immense value of the items, security personnel were stationed nearby to prevent theft. The exhibition highlights not only artistic craftsmanship but also the extreme end of luxury consumption.

E arbol, ku ta való £6 mion (1 mion di yén), ta ten rama di oro sólido adorná ku tazas, ollas, portavelas, i un estrella di oro. Toques di festa ta inklui bolas roho, lazos, i flor pa kontraste. Por e valor enorm di e objèt, seguridat ta sta na sida pa prenbi rob. E exhibishon ta rejesá no solamente e habildad artístico, tambe e extremo di konsumo di luksu.

article_content: Google’s Eric Schmidt is not naive. The tech executive has traveled extensively around the world—like the nerdy version of Carmen Sandiego—engaging with communities in isolated regions such as Myanmar and North Korea to discuss the transformative potential of the internet. He cites sobering statistics: only 2.7 billion people, or 39% of the global population, are online; just 7% of households in Africa have internet access; and countries like East Timor, Ethiopia, and Burundi report near-zero internet penetration. Yet, despite—or perhaps because of—these realities, Schmidt declared over the weekend that ‘everyone’ on Earth will be connected by 2020. ‘For every person online, there are two who are not,’ he wrote on Google+. ‘By the end of the decade, everyone on Earth will be connected.’ That’s roughly six years, eight months, and 15 days away. It sounds ambitious—and it likely is. As countless bloggers and Twitter users noted in the past 24 hours, even basic infrastructure like improved sanitation is still inaccessible to 37% of the global population. Rather than dismissing Schmidt’s prediction as unrealistic, we should treat it as a call to action. Access to information is a human right. Until a Star Trek-style universal knowledge interface emerges, the internet—on smartphones and legacy computers—is our most powerful tool to deliver it. Universal connectivity by 2020 is a worthy goal. If not by then, then soon after. Mobile technology may accelerate progress, but nothing is guaranteed. It’s undeniably convenient—and slightly self-serving—that Schmidt, whose company effectively shapes the modern internet, is leading this charge. Google stands to benefit financially from global digital expansion, and Schmidt promoted a new book on the topic, The New Digital Age, published in April 2013. Still, someone had to set a bold target. And Google’s resources and influence may uniquely position Schmidt and his team to drive meaningful change. His recent travels offer insight into the challenges ahead. In January, he visited North Korea. His daughter, Sophie, observed: ‘Ordinary North Koreans live in a near-total information bubble, without any true frame of reference... They’re hostages in their own country, unaware of their captivity.’ Access to unbiased global information could reshape perceptions and ease tensions between North and South Korea. But technology alone isn’t enough. Governments worldwide must dismantle censorship regimes and halt digital surveillance of citizens—a far greater hurdle than laying fiber optic cables. Schmidt’s March trip to Myanmar further illustrates the complexity. ‘A mobile phone costs $1,000 per year and doesn’t really work anyway,’ he wrote. ‘There is no data service on their mobile network and no international roaming... Myanmar is one of the last countries to connect to the internet—and it won’t be smooth.’ He also wonders whether cultural factors will guide the internet’s impact: ‘Because of the phenomenon of anchoring—where people fixate on the first information they receive—will the internet fuel division after 60 years of isolation, or will the Burmese people’s inherent goodwill lead to a peaceful transition?’ I hope for the latter—and I hope it happens soon.
translated_content: Eric Schmidt di Google ta no tonti. E tekniko ta bai pa mundu todo—komo e versión nerd di Carmen Sandiego—hablando ku gente na lugar isolá komo Myanmar i Kòrèa di Norte pa diskutí e potensial di e internet. E ta sibiri estadistika konsiderá: só 2.7 miliard di hende, o 39% di e populasión global, ta konectá; só 7% di kas na Afrika ta tin aksesu pa internet; i paises komo Timor Oriental, Etiopía i Burundi ta tin nivél di aksesu pa internet casi nulo. Pero malgre—ó talvez porke—esos realidat, Schmidt ta afirma pa fin di seman pasa ku ‘todo hende’ na tierra ta ta konectá pa 2020. ‘Pa ogu hende ku ta online, ta dos ku ta no,’ e ta skribí na Google+. ‘Pa fin di e dékada, todo hende na tierra ta ta konectá.’ E ta mas o menos 6 aña, 8 mes i 15 dia pa bini. E ta sona ambisioso—i e ta probabelmenti. Komo tantu blogger i usuario di Twitter ta nota na 24 ora pasa, hasta infraestruktura básica komo sanitasión mejora ta akesible pa 37% di populasión global. Mas bien ku despreciá e predikshon di Schmidt komo irrealistiko, nos ta tin ku trata e komo un kall di aksión. Aksesu pa informashon ta un dretu humanu. Hasta ku un interfás universal di informashon tipo Star Trek ta inventá, e internet—na smartphone i komputador antiko—ta e instrumento más poderoso ku nos tin pa distribuí e. Koneksión universal pa 2020 ta un meta dignu. Si no pa entons, presto después. Teknolojia móbil ta pode akelera progreso, pero nada ta garantizá. E ta indudabelmenti kómodo—i un poko egoístiko—ku Schmidt, ku kompanía e ta forma e internet modernu, ta liderá esé kausa. Google ta beneficiá finansieramente di ekspansión digital global, i Schmidt ta promoví un libri nou, The New Digital Age, publicá na april 2013. Pero algién ta tin ku pone un meta ambisioso. I recursos i influensia di Google ta puede posishoná Schmidt i e su team pa promove kambiá signifikativu. Sua biaha recenti ta ofresí insigh den desafio. Na januari, e ta bai pa Kòrèa di Norte. Su hija, Sophie, ta observá: ‘Hende normal na Kòrèa di Norte ta bivi na un burbuja di informashon casi total, sin ningun referensia real... E ta rehen di su propiu pais, sin konsientsia di e situashon.’ Aksesu pa informashon global objektivo ta pode transformá perspetiva i disminuí tensión entre Kòrèa di Norte i Sur. Pero tekonolojia sola ta no sufisienti. Gobièrnos mundial ta tin ku desmantelá leyes di sensura i pará surveilansia digital di sidadon—un obstakulo mucha más difícil ku pone kable di fibra óptika. Biaha di Schmidt na marts na Myanmar ta ilustrá komplikashon. ‘Un telefonu móbil ta kosta $1,000 pa aña i ta no funciona bini,’ e ta skribí. ‘Nan ta tin servisio di datos na red móbil i nan ta tin roaming internacional... Myanmar ta un di e últimu paises pa konektá ku internet—i e ta no ta fasil.’ E ta pregunta tambe si faktor kultural ta guida e impactu di internet: ‘Porke e fenomeno di ‘ancoraje’—ku hende ta kré e primé informashon ku e ta oye—será e internet usa pa inflamá interes spesial despues di 60 aña di silensio, o ta e naturaleza fundamental di hende Burmes ta prevalese i e transishon ta ta más suave ku mucha gente ta pensa?’ Espero pa e transishon más suave—i espero ku e ta bini presto.

article_content: Two best friends, Kelly Seymour and Victoria Bolger, have defied odds estimated at 250,000-to-1 by giving birth to baby boys on the same day—at the same hospital—just two hours and thirteen minutes apart. The 31-year-olds have been inseparable since age three, growing up like sisters. They attended the same nursery, primary, junior, and secondary schools, and even studied the same college course. Last Monday, both women unexpectedly went into labor at Nottingham City Hospital. Victoria gave birth to her second son, George, at 12:41 p.m., two days early and weighing 8 pounds 5 ounces. Just over two hours later, at 2:54 p.m., Kelly delivered her first child, Charlie, four days early, weighing 7 pounds 7 ounces. Kelly had been scheduled for a planned C-section that day—but it was postponed. Unbeknownst to her, the delay occurred because Victoria was admitted for an emergency delivery, effectively 'taking her slot.' The men in their lives—Karl Homes and Mark Stewart—were texting each other, joking that it would be funny if Victoria ended up delivering before Kelly. It happened exactly that way. Both mothers are now back home in Bakersfield, Nottingham, and hope their sons will grow up as close as they have been all their lives. Victoria, who works at Boots, said: 'We never thought it would actually happen on the same day—even though we joked about it. She was just down the hall, and we introduced the babies the next day.' Kelly added: 'It’s fitting that we shared one of the most magical moments of our lives. Her family is my family. She’s like my sister.' Ladbrokes confirmed the odds of such a coincidence are 250,000-to-1. A spokesperson called it 'an incredible story'—and Kelly’s partner, Karl, joked he was gutted he didn’t bet £10 on it.
translated_content: Dos amigu pa’i, Kelly Seymour i Victoria Bolger, ta defi’ e kota di 250.000-1 despues ku e dos ta da luz pa’i muchanen chikito na un dia, na un mismu hospitał—solo dos horan i trece minüt despues di un otro. E 31-años ku e dos ta ta inseparabel despues di e tres años, y ta grandi’ komo hermanan. E dos ta asiste’ na mismu jardín di infancia, escuela primaria, secundaria, i hasta ta studia’ un kursu mismu na kolej. Domingo pasá, e dos ta entra’ na labor na Nottingham City Hospital. Victoria ta da luz pa’i su segundu muchanen, George, a las 12:41 p.m., dos dia tempranu i pesa 8 libra 5 ons. Dos horan i trece minüt despues, a las 2:54 p.m., Kelly ta da luz pa’i su primèr muchanen, Charlie, kua ta katorse dia tempranu, pesa 7 libra 7 ons. Kelly ta tene’ un sección cesarian programá pa’i dia, mas ta postergá. E ta sin sabé ku e demora ta pa’i ku Victoria ta admi’ pa’i un entrega di emergensia, efektivamenta ‘toma su lugar.’ E hòmber di e dos—Karl Homes i Mark Stewart—ta mandá mensajen pa’i un otro, burla’ ku ta ser divertí si Victoria ta da luz antès di Kelly. E ta pasa’ exactamenta komo e ta di. E dos maderen ta regresá na Bakersfield, Nottingham, i ta esperá ku e muchanen den ta grandi’ komo e dos ta sido to’ su vida. Victoria, ku ta trabá pa’i Boots, ta di: 'Nos ta sin pensa’ ku e ta pasa’ na un mismu dia—mes ku nos ta burla’ ku e ta posible. E ta solo un pasu di distansia, i nos ta presentá e muchanen den dia despues.' Kelly ta di: 'E ta apropiá ku nos ta partilhá un di e momentonan más magik di nos vida. Familia di e ta mi familia. E ta komo mi hermana.' Ladbrokes ta konsirma ku e kota pa’i e koincidensia ta 250.000-1. Un portavoz ta di: 'E ta un historia realmente increíbel.' I Karl, pare di Kelly, ta burla’ ku e ta desapuntá ku e ta sin apostá £10.
