article_content: In 1987, Sylvester Stallone entered into a confidential financial agreement with his half-sister, Toni-Ann Filiti, following her allegations of long-term emotional and physical abuse. As part of the settlement, he provided her with a one-time payment of £1.2 million, ongoing monthly payments of £10,500, and an annual £31,000 trust fund for medical and psychiatric support. These arrangements continued until her death in August 2023 at age 48, after a prolonged battle with lung cancer — totaling over £3 million in financial support. According to court documents obtained by the New York Post, the settlement included the destruction of six audio cassette tapes that reportedly contained private conversations between Stallone and Filiti. One letter from her legal team confirmed receipt of the tapes and stated they were to be erased under the terms of the agreement. Stallone was referred to only as 'S' in the documents. Stallone’s mother, Jackie, now 91, publicly dismissed the allegations as a blackmail scheme, describing Filiti as a drug-dependent individual who exploited her brother during the peak of his fame. She claimed Filiti was taking 65 OxyContin pills daily and threatened to go public unless paid. However, Filiti’s son, Edd, has since spoken out, asserting that his mother’s claims were true and that she repeatedly recounted the abuse while hospitalized in Florida last year. He criticized efforts to vilify her memory. While Stallone has consistently denied any wrongdoing through his legal representatives, who argue that celebrities often face false accusations from relatives seeking money, no independent investigation has been conducted to verify either side’s account. The case remains a deeply personal and unresolved chapter in the actor’s life.
translated_content: Na 1987, Sylvester Stallone a firma un akordi konfidensial ku su meia-hermana, Toni-Ann Filiti, despues di su alegashonan di abuso emosional i fíziko duranti un periodo largu. Kom parte di e akordi, el a ofresé e un sumá di £1.2 miliun, pagamentonan mensual di £10.500, i un fondu anual di £31.000 pa kustodia médiko i psikiátriko. E akordi a sigui pa keda hasta su muerte na agosto 2023, ku ta 48 aña, despues di un batalla largu ku kancer di pulmon — totalisandu mas di £3 miliun pa apoyu finansiero. Segun dokumentonan kourtal ku ta obtení pa New York Post, e akordi a inklui destruksion di seis kasetnan di audio ku ta reporta ku ta konteni konsersashonan privá ente Stallone i Filiti. Un lètera di e abogadonan di e aklamá a konsirma recepción di e kasetnan i a señalá ku e ta tene pa ser borrao segun términonan di e akordi. Stallone a ser referí kom 'S' na e dokumentonan. Má di Stallone, Jackie, ku ta 91 aña, a desmiská e alegashonan kom un eskuema di chantaje, describindo Filiti kom un persona ku ta dependiente di droga i ku a eksplotá su hermano durante piko di su fama. E a klama ku Filiti a tén 65 pastíl nan di OxyContin pa dia i a amenaçá ku ta publiká e historia si no ta pagá. Sinembargo, hijo di Filiti, Edd, a hablá despues, asertando ku e alegashonan di su má era verdadero i ku e a rekordá e abuso riba yega na hospitaal na Florida aña pasá. E a kritiká e esfuerzonan pa vila e memória di e. Mientras Stallone a konsistentemente negá kulpa atraves di e representantenan lekal, ku ta argumendá ku sibilan, politikonan, i atletanan a menudo ta bini ta bítima di alegashonan falsa di familia i asosiadonan ku ta buská dina, na nan e investigashon independiente no a ser konduí pa verifika e versión di nda parti. E kasu a sigui kom un kapítulo personal i sin rezolber na vida di e ator.

translated_post: Stallone a pagá mas di £3M pa kalma e alegashonan di e hermana — i a destrui e kasetnan. 🎙️💔 Su hijo a klama ku e ta di verdá. Má a dja kom chantaje. Nadie sabe e historia kompletu. #Stallone #VerdadOuKasetnan #EscandaloCelebridad

article_content: Though marketed as a quiet tale of country life, The Archers has become an internet sensation — the most downloaded radio show in the BBC’s history. In August alone, it was streamed or downloaded nearly 1.87 million times, beating out even Mark Kermode’s popular film reviews on Radio 5Live (1.6 million) and Desert Island Discs (1.29 million). Despite its pastoral setting in the fictional village of Ambridge, the show’s emotional storylines and richly drawn characters have captured a massive online audience. Since its digital debut in 2007, The Archers has racked up a staggering 63 million total downloads, placing it second only to Radio 4’s Friday Night Comedy podcast, which has reached 70 million. Weekly, over 5.1 million people tune in live to Radio 4, while countless others catch up via BBC iPlayer on their phones or tablets. One major boost came last January, when the scandalous affair between Paul Crawford and Lilian Bellamy sent downloads soaring past one million for the first time. Fans also recognize beloved actors like Edward Kelsey as Joe, Philip Molloy as William, Tamsin Greig as Debbie Travers-Macy, Rosalind Adams as Clarrie, and Trevor Harrison as Eddie Grundy — voices that have become part of British daily life.
translated_content: Aunque ta bini komo un kònto silensioso di vida rural, The Archers a bini un sensashon di internet — e programa di radio mas bajá na historia di BBC. Na agosto, ta bini bajá o streamá casi 1.87 mion di veçes, superando hasta e kritika di filme di Mark Kermode na Radio 5Live (1.6 mion) i Desert Island Discs (1.29 mion). Malgre su ambientashon pastoral na e villia fikshonal di Ambridge, e historias emosional i karaktèrnan rikament desarrollá di e programa a kaptá un audiénsia masiva online. Desde su debut digital na 2007, The Archers a reuni 63 mion di bajadas totál, poniendu lo na segundu lugá solamente despues di e podcast Friday Night Comedy di Radio 4, ku ta alcanzá 70 mion. Semanalmenti, mas di 5.1 mion di persona ta sienta pa Radio 4, mientras ku montonanan otro ta konsultá pa BBC iPlayer na telefonu o tablet. Un auménto grandi a bini na januari pasá, ku e aventura scandalosu ente Paul Crawford i Lilian Bellamy a mandá e bajadas pa mas di un mion pa primèr veç. Bistantenan tamién konosí e atorinan estimá komo Edward Kelsey komo Joe, Philip Molloy komo William, Tamsin Greig komo Debbie Travers-Macy, Rosalind Adams komo Clarrie, i Trevor Harrison komo Eddie Grundy — voes ku a bini partidu di la vida britániko di dia a dia.
post_content: Who knew a show about farm folk could dominate the charts? 🌾🎧 The Archers is now the BBC’s #1 most-downloaded radio show — 1.87M downloads in Aug alone! Even outshines Desert Island Discs & Mark Kermode. 63M downloads since 2007. #TheArchers #BBCRadio #SoapOperaSurprise #PodcastKing

article_content: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel claims that nothing less than winning the Premier League will be acceptable for incoming manager Louis van Gaal next season. The Dutchman is expected to be officially confirmed as David Moyes’ successor next week and will be charged with restoring the club to its former glory after a dismal campaign that ended in seventh place. While returning to Champions League football would be a positive step, Schmeichel insists the 62-year-old will set his sights even higher. ‘The club needs a strong leader to guide us back to the top,’ he said. ‘We finished seventh, so top four might seem like a reasonable target—but Van Gaal won’t settle for that. He’ll aim to win.’ Manchester United are expected to make significant signings as Van Gaal rebuilds the squad. Schmeichel believes two players strongly linked to the club—Toni Kroos and Mats Hummels—would be excellent additions. ‘United have players like Phil Jones, Chris Smalling, and Jonny Evans, but according to media reports, Hummels is a target,’ he told the Daily Express. ‘He’s a great starting point—he’s a natural leader and one of the best defenders in Europe. We’ve been watching him for years.’ A central midfielder is also a priority. Van Gaal is expected to pursue Germany international Toni Kroos, a name long associated with United. ‘We need a midfielder like Toni Kroos—someone who’s been linked for a long time and would be a tremendous asset. We need players who can instill or restore confidence in the club and the squad.’
translated_content: E ex-jugador di portero di Manchester United, Peter Schmeichel, ta di ke nada mas ke ganá e Premier League ta sufisiente pa e nwe entrenadó, Louis van Gaal, pa pròksima temporada. E holandés ta espèkta ku el ta konsirmá komo suksesór di David Moyes na pròksima semanana, i ta ta karga di restaura e klup a e gloria anterior despues di un temporada desastrosa ku ta akabá na sètimo lugá. Van Gaal ta espèkta ku el ta sigui interes di su presesor pa e internacional aleman Toni Kroos. ‘Nos ta nesesita un mediocampista komo Toni Kroos—alguien ku ta ligá pa aña nan i ku ta un adision tremenda. article_content: On October 18, 2013, CNN Student News highlighted key global developments as the week drew to a close. The program covered the U.S. government’s agreement to raise its borrowing limit following negotiations in Washington, D.C., ending a brief government shutdown. It also explored the persistent issue of modern-day slavery and its global reach. Viewers were introduced to a possible meteorite fragment discovered in Russia in February 2013 — reported on in this October segment due to ongoing analysis — weighing more than 1,200 pounds. The program also examined Spain’s long-standing consideration of switching time zones to better align with its economic partners. To support learning, the site offered a transcript of the broadcast — noting possible delays in publication — along with a downloadable daily curriculum in PDF format, interactive maps of North America, Europe, Russia, and Spain, and a weekly news quiz testing knowledge on the week’s featured stories. Quiz questions addressed topics such as the identity of MRSA (a bacterium), the location of the Swat Valley (Pakistan), the name of the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca (Hajj), and the U.S. holiday observed on the second Monday in October (Columbus Day, also recognized as Dia de la Raza in many Latin American countries). The program also honored former Army Captain William Swenson, recipient of the Medal of Honor — awarded in October 2013 — and encouraged student feedback through an open comment system, inviting educators to share how they integrate the material into their classrooms.

A tabata tuma e kere di esklavitud moderno i su rango global. E mira a bini kon e posibel fragmentu di meteorito hallá na Rusia na februari, 2013 — reportá na e sección di oktôber por e analisis kontinuo — ku pèsó mas di 1,200 libras. Programa a tabata eksamina tambe e konsiderashon di España pa kambiá su zona di tiempu pa aliniá mehor ku e so partner ekonomiko. Preguntas di e kwestionario a trata temanan komo identidat di MRSA (un bakteria), lokashon di Valle di Swat (Pakistan), nomber di peregrinashon islámiko a Meca (Hajj), i e festa di Estados Unidos ku ta observá na e segundu lunes di oktôber (Día di Kolombu, tambe konosí komo Día di la Raza na muchu paises Latinuamerikano). article_content: In December 2023, a 21-year-old Louisiana man named Asani Woods allegedly attacked his pet pit bull, Tiger, with boxing gloves after she had an accident in the kitchen. Witnesses say he choked her by the neck, slammed her head into walls, and repeatedly punched and kicked her until she lost consciousness. The horrifying footage was captured by Johnny Dominick, a friend and drug suspect, whose phone was later searched by police during a separate investigation. When officers reviewed the video in March 2024, they arrested both men. Woods was charged with aggravated cruelty to an animal; Dominick was charged as an accessory for recording the abuse and failing to stop it. Woods claimed he was simply 'disciplining' the dog, asking, 'What are you going to arrest me for? She made a mess.' Despite his claims, Tiger was taken to the ASPCA in January 2024, where she was euthanized after Woods reportedly told staff she was dangerously aggressive. Authorities say the video is among the most disturbing cases of animal abuse they’ve ever seen. Woods remains jailed on a $100,000 bond, while Dominick posted $135,000 bail and was released. If convicted, Woods could face one to ten years in prison.

Testigu di dice ku e a strangulá e pa e gorgo, e a bati e kabe ku e pared, i e a panká i kická e tin e ta pierde konshensia. E filmashon horribel a ser grabá pa Johnny Dominick, un amigu i suspekto di droga, ku e telèfon a ser buská pa polis durante un investigashon separá. Ku ofisia di polis a mira e video na mart 2024, e a aresta ambos hòmber. Woods a ser acusá pa crueldat agravá ku animál; Dominick a ser acusá komo aksesori pa grabá e abusu i no intervení. Woods a dixe ku e ta solamente 'puní' e per, preguntando, 'Ku ta mihó arrestá mi pa? E ta fá un desastre.' Autoridat di dice ku e video a ser un di e kasus mas disturbante di abusu ku animál e ta mira. article_content: Tony Pulis will spend Sunday contemplating a fascinating dilemma: how does a new manager convincingly criticize a team that has just won a cup tie 7-0? As one of football’s most renowned ranters, Pulis will surely find a way — and he’ll do so knowing his criticism will be justified. For more than 40 minutes of this extraordinary match, West Brom were outclassed by Gateshead’s neat, thoughtful passing. Pulis, unusually dressed in a suit, spent the first 15 minutes watching from the stands before taking to the touchline to bellow at his new players. Saido Berahino’s performance mirrored his team’s listless energy — until the 42nd minute. Then, Berahino scored from nowhere. And suddenly, dramatically, the floodgates opened. By the final whistle, he had netted four goals — West Brom’s seventh — yet offered no celebration. Pulis handled questions about Berahino’s silence with practiced diplomacy: 'Saido Berahino is a very talented boy. I look forward to working with him for as long as I’m here. There’s always transfer speculation — and you can see why. He has pace, balance, and scores goals. But when I arrived, no offers had been made. We’ll do everything we can to help him improve.' Berahino’s first goal came from a Chris Brunt free-kick that was twice cleared off the line; Berahino pounced with icy precision. His refusal to celebrate may have stemmed from embarrassment — what followed was cruel. Within minutes, he added three more: a stunning strike from the edge of the box, a simple conversion of a cross, and a fourth in stoppage time. Each time, he offered no reaction — just a shrug, a stare. Pulis, meanwhile, remained composed. He waved to fans, smiled faintly, and quietly prepared for the real work ahead. 'It was lovely to see the lads celebrate together,' he said. 'That’s the unity we need.' Gateshead, though outmatched, played with heart. Manager Gary Mills said: 'We knew we wouldn’t win, but we wanted to give a good account of ourselves.' Their dignity earned respect. The victory exposed West Brom’s fragility — and Berahino’s brilliance. But Pulis knows: seven goals are not the point. The real challenge is building a team that wins consistently — even when they don’t dominate. Tomorrow’s training session won’t be about praise. It’ll be about pressure.
translated_content: Tony Pulis ta pasa di sundi konsidera un dilema fasinante: komo un entrenador nueno ta pòde reprende un ekipa ku ta ganá un partidu di kopa pa 7-0? Kom un di e entrenadores mas konosí pa su rants, Pulis ta seguramente bini kun un manera — i ta fá e so ku el ta sabe ke e kritika ta justifiká. Pa mas di 40 minüt di e partidu fasinante, West Brom ta outclassed pa e pasé klar i pensativo di Gateshead. Pulis, usualmente vestí ku un traje, ta pasa e primer 15 minüt mira di e tribuna antés ku ta bini na e linia pa grito na e nueno jugadores. E prestaton di Saido Berahino ta refleja e energía apática di e ekipa — tótalmenti hasta e minüt 42. Entons, Berahino ta marká nan di nda. I di repente, dramaticamente, e portanan ta abri. Pa e final di e partidu, el ta marká kuatro gol — e sétimo di West Brom — mas el ta no celebrá. Pulis ta responde preguntas riba e silensio di Berahino ku diplomasia: 'Saido Berahino ta un mucha muy talentoso. Mi ta espere trabai ku el pa tan long ku mi ta akí. Siempre ta havi spikulashon di transferensia — i mi ta sabe porke. El ta rapid, balansá, i ta marká gol. Mas kuandu mi ta ariva, no ta havi ofertan. Mi ta fá e posibel pa ayuda el melhora.' E primer gol di Berahino ta vini di un tiro libe di Chris Brunt ku ta dos vece klareá for di e linia; Berahino ta aprovechá ku precizion frío. E nega di celebrá ta pode ser por embaraso — lo ku ta seki ta kruel. Dentro di minüt, el ta marká tres mas: un tiro impresionante for di e borda di e área, un konversión simpe di un kros, i un kuarto na e tempu di añadí. Oga, el ta no reage — só un shrug, un mira. Pulis, entretanto, ta konserva komposishon. El ta onde na e fan, sonríe levemente, i ta prepara silensiosamente pa e trabai real. 'Mi ta bon ku e mucha ta celebrá junto,' el ta di. 'Ese ta e unidad ku nos ta nesesita.' Gateshead, malgras outmatched, ta joga ku kard. Entrenador Gary Mills ta di: 'Nos ta sabe nos ta no ganá, mas nos ta quiere da un buen repräsentashon.' E dignidat di e ekipa ta merece respetu. E ganansia ta eksponé e frágilidat di West Brom — i e brillanse di Berahino. Mas Pulis ta sabe: siete gol ta no e punt. E desafio real ta konstrui un ekipa ku ta ganá konsektivamenti — even ku e ta no domina. E sesión di entrenamentu maña ta no ta riba elogio. Ta ta riba presion.

article_content: The so-called 'Forest Boy'—a young man who captivated German authorities with a tale of surviving five years alone in the woods—has been revealed as Robin van Helsum, a 20-year-old Dutch citizen from Hengelo. Far from living in isolation, Robin left his home just five days before appearing at Berlin’s city hall in September 2011, claiming to be a 17-year-old English speaker named 'Ray'. His stepmother recognized him from photos released by police, confirming his identity through a necklace bearing his name. Friends and schoolmates at ROC Twente said Robin had been struggling with personal issues and saw his disappearance as a chance to begin anew. He spun an elaborate fiction: his mother died in a car crash when he was 12; his father, Ryan, raised him in the wild using maps and a compass; and after his father’s death in August 2011, he buried him in the forest and walked five days to Berlin. But investigators found no trace of either parent’s death, nor any evidence of the supposed woodland shelter. German police, initially baffled by his refusal to show his face publicly and his broken English, eventually realized he was not a native speaker. With the mystery solved, officials warned Robin could face hefty charges for wasting police time—if the story is proven false. Though the tale was dramatic, those who knew him suggest his actions may have stemmed from deep personal distress—not malice. Authorities remain focused on accountability, but the human story behind the myth lingers.
translated_content: E 'Forest Boy'—un mucha ku ta kapitivá e autoridatianan aleman ku un historia di sobreviví cinco aña solonan den e bosk—ha sidu revelá komo Robin van Helsum, un mucha holandés di 20 aña di Hengelo. Lejos di bini aki den aislamentu, Robin sali di su kasa namás sinco dia antis ku el ta aparesí na ayuntamiento di Berlín na septiembre 2011, afirmando ku el tabata un mucha di 17 aña ku ta habla inglés ku e nomber 'Ray'. Su madrastra lo identifiká el for di foto ku e politia a libera, konsirma su identidat for di un kadena ku ta tin su nomber. Amigu i kompañeru di skol na ROC Twente ta di ku Robin tabata bini pa biaha personál i el ta konsiderá su desaparishon komo un okazion pa bini na un vida niew. El ta krea un historia kompliká: su mamá ta muerí na un akidenté di auto ku el tabata 12 aña; su papi, Ryan, lo kresí el den e bosk ku mapanan i un brújula; i despues di muerte di su papi na august 2011, el lo enterrá el den e bosk i bini caminando sinco dia pa Berlín. Pero e investigadornan no ta enkontá nin un pista di muerte di nan dos, nin evidensia di e supuestu refugio den e bosk. E politia aleman, inicialmenti bini pa konfuzión pa e nega di el pa mostra su fes, i su inglés mal, lo terminá di konsiderá ku el no tabata un hablante nativo. Ku e misterio resuelto, e autoridatianan ta avisa ku Robin ta pòtensialmente responsabel pa un kosta grand pa perdé tempu di politia—si historia ta probá ku ta falsa. Ku historia ta dramátiko, keda ku konosí el sugeri ku aksionnanan di el ta podi bini di distres personál profundo—no di malícia. E autoridatianan ta kontinuá konzentra na responsabilidad, pero e historia humán ku ta bak di e mito ta permanesi.

article_content: A revolutionary renewable energy scheme dubbed 'Poopy Power' could provide affordable heating for Britain, according to reports published today. Britain’s first commercial-scale project to convert dog waste into biogas for powering turbines is set to be unveiled after three years of development. The initiative is led by Streetkleen, a Flintshire-based company founded by Gary Downie, a former Manhattan banker now residing in Cheshire. He has secured the involvement of an unnamed English local authority. The system captures dog waste collected in public bins and converts it into biogas via anaerobic digestion — a process that breaks down organic matter without oxygen. Councils currently spend £72.5 million annually disposing of the UK’s 700,000 tonnes of dog waste in landfills. In London alone, boroughs spend £9.5 million per year managing waste from the city’s 800,000 dogs. Under the proposed Green Energy Scheme, a portion of this waste would be redirected to digesters that transform it into methane, carbon dioxide, and pasteurized fertilizer. Gary Downie, 42, designed a self-contained system capable of processing four tons of waste daily — enough to power up to 60 homes. He claims the system operates odor-free and can function efficiently on as little as 500kg of waste per day, generating 200,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity annually. Each tonne of dog waste diverted from landfill displaces approximately 450kg of greenhouse gas emissions. Revenue will come from waste processing fees and National Grid feed-in tariffs for electricity generated. Downie told MailOnline: 'People already understand the concept behind this and why it’s necessary — so it’s an easy step forward.' He added: 'We’ve received significant interest and are currently in discussions with councils across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.' Inspired by frustration over walking his baby’s stroller through dog-covered streets and parks, Downie — who spent a decade working in oil and gas finance — developed the system to turn waste into resources. The automated system removes waste from plastic bags and feeds it into a digester tank. The resulting biogas powers a turbine to generate electricity, while excess heat and CO2 are channeled to an adjacent commercial greenhouse to support plant growth using bio-fertilizer. Downie plans to cultivate Christmas trees in the greenhouse, donating them annually to schools. After holiday use, the trees return to the greenhouse to regrow alongside the children who received them.

Primer proyekto komersial di Britania pa konverti ekskremento di kánino en biogás pa pone en marcha turbinas ta listo pa ser presentá despues di tres aña di desempeño. Inisiativa ta liderá pa Streetkleen, un konsernu di Flintshire fundá pa Gary Downie, un banquier anterior di Manhattan ku ta vivi na Cheshire. É ta konsegui ku un autoridat lokal inglesa sin nomber ta involusá. Sistema ta kaptura ekskremento di kánino keda na bines públiko i ta konvertí en biogás atrabés di digestión anaeróbiko — un proseso ku deskomponi matería organiko sin oksígeno. Bai bini di e propuesta di esquema di energia verde, un porción di e residuo bai ser dirijí pa digestores ku ta transforma e material en metano, dióxido di karbon, i abonu paseurizá. Gary Downie, 42, ta diseñá un sistema autónomo ku ta kapas pa procesá katorce tonelad di residuo di día — sufisient pa pone en marcha hastá 60 kas. É afirma ku e sistema ta sin olór i ta podé funsioná efisientemente ku tan solamente 500kg di residuo di día, produzí 200.000 kilovatiohor di elektrisidat anual. Ingreso bai veni di tarifas pa procesá e residuo i di tarifas di alimentashon di National Grid pa elektrisidat produzí. Downie ta di na MailOnline: 'E pòbliko ya ta komprende e konsepto detrás di ezo i pa kua ta nesesarío fá ezo — asina ku ta un paso fasil pa adelante.' É aña: 'Nos ta resebi mu honor pa interes i nos ta hablá ku autoridat na Inglaterra, Escocia, Gales, i Irlanda del Norte.' Sistema automatizá ta konsigná e residuo di balsas di plástiko i ta mandá e material pa un tanke di digestión. Biogás resultante ta pone en marcha un turbina pa produzi elektrisidat, mientras kalor i CO2 ekstra ta kanalizá pa un invernadero komersial adyacente pa apoyá kresimiento di plantas ku abonu biológico. Downie ta planifiká pa kultivá árbol di Navidad na e invernadero, donándo e bini anual pa skol. Despues di uso di fiesta, e árbol bai bini bai pa e invernadero pa kresé denkanti ku e niño ku ta resebi e bini.

article_content: Money doesn't grow on trees—unless you're the University of Michigan, which is spending nearly half a million dollars to move one. A 250-year-old burr oak, the oldest on campus, will be relocated 100 feet at a cost of $400,000 to make way for the $135 million expansion of the M. Ross School of Business. Weighing 700,000 pounds and standing 65 feet tall, the tree has been a landmark since before the university existed. Though there's a 20 to 30 percent chance it won't survive the move, school officials are proceeding, citing its historical and symbolic value. More than 290 students and faculty signed a petition to save the tree. 'The tree is a symbol of strength and resilience and far predates the university as part of the landscape,' said petition signer Jenny Cooper to the Ann Arbor News. Environmental Design, a specialist firm, is managing the operation using a custom transporter with 100 independently operating wheels to carefully lift and maneuver the tree without damaging its root system. The move, planned for late October, involves isolating the tree's root ball like the center of a cake and transporting it on a rolling platform to a new location near Tappan Street. According to Paul Cox, vice president of Environmental Design, the high cost stems not from the move itself, but from the effort to keep the tree alive: 'When you're moving something that weighs as much as 300 average cars, that's what drives the price.' The expansion, funded largely by real estate tycoon Stephen M. Ross—for whom the business school is named—is expected to enhance facilities for students and faculty. While some question the expense, many on campus appreciate the gesture as a sign of institutional respect for nature and history.

article_content: Ed Miliband will today acknowledge that Labour cannot reverse any of the Coalition’s spending cuts unless they are fully offset by equivalent budget reductions or additional revenue — not through new borrowing. After three years of opposing nearly all government efforts to reduce public spending, Miliband is taking a pragmatic turn, signaling that if Labour wins the next election, it will not restore cuts to day-to-day services without clear funding sources. However, Labour remains committed to borrowing billions to invest in long-term infrastructure — including roads and power stations — and to implement a temporary reduction in VAT. This shift comes ahead of Chancellor George Osborne’s upcoming spending review, which will outline departmental budgets for 2015/16. Osborne has stated that while tax revenue is expected to reach £660 billion, spending is projected at £745 billion, leaving an £85 billion deficit — to be covered by borrowing. Osborne plans further cuts to welfare (£3 billion), and insists an additional £11.5 billion in savings must be found. Sectors including higher education, local government, and defence are likely to face additional reductions, even as the economy shows signs of recovery. Addressing Labour’s National Policy Forum, Miliband aims to reinforce the party’s economic credibility. He emphasized that both he and Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls are united: any reversal of austerity must be fully funded — no new debt. 'We won’t get to choose the circumstances of the next Labour government,' Miliband will say. 'If we win, we’ll inherit economic conditions tougher than any in generations. That must shape how we govern.' He added that public trust depends on credibility: 'Only if we show discipline in facing today’s challenges can we change the direction of our country.' Miliband also criticized the uneven nature of the recovery: 'It feels like a boom for those at the top — but for everyone else, wages are falling, prices are rising, and living standards are lower than at any point in our history.'

Despues di trés aña di opóni casi to e intentonan di gobierno pa disminuí gasto públiko, Miliband ta toma un kambio pragmático, señalando ku si Labour gana e próksima eleksion, el no ta pòdi restablese e kortes pa servisio di dia a dia si no ta klaro pa ondè e dinero ta viní. article_content: Marlboro, the most widely sold cigarette brand globally, is facing serious criticism for its 'Don't Be A Maybe' ad campaign, which critics say appeals strongly to teenagers. The ads, featured in more than 50 countries, show young people enjoying life—kissing against walls, snowboarding, playing guitars, crowd-surfing at concerts, and standing atop buildings overlooking cities—all while smoking. The message? 'Be Marlboro.' Public health groups including the Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids and several international coalitions argue these visuals deliberately link smoking with freedom, romance, adventure, and rebellion—qualities many teens associate with identity and belonging. They claim this violates ethical marketing standards and indirectly encourages underage smoking. Philip Morris International, Marlboro’s parent company, insists the campaign targets only adult smokers and complies with local laws. A spokesperson stated the claims of youth targeting are based on subjective interpretations, not evidence. Despite PMI’s denials, Germany banned the campaign in late 2013 after determining it attracted teens as young as 14. Similar concerns have arisen in other nations. Meanwhile, the World Health Organization and allied groups warn that every day, between 80,000 and 100,000 young people worldwide start using tobacco—a habit that kills nearly 6 million people annually and could lead to a billion deaths this century if left unchecked. They’re now urging governments to enact full bans on any tobacco advertising that resonates with youth.

Mensajé? 'Be Marlboro.' Ta dixe ku e kampanha ta bini kruza kodego etiko i ta estimulá fumá pa menores. Ta pedí gobièrnanan pa implementá bani kompletu pa anunsius di tabako ku ta apela pa joves.

article_content: Contrary to popular belief, many adults in the U.S. simply choose not to use the Internet—and most are perfectly fine with that decision. According to a recent Pew Research Center survey, 15% of American adults don’t go online, and a striking 92% of them say they have no plans to start. The study, which interviewed 2,252 adults nationwide, found that age and education are the biggest factors influencing Internet use. Nearly half of those aged 65 and older report never going online, compared to just 2% of young adults aged 18 to 29. Similarly, 41% of adults without a high school diploma aren’t connected, versus only 4% of college graduates. The top reason? Most say they’re just not interested, don’t see the point, or consider it a waste of time. Financial and technical barriers like lacking a device (13%) or finding access too costly (6%) play a smaller role. Even fewer—just 3%—cited privacy fears or cybersecurity concerns. Interestingly, many offline people still rely on others: over 40% have asked a friend or relative to look something up for them, and nearly a quarter live with someone who regularly uses the web.

E studia, ku ta entervista 2.252 adoltanan den toda e pais, ta demonstra ku e edad i e edukashon ta e faktoronan mas grandi ku influensia e usá di Internet. Mas o menos mitad di ebo ku ta 65 aña ó mas ta raporta ku no ta bini, kompará ku solamente 2% di jovenan entre 18 i 29 aña. Similarménti, 41% di adoltanan ku no ta tin diploma di skol sekundario no ta konektá, kompará ku solamente 4% ku ta tin un graduaashon universitario. E razón mas komun? Mestí di ebo ta di ku no ta interesá, no ta bini nesidá, ó ta konsidera e un pérdida di tienpo. Interesantemente, mucha persónanan ku no ta konektá aki ta basá na otro: mas di 40% ta pidi un amigu ó familiá pa buska algo pa ebo, y casi un kuartu ta bivi ku alguien ku ta usa Internet regulermente.

article_content: The tragic shooting of Trayvon Martin and the initial refusal by police to arrest George Zimmerman have ignited a national conversation about Florida’s 'stand your ground' law. Zimmerman, a neighborhood watch volunteer, claimed self-defense after fatally shooting the unarmed 17-year-old, who was carrying only candy. Many find it difficult to reconcile this claim with the reality of a grown man using lethal force against a teenager. Critics argue that if such conduct qualifies as self-defense under Florida law, then the law itself demands revision. At its heart, self-defense law hinges on reasonableness: if a person genuinely and reasonably believes they face imminent danger of death or serious injury, they may use proportional force — even deadly force — to protect themselves. This holds true even if the threat turns out to be imaginary. However, interpretations of 'reasonableness' vary widely across jurisdictions, prompting states to refine their standards. Until recently, Florida followed a traditional principle known as the 'duty to retreat' — requiring individuals to attempt to escape a confrontation before resorting to lethal force. The logic was straightforward: if more people stepped back, fewer would die. This rule also helped prosecutors build cases, since failing to retreat could suggest the killing wasn’t truly defensive, especially when facts were unclear — particularly when one party was deceased. An exception to this rule existed for homes: the 'Castle Doctrine,' articulated by then-Judge Benjamin Cardozo in 1914, held that a person has no obligation to flee from an attacker within their own residence. 'He is under no duty to take to the fields and the highways, a fugitive from his own home,' Cardozo wrote. In recent years, 'stand your ground' laws expanded this doctrine beyond the home to any place where a person is lawfully present — sidewalks, parking lots, bars. Florida’s 2005 law, among the broadest in the nation, explicitly states: 'A person who is attacked in any place where he or she has a right to be has no duty to retreat and has the right to stand his or her ground and meet force with force, including deadly force, if he or she reasonably believes it necessary to prevent death or great bodily harm.' Importantly, this protection does not apply if the person was engaged in illegal activity or provoked the violence. Moreover, once self-defense is raised at trial, the burden shifts entirely to the prosecution: they must disprove it beyond a reasonable doubt — a high threshold. In an ideal system, law enforcement would evaluate Zimmerman’s claim by meticulously examining physical evidence, witness accounts, and behavioral indicators — such as fleeing the scene or attempting to conceal evidence — to determine whether his version aligns with reality. Only if a reasonable jury could conclude he did not act in lawful self-defense should charges be filed. Ultimately, the legal outcome may hinge less on moral judgment and more on how Florida’s law interprets 'reasonableness.' If the law shields actions that shock public conscience, it may spark legislative reform — potentially saving lives in the future. As many suspect, Zimmerman may not have been forced to kill Trayvon Martin. But under Florida law, that doesn’t matter — if he believed he was threatened, and met the statutory criteria, he may be legally justified.
translated_content: E trájiko tiña di Trayvon Martin i e inicial decisión di e polis pa no arresta George Zimmerman a bini e atensión di e publiko na leh di 'stand your ground' di Florida. Zimmerman, un miembro di e barrio watch, a klaima autodefensa despues di e mator di e muchachu desarmá, ku ta kantando solo dulseria. Mucha gente ta dífikil pa konprenè e klaima den konteksto di un homber adultu ku ta usá fòrza letal kontra un muchachu. Kritiko a argumenta ku si e konduktu aki ta konsiderá autodefensa den leh di Florida, entons e leh mismo ta nesesita kambia. Den su kore, leh di autodefensa ta basá na rasonabilidad: si un persona ta kresé real i rasonablemente ku el ta fasa amenaza iminente di muerte o danu serio, el ta pòt usá fòrza proporsional — even letal — pa protehse. E ta vali even si e amenaza ta demostrá ku ta ilusorio. Sinembargo, interpretashon di 'rasonabilidad' ta variá amplamente den diferent jurisdisión, ku ta promp e estadu pa refina su estándar. Hasta hodi, Florida ta sigui un prinzipio tradishonal konosí komo 'duty to retreat' — ku ta rekerí e individuo pa intenta eskipa konfrontashon antes di recórsi a fòrza letal. Lógika ta sencil: si mas genti ta baká, menos genti ta mori. E regla tambe ta ajuda e prosikutor pa konstruí kazo, porke falha pa baká ta pòt signifika ku e mator ta no realmenti autodefensa, spesialmente ku e fakto ta obskuro — spesialmente ku un partidu ta muerto. Un ekseshon pa e regla ta eksiste pa kas: e 'Castle Doctrine,' articulá pa e entons juez Benjamin Cardozo den 1914, ta mantén ku un persona no ta teni oblijashon pa eskipa di un ataka den su kas propiu. 'El no ta teni oblijashon pa také pa e kaminda i e karretera, un fugitivo di su kas propiu,' Cardozo a skribi. Den aña reciente, leh di 'stand your ground' a ekspandi e doktrina mas allá di kas pa kualke lugar ku un persona ta legalmente presént — karreta, parke, bar. Leh di Florida 2005, un di e mas ekstremo di e nashon, ta klaro: 'Un persona ku ta ataká den kualke lugar ku el ta téní drech pa esta no ta teni oblijashon pa baká i ta téní drech pa sta den su posishon i kontesa fòrza ku fòrza, inkluyendo fòrza letal, si el ta kresé rasonablemente ku e ta nesesario pa prevenir muerte o danu serio.' Importante, e protekshon aki no ta aplika si e persona ta engajá den atividat ilegal o ta provoke e uso di fòrza kontra el mismo. Mas, un vegá ku autodefensa ta presentá den juicio, e oblijashon ta pasa totalmenti pa e prosikutor: el ta nesesita pruè ku e ta no rasonablemente autodefensa — un umbral altu. Den un sistema ideal, e polis ta evalua e klaima di Zimmerman pa eksamina minuciosamenti e evidensia física, testimonio, i indikador di konduktá — komo eskipa di e skena o intenta konselá evidensia — pa determina si e versión el ta koresponde ku e realidat. Solo si un jurí rasonable ta konsidera ku el ta no akta den autodefensa légal, e kazo ta nesesita akuzashon. Ultimamente, e rezultá légal ta pòt depende mas di e interpretashon di 'rasonabilidad' di leh di Florida ku di e juzgmento moral. Si e leh ta proteh akson ku ta sorprendi e konsensu publiko, e ta pòt spora reforma legislativa — potensialmenti salba vida den futur. Komu mucha genti ta suspekta, Zimmerman ta no ta fasa nesesario pa mator Trayvon Martin. Pero den leh di Florida, e ta no importa — si el ta kresé el ta amenaçá, i el ta kumplí e kriterio légal, el ta pòt legalmenti justifiká.

article_content: The 2013 Man Booker Prize longlist has been hailed as the most diverse in the award’s history — featuring a striking mix of debut authors, unconventional formats, and global narratives. Yet many readers might find it unexpectedly obscure, given the absence of household names like Margaret Atwood, JM Coetzee, and Roddy Doyle. Among the 13 contenders is Richard House’s 'The Kills,' a 1,000-page political thriller originally released in four digital parts. The first section, 'Sutler,' was offered free to readers who shared posts about it on Twitter or Facebook. Though the novel includes multimedia elements — short films and audio clips — judge Robert Macfarlane stressed these enhancements were supplementary, not advantageous. Five of the nominated books had not yet been published, underscoring the panel’s openness to emerging voices. Three first-time authors made the list: NoViolet Bulawayo, whose novel draws from post-independence Zimbabwe; Eve Harris, whose unpublished work 'The Book of Memory' explores London’s ultra-Orthodox Jewish community; and Donal Ryan, who portrays 21 distinct voices in rural Ireland. Returning nominees include Jim Crace, up for 'Harvest' — possibly his final novel — and Colm Tóibín, nominated again for 'The Testament of Mary'. Chair of the judging panel, Macfarlane, described the list as spanning centuries, continents, and styles — from ancient settings to modern-day Hendon, and from 100 to 1,000 pages. He noted a recurring theme: disaster, both personal and societal. Bookmakers have placed Jim Crace as the early favorite at 9/2 odds, but Ladbrokes admits this is one of the toughest longlists ever to handicap. Waterstones called it 'a thrilling list,' predicting one of the most unpredictable Man Booker Prizes in years. The winner will be announced on October 15, 2013, at London’s Guildhall, following a shortlist reveal in September.

Pero muchos lectòr ta pudi bini ku e lista ta mihó ku ta obskuro, den e ausensia di nombranan famosu komo Margaret Atwood, JM Coetzee, i Roddy Doyle. Ente e 13 kandidatonan ta Richard House su 'The Kills,' un thriller politiko di 1.000 pájina ku ta fòrma originalmenti distribuíu den katro partidonan digital. E primèr seksion, 'Sutler,' ta ofresí gratis pa lektòr ku ta publicá mensaje na Twitter o Facebook. Malgre e nobela ta inklui elementonan multimedia — filmetonan korto i kliponan di audio — juez Robert Macfarlane ta stresá ku e mejhó ta supplementario, pa no vantajoso. Sinco di e kandidatonan ta aindá no publicá, lo ta refleja e apertura di e komisión pa voznan nòvèl. Trè autòres di primera vez ta bini na lista: NoViolet Bulawayo, ku su nobela ta basá na post-independensia di Zimbabwe; Eve Harris, ku su nobela aindá no publicá 'The Book of Memory' ta eksplorá e komunidad ortodokso judío na Hendon, Londres; i Donal Ryan, ku ta retrata 21 voç distinti na Irlanda rural. Kandidatonan ku ta regresa ta Jim Crace, ku ta kandidat pa 'Harvest' — posiblementi su últim nobela — i Colm Tóibín, ku ta kandidat pa 'The Testament of Mary'. Presidente di e komisión, Macfarlane, ta deskribí e lista komo ta abrashoná siglo, kontinentenan, i stil — di ambientonan antikó pa Hendon moderno, i di 100 pa 1.000 pájina. Waterstones ta kallifika e lista komo 'un lista emocionante,' predizí ku e ta un di e Man Booker Prize mas imprevisíble di aña. E ganador ta anunsiá 15 di oktòber, 2013, na Guildhall di Londres, despues di un lista kurta anunsiá na septiembre.

article_content: In Paris, six members of the Roma community have been arrested in connection with a large-scale child exploitation network that forced minors to steal across Europe, including in the United Kingdom. Authorities say the operation, centered in an unauthorized settlement in La Courneuve, trained children as young as 12 in pickpocketing and other street scams—such as feigning disability at ATMs or pretending to be deaf and mute to solicit money. Those who failed to meet daily theft quotas of at least £250 faced brutal punishment, including beatings, cigarette burns, and threats of sexual violence. Among the suspects are Stejar B, 43, and Lucica T, 44, who are alleged to have used their own four children as part of the scheme. French prosecutors believe this group was responsible for hundreds of crimes since 2010, coordinating with Roma networks throughout Europe to send children to cities like London. While the exact number of child offenders active abroad remains unknown, police confirm these tactics were designed to work in any urban environment. Children caught by law enforcement rarely face prosecution due to their age and legal protections; instead, they are typically given warnings and released, allowing the cycle to repeat. In response, French and Romanian authorities are intensifying cross-border cooperation. Meanwhile, French officials are preparing new measures to tackle human trafficking and juvenile delinquency. In a separate but related development, former Interior Minister Manuel Valls sparked public debate by suggesting most of France’s estimated 20,000 Roma residents do not wish to integrate and should be removed—an assertion criticized for fueling discrimination. Earlier this year, Fehim Hamidovic became the first person in Europe to receive a seven-year sentence for managing a similar network involving up to 500 children.

Autoridatnan dike ku operashon, ku ta sentro na un asentamentu nelegal na La Courneuve, ta instrui minór tan jóven komo 12 a roba y otro skema di kalle—komó simula diskapasidat na ATM o simula ta sordo y muto pa pidi dinero. Ku ta falha pa logra e kantidat diariu di £250, ta sufrí punishamentnan brutal, komó golpes, quemaduran di sigarillo, y amenaça di violensia seksual. Ente e sospechosnan ta Stejar B, 43, y Lucica T, 44, ku ta akusá pa usa su propio kuarto minór pa parte di e red. Prokuradurnan fransé dike ku gruponan ta responsá pa hundres di krimen desde 2010, koordinándo ku rednan Roma na Europa pa mandá minór na siudatnan komo Londres. Mientras e kantidat total di minór ku ta operá na e exterior ta indeterminá, polis dike ku e táktiknanan ta diseñá pa funshioná na kualkier siudat. Minór ku ta atrapá pa autoridatnan raramente ta procesá pa konsidera su edat y proteksion lehal; en veç, ta recibi advertensian y libera, lo ku ta permiti e siklo pa kontinuá. Pa responde, autoridatnan fransés y rumano ta intensifiká koperashon transnashonal. Entretanto, ofishianan fransé ta prepara nuen planan pa kombati tráfico di persona y delinkwensia di menores. En un desaroló separá pero relacioná, e eks-ministru di Interior Manuel Valls ta sparki debát publiko ku ta sugeri ku mayoria di e 20.000 Roma ku ta bini na Fransia ta no tene intenshon di integrá y ta debe ser deportá—un asersión ku ta kritiká pa fomenta diskriminashon. Antes di e aña, Fehim Hamidovic ta bini e primèr persona na Europa ku ta sentensiá pa siete aña pa kontrola un red simila ku ta involukrá hasí 500 minór.

article_content: Robin Cocking, a 59-year-old database administrator, was lucky to escape serious harm when a 10-pound metal jackhammer chisel shot through the window of Asphalt Green, a popular gym and community center on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. She was working out on a mat when the heavy tool shattered two panes of safety glass and struck her, leaving only minor cuts on her hand, foot, and arm. Cocking recalled hearing the glass explode and instinctively rolling away—just in time. 'If it hadn’t been for that quick move, it could’ve impaled me,' she said. The chisel came from a nearby construction site for the Marine Transfer Station, a waste facility first proposed in 2006 under former Mayor Michael Bloomberg. For years, local leaders and residents have argued the site is dangerously close to schools and youth programs, with over 34,000 children using Asphalt Green annually. Carol Tweedy, the center’s director, confirmed her team had raised safety concerns multiple times. 'Of course this happened,' she told reporters. The city responded by halting all work at the site pending inspection. While Cocking received a tetanus shot and was released from the hospital, community groups like Pledge 2 Protect say this incident proves their warnings were valid—and that the city must act before someone gets killed.
translated_content: Robin Cocking, un mester di 59 aña, ta bini salbá ku ta tèn un kousa grandi kando un pèrti di 10 libra di un jackhammer ta pasá atraves di un ventana di Asphalt Green, un gimnasio i sentro komunitario popular na Upper East Side di Manhattan. E ta estra kando e ta trabou pa un mata i e ta bini konsénti un kousa menór na manu, pie, i brazu. Cocking ta rekordá ku e oí e vidrio ta kraké i e ta rodá automaticamente—tiempo pa salbá. 'Si e ta no bini pa e movimento rapidu, e ta pude kousá e impalá,' e di. E pèrti ta sali di un sitia di konstruksión pròksimo pa Marine Transfer Station, un depósito di basura ku ta propuestu pa 2006 bai e eks-mayor Michael Bloomberg. Pa aña, lideres lokal i habitante ta diskutí ku e sitia ta peligrosamente pròksimo pa skolashon i programa pa yunienti, ku mas di 34.000 yunienti ta usá Asphalt Green cada aña. Carol Tweedy, direktor di e sentro, ta konsirmá ku e ekipa ta reportá konsèrnan di seguridat mas di un bês. 'E ta bini pa bini,' e di pa e prensa. E siudat ta responde ku e ta pará to trabou na e sitia pa un inspeksión. Mientras Cocking ta riberá un inyekshon di tetanos i e ta salí di e hospital, gruponan komunitario komo Pledge 2 Protect ta di ku e incidente ta probá ku e advertensianan ta válido—i ku e siudat ta nesesidat akshoná pa nadie ta morí.

article_content: The Supreme Court of India is scheduled to hear a key appeal in February 2024 concerning letters rogatory issued by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) during its investigation into alleged overvaluation of Indonesian coal imports by Adani Group firms. In October 2019, the Bombay High Court quashed these international legal requests—sent to Singapore, Dubai, and Hong Kong—citing procedural flaws, not the substance of the allegations. Following the DRI’s appeal, a Supreme Court bench led by then-Chief Justice S.A. Bobde issued a stay on the High Court’s order in January 2020, preserving the legal status quo pending final adjudication. On October 10, 2023, a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices A.S. Oka and Pankaj Mithal ordered that this appeal be heard together with Special Leave Petition (Crl) No. 4821 of 2023, citing overlapping legal questions. The next hearing is set for February 6, 2024. Letters rogatory are formal instruments used by courts or investigative agencies to request judicial assistance from foreign jurisdictions when evidence lies abroad. The Bombay High Court clarified that it did not evaluate the validity of the DRI’s allegations, only whether proper legal procedures were followed in issuing the letters. The case stems from a DRI probe initiated in March 2016 into Adani Group companies for suspected overinvoicing of coal imports between 2011 and 2015. The LRs sought documents from overseas branches of three Indian public sector banks.

Na oktuber 2019, la Corte di Apelashon di Bombay an anulá esas petishon internashonal — mandá pa Singapur, Dubái i Hong Kong — pa kousa di faltan di prosedur, no pa mérito di akusashon. Despues di apelashon di DRI, un bench di la Corte Suprema ku ta liderá pa e antigo Juez Jefe S.A. Bobde an emití un suspenshon di e orden di la Corte di Apelashon na januari 2020, manteniendo e situashon legal pa espera di e decisión final. Na oktuber 10, 2023, un bench di la Corte Suprema ku ta komponí pa Juces A.S. Oka i Pankaj Mithal an ordená ku esapelaashon ta bini a oye junto ku Special Leave Petition (Crl) No. 4821 di 2023, pa kousa di preguntonan lejales similaire. E pròxima audiensia ta programá pa febrero 6, 2024. Las cartas rogatorias ta instrumentonan formál ku ta usá pa kurt i agensia di investigashon pa pidí asistensia lejal di jurisdikshon internashonal ku ta tené e evidensia. La Corte di Apelashon di Bombay an klariá ku el no ta evalwá e valides di akusashon di DRI, sólo si e prosedur lejal ta seguí ku emiti e carta. E kasu ta nase di un investigashon di DRI ku ta konsiderá na marts 2016 kontra kompanianan di Adani Group pa sospeha di sobreinvois di importashon di kòl ente 2011 i 2015. Las LRs ta pidí dokumentonan di sucursalanan di tres bankonan publiko indio fora di India.

article_content: A 48-year-old woman has been sentenced to seven years in prison for subjecting her 15-year-old nephew to months of brutal physical, sexual, and emotional abuse while he was under her care. The Brisbane District Court heard harrowing details of how she tortured the boy over five months, turning his life into a 'living hell.' According to the Courier Mail, punishments included force-feeding him chili peppers and laxatives, then denying him access to the bathroom to clean himself. On another occasion, he was made to ingest multiple worming tablets and castor oil before being forced to attend school without hygiene. Court testimony revealed further acts of humiliation: the teen was forced to shave his genitals and, on a separate occasion, was filmed by his aunt and her 20-something daughter while being coerced into self-penetration with a sex toy. The women threatened to release the video if he told anyone. Physical abuse included punches to the face, beatings with a stock whip, and the use of pliers to crush his fingers. He was repeatedly warned that a 'bikie friend' would kill him if he spoke out. Police were eventually informed in mid-2012. Judge Leanne Clare described the abuse as exhibiting 'focus, deliberation, and sadism,' rejecting the defense’s claims that the woman suffered from depression, anxiety, or PTSD due to her own past trauma — and dismissing assertions that the victim was 'difficult to manage.' The woman pleaded guilty in February, though she had initially planned to call the victim to testify under cross-examination. Judge Clare emphasized that the prolonged, intentional infliction of pain warranted the postponement of parole eligibility. Her daughter, who participated in the abuse, received a two-year prison sentence.

article_content: (CNN) — Supporters and opponents of Venezuela’s government held rival demonstrations in the capital on Sunday to mark the anniversary of the 1958 popular uprising that ousted dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez. In Caracas, supporters of President Hugo Chávez gathered near the presidential palace to hear him speak on what is known locally as National Democracy Day. 'Every day, there will be more democracy in Venezuela — this democracy that empowers the people,' Chávez said, according to the state-run AVN news agency. 'Democracy is as essential to socialism as oxygen is to life.' His supporters cheered, waving flags and banners. Meanwhile, critics of Chávez’s government assembled in eastern Caracas, the state-run VTV network reported. Many held white banners; one protester carried a sign reading, 'Enough of the lies.' Protests were also planned in cities worldwide, organized by Un Mundo Sin Mordaza, to declare that 'the current Venezuelan regime is a dictatorship, both legally and politically.' Opponents have strongly criticized the recent decision by Venezuela’s outgoing National Assembly to grant Chávez emergency decree powers for 18 months. They argue the move was intended to bypass a weakened legislature following September’s elections. Chávez, however, stated the powers were needed to respond effectively to devastating floods that left thousands homeless. January 23 marks the anniversary of the 1958 overthrow of former Venezuelan dictator General Marcos Pérez Jiménez.

Na Caracas, sostinientes di Presidente Hugo Chávez ta reúne na kierba di palas presidensial pa oírlo hablá so e dia ku ta konosí komo Día Nashonal di Democràsia. article_content: An Irish atheist group, Atheist Ireland, has published a list of 25 quotes it labels as 'blasphemous' to challenge the country’s newly enacted blasphemy law, which took effect on New Year’s Day, 2010. The quotes—drawn from figures including Jesus, Mohammed, Mark Twain, Salman Rushdie, and Björk—are intended to provoke discussion about the limits of free speech under Irish law. The law makes it a crime to publish or say anything 'grossly abusive or insulting' in relation to matters held sacred by any religion, if it causes outrage among a substantial number of adherents. Violators face fines of up to €25,000 ($35,800). However, defendants can argue their words had literary, artistic, political, scientific, or academic value. Atheist Ireland, which posted the list on its website, says it supports the right of any Irish citizen to express controversial views about religion without fear of criminal prosecution—or having to prove to a court that their statement holds societal value. The group calls the law 'silly and dangerous,' arguing it encourages religious groups to take offense in order to suppress dissent. 'In a civilized society,' the organization states, 'people have the right to express—and hear—ideas about religion, even when those ideas are outrageous.' Atheist Ireland is urging the Irish government to repeal the law entirely and hold a national referendum to remove all references to God from the Irish Constitution.

E kota—tomá di figuras komo Jesús, Mahoma, Mark Twain, Salman Rushdie, i Björk—ta intensioná pa promove diskusión so limita di libertad di eksprésión bai leh irlandés. E ley ta konsidera un krimen publiká o dihi algo 'grossamente abusibo o insultante' so kuestionan ku ta sakra pa cualke relihion, si el ta kausa outrage ente un númeru substansial di aderenti. article_content: Under President Obama, the U.S. dramatically expanded its drone warfare campaign in Pakistan, conducting 44 strikes in 2009 alone — more than in any prior year. Since 2006, an estimated 83 drone strikes have killed between 760 and 1,050 people, including roughly 20 senior militant leaders and hundreds of lower-ranking fighters. Civilian casualties remain highly contested. While some analysts, like David Kilcullen and Andrew Exum, estimated that drone strikes killed about 50 civilians for every militant — implying a high civilian toll — others, such as the Long War Journal, argued that only about 10% of those killed were non-combatants. Our analysis, based on reports from reputable media outlets — including the New York Times, Washington Post, BBC, Reuters, Dawn, and Geo TV — estimates that between 260 and 320 civilians died, representing roughly one-third of total fatalities. Public opinion in Pakistan remains overwhelmingly hostile: a 2009 Gallup poll found only 9% supported the strikes, while two-thirds opposed them. Critics, including U.N. human rights investigator Philip Alston, warn that targeted killings with civilian casualties may violate international law unless legal justification is transparently provided. The killing of Baitullah Mehsud, leader of the Pakistani Taliban and mastermind behind Benazir Bhutto’s assassination, was a rare moment of alignment between U.S. and Pakistani interests. His death in August 2009 was widely celebrated in Pakistani media, reflecting broad local rejection of his brutality. Despite backlash, drone strikes have disrupted terrorist plots — notably the attempted bombing by Najibullah Zazi, an Afghan immigrant trained by al Qaeda in Pakistan’s tribal areas. U.S. authorities found detailed bomb-making notes on his laptop, acquired during a period of intense drone activity. While drone warfare continues to provoke anger and retaliatory violence, it remains the most viable option for targeting militants — given that a ground invasion is politically and militarily unfeasible. With U.S. and Pakistani interests increasingly aligned against the Taliban and al Qaeda, and with evidence suggesting tacit Pakistani cooperation, the strikes persist as a controversial but strategically vital tool.

Nuestra analisis, basá na reporta di medio di komunikashon respetá — inkluyendo New York Times, Washington Post, BBC, Reuters, Dawn, y Geo TV — ta estimá ku ente 260 y 320 sivil a mato, representando aproksimadamente un terser parti di e total di mato. E mato di Baitullah Mehsud, lider di Taliban pakistán, y arquitékto di asesinato di Benazir Bhutto, a fui un momento raro di aliniamiento ente interesan di Estados Unidos y Pakistán. Malgrá e reaksion negativo, e atakos di drone a akitá plotan terorista — notablemente e intento di atako di Najibullah Zazi, inmigrante afgano entrená pa al Qaeda na regionan tribál di Pakistán. Kon interesan di Estados Unidos y Pakistán mas aliniao kontra Taliban i al Qaeda, i ku evidensia ku kooperashon taciutu pakistán, e atakos a sigue siendu un herramienta kontroversial mas vital strategikamente.

article_content: Months after being barred from the first Republican primary debate — a move that led him to file a formal complaint with the Republican National Committee — businessman Perry Johnson has paused his presidential bid. In a statement released Friday, he said, 'With no platform to present my vision, I’ve concluded that stepping back from the campaign right now is the best course.' Though he’s suspended his efforts, Johnson hasn’t officially dropped out and still appears on ballots in early-voting states such as New Hampshire, where he recently participated in the state GOP’s leadership summit. He becomes the third Republican contender to exit the race this year, after Representatives Will Hurd and Miami Mayor Francis Suarez. Johnson has been sharply critical of the RNC, claiming the debate qualification rules were manipulated to exclude him. He filed an FEC complaint against both the RNC and Fox News, accusing them of orchestrating a coordinated effort to control who gets on stage. When asked if he still plans to pursue those complaints, his team told ABC News he hasn't ruled anything out. 'The American people, not the RNC chair and her allies, should pick our next president,' Johnson insisted. A successful entrepreneur and author, Johnson poured nearly all of his campaign funding into his run: he loaned his campaign $12 million and contributed over $1.5 million in private air travel expenses, according to official campaign filings.

Den un declaración lansá na vièrnés, el di, 'Ku ningun platforma pa prezentá mi visión, mi ta konsiderá ku bini fòr di kampanha na e momentu hende ta e meyor kursu.' Toti ku el ta pausá su esfuerzos, Johnson no ta bini fuera ofisialmente i el ta sigui na listanan di voto na estadonan temprano komo New Hampshire, ku el ta partisipá na sumít di liderasgo di GOP di e estadu mes ku ta pasa. article_content: In a heartbreaking act of violence, Mohammed Liaqat Ali, 37, was sentenced to life in prison for murdering his wife, Lilima Akter Munny, 27, in their Birmingham home in June 2013. The killing followed months of bitter conflict over land ownership in Bangladesh, where Ali became obsessed with transferring property deeds into his name. He repeatedly threatened to kill Lilima if she refused to comply, and on June 13, he carried out that threat by strangling her at the foot of the stairs. Her body was discovered the next morning after a relative raised the alarm when she didn’t pick up their two young daughters from school. At trial, the court heard how Ali calmly pretended to search for his wife afterward, even as police investigated her disappearance. A post-mortem confirmed death by manual strangulation. Judge Patrick Thomas described Ali as having a dangerous combination of rigid thinking, explosive anger, and a history of domestic abuse. Although no weapon was used and the act wasn’t premeditated in detail, the judge emphasized the prolonged nature of the attack and Ali’s chilling emotional detachment. Prosecutors highlighted the cruelty of Ali’s deception toward the children, while the defense noted the absence of planning. Detective Sergeant Ranj Sangha called the case a devastating consequence of a long-running family dispute that ended in the loss of an innocent mother. Lilima leaves behind two daughters, whose lives have been irrevocably altered by the crime. Authorities hope the sentence brings some measure of justice and peace to her grieving family.

article_content: Welcome back! With the holidays right around the corner, here’s a friendly reminder to check in on your elderly family members — it can literally help save their lives, according to scientists. In today’s big story: What does $650 billion in unrealized losses mean for U.S. financial firms? (Hint: It’s not as bad as it seems.) As of September 30, U.S. financial institutions had accumulated $650 billion in unrealized losses, per Moody’s estimate — a 15% increase since June, largely due to the bond market sell-off. With selling continuing into October, the figure may now be even higher. That’s a staggering number — if it were a country’s GDP, it would rank just below the top 20. But these losses remain unrealized, meaning they exist on paper, not in cash. Like hoping to become an NFL quarterback, the outcome isn’t guaranteed. As Insider’s Matthew Fox explains, banks have tools to manage these losses: holding bonds until maturity (avoiding losses entirely) or selling them to reinvest in higher-yielding assets. Still, unrealized doesn’t mean risk-free. The Titanic was called unsinkable too — and we know how that ended. Perception matters. Even if a bank has no plan to sell, widespread fear that it might can trigger a run, as happened with Silicon Valley Bank. While major banks like Bank of America — sitting on roughly $130 billion in paper losses — have pledged to hold their government securities to maturity, circumstances can change. If bond yields spike again, pressure to sell could mount. Even without a crisis, these losses weigh on investor confidence. As bond prices fell, bank stock prices dropped too. Regulatory limits already constrain balance sheets; tying up capital in volatile assets further weakens lending capacity — and that’s happening just as new competitors enter the space. Elsewhere this week: Short-seller Jim Chanos criticized the crypto ecosystem as ideal for illicit finance. Bank of America identified 10 potential acquisition targets, including Ralph Lauren and Expedia. Two traditional recession indicators are flashing — but their causes differ from past cycles, suggesting a downturn isn’t imminent. article_content: A letter bomb addressed to Northern Ireland Secretary Theresa Villiers was discovered at Stormont Castle in Belfast, having been delivered to the offices of First Minister Peter Robinson and Deputy First Minister Martin McGuinness. An army bomb disposal unit safely neutralized the viable device this morning. Since Friday, three additional letter bombs have been sent to high-profile targets: two to police officials—one to the PSNI Chief Constable in Belfast and another to Chief Inspector John Burrows in Derry—and a third to the Public Prosecution Service in Londonderry. Dissident Republicans are suspected of orchestrating the attacks. Ms. Villiers was in London at the time, meeting former U.S. diplomat Richard Haass, who is facilitating peace talks between Northern Irish political parties. Meanwhile, both Robinson and McGuinness had recently returned from a trade delegation in the United States. On Wednesday, a bomb addressed to the PPS forced the evacuation of Foyle Chambers in Londonderry and led to road closures along Limavady Road. Army experts responded to the scene. Similar devices were found last Friday targeting PSNI leaders, and dissidents are also linked to two pipe bomb attacks on police patrol vehicles in Newtownabbey and Derry city center, as well as a recent firebombing of a Belfast shop. The UK Home Office has classified the threat from anti-peace extremists as severe, citing their responsibility for the deaths of two soldiers, two police officers, and a prison guard in recent years. During the alert, First Minister Robinson was relocated to Parliament Buildings—where the Northern Ireland Assembly convenes—but continued his duties uninterrupted. As the Assembly is currently in recess, McGuinness was not present at Stormont Castle. Dozens of staff were evacuated from Stormont, many relocating to Parliament Buildings, though few MLAs were present due to the recess. Justice Minister David Ford praised Royal Mail employees at sorting offices in Mallusk and Lisburn for intercepting two additional viable devices addressed to top police officials. He commended their vigilance amid heightened risk, noting that thousands of parcels are processed daily across Northern Ireland. 'Royal Mail has implemented robust security measures to detect suspicious mail,' Ford said. 'Their efforts directly protect our communities. We owe them a debt of gratitude—and recognize the danger they face when criminals abuse the postal system.'

Un ekipa di desarme di l’armá a neutralizá el ‘dispositivo viable’ den esta mañaná. Desdi vièrnes, trés bombas di carta a bini enviá pa figuranan prominente: dos pa ofisialanan di polisia—un pa jefe di polisia di PSNI na Belfast i otro pa jefe di inspektór John Burrows na Derry—i un terser pa Servisio di Prosekusión Pública na Londonderry. Se sospecha ku disidente republikano ta tras di atakonan. Sra. Villiers a ta na Londres den e momentu, tabata reunió ku ex-diplomátiko di Estados Unidos Richard Haass, ku ta facilitá plática di paz ente partidonan politiko di Irlanda di Norte. Mientrás, Robinson i McGuinness a bini regrésá di un misión di komersio na Estados Unidos. Den mièrkoles, un bomba adresá pa el PPS a obligá e evacuashon di Foyle Chambers na Londonderry i tuma rutas ku ta ta pa Limavady Road. Expertonan di l’armá a bini pa e skena. Dispositivonan simila a bini diskubrí vièrnes pasá pa lideranan di PSNI, i disidente aña ta ligá ku dos atakonan ku tubo bomba contra vehikulonan di patrulla na Newtownabbey i den sentro di Derry, i tambe un incendio intensioná na un tienda na sentro di Belfast. Ministerio di Interior di Reino Uní a klasifiká e amenasa di extremistanan kontra e paz komo severo, citando su responsabilidad pa e muerte di dos soldadonan, dos ofisialanan di polisia, i un guardia di prision na aña pasá. Den e alerta, Primer Ministro Robinson a bini trasladá na Parliament Buildings—ku ta sede di Asamblea di Irlanda di Norte—but ta kontinuá ku su dutianan sin interupshon. Como e Asamblea a ta na rekés, McGuinness a no ta presént na Stormont Castle. Decenanan di empleadonan a bini evacuá di Stormont, mientrás ku mesteran di bini pa Parliament Buildings, aunke poko MLA a ta presént por e rekés. Ministro di Justisia David Ford a felisita empleadonan di Royal Mail na ofisinan di sorteo na Mallusk i Lisburn pa interceptá dos dispositivonan viable adresá pa lideranan di polisia. A agradese su vigilansia den e kontesto di risgo aumentá, notando ku miles di paquetonan a ser procesá diariamente na tota Irlanda di Norte. 'Royal Mail a implementá mekánikan seguridat robusto pa diskubrí paquetonan sospechoso,' Ford a dí. 'E esfuerzonan di e a protehí komunidadnan nos. Nos ta debí e agradesimiento—i ta rekonosé e peligro ku e ta enfrentá ku krimalan ta abuzá e sistema di correo.'

article_content: ‘You’ve seen a little glimpse of the future—and that’s what this club is all about,’ said an emotional Ryan Giggs after 18-year-old James Wilson scored twice on his Manchester United debut against Hull City. But it will be incoming manager Louis van Gaal, not Giggs, who bears the ultimate responsibility for guiding the ‘Class of ’14’—Wilson, Adnan Januzaj, Tom Lawrence, and others—to become the next legends of Old Trafford. Since the Matt Busby era, United has prided itself on integrating academy graduates into its first team. Sir Alex Ferguson believed David Moyes would uphold this legacy—but he was mistaken. Van Gaal, despite his reputation for being stern and authoritarian, has a stellar record of nurturing young talent. At Ajax, he led a 1995 Champions League-winning side with an average age of just 23, featuring teenagers like Patrick Kluivert—who scored the decisive goal against AC Milan—and Clarence Seedorf. At Barcelona, he gave 18-year-old Andrés Iniesta his debut. At Bayern Munich, he promoted Thomas Müller and Holger Badstuber. Van Gaal’s preference for attacking football aligns perfectly with the energy and creativity of youth. Young players are more adaptable, eager to please, and less likely to challenge authority—a trait that makes them ideal for his structured system. United’s current crop of academy prospects includes 16-year-old Marcus Rashford, 15-year-old center-back Ro-Shaun Williams, 18-year-old midfielder Sean Goss, 17-year-old goalkeeper Joel Castro Pereira (born in Portugal and captain of Portugal U18s), and 18-year-old attacking midfielder Andreas Pereira (Brazilian-born, eligible for Brazil)—all showing promise across age groups. Even former signings like Wilfried Zaha (21) and Nick Powell, who spent time on loan, remain part of the pipeline. The lesson from history? Youth gets a chance—but only if they’re truly ready. Fergie’s Fledglings of the late 1980s, like Russell Beardsmore and Mark Robins, were given early opportunities and helped win the 1990 FA Cup. Yet, many didn’t reach the highest level. The same standard will apply to Van Gaal’s Vanguard. As Giggs reminded everyone after the match: ‘This club always gives youth its chance.’ And now, the next chapter begins.

Pero e ta Louis van Gaal, e nèw manager, no Giggs, ku ta e responsabilidad di ta gida e ‘Clas di ’14’—Wilson, Adnan Januzaj, Tom Lawrence, i otro—for di e próksimo legendanan di Old Trafford. Desdi e époke di Matt Busby, United a stá orgulhoso di integrá jògadornan akademi pa e primèr ekipa. Sir Alex Ferguson a kresi ku David Moyes ta mantene e tradishon—pero e a yega mal. Van Gaal, malgre su reputashon di ser severo i autoritario, a un historial esplendido di desarola juventud. Na Ajax, e a gida e kampion di Liga di Campeones di 1995 ku un edad promédio di só 23, ku teenageran komo Patrick Kluivert—ku a marke e gol ganador kontra AC Milan—i Clarence Seedorf. E krop di jògadornan akademi di United ta inklui 16-año Marcus Rashford, 15-año defensor Ro-Shaun Williams, 18-año mediocampista Sean Goss, 17-año portero Joel Castro Pereira (nashí na Portugal i kapiten di Portugal U18), i 18-año mediocampista atakante Andreas Pereira (nashí na Brasil, eligibel pa Brasil)—to di e ta demonstra promesa na diferents nivelnan. Inkluzi firma anterioir komo Wilfried Zaha (21) i Nick Powell, ku a pasa tempu na prestá, ta permanese komo part di e pipeline. E leçon di historiya? Juventud ta obteen oportunidat—but só si e ta realmenti listo. Fergie’s Fledglings di fina 1980, komo Russell Beardsmore i Mark Robins, a obteen oportunidat temprano i a ajuda ganá FA Cup di 1990. Ku Giggs a reiterá despues di e partidu: ‘E klub siempre ta da juventud su oportunidat.’ Y agora, e próksimo kapítul ta bini.

article_content: In a bold campaign move, Democratic Senate hopeful Alison Lundergan Grimes has released a 30-second ad showing her shooting skeet in a field — not just to show off her marksmanship, but to make a clear point: she’s not Barack Obama. The ad directly targets her Republican rival, Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell, poking fun at a photo of him holding a rifle upside down at a 2014 conservative event. Grimes jokes that McConnell ‘thought Duke basketball players were UK,’ referencing a previous ad from his campaign that mixed up Kentucky’s two major college teams. She then turns to the camera and says plainly: 'I’m not Barack Obama. I disagree with him on guns, coal, and the EPA.' Her message is simple — she’s a Kentucky native who stands apart from both Obama’s national policies and McConnell’s perceived political posturing. McConnell’s team responded by questioning Grimes’ authenticity, arguing that her campaign is funded by groups pushing gun control and opposing coal — a claim Grimes’ campaign has not confirmed. They called her ad a recycled gimmick. But the real power play came from the NRA, which recently awarded McConnell its highest possible rating, praising his consistent opposition to federal gun restrictions and his leadership in blocking Obama and Bloomberg’s gun control agenda. Meanwhile, Grimes’ ad echoes a broader trend among moderate Democrats in red states: using gun imagery to deflect criticism of being too liberal. Yet, despite the spectacle, polls show McConnell still leads by five points, and many Kentuckians say they don’t see Grimes as offering a compelling alternative. Even though Obama’s approval in Kentucky hovers near 30%, voters aren’t rallying behind Grimes — they’re waiting for a reason to believe in her.

Videu a ataka direkto su opónente republikano, Ministro di Senadó Mitch McConnell, burlándo di un foto ku el ta sostení un rifle pa biaha na un evenemento konservador di 2014. article_content: In a quiet suburb of East Grinstead, a black Porsche Panamera Turbo rolls down the street — but it doesn’t look like a typical luxury car. Its entire body is covered in a plush, velvety fabric known as Velvet Elite 9100, turning heads and sparking online chaos. The one-of-a-kind modification, commissioned by an anonymous owner and installed by UK-based car-wrap specialists Raccoon, cost £2,500 and is believed to be the first of its kind in Britain. When former Apprentice contestant James Lester snapped a photo of the car outside his real estate office in Fulham, west London, the internet exploded. Tweets poured in — some baffled, some delighted. 'A velvet-wrapped Porsche?! What happens when a pigeon lands on it?' one user quipped. Local resident Richard Dorman called it 'a furry mouse zooming around' and admitted he looks away every time he sees it, unable to reconcile the car’s original elegance with its new texture. But Raccoon isn’t fazed. The company says the Velvet Elite 9100 wrap is engineered with industrial-grade adhesive and reinforced textile fibers to endure rain, sun, and even high-pressure washing. It’s designed to last around three years and can be professionally removed without damaging the original paint — leaving the car looking brand new again. The material comes in bold colors like fuchsia and orange, and is compatible with any vehicle type. Despite criticism from car enthusiasts like Jim Holder of Autocar magazine, who called the owner a 'laughing stock,' Raccoon’s team insists it’s a love-it-or-hate-it kind of thing. 'It’s Marmite,' said managing director Richard Clark. 'The owner adores it. And honestly? Cleaning it is easier than you think — just don’t use an automatic car wash.' Marketing manager Scott Mackay recalls how a delivery van once stopped mid-road, reversed, and let workers jump out just to stare. Raccoon reports increasing interest in the product. With social media buzz still growing, they’re hopeful that Britain’s roads might soon be filled with more velvet-clad vehicles — not as jokes, but as bold statements of individuality.

La modifikashon uniko, komisioná pa un dueño anonimo i instalá pa spesialista britániko di kapa di auto Raccoon, ta kosta £2.500 i ta konsiderá el primèr uniko di su tipo na Britania. Gerente di merketing Scott Mackay ta rekordá ku un van di entregá un kés ta pará na mita di kala, ta bira atras, i ta lansa trabayador pa mira e vehikulo. Ku e buzz na redes sosial aindá kresiendo, el ta esperá ku e karèter di Britania ta pudi bini konsidérá mas vehikulo kuverí na veludo — no komo burla, mas komo declarashon di individualidat.
