article_content: Since 2010, the number of EU citizens registering to work in the UK has jumped by 55%, with more than 420,000 National Insurance Numbers issued in the past year alone — up from 285,000 just before the coalition government took office. Countries like Romania, Spain, Greece, and Italy have seen the sharpest rises, driven largely by economic challenges at home. Prime Minister David Cameron is under mounting pressure to act on immigration, promising to make it central to his bid to renegotiate Britain’s EU membership ahead of a 2017 referendum. One proposed solution? Limiting the number of NINOs available to workers from EU nations. But legal experts, including former European Commission president Jose Manuel Barroso and Portuguese official Bruno Macaes, have firmly stated such restrictions would violate EU law. Even some Conservative MPs admit the plan is likely illegal, though they still see it as politically necessary. Meanwhile, business leaders like Katja Hall of the CBI warn that curbing free movement could damage the UK’s attractiveness to investors and hurt job creation. On the other side, Ukip’s Nigel Farage accuses Cameron of misleading voters by suggesting the UK can keep its EU membership while shutting the door on EU workers — arguing that true border control is only possible by leaving the bloc entirely. Home Secretary Theresa May is already discussing cross-border solutions with Germany, the Netherlands, and Austria, while Downing Street insists Cameron’s full plan will be revealed soon.
translated_content: Desde 2010, e kantidat di hende ku ta registrá pa trabá na Reino Uní a subí 55%, ku más di 420.000 númeronan di asuransan di nasional a ser distribuí na útimo aña — subí di 285.000 antes ku e koalishon ta forma. Paises komo Rumania, España, Grecia i Italia a bini e aumentonan mas grandi, motivá pa desafionan ekonomiko na kasa. E primer ministru David Cameron ta bini bai presion pa akta kon inmigrashon, prometí ku el ta pone e tema komo pusentral na su intentu pa renegosia e membresian di Reino Uní ku Uniun Europea pa un referéndum na 2017. Un solushon propuestu? Limítá e kantidat di númeronan di AS ku ta disponibel pa trabadoran di UE. Pero ekspertronan lejal, inkluyendo e antiguu presidente di Komison Europeo Jose Manuel Barroso i e oficial portugues Bruno Macaes, a declará firmemente ku restrishonnan semejante ta viola leh Europeo. Inkluzi alguno diputadonan Konserbador a rekonesé ku e plan ta probabelment illegal, pero aña ta mira komo nesesario politikamente. article_content: By Steve Nolan. UPDATED: 09:01 EST, 28 December 2012. One of the most memorable moments from Sir David Attenborough’s award-winning 'Frozen Planet' series was a scene depicting a polar bear giving birth in the wild — until viewers discovered the footage had actually been shot in a Dutch zoo. The BBC faced widespread criticism for misleading audiences. More than a year later, the Corporation is taking steps to avoid repeating the mistake. For Attenborough’s upcoming series 'Africa,' producers have decided he will explicitly inform viewers whenever footage is captured under controlled conditions — a move aimed at maintaining public trust and credibility. The new BBC Two series, 'Africa,' showcases extraordinary wildlife behavior, including the shoebill bird intentionally starving its younger chick, baby green turtles hatching on Comoros beaches, and elephants crossing the drought-stricken plains of Amboseli. Series producer James Honeybourne explained to the Radio Times: 'Because of the backlash over the polar bear scenes in 'Frozen Planet,' we felt it was essential to be more transparent. We want to share remarkable moments in nature, and sometimes controlled filming makes that possible. We’re not embarrassed — we’re proud of what we’ve achieved.' Crews spent four weeks locating a shoebill nest and then dragged canoes loaded with camera gear through a swamp for two days to capture the unprecedented footage. This isn’t the first time Attenborough’s documentaries have faced accusations of staging. In 1997, a polar bear birth scene in 'Polar Bear: Arctic Warrior' was filmed in a Frankfurt zoo. In 2001, a lobster spawning sequence from 'Blue Planet' was shot in a British aquarium, presented as occurring off Nova Scotia. In 2008, a dramatic encounter with a cobra in 'Life in Cold Blood' was staged in South Africa. Filming for 'Africa' spanned four years and 1,500 field days across continents — from jungles and glaciers to erupting volcanoes. While some scenes involve controlled environments, many others involved immense risk: cameramen climbed onto a dead whale carcass to film 30 great white sharks feeding off South Africa’s east coast. Despite past controversies, the production team remains committed to authenticity where possible — and transparency where it isn’t.

E BBC a bini bini akusashonan di engañá e publiko. Mas di un aña despues, e korporashon a ta taki paso pa no repiti e eror. Pa serie nwe di Attenborough, 'Africa,' e produkkonan a konsidera ku el ta mustra e konsumentnan eksplisítamente ku ta filmá den kondishon kontrolá — un paso ku ta mira mantene e konfiansa i kredibilidad di e publiko. Malgrá akusashonan pasá, e krew ta mantene komitimentu pa autenticidat dondi ta posibel — i transparensia dondi ta no.

article_content: A British woman of Kenyan descent, Sarah Penfold, who works in security for a multinational oil company, has been linked to efforts to recruit mercenaries in support of an operation to rescue Muammar Gaddafi, according to The Independent. As revolutionary forces closed in on Gaddafi in October 2011, Penfold allegedly circulated emails seeking South African private security personnel — ostensibly to protect oil assets in Libya. However, some of those recruited later joined Gaddafi’s fleeing convoy. Gaddafi was captured and killed near Sirte while attempting to escape, accompanied by South African mercenaries. At least two were killed and several wounded in a NATO airstrike before rebel forces apprehended him. His son, Saif al-Islam Gaddafi, and former military chief Abdullah al-Senoussi are now believed to be hiding in the remote Sahel region, likely with Tuareg escorts who possess unmatched knowledge of the desert terrain. Penfold denies any direct contact with the Gaddafi family, stating she only facilitated interviews for private security roles. Yet investigators suspect her network contributed indirectly to Gaddafi’s final escape attempt. Both Saif and al-Senoussi are wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity during Libya’s 2011 uprising. However, more than a dozen African nations — including Mali, Chad, and Niger — refuse to recognize ICC arrest warrants, citing institutional bias. Algeria, which once sheltered Gaddafi’s wife and children, is now attempting to rebuild ties with Libya’s interim government, even as it remains the only country in the region not party to the ICC. Saif’s exact location remains unknown. Rumors suggest he may be moving between borders near Mali, Niger, and Chad, possibly under Tuareg protection. Some analysts believe he is negotiating surrender, planning exile, or even preparing a counter-revolution — but with vast, ungoverned desert territory at his back, tracking him remains nearly impossible.

article_content: Stuart Humphreys, 24, and Claire Bragg, 25 — both graduates of Leeds Metropolitan University — have turned a secondhand Ford Transit van into their mobile home for an ambitious two-year journey across Europe. Originally purchased for £3,500, the 2007 window-glazing van underwent a meticulous two-year renovation costing a total of £6,020. Outside, it looks unremarkable — except for a single chimney rising from the roof, which connects to a wood-burning stove inside. Inside, the cramped 1.7m x 1.8m space holds a bed, a kitchen with a gas oven and sink, pine cabinetry, and a solar panel powering essential electronics. The couple made no room for a toilet or bathtub; instead, they rely on nature and nearby water sources. Bragg, who has taken a sabbatical from her postal job, and Humphreys, on leave from his culinary career, embrace this unconventional lifestyle for its autonomy. 'We can go anywhere, anytime,' she says. Humphreys, who stands 6ft 2in, sleeps diagonally in a curled-up position to fit on the narrow bed. The most demanding part? Adding insulation — a three-month project that laid the foundation for everything else. Their setup includes a 350-watt solar panel, a battery system, and LED lighting, allowing them to run small appliances — even a powerful speaker system if they feel like hosting a roadside jam session. To stay fed, they plan to pick fruit, work on organic farms, and forage wild foods. Their route starts with a ferry to the Netherlands, then north through Germany and Scandinavia, looping back through Eastern Europe. They’ve registered the van as a camper with the DVLA after submitting photos, avoiding costly ferry fees and insurance surcharges. 'We didn’t think they’d approve it,' Humphreys admits. 'But they loved the pics.' Their journey, documented on their blog europebyvan.wordpress.com, isn't a vacation — it’s a deliberate, sustainable experiment in living with less.

E pare ta no ta pone espacio pa un baño o bañera; i ta konsiña na naturaleza i fuentes di aigua próksimo. At Barnet General Hospital, defenders Eric Dier and Younes Kaboul, along with goalkeeper Michel Vorm, were joined by Tottenham Ladies’ Leanne Mabey to deliver presents. One delighted fan received a signed calendar after meeting the players. Meanwhile, Ryan Mason, Ben Davies, Nabil Bentaleb, and Danny Rose visited Princess Alexandra Hospital. Nacer Chadli, Christian Eriksen, Vlad Chiriches, and Tottenham Ladies’ Avilla Bergin made a stop at Whipps Cross Hospital in Leytonstone. On Tuesday afternoon, Jenna Schillaci of Tottenham Ladies welcomed Mousa Dembélé, Benji Stambouli, and Jan Vertonghen at North Middlesex Hospital. Tottenham currently sit in 10th place in the Premier League after a goalless draw with Crystal Palace on Saturday. The team hopes to climb the table during the busy festive period. article_content: In 2009, Chris Taylor suffered a devastating accident while jet-skiing off the coast of Torquay, Devon — a rope snagged during a wave impact, tearing his right hand away. For years, he relied on a basic NHS prosthetic that offered little dexterity, leaving him feeling disconnected from everyday tasks. But everything changed when he discovered the Michelangelo Hand, a groundbreaking bionic prosthesis developed by German company Otto Bock. Unlike traditional models, this device uses tiny electrodes embedded in a silicone socket to detect subtle muscle movements in his forearm, translating them into precise finger and thumb motions. With seven programmable grips and a fully motorized thumb, Taylor can now pick up keys, button his shirt, climb ladders, and even handle delicate wiring for his job as a service engineer. The £47,125 device, which includes a five-year warranty and professional therapy sessions, was made possible through an insurance payout. Taylor, a father of three from Ivybridge, describes the experience as surreal yet empowering: 'It’s not perfect, but it’s the first time in over a decade that my arm feels complete.' As the first UK recipient of the Michelangelo Hand through Dorset Orthopaedic’s pilot program, his journey highlights how advanced prosthetics are transforming lives — not just restoring function, but reclaiming independence.

Pa aña, el ta usá un prótesis básiko di NHS ku ta ofresí poko destreza, dejándolo sentí desconnectá di tas diario. Pero todo ta kambia kuando el ta descubrí e Michelangelo Hand, un prótesis bióniko revolusionario ku ta desarrolhá pa e kompanía aleman Otto Bock. Diferente di modelos tradisional, e dispozitivo usa eletrodos minúskulo embebí na un soket di silikón pa detektá movimientu muskular subtil di su antebrazu, tradusíndolo na movimientu preciso di dedos i pulgar. Kon siete posishon programá i un pulgar motorizá, Taylor ta pòdí agarra klavi, botóna su kamisa, subí escaleras, i hasta manehá konsékwenza eléktriko pa su trahá komo tekniko di servisio. E dispozitivo di 47.125 libra, ku ta inklui garantia di cinco aña i sesion di terapia profesional, ta posibel grats a un pagu di asurans. Taylor, un pà pa tres ku ta vivi na Ivybridge, ta deskribí e eksperiensia komo surreal mas empoderante: 'E no ta perfekto, pero e primèr vegá na más di diez aña ku mi brazu ta sentí kompletu.' Kom e primèr reseptor di Reino Uní di e Michelangelo Hand atravez di programa piloto di Dorset Orthopaedic, su historia ta resaltá komo prótesis avanzá ta transformá vidas — no solo restaurá funshon, mas tamién rekuperá independensia.

article_content: New York (CNN) — The first time Chris injected heroin, he was too scared to do it himself — so his friend did it for him when he was 16. 'I would usually inject in my feet,' he said. 'It escalated to five or six bags per session.' He spent hundreds of dollars a day to feed his addiction, stealing from his parents and breaking into homes. 'I’ve done all of that — except sell myself,' he added. Now 17, Chris is receiving treatment at Outreach House, a long-term substance abuse program on Long Island for adolescents aged 12 to 17. His path to recovery has been rocky: after three failed attempts at outpatient care, he entered an inpatient program — but ran away five times in the first few months. That’s not unusual, said John Venza, vice president of adolescent services at Outreach. 'It takes a long time,' he explained. 'We remove all distractions — no cell phones, TVs, or computers, except for homework. Teens have mandatory jobs, work their way into peer leadership roles, and learn to take responsibility for their actions.' Chris’s parents say short-term programs only exposed him to other users, leading to relapse. 'We’re able to keep them here longer, so we can truly shift their values,' Venza said. 'We also do intensive family work to rebuild their support systems.' Heroin use has surged across Long Island — described by experts as an epidemic. Users as young as 12 are being treated, many from middle-class, suburban families. Contributing factors include proximity to major transportation hubs and a statewide crackdown on prescription painkillers, which pushed users toward cheaper, more accessible heroin. Nationally, the CDC reports a 45% rise in heroin-related drug poisoning deaths from 2006 to 2010. The DEA notes a 232% increase in heroin seizures along the Southwest U.S. border from 2008 to 2012. Among four age groups, only teens and young adults aged 15–24 saw rising death rates from 2008 to 2010. In Long Island, the Long Island Expressway has been dubbed the 'Heroin Highway.' Jeff Reynolds, executive director of the Long Island Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence, says the death of actor Philip Seymour Hoffman brought national attention — but fears it won’t last. 'Hoffman was one of an estimated 100 people who died from overdoses yesterday,' Reynolds said. 'We could’ve prevented most of these deaths through prevention, treatment, and recovery support. Each one is an indictment of our failure — and should motivate us to take this disease seriously.' Reynolds notes a chilling shift: 'Ten years ago, two or three bags a day meant you were a heavy user. Now, for kids, that’s breakfast.' Heroin-related deaths on Long Island have hit record levels. DEA arrests there jumped 163% in one year. Reynolds reports a sevenfold increase in patients over five years — 80% due to heroin or other opiates. Many users defy stereotypes: cheerleaders, athletes, honor students from loving homes. 'You couldn’t look at my daughter and think she was a heroin addict,' said Susan Roethel, whose 22-year-old daughter Megan died of an overdose. 'She was beautiful — blond, bright — and no one knew.' Dorothy Johnson, who lost her 28-year-old son Maxwell, says stigma keeps families silent. 'Our children aren’t junkies. That word needs to change.' Access to long-term treatment remains difficult — insurance often doesn’t cover it. Roethel says short-term programs failed her daughter. 'You need over a year. It’s incredibly hard for these kids to come back.' Robert Scarabino, whose 24-year-old daughter Jaclyn died in her bed, said: 'In short-term rehab, they learn how to lie, steal, and manipulate to get more drugs.' Chris credits his 11 months at Outreach with saving his life. 'I was in situations where I could have died,' he said. 'Now I have tools to manage my emotions without using. I’m excited for my future.' Next week, he graduates, returns home, and begins the hard work of staying sober. His mother, Joanne, says: 'It didn’t just save my son — it saved us too.'
translated_content: Nueva York (CNN) — La primé taña Chris ta inyektá heroina, el ta miedu pa fá el mesmio — asina ku su amigu lo fá pa el ku el ta 16. 'Mi ta inyektá na mi pies,' el a dí. 'Elo ta eskalá a cinco o seis bolsa pa sesión.' El gasta hundridas di dolar diario pa sostené su adikshon, robá di su padres i burtá kas. 'Mi ta fá to eso — mas no vende mi mesmio,' el a afirma. Ahora 17, Chris ta recibí tramentu na Outreach House, un programa di tramentu di abusu di substansia pa adolésentes di 12 a 17 aña na Long Island. Su ruda pa rekuperashon ta bini kompliká: despues di tri intentu falí na tramentu ambulatorio, el ta entrá na un programa inpaçial — pero el ta hui kinsin siéte mes. E ta no rara, a dí John Venza, vicepresident di servishon pa adolésentes na Outreach. 'E ta nesesí muhó tiempu,' el a ekspliká. 'Nos ta remové to distrashon — sin teléfonu, TV, o komputadora, mas pa ta hushá. Adoleschente ta tin trabou obligatori, ta subí na posishon di liderasgo ente su pares, i ta apréndi ta responsabel pa su akshon.' Padres di Chris ta dí ku programa korto ta eksponé el a otro adikt, ta konduí a rekaida. 'Nos ta pudi mantiene el aki más lóng, pa nos ta realmenti shiftá su valór,' Venza a dí. 'Nos tambe ta fá trabou intensivo ku famílias, pa rekonstruí su sistema di apoiu.' Uso di heroina ta subí na Long Island — deskribí ku un epidemia. Uzante tan jóven ku 12 ta tratá, muhó di famílias mediu-burghés i suburbiano. Faktor ku contribuí e ta proximidad ku hubo di transportashon i un atak di estadual ku ta reduí preskripsion di analgésiko, ku ta empuja uzante a heroina más barata i más akésibel. Nashonalmente, CDC ta raporta un subida di 45% na muerte di droga relacioná ku heroina di 2006 a 2010. DEA ta nota un subida di 232% na sekesión di heroina na frontera suroeste di Estados Unidos di 2008 a 2012. Ente kuarto grupu di eda, solamente adolésentes i jóven di 15 a 24 aña ta bini un subida na muerte di 2008 a 2010. Na Long Island, Long Island Expressway ta apodá 'Heroin Highway.' Jeff Reynolds, direktor ejecutivu di Long Island Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence, ta dí ku muerte di ator Philip Seymour Hoffman ta traí atenshon Nashonal — mas el ta temí ku e ta no ta durá. 'Hoffman ta un di e estimá 100 persona ku ta morí di sobredosis ayer,' Reynolds a dí. 'Nos ta pudi prevení mayoria di ese sobredosis ku prevenshon, akésu a tramentu, i suportu pa rekuperashon. Ogaña ta un denunsiá di nos falha — i ta ta motiva nos pa ta serius ku e enfermedad.' Reynolds ta nota un kambio tristemente: 'Diez aña atrás, dos o tres bolsa di día ta signifiká ku e ta un uzante pesá. Ahora, pa niños, e ta desayuno.' Muerte relacioná ku heroina na Long Island ta bini na nivel rékord. Arresto di DEA aki ta subí 163% na un aña. Reynolds ta raporta un subida di siete veç di paziente na kinsin aña — 80% ku heroina u otro opiatos. Muhó uzante ta desafia estereotipo: cheerleader, atleta, studiante di mérito di famílias amoroso. 'Nos no ta pudi mirá mi hija i pensá ku e ta un adikt di heroina,' a dí Susan Roethel, ku su hija Megan, 22 aña, ta morí di sobredosis. 'E ta bela — rubia, brilhante — i nadie ta sabe.' Dorothy Johnson, ku ta perdí su hijo Maxwell, 28 aña, ta dí ku stigma ta mantén famílias silensioso. 'Nuestros niño ta igual ku to otro madre o padre’ niño — i e ta no junkie. E termino ta nesesí kambia.' Akésu a tramentu lóng ta difísil — seguransa no ta pagá siempri. Roethel ta dí ku programa korto no ta ayuda su hija. 'Nos ta nesesí más di un aña. E ta muy difísil pa e niño ta regresá.' Robert Scarabino, ku su hija Jaclyn, 24 aña, ta morí na su kama, a dí: 'Na tramentu korto, e ta apréndi mentí, robá, i manipulá pa obtein más droga.' Chris ta krédita 11 mes na Outreach ku ta salva su vida. 'Mi ta na situashon ku mi ta pudi morí,' el a dí. 'Ahora mi ta tin herraienta pa manejá mi emosión sin usa. Mi ta emocioná pa mi futuro.' La próksima seman, el ta gradua, ta regresá na kasa ku su padres, i ta fasa su esforsu pa ta sober. Sua madre, Joanne, ta dí: 'E no ta solamente salva mi hijo — e ta salva nos tambien.'

article_content: A Rangers shareholder has filed a complaint with financial regulators regarding investor Sandy Easdale, urging an investigation into possible misconduct. The complaint follows remarks made by Easdale on April 24—the day before Rangers published its 120-day business review—in which he described the club’s financial position as 'fragile'. Mark Dingwall, a former chairman of the Rangers Supporters Trust, has written to the London Stock Exchange, the Financial Conduct Authority, and Daniel Stewart, the club’s nominated advisors in the City, expressing serious concerns. Emails reviewed by Sportsmail request that each body investigate whether Easdale is acting as a shadow director of Rangers International Football Club plc and using confidential information obtained through that role to profit from share purchases. Although Sandy Easdale is not a member of the RIFC plc board—unlike his brother James—he serves as a director of Rangers Football Club Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary. The complainant alleges Easdale had 'apparent access' to the plc’s financial data and prior knowledge of the commercially sensitive 120-day review. Dingwall’s email notes: 'On April 24, the share price was 26p. After Easdale’s statement, it dropped to 22p. He then purchased 57,043 shares at 23p on May 1. By May 8, the price had rebounded to 27p.' It is also noted that Easdale holds voting rights—though not ownership—for an additional 22.10% of RIFC plc shares. Dingwall suggests that if Easdale possesses privileged information, those shareholders may also be indirectly benefiting. No comment has been issued by the Financial Conduct Authority, the London Stock Exchange, or Daniel Stewart. Rangers has also declined to respond to the allegations. Last week, the Union of Fans—a supporter coalition—questioned whether CEO Graham Wallace or Easdale truly holds decision-making power at Ibrox. Meanwhile, Rangers confirmed the signing of Darren McGregor on a one-year deal and announced that Kenny Miller will return for a third spell next season, following the club’s recent promotion to the Scottish Premiership.

article_content: New data reveals a 10% increase in hospital admissions for self-harm among teenage girls in just one year. Between June 2012 and June 2013, 13,400 girls aged 15 to 19 required hospital treatment for self-harm — up from 12,220 the previous year. Experts warn that today’s youth are growing up in an 'unprecedented toxic climate,' shaped by 24/7 online culture, cyberbullying, pressure to conform to unrealistic body standards, and limited job prospects. These factors, they say, are taking a serious toll on adolescent mental health. Meanwhile, boys in the same age group saw 4,000 cases of self-harm and 3,500 cases of assault-related injuries — a 24% drop from the prior year. Across all children under 19, there were 2.5 million hospital admissions in the year — a minimal 0.1% rise. Infections remained the most common cause, with 31,900 cases among boys and 19,200 among girls. Asthma was nearly twice as common in boys (6,800 cases) compared to girls (3,500). Tooth decay affected 13,300 boys and 12,000 girls aged 5 to 9. Lucie Russell, Director of Campaigns at YoungMinds, stressed that these trends cannot be dismissed as normal parts of adolescence. 'We’re seeing record numbers of parents seeking help for their children’s mental health,' she said. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has issued new guidance urging clinicians to proactively screen for depression in children, document diagnoses, and provide age-appropriate information to patients and families. Severe depression affects nearly 80,000 young people in the UK — including over 8,000 under the age of 10. NICE’s Deputy Chief Executive, Professor Gillian Leng, emphasized the need for consistent, high-quality care across the NHS. Health officials urge immediate action: early intervention, better access to mental health services, and systemic changes to reduce digital and societal pressures on young people.

article_content: In his 1970 anthem, Edwin Starr declared, 'War! What is it good for? Absolutely nothing.' But history, archaeology, and anthropology tell a more complex story. In the Stone Age, humans lived in small, fragile communities. While most disputes were settled peacefully, when violence erupted, it was unchecked—homicides, raids, and vendettas were common. With populations tiny by today’s standards, even low levels of violence added up: scholars estimate that 10 to 20% of Stone Age people died at the hands of others. Fast forward to the 20th century: two world wars, genocides, nuclear threats, and countless civil conflicts claimed 100 to 200 million lives. Yet, with nearly 10 billion people living during that century, the percentage who died violently dropped to just 1–2%. Since 2000, the United Nations reports, that rate has fallen further—to 0.7%. In other words, if you were born in the 20th century, your chance of dying violently was one-tenth of what it was in the Stone Age. How did this happen? The most startling answer: war itself. Around 10,000 years ago, victorious groups began absorbing defeated ones into larger societies. To maintain control, they built stronger governments. And to keep those governments stable, rulers had to suppress internal violence—not out of compassion, but because orderly, taxed subjects were more useful than rebellious ones. Societies that succeeded in controlling violence grew; those that didn’t collapsed. This process—termed 'Leviathan' by philosopher Thomas Hobbes—was brutal. Roman conquests in Britain, British rule in India, and American expansion across North America all involved massive bloodshed to impose peace. Democracies tended to be more humane Leviathans than autocracies, but none were gentle. And while some wars destroyed order, over millennia, enough succeeded in building larger, safer societies to slash violent death rates by 90%. Today, no global government enforces peace. But the United States, as the world’s sole superpower, often acts as a global cop—deterring aggression through military strength. International bodies like the UN and EU, along with norms of diplomacy and human rights, have helped. Yet history suggests the foundation of modern peace isn't idealism—it's the coercive order created by war and enforced by powerful states. War remains the worst path to peace. But, tragically, it may be the only one humanity has ever found.
translated_content: Na su himno di 1970, Edwin Starr declará: 'War! ¿Pa kós ta bon? Absolutamente nada.' Pero historia, arkeolojía, i antropolojía nos di un historia mas kompleks. Na e Stone Age, hende ta bini na komunidades pikin i frágil. Mientras la mayoria di disputa ta resolbe sin violensia, kuándo violensia ta bini, ta sin restrinsion—homicidio, raid, i vengansa ta komun. Ku población tan pikin pa dia di hodi, hasta nivél baj di violensia ta sumá: e scholar estimá ku 10 a 20% di hende Stone Age ta mori pa man di otro. Salta pa e 20o siglo: dos guèrra mundial, genosidio, amenasa nuclear, i innumerabel konflikto sivil ta kousa 100 a 200 milyon muerte. Pero ku casi 10 milyon hende ku bini na e siglo, e porsentaj di hende ku ta mori di violensia ta bai a 1–2%. Kuña 2000, e Nasonan Uní ta reportá, e tasa ta bai mas—pa 0.7%. En otras palabras, si tú ta nase na e 20o siglo, e kansa di tú mori di violensia ta un diesimo di ku ta bini na Stone Age. Kómo eki a bini? E resposta mas sorprendente: mesmo guerra. Kuña 10.000 aña atras, grupo ganador ta konsolidá e perdedor na sosiedad mas grand. Pa mantiene kontrol, eles ta konstruí gobièrno mas fuerte. Y pa mantene e gobièrno stabile, lideran ta tení ku suprimí violensia interna—no pa kompasión, mas pa ku sujeto ordená i ta pagá impuestu ta mas útil ku sujeto rebel. Sosiedad ku ta sukede na kontrolá violensia ta kresé; e ku ta no ta kolapsá. E proseso—konosí komo 'Leviatán' pa filósofo Thomas Hobbes—ta brutal. Konkista Roman na Britania, regno Britániko na India, i ekspansión Amerikano na Norteamerika to di e ta impliká sangre masiva pa imponé paz. Demokrasia ta bini mas humana komo Leviatán ku diktadura, mas ningun ta suave. Y mientras algun guèrra ta destruí orden, kuña milenio, sufisienten ta sukede pa konstruí sosiedad mas grand i mas segur pa reducí tasa di muerte di violensia pa 90%. Hodi, no ta yá un gobièrno global ku ta garantí paz. Pero Estados Unidos, komo e única superpoder global, ta aksa komo un polis global—disuade agresión atraves di fuerza militar. Organisashon internashonal komo ONU i UE, junto ku norma di diplomasia i direhon di hende, ta ayudá. Mas historia sugeri ku fundashon di paz moderno no ta idealismo—mas e orden koersivo ku ta krea pa guerra i ta imponí pa estado poderoso. Guèrra ta e peor kamino pa paz. Mas, trágikamente, ta posiblemente e úniko kamino ku hende a bini.

article_content: Sean Dyche expects Ashley Barnes to respond positively to the controversy surrounding his challenge on Nemanja Matic and hopes the striker will not alter his combative playing style. The Burnley forward was widely criticized after making contact with Matic’s shin with his studs during last weekend’s 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge. Matic was sent off for his angry reaction, with Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho labeling the challenge 'criminal' and warning it could have ended his player’s career. Barnes is known for his physical approach and has committed more fouls this season than any other player in the Premier League. Dyche commented on the 25-year-old: 'He’s been good this week. It’s not the ideal situation. We know how quickly things escalate at this level—especially when influential figures in the game voice strong opinions, and the media picks it up. It’s an important moment in his development. I’m certain he hasn’t faced anything like this before, but he’s a steady lad who has performed tremendously for us. The players and staff are fully behind him, so we’re moving forward. I hope he continues to play with the freedom he’s shown—that’s it in a nutshell.' Matic received a straight red card for his reaction; his initial three-match ban was reduced to two following an appeal. Chelsea’s frustration grew when the Football Association announced it would not take retrospective action against Barnes, allowing him to play against Swansea this weekend. Meanwhile, Matic’s ban was reduced from three to two matches, meaning he will miss Sunday’s Capital One Cup final. When asked about Barnes escaping punishment, Dyche said: 'There’s no relief in it. The authorities make the decisions, so I leave it to them to do their job.'

E futbolista di Burnley ta konsiderá ku e ta tuma e shín di Matic ku e studs durante e partidu di 1-1 ku ta joga na Stamford Bridge. E no ta e situashon ideal. Nos sabe ku kòs ta bini rapido pa nivél di eki, spesialmenti ku persòna ku ta tén influensia na e jògo ta da opinyon grandi riba situashonan, i e medionan ta ta bai. Frustrashon di Chelsea ta aumentá ku Asosiasón di Futbol anunsia ku e no ta punitá Barnes retroaktivamenti, permitindó e pa joga kontra Swansea den e fin di semanan. article_content: Every day at 'O, The Oprah Magazine,' dozens of dedicated professionals — women and men alike — show up, do their best, and keep the magazine running. Among them, one person has become an unexpected source of daily dread. I call her 'The Tinkler.' She doesn’t shout, she doesn’t sabotage files — she leaves tiny yellow puddles on the bathroom floor. It’s not vandalism; it’s a quiet, persistent violation of basic hygiene. I’ve spent months observing patterns: she strikes between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m., always alone, and never in the accessible stall. I’ve ruled out coworkers based on alibis — one always uses paper seat covers, another was overseas during two incidents. The rest of us have turned into amateur detectives, analyzing bathroom habits like crime scenes. We joke, we sigh, we roll our eyes — but beneath the laughter, there’s something deeper: the realization that even in a place full of creative, intelligent people, basic respect for shared spaces isn’t guaranteed. I used to think of my job as just a paycheck. But after 30 years — from washing dogs at a pet salon to serving chicken to rude customers — I’ve learned that the people around you shape your experience more than your title ever could. They make you laugh, make you angry, make you question your own sanity. And yes, sometimes they leave messes no one wants to clean up. In a world where big issues like media integrity and national security dominate headlines, it feels ridiculous to write about a bathroom problem. But maybe that’s the point. Civility isn’t about grand gestures. It’s about remembering that other people exist — that flushing properly, wiping down surfaces, or simply being mindful matters. I don’t need crystal chandeliers or pearls. I just want someone to care enough not to turn a public restroom into their personal swamp. So here’s to The Tinkler — wherever you are. You’re still out there. And we’re still watching.
translated_content: Día pa día na 'O, The Oprah Magazine', docena di profesionál kontratá — muher i homber — ta bini, ta fai su mehor, i ta mantiene revista korre. Entre e, un persona ta bini kualke vez fonte di teror di dia. Mi ta bini e 'La Tinkler'. E no ta grita, e no ta sabotá arkivu — e ta dexa gota di orina di kolor amarillo pa piso di banyu. E no ta vandalismo; e ta un violashon silensioso di higiene basiku. Mi ta pasá mes observando patrón: e ta ataka ente 10 a.m. i 8 p.m., siempres sola, i nunca na banyu aksebil. Mi ta eksklui kolaboradó pa alibi — un siempres ta usa proteksion di papel, otro ta stá fora di país durante dos inkidenti. Resto di nos ta bini detektiv di banyu, analizándo hábitu di banyu komo si ta krimes. Nos ta bai, nos ta suspirá, nos ta rola e oyo — mas baixo e risa, ta havi algo más profundo: e konprensión ku même na un loki ku ta pleno di persona kreativo i inteligente, respeto basiku pa espasio komun no ta garantizá. Mi ta pensá mi trabou komo si ta solamente un salario. Mas depués di 30 aña — di lava perro na salón di animál i sirbi kikin pa kliënt ruda — mi ta apréndí ku e persona ku ta rodiá te ta forma e eksperiensia mas ku e título. E ta bini risá, bini enojá, bini fá e mente dubidá. Y sí, aki e ta dexa mancha ku nadie ta bini limpiá. Na un mundo ku e asuntu grandi komo integridad mediatiko i sekuridat nasional ta domina notisia, ta parese ridikulo pa skribí so un problema di banyu. Mas talvez e ta e punto. Kortesía no ta so gestu grandi. E ta so te konsidera ku otro persona ta eksisti — ku flusha korrektamente, limpiá superfisi, o simpelemente ta konziente ta mporta. Mi no ta nesesita kandelabro di krisal i perlas. Mi ta bini un persona ku ta kierí sufisientemente pa no turna un banyu komunal na su pantano personal. Asina pa La Tinkler — onde e ta. E ta siempres aki. I nos ta siempres observándo.

article_content: Over a three-year span, the BBC allocated more than £220,000 to train 783 of its employees on how to effectively use iPhones — roughly £300 per person. This training came as part of a broader push to equip staff with modern tools, following the purchase of over 4,200 iPhones, 427 iPads, and 815 MacBooks between early 2012 and late 2013 at an estimated cost of £2.5 million. While critics like Andy Silvester of the Taxpayers' Alliance called the expense unnecessary — noting that even teenagers can navigate smartphones — the BBC defended the investment. They emphasized that these devices aren’t handed out universally but are issued only to staff whose roles require mobile reporting. In fact, the organization uses iPhones to film, edit, and send news reports from remote locations where traditional broadcast equipment isn’t feasible. Training expenses have also decreased over time, with last year’s bill dropping to just £42,000 — the lowest since the program began. Though the upfront cost of the hardware is substantial, the BBC argues that mobile journalism ultimately reduces long-term expenses for license fee payers by eliminating the need for bulky gear and crews in hard-to-reach areas.

Ese entrenamentu a bini komo parti di un esfuerzo mas granda pa dotá su empleadonan ku herramienta moderno, despues di e konsigna di mas di 4.200 iPhone, 427 iPad, i 815 MacBook ente principio di 2012 i fin di 2013 ku un kustu estimá di £2.5 millón. Mientras kritikonan komo Andy Silvester di e Taxpayers' Alliance a konsidera e gasto nesesario — nota ku hasta adolecentenan ta pone maneja smartphone — la BBC a defensá e investimentu. E a enfatisa ku e dispozitivonan no ta duna universalmente mas ta distribuí solamente pa empleadonan ku su rol ta nesesita reportashon mobil. Den hech, e organizashon ta usa iPhone pa filmá, editar, i mandá notisia di lugaran remoto ku ekipamentu tradishonal no ta disponible. E kustu di entrenamentu tambe a bai bai, ku e kustu di aña pasá a bai a £42.000 — e mas bajo desde ku e programa a bini. Totu e kustu inicial di e hardwaredi ta granda, la BBC ta argumentera ku e jornalismo mobil ta reducí e kustu largo plas pa pagadornan di la licensia pa evita e nezesidat di ekipamentu pesá i ekipa pa lugaran difisil di akés.
post_content: BBC spent £220K training staff on iPhones… but here’s the twist 🤯 They’re using them to report from remote areas — no crews, no trucks, just phones. £300/person? Maybe. But saving £millions long-term? Absolutely. #BBC #MobileJournalism #TaxpayerValue

article_content: In a pre-season clash in New Zealand, West Ham United suffered a 3-1 defeat at the hands of Australia’s Sydney FC. The match began poorly for the Hammers, who conceded just four minutes in after a swift counterattack led by Ali Abbas found Corey Gameiro, who calmly finished past keeper Adrian. Sydney doubled their lead before halftime when Alex Brosque converted a precise pass from Bernie Ibini. West Ham looked to turn things around after the break when Matt Jarvis’ left-wing cross took a deflection off Sydney captain Nikola Petkovic and flew past goalkeeper Vedran Janjetovic — a rare bright spot in an otherwise shaky performance. But any hope of a comeback faded when Gameiro scored his second goal in the 64th minute, capitalizing on what appeared to be a clear handball — a decision the referee inexplicably missed. Manager Sam Allardyce acknowledged the team’s struggles, admitting their defensive shape was compromised as they tried to implement more fluid attacking patterns. On a negative note, defender Guy Demel exited the game early after pulling his hamstring, making way for summer acquisition Aaron Cresswell. Despite the loss, the match served as a testing ground for tactics and fitness ahead of the new season.

Partidu tabata komensá mal pa e Hammers, ku tabata koncedí solamente kuatro minút despues di un contragolpe rápidu ku Ali Abbas tabata bini pa Corey Gameiro, ku tabata tira pa portero Adrian. Sydney tabata dobla su ventaja antes di mitat di tempu cuando Alex Brosque tabata convertí un pase preciso di Bernie Ibini. West Ham tabata mira pa kambiá situason despues di intervalo ku un pase di Matt Jarvis di banda kierda tabata bini pa Nikola Petkovic, y tabata bai pa diante di portero Vedran Janjetovic — un puntu brillantí pa un prestashon generalmente débil. Pero cualquier esperansa di un komeback tabata desaparecí cuando Gameiro tabata marke su sekundo gol na minú 64, aprovechando lo ke tabata aparentemente un manu — un decisión ku e árbitro tabata omití sin razón. Entrenador Sam Allardyce tabata akontesá e problemátikanan di e ekipa, adimitiendo ku e forma di defensa tabata komprometí mientras tabata traha pa implementá un ataká mas fluido. Pa un nota negativo, defensor Guy Demel tabata salí tempranamente despues di tirá su hamstring, y tabata sustituí pa Aaron Cresswell, e nèw signá. Malgre e perdida, partidu tabata sirbi komo un terreno di prueba pa táktikanan i kondishon física paan di tempu.

article_content: Abu Qatada, a radical Islamic cleric, has filed an appeal against his deportation to Jordan at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), a move that could delay his removal for months. The UK Home Secretary, Theresa May, had secured a landmark agreement with Jordan to ensure Qatada would face a fair trial without the use of evidence obtained through torture. However, his legal team submitted a last-minute appeal to the ECHR shortly after 11 p.m. on April 17, 2012, arguing that the court’s earlier ruling — which found no substantial risk of torture — was flawed. The UK Home Office contends that the appeal is invalid, asserting that the three-month window to challenge the ECHR’s January 17 ruling closed at midnight on April 16. According to officials, Qatada’s case should proceed through UK courts, where he remains in custody pending further hearings. The Special Immigration Appeals Commission (SIAC) has denied him bail, citing a continued risk of flight, and a full hearing may not occur until October. Since arriving in Britain in 1993 on a forged passport, Qatada has been the subject of intense legal scrutiny. Convicted in absentia in Jordan in 1999 for involvement in terror plots, he has lived in the UK under increasingly restrictive conditions — including house arrest, state-funded accommodation, and weekly surveillance costing £100,000. His legal battles have cost British taxpayers over £1.5 million. The diplomatic deal with Jordan guarantees Qatada a public trial with civilian judges, access to legal counsel, and the right to call defense witnesses. His prior Jordanian conviction will be annulled, and he will be retried under internationally recognized standards. This agreement followed years of negotiations after the ECHR ruled in 2012 that deportation without such assurances would constitute a 'flagrant denial of justice.' The timing of the appeal coincides with broader reforms being discussed by the 47-member Council of Europe ahead of its meeting in Brighton. Governments are seeking to limit the ECHR’s caseload and reinforce the authority of national courts. Meanwhile, critics, including counter-terrorism expert Robin Simcox, have praised Theresa May’s determination to remove Qatada, calling him a 'senior jihadist ideologue' whose presence undermines national security.

La Secretaria di Interior, Theresa May, a konseguí un akuerdu historiko ku Jorden pa asegurá ku Qatada ta pudié juzgá ku no ta usá evidensia ku ta obteení pa tortura. Pero su ekipa legal a presentá un apelashon últime minút ku ta 11:00 p.m. di 17 di abril di 2012, argumentando ku e kòrt a dja un rasonamentu anterior — ku no ta havi risgo substansial di tortura — ta erradu. La Ofisina di Interior britániko ta kontendu ku e apelashon ta inválidu, aseverando ku e periódo di trés mes pa desafí e rasonamentu di CEDH di 17 di janüari ta tèrmina na medionoch di 16 di abril. La Kòrt di Apelashon di Inmigrashon Espesial (SIAC) a negá e libertad bailable, siñalando ku e risgo di fuga ta kontinuá, i e audiénsia kompletu ta pudié no ta bini pa oktòber. Sua batalla lekal ta kosá e taksadorn britániko mas ku £1.5 millón. E akuerdu diplomátiko ku Jorden ta garantiá ku Qatada ta pudié juzgá na un tribunal públiko ku juez sivil, akésu a abogadon, i drechu pa llaman testigu di defensa. Su konvikshon anterior na Jorden ta anulá, i el ta ser re-juzgá ba stadánda internashonal. E akuerdu a sigui aña di negosiasion despues ku CEDH a dja na 2012 ku deportashon sin e garantianan ta konsiderá un 'negashon flagrante di justisia.' E timing di e apelashon ta koincidí ku reforma mas amplio ku ta diskutí pa e 47 membro di Konseho di Europa paan di e reunión na Brighton. Gobièrnon ta buská limitá e kantidad di kaso di CEDH i reforzá e autoridat di kòrt nashonal. Mientras, krítikon, inkluyendo e eksperto di kontreterorismo Robin Simcox, a felisitá Theresa May pa su determinashon pa ekspulsá Qatada, lo ta dja un 'ideólogo jihadista senior' ku su presensia ta subvertí seguridat nashonal.

article_content: Prime Minister Tony Abbott has faced sharp criticism from Indigenous leaders after repeatedly describing the arrival of the First Fleet as 'the defining moment in the history of this continent'. Warren Mundine, Chair of the Prime Minister’s Indigenous Advisory Council, told ABC Radio that white settlement was 'a disastrous defining moment for Indigenous people'. Abbott made the remarks during the opening of a history exhibition at the National Museum in Canberra, as reported by the Sydney Morning Herald. 'It was the moment this continent became part of the modern world. It determined our language, our laws, and our fundamental values,' Abbott said. 'Yes, it did dispossess and, for a long time, marginalize Indigenous people. But as Noel Pearson often reminds us, modern Australia has an important Indigenous and multicultural character—still, it’s British settlement that has most profoundly shaped the country we are today.' Matilda House, Head of the Stolen Generations Council for NSW, responded: 'I can’t fathom how a single ship sailing into Sydney Harbour could overshadow 60,000 years of continuous Indigenous history.' In July, Abbott stirred controversy again when he described pre-colonial Australia as 'unsettled' and likened British colonization to 'foreign investment' by the British government. He made the comments during a speech at the Melbourne Institute. Senator Nova Peris, Australia’s first female Aboriginal federal parliamentarian, called the remarks deeply offensive and factually wrong. 'British settlement was not a foreign investment. It was invasion,' she told ABC. Opposition Leader Bill Shorten condemned Abbott’s comments as inappropriate, particularly from a leader who claims to support Indigenous affairs. Mundine labeled the remarks 'silly and bizarre,' while Peris emphasized they undermined efforts to recognize Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in the Australian Constitution.

article_content: Sebastian Faulks, the bestselling author of Birdsong and a judge for this year’s Chalke Valley History Prize, has called for history to reclaim its central role in UK schools. Speaking out against its decline, he urged students to pick up their pens and explore the excitement of the living past through creative writing. Faulks emphasized that history is just as vital as science, math, and English, and criticized the policy allowing students to drop the subject before GCSEs. 'Children should never have been allowed to drop it,' he said. The Chalke Valley History Prize, run in partnership with the Daily Mail and Penguin Books, challenges young people to craft vivid stories that bring historical events to life. Faulks praised the initiative for blending rigorous research with imaginative expression, calling it a crucial step toward repairing the damage done to history education. He added: 'Until history regains its central place in schools, we rely on initiatives like this to encourage children to think beyond the narrow confines of standard curricula. This prize strikes an excellent balance between fact and imagination, hard work and fun.' Since students gained the option to drop history before GCSEs, enrollment in state comprehensives in England has dropped by nearly 20%. Meanwhile, a report from the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Archives and History revealed that the average 13-year-old receives just one hour of history instruction per week. The prize’s judging panel includes notable figures such as actress Joanna Lumley, author and comedian Charlie Higson, historian James Holland, literary agent Mark Lucas, Penguin editor Alex Clarke, and educator James Petrie. Last year’s winner, 15-year-old Rachel Thomson, credited the prize with inspiring her writing journey. After winning for her story 'Witch Child'—a tale set during the Tudor persecutions—she received guidance from a London publishing agency and continues to write with renewed passion. Winners receive £100 worth of Penguin or Puffin books and a personalized consultation with the Lucas Alexander Whitley Literary Agency. The prize is part of the Chalke Valley History Festival, taking place from June 24 to 30 in Wiltshire.

article_content: Hold on to the audacity of hope—but avoid the arrogance of over-promising. According to scholar Robert Weisbrot, President Obama can gain valuable insights from the triumphs and missteps of Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society. Weisbrot, co-author of 'The Liberal Hour: Washington and the Politics of Change in the 1960s,' describes the Great Society as 'tremendously liberating' for marginalized communities across America. Launched in the mid-1960s, Johnson’s sweeping agenda sought to eliminate poverty, end racial injustice, and protect the environment. Yet, Weisbrot argues, the political and economic landscape today makes it impossible for Obama to replicate Johnson’s bold legislative achievements. 'Obama is living in a different age,' Weisbrot explains. 'The circumstances won’t permit him to be another Lyndon Johnson.' When Obama took office, the nation’s economy teetered on collapse, partisan divisions were deepening, and public trust in federal programs had eroded. In contrast, when Johnson assumed power, America was riding a post-World War II economic surge. Both major parties included strong moderate wings, and citizens broadly believed the federal government could solve national problems—having guided the country through the Great Depression and World War II, and helping rebuild Europe. That widespread confidence, however, also contributed to the backlash against the Great Society. Johnson framed his mission as a war to conquer poverty and racism—an ambitious metaphor that backfired when the Vietnam War siphoned off funds and attention. 'Lyndon Johnson dealt in hyperbole,' Weisbrot notes. 'It helped pass legislation, but it set the nation up for disappointment when the promised utopia never arrived.'

Segun e scholar Robert Weisbrot, presidente Obama ta pò ta aprendi mas di e triunfos i faltanan di e Great Society di Lyndon Johnson. Weisbrot, ko-aotor di 'The Liberal Hour: Washington and the Politics of Change in the 1960s,' ta describi e Great Society komo 'tremendamente liberador' pa komunidatnan mas frágil di Amerika. Lanzá na meio di e 1960, e agenda amplia di Johnson ta bini pa eliminá pobreza, akabá injustisia rásial, i protehí e medio ambiente. Pero Weisbrot ta arguménta ku e konteksto politiko i ekonómiko hodi ta imposibel pa Obama repedí e logros legislativo grandioso di Johnson. 'Obama ta bivi na un otro aña,' Weisbrot ta ekspliká. 'E konsiderašonan no ta permití lu ta ser otro Lyndon Johnson.' Ku Obama ta asumí e presidensia, ekonomia di nashon ta tuma ku ta kai, divisiónnan partidista ta aumentá, i konfiansa di popula pa programa federal ta disminuí. En konsideransia, ku Johnson ta asumí e poder, Amerika ta bini na un onda ekonómiko despues di e Segundu Guerra Mundial. Ambos partidonan grandi ta tení un grupu fort di moderadonan, i habitantenan ta kredi ku e gobièrno federal ta pò solucioná problema nashonal—habiendo guiá e nashon atraves di e Gran Depresión i e Segundu Guerra Mundial, i ayudá rekonstruí Europa. E konfiansa amplia, sinembargo, tambe ta contribuí pa e reaksion kontra e Great Society. Johnson ta framá e misión su komo un guerra pa konsentra pobreza i racismo—un metafora ambishioso ku ta falá ku e Guerra di Vietnam ta drená fundonan i atensión. 'Lyndon Johnson ta traha ku hiperbolonan,' Weisbrot ta nota. 'E ta ajuda pasa leyes, pero e ta prepará e nashon pa desilusión ku e utopía prometí no ta akrá.'

article_content: Sergio Aguero eased concerns among Manchester City fans that he might face another prolonged injury layoff after being substituted for Edin Dzeko in the final 20 minutes of their 4-1 victory over Stoke City. The Argentine striker scored twice—once from the penalty spot—before being replaced at the 73rd minute as Manuel Pellegrini’s side overwhelmed Mark Hughes’ team at the Britannia Stadium. 'For those asking, I’m OK,' Aguero posted on Twitter in both English and Spanish. 'I came off only as a precaution. Now let’s keep working toward our important upcoming fixtures.' Aguero’s night was a mix of brilliance and controversy. He opened the scoring in the 33rd minute with a powerful, composed finish after beating Marc Muniesa and Phil Bardsley, then netted his 21st goal of the season from the penalty spot in the 70th minute to make it 3-1. However, his second goal was disallowed after a handball incident reminiscent of Diego Maradona’s 'Hand of God.' Referee Lee Mason, after consulting his assistant, ruled the goal invalid and booked Aguero. The Stoke crowd responded with loud boos, turning the striker into an instant villain for the remainder of the match. Peter Crouch had equalized for Stoke five minutes before Aguero’s first goal, sending the teams into halftime tied. Manchester City regained the lead legitimately through a James Milner header 10 minutes into the second half. Despite the controversy, Aguero’s performance underscored his status as one of the Premier League’s most lethal strikers—especially timely with Wilfried Bony’s imminent arrival.

E atakantante arjentino ta marke 2 goles—nan un di penalty—anta ku e ta sakí na e 73 minüt ku e ekipa di Manuel Pellegrini ta supera e ekipa di Mark Hughes na e Britannia Stadium. Manchester City ta rekuperá e lideransa legitimamente pa James Milner ku e ta fá un testa na diez minüt despues di e segundu mitat. Despues di e kontroversia, e prestashon di Aguero ta subrayá su status komo un di e atakantanan más letal di Premier League—espesialmenti oportun ku e arribá di Wilfried Bony ta bini.

Roy Hodgson’s squad donned matching grey suits for a final team photo before flying from Luton Airport to Miami, where they held two preparatory friendlies before heading to South America. Players like Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Daniel Sturridge took selfies on the team bus, with Raheem Sterling and Danny Welbeck visible in the background. Others, including Jack Wilshere and Adam Lallana, shared photos from the flight, capturing the relaxed mood of the squad. article_content: When Amal Alamuddin updated her professional profile to reflect her married name — Amal Clooney — the website of her law firm, Doughty Street Chambers, temporarily went down under the weight of online outrage. Many reacted with disbelief, even anger, questioning how a highly accomplished human rights lawyer could ‘give up’ her name after marrying George Clooney. Critics, including writers from Elle and The Hoopla, framed the decision as a betrayal of feminism, suggesting that taking her husband’s name made her seem like an accessory rather than an independent professional. But the real issue isn’t her choice — it’s the expectation that every successful woman must make a political statement with her surname. The truth is, 86% of women in the U.S. adopt their spouse’s last name after marriage, according to a 2011 survey by TheKnot.com. For many, it’s a personal, practical, or even sentimental decision — not a surrender. Amal didn’t become less accomplished because her business card now says ‘Clooney.’ She built her reputation through years of legal work, landmark cases, and global advocacy — none of which vanished when she changed her name. To judge her as anti-feminist for this choice is to ignore her agency. It’s also to forget that men rarely face scrutiny when they keep their names — imagine if George became George Alamuddin. Would that be seen as a bold feminist act? Probably not. The pressure on women like Amal to be perfect symbols of equality is unfair. Her worth isn’t measured by her last name. It’s measured by her impact. And she’s already proven she’s more than enough.
translated_content: Cuando Amal Alamuddin a aktualizá su perfil profesional pa reflehá su nombre kasado — Amal Clooney — e sitia di su firma di abogadu, Doughty Street Chambers, a bini abajo temporalmente pa e pes di e reaksion online. Mucho reaksioná ku descreé, even ira, preguntandu komo una abogada di derechon humanu tan lograda ta podé ‘perde’ su nombre despues di kasá ku George Clooney. Kritiko, inkluyendo skribidó di Elle i The Hoopla, a konsiderá e desisio komo un traision di feminismo, sugeriendo ku tuma su nombre di marido ta fá e ta parese mas komo un akesorio ku un profesional independiente. Pero e problema real no ta su desisio — ta e esperansa ku cada muller lograda ta tin pa fá un declarashon politiko ku su apellido. E realidat ta ku 86% di e muller den Estados Unidos ta tuma su apellido di kasá despues di kasá, segun e sondeo di TheKnot.com di 2011. Pa muho, ta un desisio personal, praktiko, even sentimental — no un rendision. Amal no ta ménos lograda porque su tarjeta profesional a di ‘Clooney’. E ta konstruí su reputashon atravez di aña di trabou, kasos signifikativo, i defensa global — nada di ezo ta desaparese ku e ta kambia su nombre. Juza e komo anti-feminista pa e desisio ta ignorá su agencia. E ta tambe olvidá ku hòmber rara vez ta konsiderá ku e ta mantene su nombre — imagina si George ta bini George Alamuddin. E ta ser vistu komo un aksion feminista? Probablementi no. E presion pa muller komo Amal pa ser simbolo perfektu di igualdad ta injusto. Su valor no ta medí pa su apellido. Ta medí pa su impacto. Y e ta probá e ta mas ku sufisiente.
post_content: Amal Clooney changed her name after marriage… and the internet lost it. 🤯 But here’s the thing: 86% of women do the same. Her legacy isn’t in her surname — it’s in her groundbreaking human rights work. Let women choose. #NameItYourWay #FeminismIsChoice #AmalClooney

article_content: Positive early buzz surrounds the highly anticipated biblical epic 'Noah', starring Russell Crowe, as audiences prepare for its wide release this Friday. With a reported budget of $130 million, the film reimagines the story of Noah — the biblical figure commanded by God to build an ark before a cataclysmic flood — through a visually stunning and emotionally complex lens. The cast includes Anthony Hopkins, Jennifer Connelly, and Emma Watson. On Rotten Tomatoes, 'Noah' holds a 73% Fresh rating based on 11 reviews, with eight of them positive. Jeff McCarthy of The Hollywood Reporter called it 'an arresting piece of filmmaking' with potential to captivate global audiences, praising its fresh take on a story often reduced to children’s tales. Notably, the word 'God' is never spoken aloud in the film. Variety’s Scott Foundas described director Darren Aronofsky’s vision as 'counterintuitive, perhaps, but by no means sacrilegious' — bold, personal, and visually extravagant. He commended Crowe’s performance as 'superbly played' and predicted strong opening box office numbers fueled by curiosity. Pete Hammond of Movieline hailed it as 'magnificent' and 'truly epic in scope,' saying it lingers long after the credits roll. Steven D. Greydanus of the National Catholic Register called it a 'rare gift' — blending epic spectacle with deep character drama and thoughtful engagement with ancient Jewish texts, portraying biblical figures grappling with dilemmas as relevant today as ever. However, not all reviews were favorable. Alonso Duralde of The Wrap likened the film to Kevin Costner’s 'Waterworld', calling it 'a soggy slog' — overblown and underwritten. Aronofsky spent nearly 15 years bringing 'Noah' to the screen. He rose to prominence after the critical and commercial success of 'Black Swan' (2010), which earned over $329 million worldwide on a modest $13 million budget. This isn't the first cinematic version of Noah’s story: the 1928 silent film 'Noah's Ark', produced by Daryl F. Zanuck, saw tragedy during production when three extras drowned during the flood sequence.

article_content: While physical attraction has always played a role in human relationships, modern science is revealing surprising biological drivers behind who we find appealing. It’s not just about looks — smells, voices, and even facial structure may be wired into our instincts for choosing partners. Researchers like Kendra Schmid, a biostatistician, have developed formulas to measure facial attractiveness, using 29 precise metrics. According to her model, Brad Pitt scores impressively high at 9.3 out of 10, thanks to near-perfect proportions, including a face length-to-width ratio of 1.6 — the famed golden ratio. Angelina Jolie scores a solid 7.67, though her famously full lips slightly lower her rating since ideal mouth width is twice lip height. Meanwhile, scientists Karl Grammer and Elizabeth Oberzaucher have discovered that women release a scent called copulins during ovulation — a chemical signal that boosts men’s testosterone and triggers the release of androstenone, a scent that repels women not in their fertile window. This invisible exchange, as Oprah Winfrey puts it, turns nightclubs into 'battlefields' of biochemistry. Dr. Laura Berman, a sex therapist, notes that humans can detect over 10,000 scents, many subconsciously, and that body odor is a powerful indicator of chemistry. She advises women to smell their partner without cologne: if it excites them, it’s a sign of biological compatibility. Studies also show women prefer the scent of men whose immune system genes (MHC) differ from theirs — a trait that could improve offspring immunity. But here’s a twist: women on hormonal birth control tend to prefer men with similar MHC profiles, possibly because the pill tricks the body into thinking it’s pregnant. Research links this mismatch to higher rates of infidelity, conflict, and infertility in long-term relationships. Voice pitch matters too. Men find higher-pitched female voices more attractive — especially during peak fertility, when estrogen levels rise. Facial symmetry also plays a role: women appear more attractive to men when ovulating, possibly due to subtle skin glow and health cues. Even income affects perception: women rate financially successful men as more attractive, not out of greed, but because evolution favored partners who could provide resources for vulnerable infants. Yet none of this replaces the power of human connection. Dr. Berman insists that kissing is the ultimate test: 66% of women say they’d end a relationship after a bad first kiss. It’s not just about smell — it’s touch, rhythm, confidence, and emotional resonance. Regular, meaningful kisses — at least 10 seconds daily — are linked to far lower stress and depression levels in couples. In short: biology sets the stage, but intimacy writes the script.

E ta mas ku solo aspektu — olores, voz, i hasta forma di cara ta ligá ku instinkto nos pa seleksioná pareja. Investigadó komo Kendra Schmid, un biostatistiko, ta desenvolvé fórmula pa medí atrakshon facial, usándo 29 métrika presiso. Segun su modelo, Brad Pitt ta tén un skór altu di 9.3 di 10, gràsias a proporsión casi perfekto, inkluyendo un rasio di longidud i ancho di cara di 1.6 — e famoso rasio di oro. Angelina Jolie ta tén un skór sólidu di 7.67, pero e labios grandi ku ta famus di e ta bai un poko bai pa e rasio ideal di ancho di buká ta dos veç más grandi ku alturá di labios. Entretant, investigadó Karl Grammer i Elizabeth Oberzaucher ta descubrí ku mihé ta libera un olór kalla copulinas duranti ovulashon — un señal kímiko ki ta aumenta testosterona di homber i ta aktibá liberashon di androstenona, un olór ki ta repelé mihé ki ta no duranti su fenotipo fértil. E interashon invisibel, komo Oprah Winfrey ta di, ta turna bares i discoteká den 'batallas' di bioquímika. Dr. Laura Berman, un terapista seksual, ta nota ku humanos ta pòdé detektá mas di 10.000 olór, muchu di e ta subkonsientemente, i ku olór di kuerpo ta un indikador poderosu di kímika. E ta aconselhá mihé pa oler su pareja sin kolonia: si e ta excitá, e ta un señal di kómpatibilidad biológiko. Estudia tambe ta demonstra ku mihé ta preferí e olór di homber ku genétika di sistema inmunológico (MHC) ta diferent di e su — un karaterístiko ki ta pòdé mehorá inmunidat di híjó. Pero akí ta un giro: mihé ku kontraseptivo hormonal ta tendé a preferí homber ku MHC simila, posiblemente pa e pastí ta engañá kuerpo pa pensa ku e ta embarasá. Estudia ta liga e desajuste akí ku tasas mas altu di infidelidat, diskordansia, i infertilidat en relashon larga. También ta importá e ton di voz. Homber ta halá voz mas agudá di mihé — spesialment duranti piko di fértilidat, ku nivel di estrógeno ta subí. Simetría di cara tambe ta jega un papel: mihé ta parese mas atraktibo pa homber duranti ovulashon, posiblemente pa un brillo subtil di piel i indikadó di salú. Inkluzi inkom ta influiá percepsion: mihé ta da skór mas altu pa homber ku ta ganá mas dinero, no pa avarisia, mas bien pa evolushon ta favorisá pareja ki ta pòdé prové risorsa pa bebi ki ta dependiente. Pero nengún di e akí ta reemplasa e poder di koneksion humana. Dr. Berman ta insistí ku besu ta e prueba definitivo: 66% di mihé ta di ku e ta bira un relashon despues di un besu mal. E ta mas ku solo olór — e ta toque, ritmo, konsidensia, i resonansia emosional. Besu regulá i significativo — mínimu 10 segundu di dia — ta liga ku nivél mas baju di strés i depresion en parejas. En resumen: biología ta pón e escena, mas íntimidad ta eskríbí e historia.

article_content: A former spokesperson for L'Wren Scott has publicly defended her legacy, stating that despite financial challenges on the UK side of her business, her fashion brand was not in crisis at the time of her death. 'Her business was only seven years old,' the unnamed spokesperson told WWD. 'While some areas hadn't yet reached their potential, others were thriving.' Scott was found dead in her Manhattan apartment on Monday. UK filings with Companies House revealed her UK subsidiary, LS Fashion LTD, carried a deficit of nearly $5.9 million and owed creditors over $7.6 million as of October 2013. These debts had grown steadily since 2009. However, the spokesperson emphasized that LS Fashion Limited—the U.S.-based parent company—had made a standard loan investment into the UK subsidiary and remained fully capable of meeting all liabilities. 'The idea that L'Wren Scott was hounded by creditors or drowning in debt is preposterous,' he said. Scott never filed personal or corporate financial disclosures in the U.S., leaving the full scope of her financial health unclear. While she canceled her London Fashion Week show citing delayed fabric deliveries, insiders say she was preparing a global restructuring and rebrand—not a shutdown. Cathy Horyn, a longtime friend and New York Times fashion critic, revealed in a tribute that Scott planned to announce the closure of her business that week. Yet Horyn cautioned against assuming financial distress alone led to her suicide. 'Like many small designers, she struggled with cash flow, management, and production delays,' Horyn wrote. Though romantically linked to Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger since 2001, Scott kept her personal and professional struggles private. Friends noted she had withdrawn socially in recent months. Jagger, who was touring in Australia when he received the news, called her death 'tragic' and said he was 'still struggling to understand.'

'Su negosio ta solamente siete aña antiguo,' dió e spokeman anonimo pa WWD. 'Mientras kier partidu no a aki todavía su potensial, otro partidu ta prospera.' Scott a bini gusá na apartamentu di Manhattan na lundi. Arkivu britániko pa Companies House a revelá ku subsidiaria britániko di Scott, LS Fashion LTD, ta tén un défisit di casi $5.9 mion y ta debiendo $7.6 mion pa kreditor komo na oktuber 2013. E deuda ta amentá progresibamente despues di 2009. Però e spokeman a enfatizá ku LS Fashion Limited—e kompanía párenti na Estados Unidos—a fá un inversión di préstamo estándar pa subsidiaria britániko i ta totalmenti kapas pa satisfer to e obligashon. 'E ideia ku L'Wren Scott ta perseguidu pa kreditor o ahogá pa deuda ta absurdo,' a di el. Scott no a presentá nengun informashon finansiero personal u korporativo na Estados Unidos, asina ku e eskop total di su salú finansiero ta klar. Mientras e a kanselá su presentashon pa London Fashion Week di kusa di entrega retardá di telas, insidèr a di ku e ta prepara un reestrukturashon global i rebrand—no un kierre. Cathy Horyn, un amigu di longu tiempu i krítiko di moda di The New York Times, a revelá na un tributu ku Scott tabata planear anunsia kierre di su negosio na e semana. Però Horyn a konsidera no konklui ku strés finansiero solamente ta causa di su muerte. 'Komotanti diseñador piku, e ta bini ku problemas di fluí di tesoro, administrashon, i demora di produksión,' a skribí Horyn. Malgrá e ta ligá romantikamenti ku Mick Jagger, frontman di The Rolling Stones, desde 2001, Scott a manteni su problemátika personal i profesional den privá. Amigu a nota ku e a retirá sosialmenti na mesanan pasá. Jagger, ku tabata turá na Australia ku e ta tén siete konsertronan di e gira '14 On Fire', a di e muerte ta 'trágiko' i ku e ta 'aun strugandu pa komprende.'
post_content: L'Wren Scott wasn't broke—just overwhelmed. 💔 Despite UK debt reports, her US business was solid. She was planning a rebrand, not a shutdown. Friends say stress, not money, broke her heart. Rest in power, L'Wren. #LWrenScott #FashionLegacy #MentalHealthMatters

article_content: Hundreds of asylum seekers are being temporarily housed in two seaside hotels in Bournemouth, Dorset, at public expense, as the Home Office grapples with a recent surge in arrivals. Coachloads of migrants have been transported to the area, where they are receiving accommodation, three meals daily, and basic support at the three-star Roundhouse and Heathlands Hotels. Over 88 individuals are staying at the Roundhouse, located just a 10-minute walk from Bournemouth Beach, and 67 at the Heathlands. This follows similar arrangements in Folkestone, Kent, where 130 asylum seekers are lodged at the Grand Burstin Hotel near the Port of Dover. The relocation stems from overcrowding in detention centers around London, prompting the Home Office to partner with the Britannia hotel group and contractor Clearsprings to provide emergency housing. Many of those being sheltered are fleeing conflict zones in Africa and the Middle East. Although the summer holiday season has ended, both Bournemouth hotels remain fully booked — rooms that normally cost between £50 and £160 per night are now occupied by asylum seekers. Local officials have voiced concern. Conor Burns, Conservative MP for Bournemouth West, said the group was previously based in Croydon and is now being dispersed. He expressed unease that Bournemouth might become a regular destination and pledged to raise the issue with the Immigration Minister. Tobias Ellwood, MP for Bournemouth East, acknowledged police supervision but stressed the need to ensure the arrangement remains safe and controlled. John Beesley, Leader of Bournemouth Borough Council, confirmed the Home Office assured them this is a strictly short-term measure — no longer than two weeks. Asylum seekers will not have access to local services such as schools or social care during their stay. A Home Office spokesperson reiterated that hotel use is intended only as an emergency, temporary solution and emphasized the UK’s commitment to offering sanctuary. Staff at both hotels declined to confirm or comment on the presence of asylum seekers. Meanwhile, earlier this week, 24 people were rescued from a refrigerated lorry in Dover after attempting to cross the Channel illegally.

article_content: Three-year-old Oliver Akenhead had a terrifying close call when a manhole cover gave way under his weight during playtime with his 8-year-old sister, Daisy, in Kelloe, County Durham. CCTV footage captured the moment the cover flipped open as he stepped onto it, causing him to sink chest-deep into the shaft. Miraculously, Oliver managed to brace himself with his arms, preventing a full fall. His screams alerted Daisy and nearby residents, who quickly pulled him out. He suffered cuts on his legs and back, along with a bruise on his cheek from the flipping cover. His parents, Stewart and Amy Akenhead, are now calling for more frequent inspections of public infrastructure, warning that next time, the outcome might not be so fortunate. 'He was terrified,' said Mrs. Akenhead. 'This isn't just a scare—it could change how he sees the world.' Northumbrian Water, which manages nearly half a million manholes across the North East, responded within hours by securing the cover with cement. In a statement, they expressed regret and relief that Oliver wasn’t seriously hurt. But they also noted that regular inspections of every manhole aren’t feasible, urging residents and local authorities to report visible damage immediately. With an annual maintenance budget of £800,000, the company says it prioritizes urgent reports—but many wonder if prevention should come before reaction.

Footahe di CCTV a kapturá e momento ku e tapa se rumbó bai bai ku el a pisa, y e a hende hondo pa su pecho den e drenashon. Milagrosamente, Oliver a logra konservá su pesu ku e braçanan, evitando e kada kompletu. E grito di el a alertá Daisy i residente ku ta mas ku, ku rapidamente a sacá el afuera. Northumbrian Water, ku ta gerencia mas o ménos medio mion di tapanan di drenashon na e North East, a responde den horan bini ku segurá e tapa ku sementu. Den e declarashon, e a ekspresá arrepentimento i alivio ku Oliver no ta tene lesionan serio. Ku un budjet anual di 800.000£, e kompanía a diz ku e prioriza raportonan urgente—but mesteran ta preguntá si prevensión ta mas importante ku reaksion.

article_content: The recent obsession with shirt swaps and celebrity drama in football feels exhausting—let’s talk about real performance. Mario Balotelli, Liverpool’s £16 million summer signing, hasn’t scored a single goal in the Premier League since arriving from AC Milan. While fans and former players urge him to be benched, manager Brendan Rodgers has kept faith, fearing backlash if he drops his most expensive acquisition. Against Hull City, Balotelli showed flickers of movement, but nothing close to match-winning impact. His lack of pressing, low energy, and passive positioning have become defining traits—traits that couldn’t be further from the dynamism of Arsenal’s Alexis Sanchez. Sanchez, meanwhile, has been the engine of Arsenal’s season. At the Stadium of Light, he didn’t wait for opportunities—he created them. Chasing down lost causes, harrying defenders, and turning mistakes into goals, he scored twice in one match. His second came in the 92nd minute after forcing a clumsy error from the goalkeeper, proving he never stops running. That’s the standard Balotelli needs to meet—not just in skill, but in spirit. Rodgers could show Balotelli footage of Luis Suarez’s relentless runs last season—but that might crush his confidence. Instead, showing him Sanchez’s performances offers something more constructive: a blueprint for becoming indispensable. Sanchez isn’t just talented—he’s tireless. He doesn’t react to the game; he controls it. Balotelli must stop standing still when passes go astray. He must chase, press, and fight for every ball—even when luck isn’t on his side. Football isn’t just about finishing; it’s about creating chances through sheer will. If Balotelli wants to silence his critics, he needs to start acting like the player Arsenal paid for—not the one everyone hoped Liverpool bought.

Mario Balotelli, firma di Liverpool pa £16 millón na verano, a bini pa AC Milan i a no marká un gol na Premier League. Mientras fans i eks-jugadores ta pidié pa e bini keda pa banca, entrenador Brendan Rodgers a konservá fidelidat, temiendo reaksió si e bini keda fora. Kontra Hull City, Balotelli a mustrá señales di movimientu, pero nada ku ta cerca di un prestashon ganador. Su falta di presión, energi bai, i pozishon pasivo ta kierá komo karaktiristika su—karaktiristikan ku ta masha distante di dinamismo di Alexis Sanchez di Arsenal. Sanchez, entretanto, a ser motor di sezon di Arsenal. Na Stadium of Light, e a no espèrá oportunidat—e a krea e si. E a kore pa kasos perdí, a presioná defensas, i a konvertí eror pa gol, e a marká dos gol na un partidu. Segundu e a bini na minút 92 despues di forsa un eror malo di e portero, demostrando e a no pará korí. Ese ta e nivel ku Balotelli ta nesesitá lográ—no solo pa skil, mas tambe pa espiritu. Rodgers a pudí mustrá Balotelli film di korí sin pará di Luis Suarez na sezon pasá—pero e a pudí daña konfiansa su. Mas bien, mustrá e prestashon di Sanchez ta ofresé algo mas konstruktivo: un plan pa bini indispensabel. Sanchez a no solamente ta talentoso—e ta sin pará. E a no reaksioná pa juego—e ta kontrola e. Balotelli ta nesesitá pará na posishon ku pasa ta errá. E ta nesesitá kore, presioná, i lucha pa bini bal—mes ku suerte ta no pa su lado. Futbol a no solamente ta pa terminá—e ta pa krea oportunidat pa pura voluntad. Si Balotelli ta bini pa silensia e krítiko, e ta nesesitá empeçá akta komo e jugador ku Arsenal a paga—no komo e ku todo mundo ta esperá Liverpool a konsiguí.

article_content: After a rocky start to 2015, Bayern Munich bounced back with a 2-0 victory over Stuttgart at the Mercedes-Benz Arena. Arjen Robben and David Alaba netted goals in each half, giving the team their first win since the winter break and reigniting their Bundesliga title push. To mark the occasion, players and their partners attended a themed costume party hosted by Ana Ivanovic — partner of midfielder Bastian Schweinsteiger — at Munich’s Cafe Reitschule. Many guests dressed in full Western attire, channeling the spirit of classic frontier films. One standout look came from defender Javi Martinez, who arrived dressed as Woody from Toy Story — a fun, unexpected choice that brought laughter to the crowd. Attendees included forward Robert Lewandowski with wife Anna, midfielder Mario Götze with girlfriend Ann-Kathrin Brommel, goalkeeper Manuel Neuer, and veteran Xabi Alonso, who arrived with his wife Nagore Arambur as light rain began to fall. This win followed a surprising 4-1 loss to Wolfsburg and a 1-1 draw against Schalke, making it a crucial step in Bayern’s campaign. With the victory, they now sit eight points clear at the top of the Bundesliga table.
